**Fix.** Attach whenever the signature verifies (as the attribute patch always did); the toggle decides at run
time; no restart. Proven with the reporter's rows: level 2 granted 2, level 3 granted 3.

**Rule.** A one-shot install (hook, trampoline, vtable write) must never depend on a setting that is only known
later - per-character, per-save, or loaded after the install point. Install on the signature, gate in the hook.
The check is the Patches readout at data load on a fresh launch: every group whose code was found must say
installed, whatever the toggles say. Gate rule `no-restart-gated-installers` (forbid the phrase "Turn it on and
restart" / "restart to attach" in sources) closes the class mechanically.

## The Nexus Short Description is cut at 350 characters on the live page - a longer summary ends mid-word and nobody is told (2026-09-18)

**Symptom.** the owner, after posting Apocrypha Menu Framework 1.8.9: *"the nexus short description box has word
limit so this was all that showed"* - the summary on the live page stopped at "...themes, real font". The
page file's Short Description was 419 characters; the Nexus API confirmed the stored summary is exactly 350.

**Cause.** The Short Description was written like the description - one more place to say everything - with
no check against the field it goes into. Nexus's summary field keeps 350 characters and silently drops the
rest; it also shows BBCode literally, so Infinity UI's `[b]` tags would have appeared as text. Lock
Interaction Overhaul (363) and Perfected Wheeler (353) were over the limit too, in the distro, waiting to be
pasted.

**Fix.** All four summaries rewritten under 350 (AMF 340, LIO 345, Wheeler 349, Infinity UI 226 and
tag-free). Gate rule `page-summary-fits-nexus-field` (kind `page-summary-max-chars`, maxChars 350,
forbidBBCode) fails any package whose distro page carries a longer or tagged summary; the page template says
the limit beside the field.

**Rule.** A field on someone else's form has the form's limit, not ours: when text is written for a Nexus
field, the limit of that field is looked up (or measured off the live page) and gated before the text is
declared ready. The measurement is the Nexus API's stored value, not a recollection of the limit.

## Opening a file for writing before its new content exists destroys it when the script fails halfway (2026-09-18)

**Symptom.** The Apocrypha Menu Framework distro page (`11. Nexus distro\Apocrypha Menu Framework
exus-page.txt`,
25 KB) was empty after a Python rewrite of its Short Description. The script had raised `TypeError` on the
`write` line - after `io.open(p, "wb")` had already truncated the file. Three attempts at the same script
each re-truncated it; the content had to be recovered from the Nexus API's copy of the posted description
(the 1.8.9 page was live, so it was recoverable; a page not yet posted would not have been).

**Cause.** `open(path, "wb").write(build(...))` evaluates the open (truncation) before the argument (the
build). Any error in building the bytes leaves a zero-length file. The distro folder is not under git, so
there was no local history.

**Fix.** Build the whole new content in memory first, write it to `<path>.tmp`, then `os.replace(tmp,
path)`; the original is untouched until the replacement exists. Recovery: `GET
/v1/games/skyrimspecialedition/mods/<id>.json` returns `description` (BBCode with `<br />` line prefixes to
strip and HTML entities to unescape) and `summary`; the rebuilt file matched every section the transcript
recorded.

**Rule.** Never open a file for writing in the same expression that builds its content. Build, then write
to a temporary name, then replace - for every script that rewrites a file in `11. Nexus distro`, `.MD` or a
repo, because those folders have no undo. The Nexus API is the backup for any page already posted.

## A spliced gamepad press proves the framework's own input path and nothing else - ImGui's Win32 backend polls XInput by itself, so a REAL controller reaches ImGui twice (2026-09-18)

**Symptom.** Apocrypha Menu Framework 1.8.9's on-screen keyboard passed its proof (D-pad and A through the
input splice typed "iron"), then the owner with a real controller: *"backspace didnt work, and neither did
shift, the dpad presses leak out of the keyboard"*.

**Cause.** `ImGui_ImplWin32_NewFrame()` calls `ImGui_ImplWin32_UpdateGamepads()`, which polls
`XInputGetState` every frame and feeds the D-pad, face buttons and sticks into ImGui on its own - beside the
framework's translation of the game's input events, which is where the keyboard takes its presses. A real
pad is seen by XInput, so ImGui's nav moved under the keyboard and the backend's FaceLeft/FaceUp (X/Y) events
undid the keyboard's shift and backspace. A press spliced into the game's queue never touches XInput, so the
proof could not see the second path. The framework's own guard (`io.BackendFlags |= HasGamepad`) had even
been added to make that backend path work, back when the translation was not trusted.

**Fix.** `IMGUI_IMPL_WIN32_DISABLE_GAMEPAD` in both imgui overlay ports (`cmake/ports` and
`cmake/ports-17`), port-version bumped so vcpkg rebuilds; every gamepad event now has one source. Verified by
the absence of `XInputGetState`/`xinput1_4.dll` strings in both DLLs - `build.bat` alone did NOT rebuild the
port (imgui.lib kept its 2026-09-05 date); `configure.bat` had to run first.

**Rule.** When a proof drives input through the game's queue, list every OTHER path by which the same
device reaches the same consumer (a backend's own polling, a raw-input hook, a second plugin) and either
close them or drive them too. A proof that exercises one path is a proof of that path only. And after
changing a vcpkg overlay port, check the library's timestamp: the build script does not re-install ports.

## The Loading Menu's hooks run on FOUR different threads, and only the movie's Display hook is on the one that draws - a swap from any other is a race with the draw (2026-09-18)

**Symptom.** crash-2026-09-18-05-02-11 during the owner's play: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION in SkyrimSE.exe
85721 (null [operand removed]) under DisplayLoadingScreen (38085) on the JobList thread, with Model Sync's Display hook
on the stack. The engine function on the stack under the hook started at exactly the original Display
pointer the hook had saved ([value removed] = 81728), so the crash was inside the engine drawing the loading
movie, not inside anything the plugin did directly.

**Cause.** Model Sync applied its swap (engine SetModel, [id removed]) and read the hint from whichever hook was
running: LoadingMenu::AdvanceMovie, ProcessMessage, the RequestLoadingText callback, or the movie's own
Advance/Display. Measured with a thread-id line per hook: AdvanceMovie on the game thread, ProcessMessage on
four different threads across four loads, the loading movie's Display on a different JobList thread per load.
Anything mutated from one of those while the draw thread traverses the movie is a null node in that traversal.
The first draft of the fix (a file-existence check on the NIF) was the wrong theory: the stack was a draw, not a
load - read the resolved frame under your own hook before deciding what the engine was doing.

**Fix.** Every pick path only records the wanted screen; ApplyWanted runs from the movie's Advance/Display
hooks before the engine's draw. Thread ids stay logged at info so the next crash log comes with them, and the
plugin keeps the previous run's log as .prev. Not proven end to end: the driver's spliced bumper presses do
not produce a Loading Menu Overhaul swipe during coc loads, so applied stayed 0; the hold and the absence of a
crash across eight loads are what was measured.

**Rule.** Before touching an engine object from a hook, measure the thread the hook runs on (one log line
with GetCurrentThreadId per hook) and compare it with the thread that consumes the object. A menu's
AdvanceMovie, its ProcessMessage and its movie's Display are not one thread. And when a crash stack has our
frame under an engine frame, resolve the engine frame against the pointers we saved: it names the call.

## A game that vanishes with no crash log was killed by something that writes none - check the framework's own watchdog before hunting a crash (2026-09-18)

**Symptom.** Twice in one evening the owner's game ended while he was typing here (*"if you didnt kill the game i
didnt either"*, then *"the game died again"*). No crash-*.log for either. The first time the AMF log had already been
overwritten by the next launch; the second time it ended with `watchdog: terminating the process - no frame for 120s
(window 120s) - treating the game as hung`.

**Cause.** AMF's hang watchdog counts frames from the render hook. Skyrim presents no frames while its window is not
in the foreground (or is minimised), so an alt-tabbed, perfectly healthy game looked hung and was terminated with
TerminateProcess - which runs no handlers, so Crash Logger writes nothing. The first death was read as "unexplained"
and an hour went into two real crash logs from other runs before the pattern showed.

**Fix.** The watchdog holds its clock at 'now' while the game window is not the foreground window or is minimised,
logs the stand-down and the return, and restarts the full window when focus comes back (AMF 1.9.1). Gate rule
`watchdog-stands-down-when-unfocused` requires GetForegroundWindow in any Watchdog.cpp that has a stall message.

**Rule.** A "no frames" watchdog needs a model of when no frames are EXPECTED (unfocused, minimised, a paused
device) before it may treat silence as a hang. And when a game dies with no crash log, the first place to look is
the log of anything that can end the process on purpose - a watchdog, a fast-exit hook - and that log must survive
the next launch (.prev), or the evidence is gone with the relaunch.

## A guard placed after the call it guards is not a guard - CommonLibSSE-NG's SKSE::Init opens the Address Library itself (2026-09-18)

**Symptom.** oproso's wheeler.log for Perfected Wheeler 1.3.2: the build mark, the two banner lines, then
CommonLib's bare `[critical] failed to open address library file` - and NO `[AddressLibrary]` line, the one the
1.2.9 guard was written to print for exactly this user.

**Cause.** In all five mods that carry the guard (Wheeler, AMF, Item Explorer, Model Sync, CNO) the call sat
AFTER `SKSE::Init(a_skse)`. CommonLibSSE-NG's Init touches `REL::IDDatabase::get()`, which opens the database
and calls `report_and_fail` when the file is missing, so the process was gone before the guard's first line.
The 1.2.9 proof used an environment variable that simulates a missing file while the real file was present, so
Init succeeded and the guard's message showed - the proof never exercised the order.

**Fix.** Logger init, then the guard, then `SKSE::Init`, in all five mods (Wheeler 1.3.3, AMF 1.9.2, Item
Explorer 1.1.0, Model Sync 1.0.2, CNO 1.1.5). Gate rule `address-library-guard-runs-before-skse-init`
(repo-source-forbid-regex: Init text before Guard text in a CommonLib mod's sources) fails the package.

**Rule.** A pre-check must run before EVERYTHING that can fail on the condition it checks - including the
library's own initialisation - and its proof must make the real condition true, not simulate it past the
point that matters. When a simulation is the only safe proof, say in the ledger that the order is unproven.

## PGPatcher runs only through MO2's own shortcut with the PGPatcher Output mod DISABLED, and MO2 rewrites ModOrganizer.ini and the profile lists on exit (2026-09-18)

**What happened.** After installing Faultier's PBR Landscapes and five PBR hub addons into Njordlinger, PGPatcher 2.0.0 was
launched directly (`tools\PGPatcher\PGPatcher.exe --autostart`) because its settings.json already names the MO2 instance.
It bailed: `[critical] Please verify that you are launching PGPatcher from MO2, VFS not detected.` The owner: *"it says to
launch from vfs"*. Launched through MO2 (`ModOrganizer.exe -p Njordlinger moshortcut://:PGPatcher`, with executable entry 14's
arguments set to `--autostart`) it bailed again: `[critical] If outputting to MO2 you must disable the mod PGPatcher Output
first to prevent issues with MO2 VFS`. The owner: *"you have to disable the pg patcher out put mod"*. With `-PGPatcher Output`
in the profile it ran (84 s). On MO2's exit the ini had been rewritten (LF -> CRLF, selected_profile changed to the launched
profile) and modlist.txt had gained ~40 disabled rows for folders the profile did not list - so the edits made "before
launch" were not the file MO2 wrote back, and a byte-level restore keyed on the old line ending silently did nothing.

**Do instead.** (1) PGPatcher: MO2 closed -> set `-PGPatcher Output` in the profile -> set entry 14 arguments `--autostart`
(or `--autostart-update`) -> `ModOrganizer.exe -p <profile> moshortcut://:PGPatcher` -> wait for PGPatcher.exe to exit ->
close MO2 -> re-enable the output mod, clear the arguments, restore selected_profile. (2) Any edit to ModOrganizer.ini or a
profile list is made with MO2 CLOSED and re-verified AFTER MO2 has exited, by grep, not assumed from the write. The 18
`nmn_footprints\*_m.dds` texture errors are pre-existing (same 18 in the 09-15 run) and are not PBR failures.

## A completed quest can stay ENABLED, and console completequest fires neither a stage nor a stop event - react to the flag from more than one trigger (2026-09-18)

**What happened.** The Hjerim start's Blood on the Ice clean-up listened for MS11's TESQuestStartStopEvent (stop) and
checked IsCompleted() then. On the first live test `completequest MS11` set completed=true, left the quest enabled, and
fired nothing: no stop, no stage. The clean-up never ran. `setstage MS11 250` (the completing stage, QSDT flag 1 read
from Skyrim.esm) DOES fire a TESQuestStageEvent; entering the cell fires BGSActorCellEvent.

**Do instead.** For "do X once quest Q is done", check the completed flag from every moment it can become true or
matter: the quest's stage events, its stop event, the player entering the cell where X shows, and game load. Read the
quest's completing stage out of the QUST record (QSDT flags) rather than assuming the last stage, and drive the proof
with `setstage <completing stage>`, not `completequest`, which is not the path the game takes.

## Migrating a renamed mod's INI: the OLD file's values are the player's and must win once, then be written and retired - the first cut let the shipped file win (2026-09-18)

**What happened.** Auto Audio Output Switch 1.0.3 renamed its INI; 1.0.4 added migration that read the old file first
and let the new file's values win "so nothing set since is undone". Live test: the old file said uResetDelayMs=777, the
freshly shipped new file said 500, and 500 won - the player's value was exactly what got lost, because after a rename
the new file is always the shipped defaults. The opposite of the point.

**Do instead.** Old values override the new file ONCE, are saved into the new file, and the old file is renamed
`.migrated` so the override cannot recur or undo a later edit; log the count and the rename. Prove it with a
distinctive value in the old file and the shipped value in the new one, and read the loaded value back from the log.

## A count subrecord is a promise the engine keeps even when it is a lie - COCT said five after two CNTO entries were deleted, and the crash named SPID (2026-09-19)

**What happened.** Removing the Imperial Tribune cuirass and boots from Tullius' inventory in Civil War Guard Armor
Replacer deleted two CNTO entries and left COCT saying there were still five. The plugin parsed, round-tripped
byte-exactly and opened cleanly; the game died at data load with a null form inside Spell Perk Item Distributor, so
the first hour went into SPID's own INI files and its distribution rules. The engine does not count the entries - it
reads COCT of them, and the two it read past the end of the list were whatever followed in the record.

**Do instead.** Every count subrecord is checked against the entries that follow it before the plugin is deployed or
packaged: COCT/CNTO on containers and COBJ, LLCT/LVLO on levelled lists, KSIZ/KWDA on keywords. This is now
mechanical - `.MD\scripts\esp-audit.py` counts them, also flags a reference to a record the file does not define and
an ARMO MODL that is not 4 bytes, and `.MD\scripts\plugin-gate.ps1` runs it over every plugin a test is about to load
(`game-relaunch.ps1` calls it, and a failure stops the launch). Gate rule `esp-counts-match-entries` runs the same
audit at package time. Note the shape of the false trail: a data-load crash is attributed to whichever plugin is
mid-load when the bad pointer is followed, which is rarely the plugin that holds it.

**Rule.** When an edit changes how many of something a record holds, the count is part of the edit, not a detail -
and the check belongs in a tool, because the edit script is written fresh each time and the count is invisible.

## FFDec writes colour attributes ALPHABETICALLY, so a recolour that reported success had changed nothing (2026-09-18)

**What happened.** The recolour pass for Norden UI - Black substituted
`red="\d+" green="\d+" blue="\d+"` in FFDec's exported XML. FFDec writes `alpha`, `blue`, `green`, `red` - in that
order - so the pattern never matched a single node. `re.sub` returned the text unchanged, the script rebuilt the SWF,
printed the file size and reported success, and the menu was identical in game. The next round of work went into
whether the file was being shadowed, whether the menu used different art, and whether MO2 was mounting the mod.

**Do instead.** Substitute per attribute (`(red|green|blue)="\d+"`), and never trust a transform's own report: read
the EFFECT back out of the file that shipped. `.MD\scripts\swf-colour-gate.py --against <source mod>` fails when any
SWF in a recoloured mod is byte-identical to the art it was made from, which is precisely what a silent no-op leaves
behind; its colour mode re-reads a built file's fills and fails when something that should be dark is not.

**Rule.** A tool that reports what it *intended* is not evidence. The evidence is the artefact, read back by
something that did not perform the transform.

## A light plugin's index belongs to the LOAD ORDER, not to the plugin - a FormID written down earlier in the session addressed nothing (2026-09-19)

**What happened.** The armour photo run built console commands from light index [value removed], read from the game earlier the
same evening. Two new mods had been installed since, the plugin had moved to index 210 (FE0D2), and every
`player.additem FE0D0xxx` added nothing at all - silently, because the console reports no error for a form that does
not exist. Three runs were spent looking for the fault in the equip order, the camera and the console's timing.

**Do instead.** Resolve the id against the RUNNING game at the moment the command is built:
`.MD\scripts\Resolve-FormId.ps1 -Plugin <name>.esp -Local [value removed]` asks DevBench's mods inspector for the live index,
refuses a local id outside [value removed]-[value removed] for a light plugin, and fails outright when the plugin is not loaded - which is
the answer that matters, because the alternative is a command that quietly does nothing.

**Rule.** Anything derived from the load order is re-read after anything that can change the load order, and a
session-old number is treated as stale by default.

## A frame recorder that dies silently turns every later capture into the same old picture (2026-09-18)

**What happened.** GameWatch's recorder stopped at 23:13. Three subsequent capture runs copied `latest.jpg`, reported
new screenshots, and were all the same frame from before the first equip. The armour that was supposedly not
rendering had been rendering the whole time.

**Do instead.** Capture through `gamewatch.ps1 snap <name>`, which refuses to copy a frame older than `-MaxAge`
seconds (default 8) and exits non-zero, and `latest` now fails the same way. A picture that predates the action it is
meant to show is not weak evidence, it is evidence of the previous state.

**Rule.** Any watcher that can die must prove it is alive at the moment its output is used - a timestamp check is
one line and removes a whole class of confident, wrong reporting.

## Skyrim's console is asynchronous: a burst of commands drops some, and an unequip queued before an equip lands after it (2026-09-18)

**What happened.** Driving the armour test through DevBench's console, `player.additem` and `player.equipitem` were
sent together; the equip ran against an inventory that did not hold the item yet. An `unequipall` sent just before an
equip arrived after it and stripped the character bare in the photograph. `tfc 1` froze the game, so equips issued
afterwards never appeared on screen at all - plain `tfc` does not freeze it.

**Do instead.** One command at a time, with the state read back between them: add the items first, confirm they are
in the inventory, then equip; never send a strip and a dress in the same burst; free the camera with `tfc`, never
`tfc 1`, when anything still has to change on screen.

## Folding one mod into another is a merge with a winner - the Dynamic Interface Patcher's grey output overwrote the black race menu (2026-09-18)

**What happened.** Consolidating the black reskin into a single mod copied `Norden RaceMenu DIP Output` into
Norden UI - Black wholesale. That output is the patcher's result built from NORDEN's own grey art, so it replaced the
black `racesex_menu.swf` with a grey one, undoing the work it was meant to preserve. Nothing reported it: both files
existed, both were valid, and the mod looked complete.

**Do instead.** A consolidation lists, for every file, which copy wins and why, before anything is copied; where two
sources provide the same path, the one that is the product of our own pass wins and the other is rebuilt from it.
Afterwards the result is read back (`swf-colour-gate.py`) rather than assumed from the copy succeeding.

## Before recolouring art, ask the RUNNING game which movie draws the thing - an hour went into the quest tracker instead of the item popups (2026-09-18)

**What happened.** The "item received" popups were assumed to be drawn by `QuestItemList.swf` because its position in
the file (0.775, 0.28) matched where they appear. They are drawn by the HUD. A whole pass recoloured the quest
tracker, and the owner's answer - *"Those little pop-ups are fine for now"* - was the only reason it did not go
further.

**Do instead.** Open the menu in game, list the loaded movies (`menu list` through DevBench) and identify the file by
what the game has loaded while the element is on screen, not by geometry or by name. Rule 30 in one line: ask the
object what it is, do not infer it from what it looks like.

## A packager that SEEDS from the previous release ships the previous release's content under the new number (2026-09-19)

**What happened.** `package-mod.ps1` builds a package by copying the previous one and replacing the binaries. Three
kinds of content therefore travelled forward untouched, all in one evening on Item Explorer 1.1.1 and Apocrypha Menu
Framework 1.9.5:

* the **INI**, so a release whose compiled defaults had changed shipped last version's defaults beside them (rule 16);
* the **translation files** - and a FOMOD carries each language twice, under `Languages\<Lang>\` and `Languages\All\`,
  plus English under `Common\` - so a version that added text to a page would have shipped that text missing in every
  language while the repo's own files were correct (rule 66);
* the **README**, whose version line was only retargeted when it read `Version X.Y.Z`; a heading of the form
  `Item Explorer 1.1.0` was left alone, and the lookup only ever searched the package ROOT while a FOMOD keeps the
  README under `Common\`.

Separately the same script wrote a single flat `SKSE\Plugins\` for a mod with TWO build lines, dropping `Line-17` and
`Line-SE-AE16` that the FOMOD installs from - so the package's own installer pointed at folders that were not there.

**Why it was invisible.** Every one of these produces a package that exists, is the right size, and opens correctly.
Nothing is missing in a way a human notices, and the seeded content is *plausible* - it is simply one version old.

**What actually closed it.** `gate-rules.json` already held `both-build-lines-match-the-build-tree`, written after an
earlier instance of exactly the last defect - but the only caller was `pre-finalize-check.ps1`, so it could not fire
until long after the broken package had been installed and tested. `package-mod.ps1` now runs `package-gate.ps1`
itself and exits non-zero on any hit that is not a distro/page-text rule, and it caught both defects on the very next
run. The producing side was fixed too: both build lines are written and version-stamped separately, and the INI,
translations and README are refreshed from the repo rather than inherited.

**Rule.** A gate that runs only at the END of a pipeline cannot stop a defect entering the middle of it. Run the check
at the step that can create the fault, not only at the step that publishes it. And anything a packager COPIES from a
previous release is stale by default - content with a source of truth in the repo is refreshed from the repo, and
only content with no other home is inherited.

## DevBench's `console` op kills this game every time it is used - two crashes, same address (2026-09-19)

**Symptom.** Driving `console` through the gamelink DevBench tool crashed Skyrim instantly, twice in one session:
`crash-2026-09-19-23-27-37.log` on `help` at the main menu, and `crash-2026-09-19-23-33-00.log` on
`coc WhiterunDragonsreach` with the player loaded in the Winking Skeever. Both are
`EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION ... Tried to execute memory at [value removed]` - the SAME address both times - with the
command string sitting in RDI (`"help"`, `"coc WhiterunDragonsreach"`) and `devbench.dll ... RE::Console::ExecuteCommand`
on the stack. So it is not a main-menu-only fault, and it is not state-dependent: the call itself jumps somewhere that
is not code.

**Attribution.** Targeted, one check, the PDB-resolved log (the standing rule): the mod under test,
`LoadingMenuOverhaulModelSync.dll` v1.0.3, appears only in the module list and the plugin list - ZERO frames in the
stack - and the two crashes are separated by a full game restart and a different command. The console op is the
common factor and the only frame that names our tooling.

**Cost.** It cost the in-game proof it was meant to get: the loading screen that the `coc` would have produced never
happened, so the merged build's swipe-driven model swap stayed unproven that session even though everything else was
verified.

**Rule.** Do not drive Skyrim through DevBench's `console` op on this instance until that op is fixed in DevBench -
use the player's own input path (SendInput scancodes into the focused window worked for the whole main-menu -> load
sequence the same evening) or a tool op that does the work in-process. The wider lesson is the familiar one: a driving
tool that crashes the game is worse than no driving tool, because the crash looks like the mod under test until the
log is read.

## A 32-byte INPUT struct makes SendInput refuse every key with error 87 - the "proven" scan-code drivers never pressed anything (2026-09-20)

**Symptom.** `send-scan.ps1` (lifted from `devbench-loops/tween-press.ps1`) reported `focus: True` and printed every
press on time, `SetForegroundWindow` had the game in front, and the game did nothing: no Tween menu on Tab, no
`Dodge key 42 pressed` in TK Dodge AIO's debug log, the vanity camera kept spinning as if nobody had touched a key.

**Cause.** The P/Invoke `INPUT` was declared with a union of three `long` pads (offsets 0, 8, 16), which marshals to
24 bytes; with the `type` field that is a 32-byte `INPUT`. On x64 the real union is 32 bytes (`MOUSEINPUT`) and
`INPUT` is 40. `SendInput` checks `cbSize`, returns 0 and sets error 87 (`ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`) - and the
scripts discarded the return value (`[void]`), so the failure was silent. Verified in one call: the 32-byte struct
sends 0, the same struct with a fourth pad at offset 24 sends 1.

**What that means for the record.** `tween-press.ps1` and `aie104-inventory-highlight-real.ps1` carried the same
struct, so whatever those runs concluded from "after Tab #N" samples was measured with no key ever reaching the game.
The 2026-09-19 entry above that says SendInput scancodes "worked for the whole main-menu -> load sequence" was a
different, in-process route (the gamelink step tool), not these scripts.

**Rule.** Every SendInput wrapper in this project checks the return value and throws when it is not the count sent
(`send-scan.ps1` does now); the `INPUTUNION` carries `pad4` at offset 24 so `Marshal.SizeOf(INPUT)` is 40. A driver
that reports success it cannot see is the same class of failure as the frame recorder that died silently (6151):
the proof looks like a proof of the mod when it is a proof of nothing.

**Amendment, the same hour.** With the struct fixed, `SendInput` returned 1 for every key, the game was the foreground
window at High integrity like the sender, Tab still opened no menu and A + Left Shift moved nothing (a 9-second
recording of the character standing still). InputBench's own README states why: Skyrim reads its keyboard through
DirectInput / raw input and `SendInput` "never reaches a game that reads raw input directly". So the scan-code
driver is for ordinary windows only; **the game is driven in-process through InputBench's `bench.input` tool on
DevBench** (`6. current wip mods\InputBench`, built 1.0.1, MO2 folder `InputBench 1.0.1` - enable it in the test
profile before a run that needs key presses). `send-scan.ps1` says so in its header now.

## A byte shape that starts at a function's entry stops matching the moment another plugin hooks that entry - and the evidence that listed the groups that DID install hid the ones that did not (2026-09-20)

**Symptom.** xLenax on Nexus (2026-09-20): Character Progression Control with skill points on, "I'm still gaining
skill levels through use". On the owner's own Njordlinger Test the CPC log of every launch since at least 1.1.8 said
the same thing in plain words - `patch group "Skill experience rates" is NOT active - this signature is not present
in this build of the game` and `Skill points: the skill-improve site is not present in this build, so ordinary skill
experience still banks alongside points` - and on 2026-09-05..11 the same log had said `verified at game offset
[value removed]`. Nobody read the difference.

**Cause, read out of the running game's memory (ReadProcessMemory, read-only, the owner playing).** `[value removed]`
began [bytes removed] - a branch through an SKSE trampoline into `[offset removed]`. Actor Value
Generator hooks the skill-improve function at its entry, the same way the Skyrim Skill Uncapper does. CPC's shape
`[bytes removed] ...` starts with the five bytes such a branch overwrites, so it matched nowhere, and the
locator's honest answer was "not present". A second defect sat behind the first: the block fed the improve 0
experience, but the game adds the skill's use OFFSET after the multiplier (Lockpicking 25, Pickpocket 8.1,
Alchemy 3, Sneak 1.5), so even with the hook attached those skills would have levelled through use.

**Fix (1.1.9).** The shape minus its first five bytes is matched (offset -5) when the full shape matches nowhere;
the entry must then hold an [bytes removed] or it is refused as before. The "original" thunk becomes `[instruction removed]` to the other
plugin's hook, so CPC runs first and hands every call it does not stop on to them; the log names the module. With
points on, the improve is skipped outright, not fed 0.

**The process half.** The 1.1.8 evidence line reads "Patches: Perk points / Skill caps / Formula caps / Legendary
reset level / Skill points installed" - a true sentence that omitted three groups the shipped feature needs. A list
of what worked is not a check that everything needed worked. Rule
`cpc-every-patch-group-the-features-need-is-active` (kind `skse-log-forbid-regex`, new) now reads the mod's SKSE log
at package time and fails on any refused group a feature depends on, so this class cannot reach a package again.

**Rule.** A signature that anchors at a function ENTRY must expect a foreign 5-byte branch there and either match
behind it and chain, or say "hooked by X" - never "not present". And whenever a patch group is refused in the log,
the finalize evidence must name it, not the ones beside it.

## A behaviour engine's OUTPUT shipped in a package outranks the player's own Pandora run wherever the mod sits above it - the T-pose with magic in hand (2026-09-20)

**Symptom.** The owner: "tk dodge aio t poses when dodging while wielding magic". With a weapon the dodge rolled.

**Cause.** TK Dodge AIO 1.0.0/1.0.1 carried TK Dodge RE 0.55-rc3's pre-generated behaviours from 2021
(`[asset path removed]`, `[asset name removed]`, the `_1stperson` pair) plus a 2019
`animationdatasinglefile.txt`. In Njordlinger Test the test build (modlist line 39) outranked Pandora Output (line 95),
so those stale graphs were the ones the game loaded. Strings pulled out of the files: the shipped magicbehavior has none
of the step-dodge clips and the shipped first-person one references `Animations\Roll_*.hkx` files that do not exist -
a clip the graph cannot bind is a T-pose. The one-handed graph happened to still reference the files that ship, so a
weapon dodge looked fine and the defect hid behind it.

**Fix (1.0.2).** The package ships the `Nemesis_Engine\mod\tkds` patch and the animations only; the generator's output
is the player's Pandora run. Proven with Flames drawn (Papyrus EquipSpell, InputBench presses, game-video.ps1
recording): [code removed] in the magic graph and the step-dodge
on the frames. Gate rule `no-behaviour-engine-output-in-a-package` (forbid-path-regex, all packages) fails any package
that carries `behaviors\*.hkx`, `animationdatasinglefile.txt`, `animationsetdatasinglefile.txt` or an FNIS check file;
it fired six times on the 1.0.1 package and nothing on 1.0.2.

**Rule.** A behaviour engine's output (behaviour .hkx, animationdata/animationsetdata singlefiles) never ships in one of
our packages, whatever the upstream download carried. What ships is the patch the engine consumes.

## The Bash tool eats one level of backslashes inside a heredoc - a regex, a Windows path or a changelog line written that way ships mangled (2026-09-20)

**Symptom, three times in one day.** A Nexus page written through `cat > file <<'EOF'` failed to parse in bash at all
("unexpected EOF while looking for matching `''"); a changelog line written through a Python heredoc came out as
"meshes\x07ctors" (the `\a` and `\b` of `\actors` and `\behaviors` became bell and backspace); a gate-rule regex
written the same way was stored as `[\/]` instead of `[\\/]` and matched nothing, so the rule that was supposed to
close the loop passed the very package it was written for.

**Cause.** The Bash tool hands the command through a layer that consumes one level of backslash escaping before bash
sees the heredoc, quoted delimiter or not. Short heredocs without backslashes are fine; anything carrying Windows
paths, regexes or `\n` inside string literals is not what was typed.

**Rule.** Content with backslashes - regexes, Windows paths, changelog text naming folders - goes through the Write
tool into a file (a `.py` or `.ps1` in the scratchpad, or the target itself), never through a Bash heredoc. And a gate
rule is tested against the package it was written for BEFORE it is called closed: the test that proved the
behaviour-output rule was running package-gate on the 1.0.1 package and counting six hits.

## A "FOMOD" second install of a mod carries the MAIN plugin too - moved above the real main as a patch folder, its old main plugin wins (2026-09-20)

**Symptom.** After the order pass moved "Skyrim Landscape and Water Fixes - FOMOD" (v8.6.2, the page's patch
options) into Patch Hubs above the v10.1 main, loadorder.txt showed `Landscape and Water Fixes.esp` at position 17 -
where the MAIN's copy belongs - while the VFS would serve the FOMOD folder's copy of the same file name, the 2024
plugin, from the top of the pane. The 74 duplicated asset files had been stripped from the FOMOD folder deliberately;
the duplicated main plugin had not been noticed among its four plugins.

**Rule.** A second install of one Nexus page (a FOMOD run, a patch-options folder) is checked plugin by plugin against
the main folder before it is placed above it: any plugin the main folder also ships is quarantined from the second
folder, not only the assets. `nj-order-plan.py`'s ASSET_STRIP now strips those plugins too, and the audit's
duplicate table (containment with identical=None) is the list to read for this class - those pairs are two installs
of one page whose files differ by version.

## Plugin Sync's comparator is not transitive, so the order among ties depends on the input order - write the dependency-bearing order yourself and treat tie order as free (2026-09-20)

**What was measured.** Plugin Sync 2.3.0 orders plugins by mod priority, then inside one mod by a name heuristic
whose last step is `len(a) < len(b) or a < b` (case-sensitive). That predicate can be true in both directions
("TOTS - Icy Waterways.esp" vs "Turn of the Seasons.esp"), so Python's sort gives an order that depends on the input
order; re-running `nj-order-plan.py` on the lists it had just written reproduced 696 plugins with a handful of
tie-pairs swapped (two CC masters, plugins inside one folder with no relationship).

**Rule.** The order this project writes into plugins.txt / loadorder.txt is proven by its master violations (zero) and
its read-through of asset winners, not by byte-equality with a later Sync click. Every same-folder pair that HAS a
relationship is pinned by an entry in the shipped `plugin_sync\__init__.py` `self.dict` (nine of them today), so the
player's click cannot invert it; pairs with no relationship may come out either way and it does not matter.

## Disabling a folder as a "DLL twin" takes its INI and config folder with it - the surviving DLL then stops the game at its own error dialog before the main menu (2026-09-20)

**Symptom.** The boot test of the reordered Njordlinger Test profile (19:36) never reached the main menu: a modal
`BehaviorDataInjector` box - "Loading failed -> Data\SKSE\Plugins\BehaviorDataInjector.ini, No such file or directory".
The dedupe pass had disabled **Behavior Data Injector** because **Behavior Data Injector Universal Support** ships the
same DLL and is newer. It does; it ships ONLY the DLL and a PDB. The INI and the `BehaviorDataInjector\` config folder
live in the base folder alone, and the DLL refuses to start without them. The Test profile had the same shape a second
time: `test Local Map Upgrade 1.3.1` (our test build, DLL + PDB) enabled over a disabled base that owns
`LocalMapUpgrade.ini`.

**Rule.** "Same DLL, newer" is not a reason to disable a folder. A folder is redundant only when EVERY file it ships
is provided by an enabled folder that wins; a DLL's same-stem `.ini` / `.json` / `.toml` or its same-named folder under
`SKSE\Plugins` counts as part of the DLL. When a newer DLL-only build supersedes a base, the base stays enabled BELOW it
(lower priority) so the new DLL wins and the old INI still loads - the pattern now in both profiles for Behavior Data
Injector and, in Test, for Local Map Upgrade.

**Gate.** `nj-order-audit.py` section 1d: for every enabled SKSE DLL, if a same-stem config exists in any disabled
folder and in no enabled one, the run prints `FAIL enabled DLL with its config only in disabled folders` and exits 1.
`game-relaunch.ps1` runs the audit as its third launch gate after the overwrite and plugin gates, so this class cannot
reach a launch again. The move file `category-moves-2026-09-20.json` has the disabling row marked REVERTED.

## Same file NAME is not same file CONTENT: four 'CC - *' folders disabled as duplicates of 'CC Content little C' handed the 1.6.1130-era Creation Club plugins to a 1.5.97 game, which died in InitTESThread (2026-09-20)

**Symptom.** After the Behavior Data Injector INI was restored, the Njordlinger Test boot (19:49, again 20:02) crashed
30 s in: `[offset removed] [instruction removed]`, RAX null, RCX/RBX the PlayerCharacter with "Object Reference:
None", thread `InitTESThread`, no plugin frame. Offset [value removed] is `TESNPC::TESRaceForm::race`, so the player's base
record was null at world init. Restoring the pre-reorder plugins.txt / loadorder.txt changed nothing (same crash), which
cleared the plugin-order layer; the enabled-set delta showed only two files lost, but a byte comparison of plugin
WINNERS before and after found the real change: `ccbgssse001-fish.esm`, `ccbgssse025-advdsgs.esm` and
`ccqdrsse001-survivalmode.esl` now came from **CC Content little C** (HEDR 1.71, the lower-cased 1.6.1130 files)
instead of **CC - Fishing / Saints & Seducers / Survival Mode** (HEDR 1.70, the SE-era files), because the dedupe pass
had switched the four "CC - *" folders off as duplicates. Re-enabling them (they sit above little C, so they win again)
gave the main menu at 20:08.

**Rule.** A folder is redundant only when every file it ships is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the copy that wins with it off.
Name-equal files with different bytes are a conflict to ORDER, never a duplicate to disable. The same pass had also
inverted two patch pairs by category moves (Xtudo's Ysmir patch under its base; the Nature of the Wild Lands collection
under the Nordic Cut FOMOD) and disabled the Environs patch collection whose main plugin differs from the base's by
4.6 KB - all three restored to the copy that was running.

**Gate.** `nj-move-mods.py` refuses a `"disable": true` row whose folder is not byte-identical-redundant (exit 1; a
`"force": true` row with a why overrides); `nj-order-plan.py` applies the same test to DISABLE before writing;
`nj-order-audit.py` labels every shadowed folder "redundant (identical bytes)" or "CONFLICT - n file(s) differ".
Diagnosis tool for next time: compare plugin WINNERS by hash between the last good modlist backup and the current one -
it names the changed record files in seconds, where the enabled-set diff and the plugin-set diff both looked clean.

## The Bash tool (Git Bash) rewrites slash options - robocopy /E /MOVE ran as a no-op twice; Windows tools that take /flags go through the PowerShell tool (2026-09-20)

**Symptom.** `robocopy "D:\..." "C:\..." /E /MOVE ...` from the Bash tool printed an empty summary and moved nothing,
twice in one evening (the downloads folder at 20:45, two MO2 instances at 21:12); the same line from the PowerShell tool
moved 510 files in four seconds. MSYS path conversion turns `/E` into a drive-style path before robocopy sees it, so
robocopy gets no switches and an extra "source" it cannot use.

**Rule.** Anything that takes Windows-style `/switches` (robocopy, tasklist /FI, reg, sc, icacls, wmic) runs through
the PowerShell tool, or gets `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` in front of it in Bash. Read the tool's own summary lines (robocopy's
"Files :" counts, exit code 1 = copied) before treating a move as done - an empty summary is a failed call, not a quiet
success. This joins 6344 (heredocs eat backslashes) as the second Bash-tool-on-Windows trap of the day.

## An import that installs mods without ticking their plugins leaves their archives unloaded and their masters unchecked - audit active plugins for missing masters and packed BSAs for a live plugin (2026-09-21)

**Symptom.** A new audit check (packed archives with no active plugin) failed on 66 archives in Njordlinger Test and 5
in the main profile right after the Apostasy import. The archives were fine; their plugins were listed but unticked -
59 of them active in Apostasy. The same pass showed 47 imported plugins whose masters Njordlinger does not have at all
(Snazzy Location Resources, Northern Roads, High Poly Head, Vigilant, occlusion outputs, paid CC content), and one
live break: WadeInWaterRedone.esp active while its master WadeInWater.esp came from "Loki's Wade In Water", which the
dedupe of 2026-09-20 had switched off as a DLL twin. Both profiles still reached the main menu, so a boot proves
nothing about any of this.

**Rule.** After any install batch, every enabled mod's plugin is either ticked with all its masters active, or its
folder is off. nj-plugin-state-fix.py ticks the ones whose masters are present (Apostasy's state as the reference) and
switches off single-plugin folders whose masters are absent, with the report in plugin-state-fix.md.

**Gates.** nj-order-audit.py now FAILs (and so blocks game-relaunch.ps1) on an active plugin whose master is not
active, and on a BSA in a packed mod with no active plugin of the same base name. The BSA packer lists each dummy plugin
as soon as its mod is packed, so an interrupted run cannot leave archives without their loader.

## game-relaunch.ps1 ignored -Profile: MO2's moshortcut launch uses whatever profile MO2 last had selected, so every 'main profile' boot on 2026-09-20 was the Test profile (2026-09-21)

**Symptom.** After the PGPatcher run (launched with `-p Njordlinger`) a "Njordlinger Test" boot came up without
DevBench and with 259 SKSE plugins instead of 271 - it was the MAIN profile. game-relaunch.ps1 ran the gates against
the -Profile it was given, then started `ModOrganizer.exe moshortcut://:Njordlinger` with no `-p`, so MO2 used
`selected_profile` from ModOrganizer.ini - whatever the last MO2 session had open. Read backwards, the DevBench health
check that "confirmed" the 20:08, 21:41 and 21:45 main-profile boots on 2026-09-20 proves those were Test-profile
boots: DevBench only exists in Test. The main profile's first real boot was 2026-09-21 03:08 (main menu, no crash).

**Rule.** A launch names its profile on the MO2 command line (`-p "<profile>"`), and a boot claim names the evidence
that it ran THAT profile (a mod only that profile has, or MO2's log line naming it), not just "reached the main menu".

**Fix.** game-relaunch.ps1 passes `-p "$Profile"`. Also seen: DevBench's console tool crashed the game on
`coc WhiterunOrigin` (execute violation inside devbench.dll, same address family as its quit-time crashes) - the
console tool is not safe for world-changing commands; load and quit only.

## The 2026-09-19 Apostasy import left 156 mods unsorted: parked in the main profile's Test Mods Area, and directly under the USER INTERFACE and FINISHING LINE headers in the Test profile (2026-09-21)

**Symptom.** the owner saw a long block of mods under the USER INTERFACE header in the Test profile. They were 151 of the
180 Nexus reinstalls from the 2026-09-19 Apostasy [NoDelete] import (weapons, quests, HUD mods, patches), plus five
patches under FINISHING LINE. In the main profile the same mods sat, disabled, in the Test Mods Area, which is meant
only for test builds and test copies. The import installed them disabled and never placed them, and the two profiles
drifted apart because a section header's members are whatever lines happen to sit above it.

**Rule.** A mod never sits directly under a "--- SECTION ---" header; every mod belongs to a category separator. The
Test Mods Area holds only "test " builds and the named test copies.

**Fix.** Sorted by Nexus category into their separators in both profiles (4. plans\njordlinger\ui-section-moves-2026-09-21.json
and finishing-line-moves-2026-09-21.json), 131 of the 151 enabled. nj-order-audit.py now FAILS on any mod directly under a
section header, which also blocks game-relaunch.ps1. nj-move-mods.py gained "enable": true on move rows. Still open:
about 50 non-test mods remain parked in the main profile's Test Mods Area (the Test profile has most of them sorted).

## Njordlinger's first xLODGen/TexGen/DynDOLOD run: the LOD tools read the Steam game unless given -D:, SSE Terrain Tamriel Extend blocks DynDOLOD, and version-mismatched patches stop it one at a time (2026-09-21)

**Symptom.** xLODGen's Seasons box was greyed out. Its log showed it was reading
C:\SteamLibrary\...\Skyrim Special Edition\Data, the Steam install, instead of Njordlinger's Stock Game\Data, so it
never saw the list's mods or their season swap files. DynDOLOD then refused to start while SSE-Terrain-Tamriel-Extend.esm
was active ("remove it permanently", dyndolod.info/Help/xLODGen#Requirements). After that it stopped three times on
"Unresolved FormID": each stop was a compatibility patch built against a different version of the mod it patches
(Arby's Millwater Retreat, Winterhold Restored and Fortified Morthal patches). Each stop cost about 12 minutes.

**Rule.**
- Every LOD tool's MO2 executable carries -D:"<instance>\Stock Game\Data\", as the xEdit entries already did.
- SSE Terrain Tamriel Extend stays out of the load order.
- Before DynDOLOD, run nj-unresolved-formids.py. It reads every active plugin in about 5 seconds and lists every
  reference to a record that no active plugin defines. Deactivate the broken patches first (DEACTIVATE lists in
  nj-order-plan.py and nj-plugin-state-fix.py), then run.
- Driving the tools' windows: send clicks as window messages (BM_CLICK, LB_SETCURSEL plus a space key to the list).
  A real mouse click only goes out after confirming the tool's window is in the foreground. The owner uses the machine
  while this runs, and one batch of worldspace clicks landed in another window.

**Fix / result.** Terrain LOD (all 18 worldspaces, Default + WIN), TexGen and DynDOLOD (Medium, Default + WIN with Snow,
occlusion, terrain underside) are installed under LOD Outputs as xLODGen Output, TexGen Output and DynDOLOD Output.
DynDOLOD.esm sits after its ESP-named masters (PGPatcher.esp, Wyrmstooth.esp), and DynDOLOD.esp and Occlusion.esp are last.

## A counter the engine shares with other mods must be held, not set once: AMF raised ControlMap's text-entry count when a field took focus, and another mod lowering it mid-focus killed typing until Escape (2026-09-21)

**Symptom.** phbd01, on AMF 1.9.5: typing in the search bar works at first, "but it returns after some time, i can click
but not type, i have to press escape again to type". 1.9.5 (and the unreleased 1.9.6 fix before this) raised
ControlMap's text-entry count once, on the edge where an ImGui field took focus. The engine makes CharEvents only while
that count is above zero, and any other mod can call AllowTextInput(false) at any time. So a single drop while the field
kept focus stopped typing, and only a new focus edge (Escape, then a click) raised the count again.

**Rule.** Shared engine state that a feature depends on is re-checked every frame for as long as the feature needs it,
never asserted once. Our undo matches only what we did, and it is bounded at the engine's floor (lowering stops at zero),
so a mod that reset the state is not pushed negative.

**Fix.** Input.cpp SyncEngineTextInput tops the count up every frame while a field wants text, and logs the first drop
per hold. It releases only while the count is above zero. Proven in game: devbench `amf.menu textentry drop=2` knocked
the count to 0 mid-focus, AMF restored it the next frame, and real SendInput keystrokes typed "wheel" into the search box.

**Also closed the same day (packaging).** repack-fomod.ps1 copied a repo README.md over the player README
(dist\README.txt), breaking package-mod.ps1's rule, and it left a FOMOD's Languages\ tree on the previous release's
translations, which the gate caught 20 times. It now skips README.md when dist\README.txt exists, and refreshes every
Languages\ file from dist\Interface\Translations.

## Installing a test build by copying the package overwrote the player's settings INI - AMF's saved System-row window position and size were lost on the next launch (2026-09-21)

**Symptom.** The owner asked for the AMF window opened from the System row to remember its position and size across
reloads. The code already saved every move to ApocryphaMenuFramework.ini, and the log showed the saves. But the first
System-row opening after the 1.9.6 install used the measured journal panel: the INI had been replaced. The install had
been `cp -r <package>\Common\. <mod folder>\`, which carried the package's default INI over the one the game writes
through MO2's VFS.

**Rule.** In an MO2 instance, a mod folder's INI is the player's live settings. Install test builds with
`install-test-build.py`, which keeps any existing *.ini and writes the packaged default beside it as .default. It also
moves a DLL the running game holds aside instead of failing to overwrite it.

**Fix.** Tool written and used for AMF 1.9.6; PREFLIGHT row added. AMF also logs "window profile (nested) applied on
open: the player's saved position ..." at each System-row opening, so a reload test is read from the log.

## A form-43 plugin is not made form 44 by restamping the number - weapons carry a 16-byte CRDT that form 44 reads as 24 (2026-09-22)

**What happened.** Asked to bring Fenrir Blades.esp to form 44, the obvious move was to write 44 into every record
header. Its four WEAP records carry the form-43 CRDT (16 bytes: damage, pad, multiplier, flags, pad 3, effect); form
44 expects 24 (flags, pad 7, effect, pad 4). A bare restamp keeps the file loading and makes the engine read each
blade's crit spell from the wrong offset - nothing would have reported it.

**Do instead.** `esp-form44.py`: stamps 44, expands CRDT, recomputes GRUP sizes, refuses BODT (ARMO/ARMA) and
compressed WEAP. `esp-audit.py` now FAILS a form-44 WEAP whose CRDT is not 24 bytes, so the package gate's
esp-record-integrity rule catches a bare restamp.

## A flat 'nothing brighter than 40' colour gate fails a correct black menu with white labels and passes a grey one - check the BAND the recolour removes (2026-09-22)

**What happened.** Finalizing Norden UI - Black, `swf-colour-gate.py --max 40` failed the correctly built black
racesex_menu (its labels are white by design) and failed RaceMenu's unrecoloured original for the same reason, so it
could not tell them apart; it passed the bottom bar either way. The recolour only ever touches neutral greys 51-102.

**Do instead.** `--band 41,102` (neutral = channel spread <= 3, recolour.py's own definition; per-file shape
allowances as `tweenmenu.swf:32,83`). Wired as gate rule norden-black-colour-band (kind swf-colour-band) and into
tools/build-package.py. Gate rule no-dip-runtime-inputs stops a package shipping DIP deltas, descriptors or .prev files.


## The fix was right and the test was wrong: a rebuilt DLL never reached the MO2 mod folder, so the same crash came back byte for byte (2026-09-22)

**What happened.** Back Pocket For Controller crashed the moment a favourite was toggled (`[source reference removed]`,
access violation reading `[value removed]`). The cause was real - `ControlMap::contextPriorityStack` read as a direct
member instead of through `GetRuntimeData()`, which on a SE+AE build lays RUNTIME_DATA at AE's offsets, so the array's
size came back as `[value removed]` and the first index was `-2`. It was fixed, built and committed at 16:49. The owner then
tested and reported "the game crashed again after unfavoriting an item" - and the second crash log named the identical
faulting offset, `[offset removed]`, because the installed DLL was still the 15:49 build. The
install step had never run. The evidence that looked like "the fix failed" was actually "the fix was never loaded".

**How it was caught.** Comparing the two crash logs rather than re-reading the code: two builds of changed source do
not produce the same faulting offset and the same register values. The installed DLL's timestamp (15:49) against the
build's (16:49) confirmed it in one line.

**Do instead.** Before anyone is asked to test, prove the binary the game will load IS the package's binary -
`install-test-build.py` and then compare sha256. Gate rule `installed-build-is-the-package` (new kind
`mo2-install-matches-package`) now hashes every DLL in the package against the MO2 mod folder of the same display name
and FAILS on a mismatch or a missing file; it was proved to bite by replacing the installed DLL with junk.

**Second lesson, same evening.** The gate rule written for the first cause, `runtime-data-members-through-the-accessor`,
was given a bare `pattern` field, which kind `repo-source-forbid-regex` does not read - it wants `markerFile`,
`markerPattern` and `contentPattern`. Every test then matched the empty string and the rule failed all 41 source files
of the very package it was written to protect. A new gate rule is run against a package that should PASS and one that
should FAIL before it is considered added.

## A backup folder beside MO2's plugins IS a plugin to MO2 - it imported "Mod Organizer Plugin Browser.bak-20260922" and failed at start (2026-09-22)

**What happened.** Theming the Plugin Browser, its folder was copied to `plugins\Mod Organizer Plugin Browser.bak-20260922`
first. MO2 loads every top-level `.py` and every folder with `__init__.py` under `plugins\`; the copy had one, the dotted
name is not importable, and MO2 showed "failed to initialize plugin ... ModuleNotFoundError" on the next start.

**Do instead.** Backups of instance plugins go under `plugins\data\backups-<date>\` (MO2 does not scan inside `data`).
`mo2-launch.ps1` now refuses to launch while `plugins\` holds a `.bak`/`backup`/`.orig`/`.old` entry that MO2 would import.

## An MO2 crash "in" a native plugin was a Python plugin's application-wide event filter - read the whole thread, not the first plugin frame (2026-09-22)

**What happened.** Ten MO2 plugins went in at once; the next install closed MO2 ("ModOrganizer has crashed, core dump
created"). MO2's dumps carry no exception record, so the crashing thread (the one inside dbgcore, writing its own dump)
was walked from the dump's memory segments. First reading: `install_to_separator.dll` sat right under the Qt frames -
the DLL was removed and the entry written. Second crash with the DLL back and a slot guard installed: the full thread
read Python -> `installMod` -> Quick Install dialog -> the picker's signal -> **Python frames at the top, faulting inside
the interpreter**. The Python code that runs on every event during that dialog was Install Multiple Mods'
application-wide event filter (`QApplication.instance().installEventFilter`, switched on to re-point the list-options
Install entry). A global filter is handed foreign widgets while another plugin tears them down. Replacing it with a
targeted hook on `listOptionsBtn`'s menu ended the crashes; the owner: "its good".

**Do instead.** Never conclude from the first plugin frame on the stack; walk to the top and name what was executing.
In our MO2 plugins, no application-wide event filter when a narrower hook exists (a widget's own signal, its menu, a
QAction) - MO2 File Explorer's filter, which looks only at presses on its own box and list, is the tolerated shape.
A slot-exception guard (`sys.excepthook` set, so PyQt6 logs instead of qFatal) lives in Njordlinger Icon and turns a
Python exception in any plugin's slot into a traceback in `plugins\data
jordlinger\slot-exceptions.log`.
To read an MO2 dump without a debugger: `pip install minidump`, find the thread whose top frames are dbgcore, list the
module of every return address in its stack segment, and read it to the top.

## "It didn't scroll" three times while the log said it had: the pane on screen was another plugin's replacement of the one being scrolled (2026-09-22)

**What happened.** Startup Scroll reported the plugin list at 1775 of 1775 for two minutes while the owner's screenshot
showed it at the top. Bethesda Plugin Manager replaces MO2's plugin panel with its own `QTreeView` named `pluginList`;
MO2's `espList` lives on hidden, and that is what was being scrolled. Two rounds of timer and model-watch fixes were
built on the assumption that the named widget was the visible one.

**Do instead.** When a plugin drives a widget by objectName, check `isVisible()` and prefer a visible candidate; keep a
table of known replacements (`espList` -> `pluginList` under BPM). And before the second fix of a "did not happen"
report, ask for the screenshot: the log proved the action, only the picture showed it was aimed at the wrong widget.

## `organizer.refresh(True)` after writing a profile file hands the file back to MO2's memory - 350 plugins went back into their old BPM groups (2026-09-22)

**What happened.** The Modlist Order Generator's Apply wrote `plugingroups.txt` (and the modlist / plugin lists), then
called `refresh(True)`. The `True` means "save the current lists first": MO2 and Bethesda Plugin Manager wrote their
in-memory state over the files just written, and BPM's stale groups won for every plugin whose group had changed
between two Applies. The left pane looked right (MO2 only writes a modlist it has marked dirty), so the damage was only
in the right pane's groups, found by the pane audit, not by the dialog.

**Do instead.** After writing anything MO2 also holds in memory, refresh with `refresh(False)` so it re-reads the
files; `refresh(True)` is only for BEFORE reading the pane's state. Read the file back a few seconds later and log a
mismatch. Gate rule `mo2-plugin-no-saving-refresh-after-profile-write` fails a package whose source calls an
apply/write/save function and then `.refresh(True)` within three lines.

## A plugin shipped by two enabled mods is anchored to the mod MO2 loads it from, not the first one found (2026-09-22)

**What happened.** The generator's plugin order took the first mod (highest in the pane) that ships a plugin name, but
MO2 uses the LOWEST enabled copy (patch collections re-ship a main plugin; "Cleaned Plugin" variants). Twenty-five
plugins sat out of pane order for that reason, and one (`SGEyebrows.esp`, ESM-flagged in one copy only) landed in the
wrong block. Separately, `.esl`-EXTENSION files load in the master block whatever their header says; classifying them
by the flag alone put twenty of them after the generated outputs.

**Do instead.** Resolve a plugin's owner as the last enabled provider in pane order, and let that copy's header decide
its block; master-block = ESM flag or `.esm`/`.esl` extension. Verify with the longest-agreeing-run count (plugins
outside the longest subsequence that follows the pane), not pairwise inversions, which one early outlier inflates.

## A plugin walking `mod.fileTree()` from a timer crashed MO2 on every rename - and faulthandler named the line where three minidumps could not (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** MO2 closed whenever a mod or separator was renamed. Three minidumps had the same shape - a Qt
signal into Python, Python into mobase, mobase into ModOrganizer.exe - and no symbols, so the first fix (gating
Custom Filters' recount behind `onNextRefresh`) was a guess and wrong. With `faulthandler.enable(all_threads=True)`
armed, the next crash wrote the Python frames: `MO2CustomFilters._contents_of` line 531,
`getContentsFor(mod.fileTree())`, from the recount timer. The file tree of a just-renamed ModInfo is not safe to walk.

**Do instead.** Never walk a ModInfo's file tree from a plugin slot; read what is needed off the mod folder with
`os.scandir` and map to MO2's content ids by name from `getAllContents()`. And the owner's standing rule from this
night: every MO2 plugin of ours logs and arms faulthandler on import (gate rule `mo2-plugin-arms-faulthandler`),
because a native crash that names its Python line is a file read, not a bisection. Gate rule
`mo2-plugin-no-getcontentsfor-filetree` closes this exact class.

## A mobase callback that does its work synchronously crashed MO2 on "enable a mod" - callbacks start timers, timers do the work (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** MO2 Custom Filters registered `onModStateChanged(lambda *a: self.rebuild())` (and the same for
onModInstalled / onModRemoved / onModMoved / the plugin list's onRefreshed). `rebuild()` asks mobase about every mod;
running it INSIDE MO2's own `ModList::setData` - the state change that fired the callback - was an access violation
the moment a mod was ticked. faults.log named the lambda. The same morning's fix for renames had put
`organizer.onNextRefresh(...)` inside a `dataChanged` handler, which is the same mistake in another coat: a mobase
call made from within a Qt signal MO2 emits mid-update.

**Do instead.** In our MO2 plugins a mobase callback and a mod-list model signal only ever `start()` a single-shot
QTimer (a few hundred ms). The timer slot runs on an empty stack; it gates on `organizer.onNextRefresh(fn, True)`
and does the mobase work there. Gate rule `mo2-plugin-no-work-inside-mo2-callbacks` fails the shape
`.onX(lambda ...: self.rebuild()/_apply()/compute()...)`.

**Same class, third coat (2026-09-23, an hour later).** NjordlingerIcon pinned the themed toolbar icons by doing
`setIcon` synchronously inside `QAction::changed`; MO2 rebuilds its toolbar and re-sets those actions itself, and
the handler running mid-change took MO2 down 24 s after start (faults.log: `NjordlingerIcon.restore`). The rule
is not about mobase specifically: **any handler fired from inside MO2's or Qt's own mutation of an object only
queues a zero-length timer**; the deferred call still lands before the repaint, and it checks
`sip.isdeleted(obj)` first, because MO2 deletes and recreates actions.

## A QTimer parented to an MO2 pane died with the pane; the next callback started a dead timer (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** MO2 Custom Filters created its three timers as `QTimer(group)`, `group` being MO2's own
`categoriesGroup` box. MO2 rebuilt that pane, Qt deleted the timers with it, and the plugin's `onModStateChanged`
lambda - by then only `timer.start()`, the "callbacks start timers" rule from the morning - started a dead C++ object.
Access violation on deactivating a mod; faults.log named the lambda. The earlier fix had moved the WORK out of the
callback but left the timer's lifetime in MO2's hands.

**Do instead.** A plugin's QTimer is Python-owned (`QTimer()` with no parent, held on `self`) or parented to the main
window, never to a pane or widget MO2 may rebuild; every `start()` goes through a guard that checks
`sip.isdeleted()`. Gate rule `mo2-plugin-timers-not-parented-to-mo2-widgets` fails `QTimer(group|tb|widget|...)`.


## `$PSScriptRoot` is empty inside a `[CmdletBinding()]` param default, `$args` cannot be a parameter name, and `Copy-Item -LiteralPath` does not expand `*` (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** Three separate runs of the Pipeline Kit's self-test failed on plumbing, not on the pipeline. (1)
`[string]$Kit = (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)` as a param default under `[CmdletBinding()]`, invoked with
`powershell -File`, threw "Cannot bind argument to parameter 'Path' because it is an empty string": the automatic
variable is not populated when a cmdlet-bound script's defaults are evaluated (a plain `param()` without the attribute
had worked in a quick test, which is why it was trusted). The same shape had just been written into every gate
script's `$Root` default by the kit's build. (2) A helper declared `function Run([string]$name, [string[]]$args)`:
`$args` is PowerShell's automatic variable, the parameter silently received nothing, and every child script ran
with no arguments - the failure looked like the version gate refusing to register. (3)
`Copy-Item -LiteralPath "...\ExampleMod\*"` copied nothing: `-LiteralPath` is literal, the `*` is a file name.
A fourth, smaller one: `Write-Output` inside a function whose caller pipes to `Out-Null` swallows the "ok/FAIL"
lines the function was printing; `Write-Host` is the console.

**Do instead.** Default the parameter to `''` (or an environment variable) and resolve `$PSScriptRoot`-derived paths
in the body: [code removed] - the kit's build now
rewrites every gate script that way. Never name a parameter `$args`. Enumerate with `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath
<folder>` and copy each item. Print progress with `Write-Host` in helpers whose output is captured.

## A build that leaves the machine needs a leak scan AND a gate rule - and the rule must not contain the literal it forbids (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** Pipeline Kit 1.0.0 is a sanitised build of the live `.MD` documents and gate scripts for outside users. Its `build_kit.py` fails on any surviving private identifier (user folder, project root, MO2 drive paths,
account name) - 16 survived the first pass, all references to the key FILE's name, which is not a secret; the scan
was narrowed to the identifiers. Per the standing rule the same check became a package-gate row,
`shipped-text-carries-no-machine-identity` (rule 45 for text files) - and the first version of that row's
`contentPattern` spelled the account name out, so `gate-rules.json`, which ships inside the kit, tripped the kit's
own build and the gate. The pattern now spells it with a character class (`[pattern removed]`): it matches the name and
does not contain it. The sweep over every existing package found one real hit the rule is right about: Apocrypha
Menu Framework 1.9.6's shipped `CHANGELOG.md` names `<MO2>\` and `<MO2>\` - reported to the owner, not
changed.

**Do instead.** Anything built to leave this machine gets a mechanical leak scan in its build AND the equivalent
gate rule; a rule that forbids a literal string must be written so the rules file itself does not carry that
string, or the rule fails the package that ships the rules.


## A fault whose only Python frame is a lambda "line ???" is a slot being INVOKED from MO2's emit - no slot body can prevent it; read MO2's own implementation and stop subscribing (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** MO2 Custom Filters crashed MO2 at 02:57 (deactivating a mod) and again at 04:34 with nobody
touching MO2, three minutes after start, the moment MO2's directory refresh finished and it rebuilt its filter list
(the `failed to load icon :/MO/gui/content/*` storm in mo_interface.log three seconds before `ModOrganizer has
crashed`). Both faults.log blocks were identical in shape: the main thread with ONE Python frame,
`MO2CustomFilters.py, line ??? in <lambda>`, and nothing beneath it. Two issues of 1.0.5 had each fixed something
real but narrower - callbacks that only start timers, then Python-owned guarded timers - and each was declared on
the strength of the fix's reasoning, not on a run past the crash point. The frame shape had said all along that
the crash was not inside anything the slot did: with no line number and no callee frame, the interpreter had not
begun executing the lambda; Qt/PyQt was invoking it, from a signal MO2 emitted during its own mutation
(`dataChanged` / `rowsInserted` on the mod list's model and the filter tree's model, the mobase callbacks, and the
`onNextRefresh` callback are all C++ -> Python entries of that kind).

**What MO2 does (the owner: "why doesn't MO2's filter crash? we should learn from MO2's implementation").** v2.5.2
`src/filterlist.cpp`: `refresh()` is `ui->filters->clear()` and a refill, called as a plain function from
`ModListView::refreshFilters()`, never from a model signal. `src/modlistsortproxy.cpp`: filtering is
`setCriteria` / `updateFilter` / `setOptions` -> `invalidateFilter()`; the view's model is the proxy, set once.
Nothing outside MO2 runs during either.

**Do instead.** An MO2 plugin of ours takes nothing from MO2's internals: no model-signal subscriptions (gate rule
`mo2-plugin-no-model-signal-subscriptions`), no filter-tree hook, no mobase callbacks, no `onNextRefresh`. A
Python-owned QTimer polls a cheap signature (modlist.txt and mods-folder mtimes, the view's row count and end
names, the filter tree's item count, whether our counts are on it) and starts the work once it has held still for
a tick; only user-driven widget signals (clicks, edits, toggles on persistent widgets) may re-apply at once. The
owner's proof: hands-on toggles and renames with no crash and, for the first time, no busy cursor - the stutter
had been the plugin recounting inside MO2's own update. And the standing gate from the same night: every MO2
plugin repo carries `MO2-REFERENCE.md` citing MO2's source at the tag for the feature it touches
(`mo2-plugin-documents-mo2s-own-implementation`; PREFLIGHT 1.0.5). A proof of a crash fix is a run past the crash
point with the fault log watched, never the fix's own reasoning.


## A resolver rule keyed on a WORD ("patch" in the name) cascades through masters: USSEP went to the bottom and 80 mods followed it; key it on the decision (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** With the Modlist Manager's inherited mechanisms stripped out (keep-winners, learned order, review
rules), the first clean run over the Test profile put 258 mods under Patches, 80 of them displaced. The chain: the
file-conflict resolver's "a patch loads after the mod it shares files with" tested `_is_patch_mod` by the [Patch]
tag or the word "patch" in the name, so the Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch - Bug Fixes on Nexus, a master to
116 plugins - was ordered after everything it shares a file with, landed in the Patches block, and every mod with
USSEP as a master was displaced after it. A second cascade in the same run: "specific over general" (a small pack
whose files are mostly a big pack's loads after it) applied across categories, so More Accurate Collision (Immersion,
4,192 files) pulled 36 texture packs under Immersion by size alone. A third: USSEP's own 137 new quest records
outvoted its Bug Fixes label until "a fixer alters more than it adds" (9,289 altered against 455 new) was a rule.

**Do instead.** In the Modlist Manager a heuristic that moves mods reads the DECIDED category (the evidence model's
verdict), never a word in the name; size-based evidence (specificity, PBR companions) holds only between mods of the
same category, where nothing else orders them; and every mass displacement is traced to its holder before tuning
(the dry run's `displaced` rows name the edge). Test profile after the rules: displaced 240 -> 104, absorbed
160 -> 17, Patches 151 with 5 displaced, and what remains is master edges (Campfire's addons under Campfire, Bruma's
under Bruma), which is where those mods belong.


## A scan budget shared across a plugin's top-level groups let 4 MB of interiors hide a 19 MB new worldspace: give each group its own (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** The Modlist Manager's `plugin_refs` walks a plugin's CELL and WRLD groups with one 6000-record
budget. Wyrmstooth's CELL group (4 MB of interiors) came first and used it all, so the WRLD group - WyrmstoothWorld,
19 MB - was never entered: `worlds_new` came back empty, no "adds worldspace" vote existed, and a new land was filed
as NPC - Appearance from its 171 NPC records. Every placement that read the reference distribution (interior share,
town concentration) was computed from the interiors alone on any plugin big enough to hit the budget.

**Do instead.** A bounded walk bounds each INDEPENDENT unit, not the file: reset the budget per top-level group, so the
cheap, decisive records at the head of a later group (the WRLD record itself) are always read. When a classifier has
no vote for something the mod plainly is, check whether the reader ever reached that part of the file before tuning a
weight. The full walk also corrected Holds The City Overhaul, The Great City of Winterhold and Immersive College of
Winterhold - placements that had looked like weighting problems.


## A package seeded from the previous release carries every file the assembler does not refresh - repack-fomod.ps1 never refreshed CHANGELOG.md (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** Repacking Apocrypha Menu Framework 1.9.7 with the Theo's Render Pipeline fix, both of the
package's `CHANGELOG.md` copies (root and `Common\`) were the previous package's: `repack-fomod.ps1` refreshes the
DLL/PDB pairs, README, NOTICE, translations and INI from the repo, but not the changelog, so the release notes would
have shipped without the fix they were cut for. The package gate did not notice - `package-file-matches-repo` rules
existed for translations and the INI only.

**Do instead.** Every file with a source of truth in the repo gets both a refresh in the assembler AND a
`package-file-matches-repo` row: `repack-fomod.ps1` now copies the repo's `CHANGELOG.md` over every copy in the
package, and gate rule `shipped-changelog-is-the-repos` fails a package whose changelog differs. When adding a new
shipped document to a mod, add its row the same day.


## Four package-tool assumptions that broke on real repos in one evening: -BuildDir ignored, "the first *.ini", an empty build folder, a suffix-matched install folder (2026-09-23)

**What happened.** Packaging Dragon's Eye Minimap 1.7.3 and Apocrypha Menu Framework 1.9.7:
(1) `package-mod.ps1` refused with "pass -BuildDir for a single-line package" while ignoring the -BuildDir passed;
(2) with two INIs in the package it replaced "the first *.ini" - the Time Widget file - with the main INI's text, and
the stale main INI (1.7.0's, with the removed `sTheme`) shipped on, as it had in 1.7.1 and 1.7.2;
(3) `lines-match-build-tree` read an existing `build\relwithdebinfo-17` folder as "the repo builds a 1.7 line" though
it has never produced a DLL; (4) `mo2-install-matches-package` suffix-matched folder names, so it judged the published
Nexus folder "Dragon's Eye Minimap", missed "test Dragon's Eye Minimap 1.7.3", matched "Perfected Wheeler - Apocrypha
Menu Framework" for AMF, and compared FOMOD `Line-*\` paths against a flat install.

**Do instead.** Tools that pick "the" file or folder must pick by exact identity: the INI by its name, the build line
by a DLL in its tree, the install by Njordlinger's convention ("test <Name> <X.Y.Z>" / "test <Name>" / "unpublished
<Name>", else exactly "<Name>"), a FOMOD path by the flat path it installs to. All four are fixed in the scripts; the
gate rules that exposed (2) and (3) are the ones that caught it - read a gate hit as possibly the rule's own defect
before bending the package to it, and fix the rule with a dated reason when it is.


## Blank boxes in every message box: the winning fontconfig.txt loaded font libraries no mod in the list ships (2026-09-24)

**What happened.** In Njordlinger's Test profile the save's missing-content prompt rendered as blank boxes, buttons
included. Oblivion Interaction Icons ships its own `Interface\fontconfig.txt` (written for the Sovngarde font mod: it
maps every `$Everywhere*` font to "Sovngarde" from `fonts_sovngarde.swf`); it outranked Norden UI's fontconfig, and no
enabled mod - loose or in a BSA - ships `fonts_sovngarde.swf`, `fonts_sovngardeconsole.swf` or
`fonts_drukaatieburti.swf`. The main profile was fine only because Norden UI happened to outrank it there. A
scan then showed Norden UI losing restyled SWFs to ten other mods across tiers 1-4.

**Do instead.** The order audit (`nj-order-audit.py`, run by every launch) now FAILs when the winning fontconfig.txt
names a fontlib that is neither a winning loose file nor inside an enabled mod's or the game's BSA (mmap search, game
archives first; ~15 s when clean). The Modlist Manager places the UI Overhaul block last among content blocks and
files font mods under User Interface. Blank-box text in Skyrim is a font mapping to a glyph set that is not loaded -
look at which fontconfig.txt wins before anything else.
