## "PapyrusUtil is not correctly installed": Campfire's bundled 2018 PapyrusUtil.dll outranked PapyrusUtil SE's (2026-09-24)

**What happened.** Njordlinger Test showed the PapyrusUtil warning naming Campfire, and OBody crashed on load inside
its StorageUtil-migration code. Campfire ships only `SKSE\Plugins\PapyrusUtil.dll` (2018) - no scripts; the
PapyrusUtil scripts it calls come from "PapyrusUtil SE" (2020 DLL). In the Test profile Campfire outranked PapyrusUtil
SE, so the old DLL ran under the new scripts; in the main profile the order was the other way round.

**Do instead.** A mod's bundled copy of a framework's DLL is hidden (`.mohidden`, MO2's own convention) so the
framework's own mod always supplies it, whatever the order - no duplicate copy needed. `nj-order-audit.py` now FAILs
when the mod named for a DLL loses it to another mod's copy (a "for Skyrim 1.5" port winning stays allowed).

## TestBench's `input tap` crashes SE 1.5.97 on every key: the CommonLib it builds on lays out BSInputEventQueue for 1.7.99 (2026-09-24)

**What happened.** Three taps (Enter at a message box, M in game, R in RaceMenu) each crashed Njordlinger at
`RE::ButtonEvent::Init` -> `SetUserEvent`. It was first blamed on the tap landing mid-load, then on InputBench running
beside TestBench; the third crash, after InputBench was removed and with nothing loading, disproved both. The
`BSInputEventQueue` header TestBench compiles against carries the 1.7.99 event arrays (SixAxis, MotionGesture, Amiibo)
under `ENABLE_SKYRIM_AE`, so on 1.5.97 `AddButtonEvent` writes into the wrong slot and `SetUserEvent` releases a
garbage BSFixedString.

**Do instead.** Until TestBench's queue access is made runtime-aware, drive keys with TestBench's `bench.input`
(`{"op":"press","code":<DIK scancode>}`), which injects a different way and worked for R, Enter, Tab, M and L on both
1.5.97 and 1.7.104; message boxes take `menu` `{"action":"accept","index":N}`. The same TestBench.dll runs on 1.7.104,
where the layout matches.

**Repeated 2026-09-28, four days after this entry.** An Esc tap through `input` crashed the Unbind Vanilla Controls
journal test the same way (crash-2026-09-28-09-12-20.log, RDI [value removed]), while the owner had the Controls page
open. The area check had grepped for journal / controls / foreground, not for the input TOOL about to be used, and the
tool's own capability report still says `available: true` on 1.5.97. Before using any synthetic-input tool, grep this
index for "input". TestBench's `input` should refuse on 1.5.97 until the header is runtime-aware.

**Repeated a third time 2026-10-04, and now fixed.** Testing HUD Position Manager's casting bar, a `r` tap through `input`
crashed Njordlinger (crash-2026-10-04-07-34-52.log, same [offset removed]). The area grep had been for HPM / widgets / Scaleform,
not for the tool - and a mouse-button extension to `input` had just been built, when `bench.input` already presses
`device:"mouse"`. TestBench's `RequireReady()` now throws 501 on any non-VR runtime below 1.7.99, naming `bench.input`
(verified: the tap returns 501 and the game lives).

## A packaged changelog, a release-link label and a generated header: three things a two-line release carried stale (2026-09-24)

**What happened.** Local Map Upgrade 1.3.2's first package (a) carried 1.3.1's CHANGELOG.md, because package-mod.ps1
seeds from the previous release and - unlike repack-fomod.ps1 since 2026-09-23 - never refreshed it; (b) failed
dll-built-after-the-last-source-change because `make_includable` rewrote `include\ISLocalMap.hlsl.h` on every configure,
so building the 1.7 line made the SE line's DLL look older than its sources (a string-compare guard in CMake did not
hold; `file(COPY_FILE ... ONLY_IF_DIFFERENT)` did). Separately, DEM, LMU, Lock Interaction Overhaul and Potion of
Clarity pages said "vX-1 on GitHub" beside a `releases/tag/vX` link: sync-nexus-distro.ps1 moved the URL, never the label.

**Do instead.** package-mod.ps1 now takes every CHANGELOG.md from the repo; a generated file in a source folder is
written only when its content changes; the sync script relabels the link and gate rule
page-release-link-label-matches-tag fails a page whose label names another version.

## A FOMOD passed every package rule and still could not install a file its previous release shipped (2026-09-24)

**What happened.** Norden UI - Black 1.0.3 (a FOMOD mirroring Norden UI's installer) cleared the package gate, then
replaying the owner's installer choices against his installed 1.0.2 showed one file no option could deliver:
`[asset path removed]`, which Norden's separate RaceMenu download ships loose and 1.0.2 shipped black.
build-fomod.py's RaceMenu extra carried the DIP patch and descriptor but not that file, and
keep-file-classes-of-previous only asks whether a CLASS (SWF) survived. MO2 keeps no record of FOMOD choices, so the
choices had to be read back from what was installed; a first pass also picked a TrueHUD add-on on a 60% match and
skipped Wheeler, whose Yes/No question only sets a flag for a later step.

**Do instead.** Gate rule fomod-delivers-every-file-of-previous compares install DESTINATIONS
(fomod-destinations.py) with the previous release's files. NordenUIBlack\tools\install-with-choices.py replays
choices: an add-on option must reproduce >= 80% of what is installed, and a flag-only question takes the answer whose
later files reproduce the most.

## Actor::CalcArmorRating counts equipment only - armour from spells and stones is not in it (2026-09-24)

**What happened.** Localized Damage split an actor's non-piece armour into categories as "CalcArmorRating - worn
pieces - effects", assuming the engine total included DamageResist effects. On 1.7.104 with Oakflesh (+40) and the
Lord Stone (+50) active the total read 65 = 60 worn + 5 skill, so the remainder went to -85, was floored, and the
skill share vanished whenever a buff was up.

**Do instead.** Treat CalcArmorRating (vtable [value removed], all three runtimes) as equipment armour with skill, perks and
tempering; count DamageResist effects separately from the active-effect list. Checked on SE, AE and 1.7.

## Driving a combat test headlessly: god mode zeroes damage, console casts do not take, the ref list is capped (2026-09-24)

**What happened.** Four things cost a Localized Damage test round each: `tgm` makes every hit reach Core Impact
Framework's pre-hit callback with physicalDamage 0 (skipped as no damage); `player.cast <spell> player` from the
console did not apply Oakflesh on any instance; TestBench `inspect kind=refs` returns only the first 100 of thousands
of references, so spawned bandits were "missing"; spawned bandits near Riverwood fight the guards and wolves instead of
the player even after `startcombat player`.

**Do instead.** `player.setav health 100000` instead of god mode; cast through TestBench Papyrus
(`papyrus action=call script=Spell function=Cast self={form} args=[{form:[value removed]},{form:[value removed]}]`); filter refs with
`formType=NPC_`; let TestBench auto combat (`playerbot order=engage`) start the fight, which draws the enemy onto the
player. In PowerShell test scripts, never name a parameter -I (it collides with -InformationAction) or a function Set
(the built-in alias for Set-Variable).

## A tool that writes the load order must pass the same audit the launch runs - before it writes (2026-09-24)

**What happened.** The MO2 Modlist Manager ordered by category and factual edges, but knew nothing about two things
nj-order-audit.py fails a launch on: which mod must win a shared SKSE DLL (a 1.5 port over the AE build; a framework's
own mod over a bundled copy) and that DynDOLOD's output is the very last plugin. An apply on the Test profile put Magic
Fixes and Tweaks for Skyrim 1.5 above the AE magictweaks.dll; the main-profile plan put PG_1.esp after DynDOLOD.esp.
Each was found only after the order was in the profile.

**Do instead.** Every audit FAIL class that is about order is an ordering edge in the Modlist Manager, and
`MO2ModlistManager\tools\selfcheck.py` dry-runs every Njordlinger profile and audits the PROPOSED order through a
temporary profile (gate rule modlist-manager-order-passes-the-launch-audit, kind repo-script-passes). When the audit
gains a FAIL class about order, the Modlist Manager gains the edge in the same change.

## Windows PowerShell 5.1 Compress-Archive writes backslash entry names, and 7-Zip's listing hides it (2026-09-25)

**What happened.** AMF 1.9.8's finalized zip was built with `Compress-Archive` from powershell.exe (5.1). Every entry
came out as `Common\SKSE\Plugins\...` with backslashes. `archive-matches-folder` passed it, because `7z l -slt`
prints normalised paths. Some mod managers extract such an entry as ONE file whose name contains backslashes.

**Do instead.** Build release zips with Python `zipfile`, writing `relpath(...).replace(os.sep, "/")`. Gate rule
`distro-zip-entries-use-forward-slashes` (kind `archive-entries-forward-slash`) reads the zip's own central directory
through System.IO.Compression and fails on any backslash.


## A test installer that keeps every *.ini as "the player's settings" keeps a package's data INIs too (2026-09-25)

**What happened.** install-test-build.py keeps any existing *.ini so a reinstall never overwrites what the game wrote.
AMF 1.9.8's theme files (`SKSE\Plugins\ApocryphaMenuFramework	hemes\*.ini`) are package DATA, not settings, and a
reinstall kept the previous build's theme colours while its read-back reported success - it only compared DLLs, SWFs,
plugins and *.defaults.ini.

**Do instead.** `package_owned()` takes the package-relative path and treats `themes/*.ini` (with *.defaults.ini and
*.factory.ini) as the package's; the read-back covers every package-owned file, so a stale one fails the install.
When a mod ships an INI that describes content rather than settings, add its path pattern there.


## A DevBench status reply built with std::format was not JSON once a Windows path went into it (2026-09-25)

**What happened.** AMF's `amf.process op=skin` formatted art paths straight into a JSON template. The resolved path is
`Data\SKSE/...`, so the reply carried a bare backslash and PowerShell's ConvertFrom-Json refused it - the tool looked
broken exactly when art WAS loaded. It had been that way since [Skin] shipped; nothing loaded art until the 1.9.8 themes.

**Do instead.** Escape `\` and `"` in every string value a hand-built JSON reply carries (Skin.cpp StatusJson's `esc`),
and when a test reply comes back as TestBench's `raw` wrapper instead of an object, treat it as a defect in the tool,
not something to parse around.

## A theme's toolbar icons "did not show" in Njordlinger because Njordlinger Icon re-applies its own set every second - test a theme on a clean instance (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** The Njordlinger MO2 theme set `#actionX { qproperty-icon: url(...) }` and MO2 was restarted, but the
toolbar kept its old icons. The sheet was fine: on the Steam 1.7.104 Test instance (no Njordlinger plugins) the same sheet
showed every icon. In Njordlinger, `plugins\NjordlingerIcon.py` loads `plugins\data\njordlinger\toolbar\<action>.png` and
sets them on the actions from a one-second timer, so any theme's toolbar icons are overwritten there. The owner then asked
for the theme to ship that same set ("the buttons did change but they arent the same").

**Do instead.** Judge a theme on an instance with no plugin that touches the same widgets; in Njordlinger, the toolbar
icons are Njordlinger Icon's. Two more facts found on the way, both verified: separators can be coloured by a stylesheet
alone - with collapsible separators MO2's list is a tree whose parent rows are the separators, so
`QTreeView#modList::item:has-children` matches separators and never a mod row (MO2's conflict brush on mods survives);
an empty separator has no children and is not matched. And Windows PowerShell 5.1's `Compress-Archive` writes
backslash entry names (gate rule distro-zip-entries-use-forward-slashes caught it) - build zips with Python's zipfile.

## A theme framework was built for a problem the owner's own baseline test then showed did not exist; and "the warning triangle in black" was read two wrong ways (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** Asked for a theme whose colours reach other plugins "like AMF's theme reaches every mod menu", a
companion plugin (MO2 Theme Framework) was designed, written, translated into eleven languages and tested offline to
re-colour the Mod Organizer Plugin Browser's hard-coded widget colours - on the strength of a source reading that listed
~40 setStyleSheet calls. The owner then ran the obvious experiment himself (Plugin Browser alone on a clean instance, then
with a theme): "it seems plugin browser already responds to the theme so no need". Most of its colours come from the
application sheet; the plugin was set aside. Separately, "i like the warning triangle in black more than the bell" was
first answered by removing the icon (MO2's stock triangle), then - after "i said i want the warning triangle in black" -
by a black-filled triangle in the set's outline.

**Do instead.** Before building to fix another program's look, observe that program under the condition first - a
baseline capture with and without the theme - rather than inferring the gap from its source. Counting hard-coded colours
does not say how many of its widgets they cover. And read a request's adjectives as specification: "X in black" names
the colour X is to be drawn in; do not substitute the nearest existing asset. The owner's own test design (baseline,
then one change at a time, on an instance with nothing else installed) is the method to reuse for any MO2 UI question.

## The version gate wrote every stamped file with a byte-order mark; U+FEFF reached five package folder names and a built stylesheet (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** Packaging the five MO2 UI themes produced folders named `Norden MO2 Theme <U+FEFF>1.0.0` in 7, 10 and 11.
`version-gate.ps1` Write-Locations used `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`, which on Windows PowerShell 5.1 adds a BOM, and the
`VERSION` pattern `^\s*\d+\.\d+\.\d+\s*$` swallows the newline, so even an unchanged version was rewritten - with the mark.
Builders read `VERSION` as plain utf-8 and carried the mark into names and text: Njordlinger MO2 Theme 1.0.0's built
`Njordlinger.qss` header says `Version <U+FEFF>1.0.0` (a comment, harmless to Qt, but shipped).

**Do instead.** A tool that stamps other files keeps each file's own encoding (BOM only if it had one) and reads with the
mark stripped; readers of one-line files use `utf-8-sig`. Fixed in version-gate.ps1 the same day; gate rules
`no-byte-order-mark-inside-text-or-names` and `no-byte-order-mark-in-package-paths` refuse any package carrying U+FEFF
anywhere but a leading BOM - the first rule immediately failed Njordlinger MO2 Theme 1.0.0, which needs a 1.0.1 rebuild.

## On an update, `pre-finalize-check -SyncNexusDistro` fails its own first pass: the check runs before the sync (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** Njordlinger MO2 Theme 1.0.1: the combined run reported FAIL on `page-version-matches` and
`distro-archive-equals-finalized-folder` - the distro still held 1.0.0 - then the sync that runs AFTER the check fixed
both (page to v1.0.1, notes counter, zip swap). A plain re-run was clean (13 PASS).

**Do instead.** For an update of a mod already in `11. Nexus distro`: move the package into `10. finalized mods`, run
`sync-nexus-distro.ps1` (or the check with `-SyncNexusDistro`) first, then the check on its own. The FAIL on the first
combined pass is the ordering, not the package.

## A test driver's XInput hook sees no reads in Oblivion Remastered: Steam Input answers XInputGetState first; drive the pad through AMF's inject op (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** Testing AMF for Oblivion Remastered's controller path, TestBench's virtual pad (a MinHook detour on
XInputGetState in xinput1_3/1_4/9_1_0) never reached the menu. AMF reads XInput every frame and logged "XInput user 0 is
connected", yet TestBench's own read counter stayed at 4 for the whole session. `gameoverlayrenderer64.dll` and
`steamclient64.dll` are in the process: Steam Input answers the call itself and never calls the function TestBench patched,
so neither the game nor AMF ever runs the detour.

**Do instead.** For AMF's pad handling, drive `amf.menu` `op=inject device=gamepad code=<XInput mask>` - it enters the same
per-edge decision (`DecideButton`) a real button does. One press per step: two injections queued together land on the same
frame. A real controller is the owner's to test by hand. A virtual pad the GAME obeys needs a hook below Steam Input (or
Steam Input off for the game) - not solved yet.

## Code carried from a Skyrim mod keeps Skyrim's file roots: the Oblivion AMF looked for theme art under Data\ (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** AMF for Oblivion Remastered replaced every "Data/SKSE/Plugins/" string literal with "OBSE/Plugins/",
but `Skin::Resolve` built the root separately (`std::filesystem::path("Data") / p`). The Norden theme's frame and background
were looked for at `Data\OBSE\Plugins\...`, the log said "does not exist", and the menu fell back to plain colours - which
looks like a finished theme unless the log is read.

**Do instead.** When porting, search for the ROOT as well as the literals - `path("Data")`, `"Data" /`, `My Games\Skyrim` -
and read the log's skin/texture lines on the first run. Gate rule `oblivion-port-no-skyrim-data-paths` now refuses a
CommonLibOB64 repository whose sources still name a Skyrim root.

## A plugin that loads xinput1_4.dll at load kills the controller in Oblivion Remastered for the whole session (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** With AMF for Oblivion Remastered installed, the owner's controller did nothing in the game - before
AMF's menu was ever opened. The bisect was his hands on the pad, one launch each: OBSE64 + AMF + TestBench - dead;
TestBench off - dead; AMF off too (OBSE64 and Address Library only) - works; AMF back with its XInput lookup made lazy -
works. AMF's `input::Install` had called `LoadLibraryW(L"xinput1_4.dll")` in the OBSE Load, before the game (which uses
xinput1_3) and Steam Input's in-process emulation had set up their controller path. Two earlier guesses were wrong and
are on record as such: the per-frame XInput reads (removed; still dead) and swallowing HID raw input while the menu was
open (it never was open).

**Do instead.** Never load an input DLL at plugin load. Resolve XInput when the pad is first needed, from the game's own
copy (`GetModuleHandleW` over xinput1_4/1_3/9_1_0) and load one only if the game has none. Gate rule
`oblivion-plugin-never-loads-xinput` fails a CommonLibOB64 repo with an unmarked LoadLibrary in a file that deals with
XInput (TestBench fails it and is off until fixed). A controller fault is the owner's to test by hand here: the virtual
pad cannot reach the game (see the entry on Steam Input answering XInputGetState).

## Force-stopping MO2 leaves Root Builder's copies in the game folder - the next launch loads a mod the profile has switched off (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** The Oblivion Remastered instance deploys OBSE plugins with Root Builder, which COPIES a mod's Root
files into the real game folder at launch and removes them when MO2 closes. Every relaunch that night ended MO2 with
prockill's force rung, so the removal never ran: with TestBench disabled in modlist.txt, `TestBench.dll` from 02:57 was
still in `Binaries\Win64\OBSE\Plugins` and loaded anyway - in the launch that was meant to test the controller without
it. A graceful game exit lets MO2 close by itself and Root Builder then clears the folder completely.

**Do instead.** End the game gracefully and wait for MO2 to close on its own; check the game folder is clean before a
launch. `.MD\scripts\or-relaunch.ps1` does both and refuses to launch while any file remains in the game's
OBSE\Plugins (gate root-deploy-clean), and PREFLIGHT's launch line names it. The same risk applies to any instance
that deploys through Root Builder.

## Swallowing window messages does not take the controller from an Unreal game: it polls XInput, so A in the menu also fired in the game (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** AMF for Oblivion Remastered swallowed every key and mouse message while its menu was open and the game
saw none of them - but the owner's first SDK test found that pressing A on a menu entry, with the cursor over a main-menu
option, activated that option too. The pad is not a message: Unreal polls `XInputGetState` every frame, so blocking the
window procedure blocks nothing of it. Skyrim never had this because its engine delivered pad presses in the same event
list as keys, and the hook consumed them there.

**Do instead.** Route the game's own pad reads through the framework and answer neutral while the menu is up: the game
executable imports `XInputGetState` from XINPUT1_3.dll by ordinal 2, and repointing that import slot (found in the PE
import table at first menu open, after Steam has put whatever it puts there) gives one place where the framework decides
what the game sees. Keep the packet number moving so the game processes the empty state as releases, and stay neutral
after closing until every button is up, or the press that closed the menu fires in the game. When porting anything that
takes input from a game, list every path the game reads input by - messages, raw input, XInput, DirectInput - and
close each; "the game saw none of my clicks" proves only the message path.

## A repo started from a shallow template clone cannot be pushed: 'remote unpack failed ... did not receive expected object' (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** The first push of AMF for Oblivion Remastered to its new public repo was refused with
`remote: fatal: did not receive expected object 18e32708...` / `remote unpack failed: index-pack failed`. The repo had
been started from the CommonLibOB64 template with a depth-limited clone, so its history bottomed out in a graft:
`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` said true and the object the server asked for was not on disk. Nothing in the
working tree or the commits looked wrong.

**Do instead.** `git fetch --unshallow <template remote>` first, then push - which is also what rule 3 asks for
("recover real upstream history before pushing"). `pre-finalize-check.ps1` now fails a shallow repo under rule 9
(gate `repo-is-not-shallow`), so the push cannot be the first thing to find it.

## The SMF export-parity check counted SKSE's loader entry points as consumer names: an OBSE build can never carry SKSEPlugin_Load/Query/Version (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** Finalizing AMF for Oblivion Remastered, `check-export-parity.py` failed with exactly three
"missing" exports: `SKSEPlugin_Load`, `SKSEPlugin_Query`, `SKSEPlugin_Version`. Those are what SKSE calls to load a
plugin, not anything a mod's settings page resolves; an OBSE64 build exports `OBSEPlugin_Load` instead and is right not
to have them. The check compared raw export tables, so a game boundary read as a compatibility gap.

**Do instead.** Compare the CONSUMER surface, not the whole export table: loader entry points are excluded when the
build is not an SKSE plugin (it exports `OBSEPlugin_*`). Fixed in the script the same day; the Oblivion build passes at
full parity with 25 names of its own.

## A separator the plan renamed only in letter case vanished on Apply: on Windows "Player homes" and "Player Homes" are one folder (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** MO2 Modlist Manager 1.0.0, Apply exercised on a scratch copy of the Apostasy author's original
order. The plan listed `Player homes_separator` and `VIGILANT_separator` as CREATED and the author's
`Player Homes_separator` and `Vigilant_separator` as RETIRED - different strings, so the plan's set arithmetic
(`new - old`, `old - new`) treated them as different separators. Apply then made the new folder (a no-op: it already
existed under the other spelling), and retiring the old one moved that same folder into the backup, so both
separators were missing from `mods\` while `modlist.txt` still named them. The Apply test on Njordlinger had passed:
its separators already matched the plan's spelling, so the case never came up there. It took a second list, written by
someone else, to show it.

**Do instead.** Any comparison of names that become Windows folder names is case-insensitive, and when a planned name
matches an existing folder in all but case, the existing spelling is kept (the manager now rewrites its planned rows to
the existing separator's spelling before computing created / retired). Test a file-writing tool on at least one list
it did not write. `tools\selfcheck.py` and `tools\apostasy_score.py` now FAIL any dry run whose created and retired
separators share a folder name ignoring case, and the self-check is what gate rule
`modlist-manager-order-passes-the-launch-audit` runs before every package.

## Third time: an edit script piped through a Bash heredoc lost a level of backslashes, and it wrote the file BEFORE checking it parsed (2026-09-26)

**What happened.** Fixing the Modlist Manager's MO2 departures, a Python edit script went through `python - <<'PYEOF'`.
Its `"\\r\\n"` string literals arrived as `"\r\n"`, so the replacement text carried real line breaks inside string
literals. The script wrote the plugin source and only then ran `ast.parse`, so the broken file was on disk when the
error came; a `git checkout` of the file restored it, since nothing else was uncommitted. The same edit to the test
script then broke the same way. This is the class already logged twice (the 2026-08-29 gotcha and 2026-09-20), and
neither entry was looked up before the heredoc was written.

**Do instead.** Any script containing a backslash goes into a file through the Write tool and is run from there - the
earlier entries' rule, which holds without exception. And an edit script checks its result BEFORE it writes:
`compile()` / `ast.parse` the new text, then write it, so a failure leaves the file untouched.

**The gate (added the same evening, after a FOURTH hit).** Minutes after this entry was written, a `printf` appending a
to-do line turned `\assets` into a BEL character - the same class, again, with this entry fresh. So it is now
mechanical: `.MD\scripts\bash-backslash-guard.py`, a Claude Code PreToolUse hook on Bash (user settings.json), refuses
any command that has a heredoc, a `printf` or an `echo -e` together with a doubled backslash, and says to use the Write
tool. Tested on six shapes (blocks the two failing ones, passes a single-backslash heredoc, a grep pattern, a plain
printf and non-Bash tools) and live in the session that added it.

## A patch LOOT recommends can be for another variant of the master: JK's Temple of Talos patch overrides a record "Solitude Only" Frescoes does not have (2026-09-27)

**What happened.** Working through Njordlinger's LOOT Warning Checker notes, LOOT said JK's Temple of Talos needed its
Solitude and Temple Frescoes patch. The patch's masters were all present, so a master-level check (and MO2) was
satisfied. A record-level check (`.MD\scripts\loot\esp_refs.py patch master`) showed every variant of the patch
overrides a record the installed "Solitude Only (No Lanterns)" Frescoes does not contain - the patch is for the
full variant, and the Solitude-only one does not touch the temple at all, so no patch applies. The same check found
smaller mismatches in other LOOT-recommended patches (Dawnguard Arsenal - Ars Metallica 3 of 3, Mysticism - Vokrii 2,
a COTN Morthal patch 3 of 193), and a survey of every active "[Patch]" mod found 22 such pairs already in the list
before today, some clearly for another version (a Northern Roads rocks patch: 42 of 43 records absent).

**Do instead.** Before enabling a patch that LOOT or a patch collection recommends, check it at the record level
against the master that WINS in the profile: `python .MD\scripts\loot\verify_new.py "<profile>" "<mod folder>"...`.
A record from master N that the installed master lacks means the patch was made for another version or variant;
masters being present proves nothing. Park a patch whose target records are absent (Optional ESPs) rather than
enabling it.

**The gate.** `nj-order-audit.py` (run by `game-relaunch.ps1` before every launch) now checks every active plugin of a
"[Patch]" mod against its winning masters record by record and FAILS on a pair not in
`.MD\scripts\nj-patch-records-baseline.json` or with a higher count than listed there. The baseline holds the 23
pairs reviewed on 2026-09-27 and reported to the owner. Proven: removing the Ars Metallica pair from the baseline made
the audit exit 1 naming it; restored, exit 0. Runs in under two seconds.

## A plugin I parked by hand came back the next time the Modlist Manager applied: a one-off fix in the list is undone by the tool that owns the list (2026-09-27)

**What happened.** Working through the LOOT notes, JK's Temple of Talos Frescoes patch (made for a Frescoes variant
Njordlinger does not have) and OCW_WR2_FEPatch.esp (contained in its JK's Skyrim version) were moved to Optional ESPs
by a scratch script. An hour later the owner applied MO2 Modlist Manager 1.0.0 on the Test profile; its plugin-state
plan brings an optional plugin back whenever its masters are present, so both were active again, and the owner then
reported placements the manager had made (an SMP optional file in Physics, Legacy of Ysgramor add-ons in Models and
Textures, Cold Welcome's patch in Patches). His ruling: *"make sure your teaching the mm plugin as we go instead of
makwing these one off changes that we did only on our end"*.

**Do instead.** A correction to a list the manager owns is made in the manager: find the vote or plan step in its
dry run, add the evidence, check every placement it changes (the first attempt here moved 89 mods, many wrongly; the
narrowed rules moved 34, each for the stated reason), add the owner's cases to `expectations.json` (they must fail on
the old build and pass on the new), run `tools\selfcheck.py` and the reference score, then reach the list by applying
the manager. Evidence must hold on a list in any order: the "made for another version" check first fired on the
reference instance's shuffled order, where an old copy of a patch happened to win, and had to consider every
installed copy of the patch and of its master.

**The gate.** Manager 1.0.1 decides these itself (a patch none of whose records from a master exist in any installed
copy, and a FOMOD alternative contained in its fuller version, stay in Optional ESPs); `expectations.json` holds the
four reported placements; `nj-order-audit.py` fails a patch made for another version of its master (baseline of
reviewed pairs) and an "unpublished" build of a mod that is now on Nexus. Memory
`teach-the-modlist-manager-not-one-off-fixes`.

## The Modlist Manager never stripped a "[Patch]" tag from a name: one regex pass let the separator class eat the space and the "[" first (2026-09-27)

**What happened.** Teaching the manager that "JK's Guild HQ Interiors Patch Collection - Thieves Guild USSEP 4.3.0a
patch [Patch]" belongs to "JK's Guild HQ Interiors Patch Collection [Patch]", the parent was not found. `_core_name`
ran `_NAME_NOISE.sub("", name.lower())`, an alternation whose tag branch `\[[^\]]*\]` comes first - but at the space
before the tag the separator branch `[^a-z0-9]+` matches " [" and consumes the bracket, so the tag branch never sees
it: "X [Patch]" became "x...patch". Every "[Patch]"-tagged parent (the owner's Keyword Tagger adds the tag to hundreds
of mods) was invisible to the name evidence of its children. Fixing it moved 12 placements, each for the stated reason.

**Do instead.** In a regex alternation that removes both whole tokens and separators, remove the tokens in their own
pass first; an alternative listed first only wins where the match STARTS at the same position. Test a name function
on a tagged name.

**The gate.** `tools\selfcheck.py` (run before the manager is packaged) fails when `_core_name("X [Patch]")` differs
from `_core_name("X")`, or `_full_initials("Legacy of Ysgramor")` is not "loy".

## The LOOT Warning Checker reads a plugin's "version" from the MO2 mod's meta.ini, not from the plugin (2026-09-27)

**What happened.** With Ultimate College of Winterhold installed, the checker said OCW_CellSettings.esp was
incompatible with UltimateCollege.esp and to "use the Ultimate College version" - though the copy that wins is UCOW's,
whose header says "Version: 100.99.98" and meets LOOT's rule (100.99.97 or later). The checker resolves `version()`
through the file's origin mod and reads that mod's MO2 version (UCOW 1.1.0).

**Do instead.** When a LOOT version condition fires, read the winning file's header description before acting; a
mod whose plugin versions differ from the mod's own version gives false notes here. The ignore file records each such
case with the header version.

## "It's not letting me take screenshots of MO2 again": three direct MO2 launches from the elevated shell, with the unelevated launcher already written (2026-09-27)

**What happened.** During the Modlist Manager and Winterhold work, MO2 was restarted three times with
`Start-Process ModOrganizer.exe -p "Njordlinger Test"` from Claude's PowerShell, which runs elevated. MO2 inherited the
administrator token, and Windows' UIPI stopped the owner's screenshot tools (Win+Shift+S, Snipping Tool, ShareX)
while MO2 was in front - the same failure as 2026-09-22, for which `.MD\scripts\mo2-launch.ps1` (launch through
Explorer at normal integrity) had been written. The tool existed; nothing made it the only way.

**Do instead.** Start MO2 only with `& "<ROOT>\.MD\scripts\mo2-launch.ps1" -Profile "<profile>"`; it
reports `Elevated False`. To bring a running MO2 down first, close it through its main window (a graceful close saves
the owner's in-MO2 changes) unless the lists were edited on disk while it ran.

**The gate.** `.MD\scripts\mo2-elevated-launch-guard.py`, a PreToolUse hook on Bash and PowerShell (user settings.json),
refuses any command that starts ModOrganizer.exe (Start-Process, `&`, cmd start, Invoke-Item, the path as a command)
unless it goes through mo2-launch.ps1; reads, tasklist, taskkill and Get-Process pass. Tested on ten shapes and live
in the session that added it (it blocked a no-op launch). PREFLIGHT's "launch MO2" row names it.

**Extended 2026-09-28: the hook sees the command line, not what the command runs.** `powershell -File x.ps1` passes it,
and 85 statements in script files under `.MD\scripts` still started MO2 themselves - five live scripts
(`nj-pgpatcher-run.ps1`, `wj-boot-proof.ps1`, `translation-rollout\proof-lang.ps1`, `nj-lod-dyndolod-start.py` with a
`subprocess.Popen`, `mo2-modlist-capture.ps1`) and 80 `devbench-loops` scripts - 13 of the 85 through a variable
(`$mo = '...\ModOrganizer.exe'`, `Join-Path $Instance ...`), which a plain grep for `Start-Process '...ModOrganizer.exe'` misses. All now call
`mo2-launch.ps1`, which gained `-WaitForClose` (a relaunch right after a stop no longer races MO2's exit), polls for the
process instead of a fixed sleep, and ends `exit 0` so `$LASTEXITCODE` is trustworthy. **The file gate:**
`mo2-direct-launch-gate.py` reads every `.ps1` (its own tokenizer: comments and string contents are masked, variables
assigned from the exe are followed) and every `.py` (the `ast`: docstrings and comments never count, only launch calls
whose program is the exe or a shell carrying it), and fails any launch not through mo2-launch.ps1. It runs in
game-relaunch, or-relaunch and wj-boot-proof beside the capture-foreground gate; fixtures: 17 launch shapes caught,
tasklist/taskkill/comments/here-strings/mo2-launch calls passed. **Do instead:** when a hook guards a command, gate the
FILES the command can run as well.

## The Modlist Manager's plugin plan judged only today's winning copy of a plugin, and a reorder then handed the plugin to a copy with a missing master (2026-09-27)

**What happened.** Two enabled mods ship "Ghosu - Auriel.esp": Auriels Crossbow and Swords SE (base masters) and its
Technical Overhaul (needs mihailundeadsnowelf.esp, then absent). `plan_plugin_state` decides a plugin's state from the
copy that wins in TODAY's order (the SE copy - loadable), and the new whole-word "named for" evidence then moved the
Technical Overhaul after it, so its unloadable copy won. The launch audit (via the self-check) caught it before any
game start. The same afternoon, two first drafts of new rules overreached before the placement diff was read: a
same-page "superseded" rule by paths alone switched off Illustrious Whiterun's Alt Stonefloor (same paths, different
textures - a choice) and the JK's Thieves Guild USSEP patch kept on purpose for USSEP 4.3.0a (the patch-records audit
caught that one); and a version rule compared file versions across different files of one page (a 1.0 AIO patch file
against the 1.6 main file) and dragged Stonehills into the NPC block.

**Do instead.** A rule about "which copy" must hold for every copy, not the one that wins now: the manager's build now
orders a loadable copy after an unloadable one whatever the evidence (structural), counting copies the plan just
parked. For any new manager rule, read the full placement diff against the previous build before accepting it, and
require the strongest reading of "the same": a copy is the same only when path AND size match; a Nexus file version
compares only between copies of one file (the older copy's plugins all in the newer one).

**The gate.** The self-check's launch audit and patch-records audit (both caught real cases this session), plus the
owner's rulings in `expectations.json` - each fix today added the reported mods to it, so the placement is checked on
every future build.

## A third-party SKSE plugin that links xinput1_4.dll leaves a Steam Input controller dead from the main menu on - and a virtual DualShock 4 through ViGEmBus reaches Skyrim, so it can be proven without the owner's hands (2026-09-27)

**What happened.** The owner: Outfit Wheeler 3.2 (Nexus 187557, closed source, PrismaUI) stopped his controller doing
anything "as long as that mod is loaded and activated on Mod Organizer 2 ... even on the main menu". His pad is a
DualShock 4 over Bluetooth; Skyrim sees it only through Steam Input's in-process XInput emulation. I first read "when
using it" as "while the wheel is open" and chased PrismaUI's focus code (its pre-1.5.1 ToggleControls-from-the-view-
thread race is real, but was the wrong bug) - a dead pad on the main menu can only come from something done at LOAD.
The DLL's import table links `XINPUT1_4.dll` (ordinal 2, XInputGetState), so Windows maps it when SKSE loads the
plugin; the game uses `XINPUT1_3.dll`. Same shape as the Oblivion Remastered entry on AMF's LoadLibrary at load.

**Proof, without the owner.** ViGEmBus (winget `ViGEm.ViGEmBus`, silent) plus the ViGEmClient.dll from the vgamepad
sdist, driven by `.MD\scripts\vpad\vpad.py` (a virtual DS4 that reads `press <button>` lines from `vpad.cmd`). Steam
Input picks it up like the real pad. TestBench `record` start/stop at the main menu counts the engine's own input
events by device; a spliced keyboard press is the control. Released DLL: 0 gamepad events (keyboard recorded). Import
renamed to XINPUT1_3 (same length, ordinal 2 is XInputGetState in both): 50. Both strings renamed: 58. Loading
xinput1_4 LATER is harmless - another module loads it after start-up in every working run.

**Do instead.** Never link or load an XInput DLL in an SKSE plugin; take `XInputGetState` from the game's loaded module
on first use (GetModuleHandleW). Gates: `xinput-import-gate.py` runs in game-relaunch.ps1 (an enabled plugin that links
any XInput other than xinput1_3 stops the launch) and as package rule `skse-plugin-never-links-xinput` (new kind
`package-script-passes`). A controller claim in Skyrim is now testable without the owner: vpad + record. Also: do not
`pip download` vgamepad's sdist - its setup opens the ViGEmBus installer window on the owner's desktop and waits.
Report and fixed DLL for the author: `3. analyze mods\Outfit Wheeler controller fix`.

## An ExtraDataList handed to RemoveItem is not yours afterwards - equipping through it crashed a later loadout switch (2026-09-27)

**What happened.** Simple Loadout System for Controller 1.0.0 brought a loadout's gear back with
[code removed] and then `EquipObject(player, obj, extra, ...)`,
reusing the `extra` pointer it had collected from the container's `GetInventory()`. The move can merge that
ExtraDataList into another or free it. Several runs passed by luck; testing Perfected Wheeler 1.3.8 beside it, a
switch back crashed executing freed memory (crash-2026-09-28-03-16-05.log, our DLL at [source reference removed] under
engine ExtraDataList code). CommonLib's `GetInventory()` copies are shallow - the ExtraDataList pointers in them are
the engine's live objects - so nothing about the copy made the pointer safe.

**Do instead.** Before the move, note what identifies the piece (ExtraEnchantment, ExtraHealth, the display name);
after it, walk the receiver's `InventoryChanges` for the same object and take the unworn ExtraDataList that matches,
or pass nullptr for a plain item. Fixed in 1.0.1 and proven with five round trips. Gate rule
`no-extradatalist-reuse-after-removeitem` fails any CommonLibSSE repo whose source passes the same variable to
RemoveItem and then to Equip/UnequipObject.

## A menu action linked to SEVERAL gameplay controls has one mapping per link - converting links one key per action collapses Cancel's Tab and Esc into one (2026-09-28)

**Symptom (caught before shipping).** Unbind Vanilla Controls 1.1.1's first conversion of controlmap.txt links into
separate mappings looked each link up, then wrote that link's default key into EVERY mapping of the action. Njordlinger's
control map (Modern Toggle Walk-Run Fix) writes `Cancel !0,Tween Menu,!0,Pause` - Tab and Esc - `Favorites Cancel` with three
links, `Lockpicking RotateLock` with four (W, A, S, D) and `Journal TabSwitch` with two on the gamepad. Each link produces its
own UserEventMapping with the same eventID, so the per-link write would have left every Cancel on whichever key came last.

**What is true.** `ControlMap::linkedMappings` holds one `LinkedMapping` per `!0,<control>` token, and the context's device
array holds one mapping per token for that action, sorted by key (so array order is not file order). The mappings of one
action differ only in `inputKey`, so the keys can be assigned as a set: group the links by (context, device, action), keep
any mapping already on one of the group's keys, give the leftover keys to the leftover mappings, and leave a mapping whose
link has no Gameplay default on the key it has. Proven: Cancel Esc+Tab, Favorites Cancel Esc+Tab+Q, RotateLock W/A/S/D.

**Check.** Before writing any per-link change, grep the control map for lines with more than one `!0,` in a field.

## A Controls-page row this mod draws must use the GAME's key name - "Escape" has no key tile, "Esc" does (2026-09-28)

**Symptom.** The 1.1.1 menu rows on the keyboard page showed "Menus: Cancel" with a tiny "Escape" label where every real
row draws a key tile; "Left Shift" the same. The extra [Functions] rows had carried the flaw since 1.0.8, unseen because
their keys (B, R2) happen to have the same name in both tables.

**Cause.** The row's `buttonName` came from the mod's own INI name table (`unbinder::ButtonName`). The journal's list draws
the tile by looking the name up in its art; the engine's names come from its keyboard/mouse device tables ("Esc",
"L-Shift", "CapsLock", "M1").

**Do instead.** Ask the engine: [code removed] - the lookup its own rows
use - and fall back to the mod's name only when the game has none. Gamepad rows already read gamepad.txt for the same
reason.

## "It is by design" was written from a tooltip - the source gated the stick behind the key, so something else was rotating the character (2026-09-28)

**What happened.** The owner: Show Player In Inventory 1.4 rotates the character on the right stick without the rotate
key (L2, `iRotateKey = 280`) held. I answered "by design", from the settings tooltip *"Hold this button and drag the mouse,
or use the right thumbstick on a controller"* and the 1.3 changelog line, both of which read either way. He pushed back:
why offer a controller hotkey if it is not meant to gate the controller? The GPL source (github.com/ItzIvy05/Show-Player-
In-Inventory, EventProcessor.cpp) settles it: in 1.4 and 1.6.1 the stick rotates only when `rotating` is true, set by the
key's ButtonEvent (gamepad masks through `GamepadMaskToKeycode`, LT [value removed] -> 280). So the reported rotation does not come
from that mod's rotate path at all.

**Do instead.** A description (tooltip, string, changelog) is the weakest evidence; read the code or run a control before
telling the owner a behaviour is intended. Still open: what rotates without L2 - the mod sets ThirdPersonState
`freeRotationEnabled` while the menu is open, so the game's own camera may be turning on stick input; rule UVC out with a
run that has it disabled.

## "0 gamepad events" and a dead controller in one run - Steam was not active, so Steam Input passed nothing to the game (2026-09-28)

**What happened.** A release boot check read 0 controller events from the ViGEm virtual pad (TestBench `record`, engine
layer), and the owner's own DualShock 4 did nothing in the same run. The suspects were the new builds and a launch path
changed an hour earlier (MO2 through Explorer). The owner: *"I don't think that Steam was activated this whole time."* With
Steam up, a launch by the same script loaded gameoverlayrenderer64.dll and his controller worked at once (Back Pocket
holds on the gamepad, 06:38).

**Why it matters.** Both pads - his DS4 and vpad's virtual DS4 - reach Skyrim only through Steam Input. Without a signed-in
Steam every controller test is silently empty, and the empty result points at whatever changed last.

**Do instead.** `scripts\steam-gate.ps1` runs in game-relaunch.ps1 before every launch: steam.exe running AND
HKCU\Software\Valve\Steam\ActiveProcess ActiveUser non-zero, or no launch. When a controller test reads nothing, check
Steam before suspecting code.

## The virtual pad takes the owner's controller slot - plugging vpad in while he plays leaves his DS4 dead in the game (2026-09-28)

**What happened.** For the Unbind Vanilla Controls banner captures, vpad.py (ViGEm virtual DS4) was plugged in while the
owner's DualShock 4 was connected and the game running. The owner: *"my controller isn't working ... I tried pressing the
D-pad and it didn't work."* Skyrim reads XInput slot 0 only; the virtual pad, created later, can take that slot through
Steam Input, and his real pad is left on another slot. A leftover vpad.py from an earlier round (its `quit` never landed)
was still running beside the new one - two virtual pads.

**Do instead.** Never plug vpad in while the owner is playing or has his controller connected unless he agrees; unplug it
the moment the step is done, and check no vpad.py process is left (`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` for vpad.py).
If his controller is dead after a vpad step, stop every vpad.py first; a game restart restores the slot order.

## Opening InventoryMenu with DevBench `menu open` crashed Njordlinger - item menus must be opened the way the player opens them (2026-09-28)

**What happened.** To look at the category bar under Dragonborn UI, `menu {"action":"open","name":"InventoryMenu"}` was
sent in game. The game died at once (crash-2026-09-28-20-18-17.log): EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION in SkyrimSE [offset removed]
(`[instruction removed]`, r13 null), under DescriptionFramework.dll's and PersistentFavorites.dll's InventoryMenu hooks. A menu
queued straight onto the UI message queue skips what the game sets up when the player opens it (the inventory data the
menu and every hook on it read), and a hook that trusts that data reads a null.

**Do instead.** Never open an item menu (Inventory, Magic, Container, Barter, Gift) with `menu open`. Have the owner open
it, or send the real key through `bench.input` (Tab / the Tween Menu, then the item category), and arm a Monitor that
captures when `menu list` reports the menu open.

## A folder "took 366 GB" by name sum and 266 GB on disk - vcpkg hard-links every installed file, so sizes must be counted by file ID (2026-09-28)

**What happened.** The storage audit of `<ROOT>` summed file sizes by path and got 366.27 GB; 183,651 of the
files are NTFS hard links (vcpkg links each file in `vcpkg_installed\vcpkg\pkgs` to its installed copy), and counted once
per file ID the folder is 265.67 GB. `storage-report.ps1` counts one link per name and reads about 100 GB high here. The
same trap in the other direction: `_lux-sandbox` shows 350 MB but frees 5.4 MB, because its masters are hard links into
Njordlinger's Stock Game.

**Do instead.** Count bytes per file ID (volume serial + file index), and call bytes "freeable" only when every link to
the file is inside the set being removed. Before calling two same-named packages duplicates, hash them: 13 entries with
the same name in `7. current test builds` and `10. finalized mods` had different files (a different DLL, `.esp` vs `.esl`).

## A 1 GB file named `.zip` in 7 and 10 - a package path built from an empty name IS the stage folder, and four scripts then `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` it (2026-09-28)

**What happened.** The storage audit found a 1 GB file called just `.zip` in both `7. current test builds` and
`10. finalized mods`. It was a snapshot of all of 7: on 2026-09-05 a finalize step ran with an empty package name, zipped
`7\` into `7\.zip`, then copied all of 7 into 10. `"$stage\$name $ver"` with empty variables is `"$stage\ "`, and Windows
drops the trailing space, so `Test-Path` returns True and the path IS the stage folder. Four saved packaging scripts
(`devbench-loops\finalize-batch.ps1`, `repack-fomods.ps1`, `package-uvc.ps1`, `package-fb-aaos.ps1`) clear the old package
with `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` on that shape - an empty name there would have permanently erased 10 (or 7, or 11).

**Do instead.** Dot-source `.MD\scripts\package-path-guard.ps1` and call `Assert-PackagePath <path> <stage>` before any
write, zip or delete of a package path; it refuses an empty, padded or dot-leading name, a leaf that is not `<Name> X.Y.Z`,
and any path that is not directly inside the stage. The four scripts call it since 2026-09-28. Two companions from the same
cleanup: `version-gate.ps1 -Action status` is NOT read-only (its Nexus sync rewrites the registry and ledger - use
`-Action list` for a look), and the D: Recycle Bin is capped near 48.6 GB - a recycle past the cap silently makes the oldest
items permanent deletions, so check the bin's size first (`_proposed\abandon-2026-09-28.ps1` stops at 95%).

## A UE4SS Lua mod's hook list does not prove a native ProcessEvent hook will see those calls - and Oblivion Remastered's camera is table-driven, so spring-arm writes may not stick (2026-09-28)

**What happened.** Planning Camera Configuration Menu (CCM) from Player Camera (Oblivion Remastered, UE4SS Lua). Its Lua
`RegisterHook`s BlockInput_Pressed, OnAttackRequestPressed, the OnCast*Enter events and GetCompassDirectionValue. UE4SS
hooks BOTH ProcessEvent and native functions (by swapping the UFunction's native pointer), so a hook that works in Lua can
be invisible to our OBSE64 plugins, which only MinHook `UObject::ProcessEvent`: a Blueprint's call into a NATIVE function
never passes through ProcessEvent. Separately, the UE4SS SDK dump shows the game sets its camera per state from
`DT_CameraSettings` (arm length, offsets, FOV, lag, transition curve per gameplay tag) through
[code removed] - a direct spring-arm write may simply be overwritten every frame.

**Do instead.** Before porting a UE4SS mod, probe each hook it uses in TestBench's `ue.trace` (does the call reach
ProcessEvent, on which thread) and plan a native-pointer hook for the ones that do not. For the camera, read
`Config/DefaultAltar.ini` and the camera table first, and prove a write sticks for several frames before building on it.
Porting Lua math: Lua `%` is floored (never negative), C++ `fmod` truncates - use a floored modulo for angle wrapping.

## An OBSE plugin's MinHook on UObject::ProcessEvent, placed before UE4SS starts, breaks UE4SS's own ProcessEvent hook - ExecuteInGameThread never runs, and with two hooks the chain jumps to [value removed] (2026-09-28)

**What happened.** Testing the Ultimate Combat AMF rebuild (a UE4SS Lua mod) beside our OBSE64 plugins. The rebuilt UC's
settings-file watcher applies changes through UE4SS's `ExecuteInGameThread`. With Perfected Wheeler OR, TestBench and the
menu bridge all MinHook-ing `UObject::ProcessEvent` (vtable slot [value removed], body `[offset removed]`), the first settings change
crashed the game 0.35 s after the write, "in" `PerfectedWheeler!HookedProcessEvent` ([source reference removed], the call to its
original), reading [value removed]. Without Perfected Wheeler the game survived but the change was never applied and
nothing was logged. UE4SS.log gave it away: "ProcessEvent address [value removed]" - not the body. The body began with our
`e9` jump; UE4SS followed it into MinHook's relay (`ff 25` + an 8-byte absolute target at `[offset removed]`) and took the relay's
DATA for ProcessEvent. Its hook there never fires on vtable calls (so ExecuteInGameThread's queue is never drained), and
patching the relay can corrupt the chain's target (the crash).

**Do instead.** A plugin that may share a process with UE4SS must not hook ProcessEvent before UE4SS has hooked it:
* a menu/bridge for a UE4SS mod needs no game thread at all - talk to the Lua through a file it polls (the UC bridge's
  `Ultimate Combat.menu`), never a ProcessEvent hook;
* a plugin that truly needs ProcessEvent (TestBench's pump, CCM, Perfected Wheeler OR) checks `GetModuleHandleW(L"UE4SS.dll")`
  and defers its hook until UE4SS is up (TestBench: until a UObject tool is first used), so MinHook chains onto UE4SS's hook
  rather than UE4SS onto ours;
* after a launch with UE4SS, check UE4SS.log's "ProcessEvent address" equals the vtable body our tools report - a
  different address means something hooked it first.
* **Better when only ONE class matters (2026-09-29, Improved Wheel Menu):** swap that class's vtable ENTRY for
  ProcessEvent (slot [value removed], VirtualProtect + one pointer write, calling the pointer the slot held) instead of hooking the
  shared body. Nothing is patched, so UE4SS's body hook keeps working in EITHER load order - no deferral needed. Proven
  in game: the Quick Keys widget's slot swapped at the main menu with UE4SS loaded, Ultimate Combat Redux's settings
  still applied through ExecuteInGameThread, no crash. The vtable is shared by the native class's other instances, so
  keep the class filter in the replacement.

## Editing modlist.txt from Windows PowerShell 5.1: `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` writes a BOM, and `$string + $array` joins the whole list onto one line (2026-09-28)

**What happened.** Installing Attack Speed Rebalance into the Oblivion Remastered test profile by hand (MO2 closed). The
first pass wrote `modlist.txt` and the new mod's `meta.ini` with `Set-Content -Encoding utf8`, which in Windows
PowerShell 5.1 prepends a UTF-8 BOM ([bytes removed]) - MO2 then reads the first line with a stray U+FEFF in front, and
QSettings can miss `[General]` in meta.ini. The "fix" built the file as `$comment + $rest`, where `$comment` was ONE
matching line (a string, not an array): `string + array` is string concatenation, so all twelve entries collapsed onto
the comment line - a modlist MO2 would read as empty. Caught by printing the diff against the backup taken before the
edit.

**Do instead.**
* Write MO2 files with [code removed] - no BOM -
  and check the first bytes (`#` = 35) afterwards.
* Build line lists with `@(...)` or a `List[string]` and add entries by index; never `+` a filtered result that may be
  a single string.
* Back up `modlist.txt` before the edit and print `Compare-Object` against the backup: the only difference must be the
  intended line.


## An xmake `/d1trimfile` flag that compiles cleanly can trim nothing: a bare string is split on the path's spaces, and a quoted value reaches cl with the quotes in the prefix - wrap the flag in a TABLE (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Ultimate Combat Redux 1.0.0 and Apocrypha Menu Framework for Oblivion Remastered 1.0.1 each shipped
one `<ROOT>\...\lib\commonlibob64\include\OBSE/Interfaces.h` string: a `REX::ERROR` inside an inline function
of that header, whose `std::source_location` default argument records the HEADER as the call site. UC's xmake.lua had
`add_cxflags("/d1trimfile:\"$(projectdir)\"", {force = true, expand = false})` on all 34 CommonLibOB64 compile lines
and it still survived, so the PCH's absolute `-FI` path was suspected. Two findings from the real compile line
(`xmake build -v`) and a four-line scratch test:

* **The flag was a no-op everywhere.** cl received `/d1trimfile:"D:\...\UltimateCombatAMF"` with the quote characters
  INSIDE the value, so the prefix matched nothing - the scratch test gave an identical untrimmed path with that flag and
  with no flag at all. The `.cpp` paths only LOOKED trimmed: xmake hands cl relative source paths and relative `-I`
  dirs. The absolute path came in through the PCH, the one thing xmake passes absolute (`-FI`/`-Yu` to
  `build\.gens\...\PCH.h`), and a header reached from inside it resolves against that absolute includer.
* **The obvious repair fails differently.** `add_cxflags("/d1trimfile:$(projectdir)", ...)` without inner quotes is
  split by xmake on the path's spaces (`C1083: Cannot open source file: 'output\6.'`); quoting the whole string
  (`"\"/d1trimfile:...\""`) passes the quotes through as part of the argument. `expand = false` did not stop either.

**Fix.** `add_cxflags({"/d1trimfile:$(projectdir)"}, {force = true, expand = false})`, a TABLE, the form xmake's own
`modules/core/tools/cl.lua` uses for `-Fd` so a flag is never re-split. xmake then quotes it as one argument, cl
receives a clean prefix, and the header string becomes `\lib\commonlibob64\include\OBSE/Interfaces.h`. With
`add_shflags("/PDBALTPATH:%_PDB%", {force = true})`: 0 occurrences in UC 1.0.1, AMF OR (framework and example),
CameraConfigurationMenu and PerfectedWheelerOR, PDB records bare names, `Test-PdbPairing` Ok on every one. No
relocation, no `subst` (which broke the PCH with C2011) and no change to CommonLibOB64 was needed. Wait Your Turn Redux
and LocalizedDamage (Skyrim, xmake) carry the same no-op quoted spelling.

**Gate rows (same day).** `xmake-d1trimfile-reaches-cl-intact` fails any repo whose xmake.lua spells the flag as a bare
or inner-quoted string. `oblivion-dll-carries-no-project-root` fails an Oblivion Remastered package whose DLL carries
the project root; it is limited to the OR mods because the sweep that day found 5-28 occurrences in nearly every Skyrim
DLL in stages 7 and 10 (the vcpkg CommonLibSSE-NG residue rule 45 defers to auto sort mode, plus the two xmake repos).

**Do instead.** A compile flag is verified on the ARTEFACT, never on its presence in the command line: count the
project root in the built DLL (rule 45 point 1) after any change to a trim flag. Test an undocumented switch's
spelling in a four-line scratch compile, with a header-side `source_location` call, before rebuilding a whole project
on a guess. A `source_location` default argument records the CALLER's file, so a test that calls it from the `.cpp`
proves nothing about headers.

## A mod with an optional-file zip beside its main zip: the archive gate compared the optional file and never checked the main one, and the distro sync deletes the optional zip (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Finalizing Apocrypha Menu Framework for Oblivion Remastered 1.0.2, whose Nexus page carries an SDK
optional file. After the sync, `pre-finalize-check` failed `distro-archive-equals-finalized-folder` with 32 hits, every
one against `... 1.0.2 - SDK.zip` ("lacks OblivionRemastered\...", "has extra file include\amf.h"). The rule picked
`*1.0.2*` with `Select-Object -First 1`, and `"<Name> 1.0.2 - SDK.zip"` sorts before `"<Name> 1.0.2.zip"` because a
space sorts before a dot. So it had never looked at the main archive, and a release WITHOUT the SDK zip would have
passed it on the main zip by luck of there being only one. Two more gaps found in the same step:
`sync-nexus-distro.ps1` keeps one zip per mod, so it removed the SDK optional zip along with the 1.0.1 main zip, and
it rewrote the release-tag URL and the "This package is vX" line but left the link LABEL reading "release tag v1.0.1".

**Why it looked fine.** 1.0.1's finalize ran the check before the SDK zip was added to the distro, so the rule had never
met two zips of one version. A gate that picks "the first match" is only correct while there is exactly one candidate.

**Do instead.** `package-gate.ps1` now prefers the archive whose base name IS the package folder's name, then any
archive not named like an optional file (`<Package> - <words>.zip`). After a sync on a mod with an optional file, put
the optional zip back (the sync removes it) and grep `nexus-page.txt` for the previous version: a URL corrected
beside a stale label reads as a mismatch on the page. When a gate rule selects ONE file from several candidates,
select by exact name, never by position.

## An OBSE plugin's own thread calling StaticFindObject while Oblivion Remastered builds objects: a start-up died in UObjectArray ("another object exists at that index") - look engine objects up on the game thread (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Improved Wheel Menu found the quick keys widget class and the inventory and magic menu classes
from a detached thread of its own, calling `UE::StaticFindObject` every 200 ms from OBSE's post-load onward. Six
seconds into one launch the engine stopped with `LowLevelFatalError ... UObjectArray.cpp [Line: 234] Attempting to add
CheckboxTextBlock at index 59623 but another object exists at that index!`, under UE4SS's HookedStaticConstructObject
and HookedLoadMap. The plugin had done nothing else yet: its log flushes every info line and stopped before "widget
class found". The same code had started cleanly several times, so this is a race, not a certainty. The same day, the
TestBench `re.memfind` probe (a whole-process memory scan from the TestBench server thread, unguarded) crashed the game
on a page freed under it.

**Why it looked fine.** StaticFindObject reads, and the object array has a lock, so a background look-up looked
harmless; the earlier launches that survived proved nothing about a race.

**Do instead.** Touch engine objects only from the game thread. In an Oblivion Remastered plugin that already chains
the game's `XInputGetState` import, run the look-ups from that read (it is on the game thread every frame), throttled
to about 200 ms - Improved Wheel Menu does this since commit 28e0827, with no thread of its own. A memory scan from any
other thread copies each chunk under SEH (`__try` memcpy) and skips what faults. Not proven as the cause: if the
UObjectArray fatal comes back with no plugin thread running, this entry is wrong about it and says so.

## A runtime-built UMG widget taken off the viewport is garbage collected: the plugin's pointer to it then crashes the next open - keep it on the viewport and toggle its visibility (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Tween Menu for Oblivion Remastered builds its menu at runtime: a UserWidget from
`WidgetBlueprintLibrary::Create`, a WidgetTree and CanvasPanel from `NewObject`, game widgets as children. The first
open worked. Closing called `RemoveFromParent`, and the next open crashed with an access violation reading
[value removed] inside `menu::Toggle` - on the root widget's pointer the plugin had kept.

**Why it looked fine.** The widget drew, navigated and closed correctly, and a C++ pointer held in a plugin's global looks
like ownership. It is not: Unreal's garbage collector sees only UPROPERTY references and the root set. On the viewport
the widget is held by the viewport's Slate wrapper; taken off it, nothing references it and the next collection frees
it.

**Do instead.** Add a runtime-built widget to the viewport once and show or hide it with `SetVisibility` (Collapsed /
HitTestInvisible). Before each use check the objects are still live (the object array still lists them) and still
`IsInViewport` - a level change can take viewport widgets away - and rebuild if not. Anything created with NewObject
that must outlive the screen needs a real reference (a UPROPERTY chain from a rooted object) or the root set.

## A plugin that re-asserts its Enhanced Input bindings only when its own mapping is missing misses the game re-applying the saved map around it (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Tween Menu for Oblivion Remastered moves Wait off Select and T, puts its own runtime input action on
them, and puts System on Start, all in IMC_Game_Default. A check every 60 ticks re-asserted all of that when the tween
action's keys went missing (the Controls page's Apply wipes them). After a round of menus in a test, IMC_Game_Default
held the game's saved map again - Wait on T and Select, Start on the Character menu - while our transient action still
had both keys. The check saw its own keys and did nothing; T opened Wait instead of the tween menu.

**Why it looked fine.** The status tool reported the tween action bound to Select and T, which was true. And the tween
key was never logged as pressed, which read like an input-detection bug: Wait opened in the same frame, menu mode left
gameplay, and the tick (gameplay only) returned before it read the key.

**Do instead.** Check every part of what the plugin asserts, not the part it owns: here, Wait on either of our keys or
Start off System also triggers the re-assert. Run the check on the first gameplay tick after any menu as well as on
a timer, since a menu's close is where the game re-applies bindings. When a key does something else, dump the IMC
(TestBench ue.imc) before theorising about input. The trigger was not reproduced in two follow-up rounds (keyboard ESC
and controller B out of the Magic menu).

## A reflected UFunction call with a zeroed parameter buffer passes 0 for every enum and struct: Enhanced Input's rebuild got RebuildType None and never rebuilt (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Tween Menu for Oblivion Remastered changes IMC_Game_Default at runtime (moves Wait's keys to its own
action, Start to System) and then calls IEnhancedInputSubsystemInterface::RequestRebuildControlMappings through
ProcessEvent with the parameter buffer left zeroed. After loading a save, the first Select opened the game's Wait menu
AND the tween menu; later presses were fine. The log showed the context already corrected 11 seconds before the press.

**Why it looked fine.** The call ran, logged "asked to rebuild", and the bindings did change - a little later, because
the game rebuilds the player's compiled mappings itself whenever a menu pushes or pops a mapping context. The
UFunction's second parameter is EInputMappingRebuildType RebuildType, whose value 0 is None (None, Rebuild,
RebuildWithFlush); the C++ default argument (Rebuild) does not exist for a reflected call. Options likewise lost its
default bIgnoreAllPressedKeysUntilRelease.

**Do instead.** Before calling a UFunction by reflection, list its parameters (TestBench ue.call with dry:true) and set
every one the C++ default arguments would have set - enums especially, since 0 is often a do-nothing value. Verify
the effect of the call itself (the next key press, not the next menu), not only that it ran.

## An MO2 plugin that builds basePath()/profiles or basePath()/mods breaks on any instance whose ModOrganizer.ini points its folders elsewhere (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** A Nexus user (Mordre) got "No such file or directory: 'C:/Mo2\\profiles\\Test\\modlist.txt'" from MO2
Modlist Manager 1.1.1: his profiles live in Mo2/SSE/profiles. Every path in the plugin was os.path.join(basePath(),
"profiles", profile) and basePath()/mods. MO2 Keyword Tagger and MO2 Patch Tagger built basePath()/profiles the same
way for their rename pass.

**Why it looked fine.** Every instance on this machine keeps the defaults, so basePath()/profiles is where the profiles
are. MO2 2.5.2's PathSettings (src/settings.cpp) reads base_directory, mod_directory, profiles_directory, overwrite_
and download_directory from ModOrganizer.ini's [Settings], each %BASE_DIR%/<name> by default and free to point
anywhere; categories.dat and nexuscatmap.dat are in the data folder (qApp's dataPath property), not the base. The
doubled backslashes in the user's message were only Python's repr of a Windows path - not the bug.

**Do instead.** Ask MO2: profilePath() (the active profile's folder - its parent is the profiles folder, the one
Profile::renameModInAllProfiles walks), modsPath(), overwritePath(), downloadsPath(), and
QApplication.instance().property('dataPath') for the data files. An offline tool resolves ModOrganizer.ini the way
PathSettings does (the Modlist Manager's instance_from_dir). Test against a scratch instance with moved folders, with
the old file as the control. Gate rule mo2-plugin-instance-folders-from-mo2 refuses the pattern.

## Oblivion Remastered's Controls-page key selector holds only a key chosen on the page this session - an untouched row reads None (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Unbind Vanilla Controls for Oblivion remembered a row's key when its selector started listening
(VNavigableInputKeySelector::GetCurrentKey) and unbound the slot when the same key was pressed. The owner's first test:
"it doesn't work". The live counters showed 5 listens and 5 selections, 0 matches; a listing of every row's selector
showed a key on exactly the five controller rows the owner had just set, and None on every other row, keyboard included.

**Why it looked fine.** The selector is what draws the key on the row, so its current key read like the binding. It is
the key chosen on the page since the menu opened; the row's actual binding is shown from elsewhere.

**Do instead.** Read the binding from the row's own rebind data: GetRebindData returns the ModernRebindSettingTableRow
(RebindData.InputAction, RebindData.MappingContext); that action's entries in the mapping context are, in order,
keyboard primary, keyboard secondary, controller (None for an empty slot). Prefer the selector's key only when it holds
one - a change made on the page and not yet applied. Before trusting a 'current value' getter on a UI widget, list it
across rows that were never touched.


## Oblivion Remastered's plugin loader silently skips an ESP whose CELL lighting block is not 36 bytes - and it reads ESPs past MO2's virtual Data mapping (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Simple Loadout System for Oblivion Remastered's storage plugin (a global, an interior cell, ten
persistent chest references, written as raw TES4 records) never appeared in the game's file list, with nothing logged
anywhere. Four launches went to the plugin-list side before the file itself was suspected: the entry had a Skyrim-style
`*` prefix (Oblivion's `Plugins.txt` has none); MO2 (basic_games' OR plugin) lists a mod's ESP only from the TOP
level of the mod folder (corrected 2026-09-30: this line first said "its `Data\` subfolder", which is wrong - MO2's
core treats the mod root as Data, so `<mod>\Data\x.esp` is `Data\Data\x.esp`; a copy there was dropped, a copy at the
mod root survived MO2's start and close) and drops a plugins.txt entry it does not list when it starts or closes; and - the part that cost the most - even a valid, listed ESP is
not loaded from the mod folder: the game's Gamebryo loader enumerates the REAL `Content\Dev\ObvData\Data`, past
usvfs's mapping, while `plugins.txt` IS read through the mapping (the profile's file). A vanilla unlisted ESP
(`TamrielLeveledRegion.esp`) added to the list loaded at once, which isolated the file's content; two test plugins
(global only; global + cell + refs with a 36-byte `XCLL`) both loaded, so the 48-byte lighting block the first writer
produced was the whole fault. Oblivion's `XCLL` is nine values: ambient, directional, fog colour, fog near, fog far,
rotation XY, rotation Z, directional fade, fog clip.

**Do instead.**
* A hand-written OR plugin is checked by loading it: the plugin's own log lists `TESDataHandler::listFiles` with each
  file's compile index (Loadouts.cpp Init). A file missing from that list with no message means a record the loader
  refused - bisect by content, not by the plugin list.
* Ship the ESP under the mod's `Root\OblivionRemastered\Content\Dev\ObvData\Data\` so Root Builder copies it into the
  real Data folder for the launch (it deploys any path under `Root\`, not only the binaries folder) - proven with the
  physical copy removed and the real `Plugins.txt` restored. AND keep a second copy at the mod folder's top level, so MO2
  lists the plugin and keeps its plugins.txt line (2026-09-30: with the Root copy alone, MO2 dropped the line on a later
  start and the loadouts went dead with no error). `or-relaunch.ps1` gate `or-esp-listed` refuses a launch otherwise.
* The plugin's records resolve a few seconds AFTER the player object exists: look them up again every 5 s until all
  are there (rule 17), never once.
* Pick a storage base with no `CNTO` items: the first choice (`ChestHouseTreasuryMiddle02`) spawned loot in every
  reference; `ChestClutterLower01Empty` ([value removed], no items, no Respawns flag) is the one used.

## procdump on Oblivion Remastered freezes the game for minutes and, stopped, takes the game with it (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Chasing a crash the game leaves no record of (no Saved\Crashes folder, no Windows Application
Error event: its handler ends the process), procdump was attached with `-e -ma`: a first-chance exception during
loading started a full dump of a 7 GB process, which suspended the game for as long as the write took - the owner
reported "crash" and "frozen" twice. Killing procdump then ended the game too (a debugger's exit ends its debuggee).

**Do instead.** No debugger on this game while the owner is testing. A crash inside our own code is found by a step
log written at info level and flushed (the bar's build logged step 1..9; the crash between two steps named the
function), and by SPLITTING the suspect into single-call tool ops (the spike's unequip / store / take / equip): the
call that never answers is the culprit. The InnerTextBlock crash of the day was exactly that: a scan over every
reflected property treating each as an object pointer and dereferencing it through `IsLive` - only walk pointers the
reflection names as objects (a panel's `Slots` -> each slot's `Content`).

## Adding a row to one of Oblivion Remastered's UMG menus: insert into the menu's own layout, re-ACTIVATE what came off, and join the game's navigation subsystem (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** The Simple Loadout System's row of five brown boxes had to sit inside the inventory menu below the
category tabs and above the category title (the owner: part of the interface, not drawn over it). Three lessons from
the route there:
1. **Placement.** A panel's insert-at-index is not reflected, add-to-end is: the row goes FIRST in the content box's
   vertical layout by taking its children (header, separator, list overlay) off with `RemoveFromParent` and adding
   them back behind the row with `AddChildToVerticalBox`, re-applying each slot's size / padding / alignments. The
   game's layout then pushes the title and the list down and bounds the row. Boxes are equal `Fill` shares of the
   row (no fixed widths - fixed ones ran past the panel). A first attempt on the canvas (coordinates from a slot
   whose auto-sized numbers were stale) floated over the title and past the panel.
2. **The D-pad died after the rebuild.** The list is a CommonUI ACTIVATABLE widget (`VAltarNavigableListView`):
   `RemoveFromParent` deactivates it, and re-adding it does not re-activate it. `SetFocus` was not enough (the mouse
   click that "fixed it" was the game re-activating the list: `BP_OnActivated` -> `BP_GetDesiredFocusTarget` ->
   `OnFocus` in the ProcessEvent log). Its own reflected `ActivateWidget` after the re-add is the fix.
3. **Navigation.** The game's module VCommonUIEnhancedInputNavigation (SDK dump): every navigable widget implements
   `IVEnhancedInputNavigable` and carries a `LayerTag`; `UVUINavigationGlobalSubsystem::NavigateToWidget(TScript
   Interface)` moves the focus (the interface pointer comes from the class's `interfaces` table - offset > 0 for a
   native implementation); the game's invisible button prefab (`WBP_ModernPrefab_InvisibleButton_C`, a
   `VNavigableButton`) over each box gives mouse hover / click (`BP_OnHovered`, `BP_OnClicked`) and a focus target;
   D-pad Up on the list's top row (`BP_GetSelectedItem` + `GetIndexForItem` on the INNER `VModernListView`, not the
   wrapper) is swallowed on the XInput import and handed to `NavigateToWidget(button)`; Down / B hand it back and
   `NavigateToIndex(0)` puts the list on its top row; `ClearSelection` on the way up, because the list keeps its last
   SELECTED item lit after its focus leaves. Sounds: the button styles are silent; the menus' sounds are Wwise
   events (`ui_glb_hover`, `ui_glb_select` under `/Game/WwiseAudio/Interface/Global/Redesign/`) posted with
   `UAkAudioEvent::PostOnActor` on the player controller.

**Do instead.** For any row added to an OR menu: real widgets through `WidgetBlueprintLibrary::Create` (the Tween
Menu's helpers), inserted into the menu's own layout; every activatable widget that came off the layout gets
`ActivateWidget`; navigation through the subsystem and the game's own navigable button, never a private highlight
alone; the events a widget fires are learned by logging every ProcessEvent function name on it once.

## Oblivion Remastered's InterfaceManager::menuMode is 1 in gameplay, not 0 - a truthy test reads "a menu is open" every frame (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Better Third-Person Selection's first test round (09:12, the primary agent's report) loaded, registered
its page and tool, logged the game's pick fields - and never read the camera: no "property offsets proven", no "player
controller found". Its frame tick returned at [code removed] every frame. In Oblivion Remastered menuMode is **1
while playing**; Tween Menu (`menuMode == 1` = in gameplay) and Improved Wheel Menu (`menuMode != 1` = a menu) already
read it that way, and nothing said so anywhere a new mod would look. The early returns logged only at debug, so the
shipped info-level log showed a tick that simply stopped - it could not say where.

**Why it looked fine.** In the original engine's source convention a mode byte of 0 is "none", and the member's name
says nothing about the value; the build compiles and the tick visibly runs.

**Do instead.** Test gameplay as `menuMode == 1` and a menu as `!= 1` (gate rule `or-menumode-gameplay-is-one` fails a
CommonLibOB64 repo that tests it for truth or against 0). In a new mod's first build, log each stop reason of a
per-frame pipeline ONCE per change at info ("state: a menu is open", "camera: not read - ..."): a test round at the
shipped level then shows which stage it reached. Same round, same lesson class from the Improved Wheel Menu crash at
