09:15 (TestBench crash writer: `reflect::IsLive` from `rows::HighlightedItem` reading freed memory): `IsLive(ptr)` reads
`ptr->internalIndex`, so it is only safe for an object read this frame from a live owner - a pointer KEPT across frames
must carry the object-array slot it was found in and be checked by asking the slot (`ue::Handle` in
BetterThirdPersonSelectionOR/src/Ue.h), never by reading the object.

## Oblivion Remastered's equipment path traps every thread but the TES thread - a silent death with no crash record until TestBench wrote one; the 'Oblivion Main loop' per-iteration call is the hook (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Simple Loadout System OR's first unequip calls - `Actor::UnequipObject` (address library) and the
vtable's `RemoveWornItem` - each took the game down the instant they ran, from a TestBench tool in gameplay and from
the loadout box's A press alike: no WER report, no Application Error event, no UE crash folder, three crashes and
nothing to read. A vectored exception handler added to TestBench (`CrashLog.cpp`: code, module+offset, registers, a
stack scan, the module list, written before the engine's handler) named it on the fourth:
`[offset removed]`, `inc dword [operand removed]` with rsi = 0 right after
`[instruction removed] call GetCurrentThreadId; [instruction removed] je ok` - a deliberate wrong-thread assertion. The remaster
runs the TES simulation on its own thread (an FRunnable whose Run tail-jumps into the 'Oblivion Main loop',
`[offset removed]`); reads from the UE game thread are fine, the equipment path is not.

**Wrong turns.** The player's vtable `MobileObject::Process(float)` (slot [value removed]) as the per-frame hook: it ran once
per session. The console (`KismetSystemLibrary::ExecuteConsoleCommand`) as a route round it: not proven either way,
and asynchronous. OBSE64 has no task interface.

**Do instead.** A queue drained from the TES thread: the main loop calls ONE function unconditionally at the top of
every iteration (`[offset removed]`; the call site `[bytes removed]
[bytes removed]`, one match, resolved from the E8 - MinHook on the target, the detour runs the
queued tasks after the original). It keeps ticking while a menu is open (a switch runs within 3 ms of the press).
And when a game dies with no record, put the crash writer in FIRST: three guesses cost three of the owner's rounds;
the record cost one. (`SimpleLoadoutSystemOR/src/TesThread.cpp`, `TestBenchOR/src/CrashLog.cpp`.)

## Actor::EquipObject's last argument is the console's NoUnequip lock - CommonLibOB64 calls it a_force, and true made every restored piece permanent; and a WORN armour piece will not move out of the inventory (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** The loadout restore equipped each piece with `EquipObject(obj, n, extra, true, true)`; the gear
went on, then nothing could take it off - "you cannot unequip this item", weapon swaps that said "equipped" and did
nothing (the owner's report, 09:45). The fifth argument is what `player.equipitem <id> 1` passes: the item gets
`ExtraCannotWear` ([value removed]) and stays. `UnequipObject`'s `a_force` is the same lock. Earlier the same session the store
pass logged five pieces moved into the chest while four were still worn: `TESObjectREFR::RemoveItem` moved the sword
and refused every worn armour piece, silently.

**Do instead.** Equip with the lock argument FALSE (`EquipObject(obj, n, extra, false, false)`; gate rule
`or-equipobject-never-locks`), and report the lock after every restore (`Locked(extra)` in Loadouts.cpp, the state
op's `locked`). Store in two passes: every worn piece off through `UnequipObject`, then each piece found again in the
inventory (a fresh unworn list - the one it was worn through may be gone) and moved. The vtable's `AddWornItem` /
`RemoveWornItem` only mark the piece; their return value is not a success flag, and a weapon put on that way leaves
the actor's weapon state stale.

## Oblivion Remastered's inventory menu shows what the TES side last pushed - the refresh is the argument-less rebuild [offset removed], not the UE-side pusher nor the widget's UpdateItemList (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** After a loadout switch the menu's rows kept the moved items until the menu was closed and
reopened. `UpdateItemList` on the inventory widget rebuilt the rows from the view model's stale arrays (Items 70 ->
70). Hooking the virtual `UVInventoryMenuViewModel::SetInventory` (vtable [value removed]) showed the push arriving on the UE
game thread through a pairing message whose handler calls a pusher (`[offset removed]`); replaying that pusher with its
captured arguments pushed the same stale 70 - it only forwards the item array the TES side built.

**What is true.** The TES side builds the array in ONE function that takes no arguments: `[offset removed]` does
`GetMenuByClass(kInventoryMenu [value removed])` (returns at once when the menu is closed), frees the legacy menu's old item
array (`[operand removed]`), walks the player's inventory into a new one and queues the push - the same function the game
runs when the menu opens and after its own equip. Called on the TES thread right after the switch's moves, the rows
update in place through the game's own binding. Found by the `lea` reference to the pusher; pattern at [value removed]
(`[bytes removed] ... [bytes removed]`, one match).

**Same round, the row's focus.** The navigation subsystem's `NavigateToWidget` on the mod's invisible button did not
move Slate's focus: the entry that had it fired OnFocusReceived 2 ms after the ask, every time (the "highlight"
that teleported the D-pad). `SetFocus` on the button - now, next frame, and back from any entry that regains it -
settled it; and the mod owns the list's selection (a focused entry becomes the selected item) so the Up hand-off
reads the focused row. A widget's tab input events (`InpActEvt_..._NextTab`) called by ProcessEvent fire and change
nothing; the view model's `SetCurrentPageInventory` does the page change.

## Root Builder (copy mode) copies the game folder's deployed files BACK over the mod folder when the game exits - a build installed into the mod folder in that window is silently reverted (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** Better Third-Person Selection's crash fix (no engine Activate call) was copied into its MO2 mod folder
2 seconds after the game exited; the installer read the hash back and reported the new DLL. The next launch crashed on
the OLD code (`activate::Run` in the stack - a function the new build does not have). The mod folder held the old DLL
again, with the old file's timestamp: Root Builder's cleanup, which runs after the game exits, had copied the game
folder's deployed copy back over the mod folder's file. The same session had assumed it synced back only files the game
changed (the INI the page saves) - it takes the deployed files as they are.

**Do instead.** Install into an Oblivion Remastered (Root Builder, copy mode) mod folder only after the cleanup has
finished: wait until the deployed copy under the game folder (`...\OblivionRemastered\Binaries\Win64\OBSE\Plugins\<Mod>.dll`)
is GONE, then copy, then read the hash back again a few seconds later. A hash read straight after the copy proves
nothing about what the next launch loads.

## A native UClass found at startup can still have no properties linked - a layout self-check that treats "not found" as "wrong" latches a failure and the whole plugin stays off (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** CCM's resumed build called `ue::SelfCheck()` (reads `VQuickKeysMenuViewModel.KeyIndex`, expects [value removed])
from its first frames. 2 s into the launch the class was found but `Offset(..., "KeyIndex")` returned -1, the check
stored "failed" for good ("KeyIndex read at 0x-1"), and nothing that depends on reflection ever ran - no camera, no class
watches. Better Third-Person Selection, with the same code, only reached the check once a player existed, so it had
never failed there.

**Do instead.** A property that is not found is "not ready yet": return false and ask again later (rule 17); latch a
failure only on a property found at a WRONG offset. The same goes for any check run before a save is loaded - a class
object existing is not the class being linked.

## A write made in a PRE handler of a Blueprint event is undone by the event's own body - CCM's free camera did nothing until it wrote after ReceiveTick, as UCR does (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** CCM's per-class ProcessEvent watch (pe::Watch) ran its handler BEFORE the original, and CCM wrote the
four free-camera flags there, on the player's `ReceiveTick`. The owner, with UCR's free camera off: "it doesn't work".
The player's Blueprint tick re-applies the stance flags (probe P2 had already seen a write undone after walking), so
every write was overwritten the same frame. Ultimate Combat Redux writes the same flags in a POST hook on the same event.

**Do instead.** When the point of hooking an event is to change state the event's body also sets, act AFTER the body:
pe::Watch(cls, handler, /*post*/ true) runs the handler after the original ProcessEvent. Before choosing pre or post,
look at what the reference mod does (UCR's HookManager `kind = "post"`) - the hook's timing is part of the behaviour.

---

## Oblivion Remastered's menu navigation reads a row's parent and direction map when the row is CONSTRUCTED - a row edited afterwards looks right and goes nowhere; re-add the neighbour (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** AMF OR 1.0.4 adds an "Apocrypha Menu Framework" row to the System page (WBP_Modern_Settings_
SaveLoadPage_C, rows of WBP_Modern_Settings_SystemButtonWrapper_C). The row drew, the mouse pressed it, and the D-pad
never reached it - through four builds: the rows' `WidgetForNavigation` maps rewritten in place (Exit Game's Down ->
ours, ours' Up -> Exit Game, the raw TMap laid out exactly as the engine's), the page's `Buttons` array and
`FocusIndex`, `NavigableParent` and the subsystem handle copied from a game row, Slate explicit rules, and
`ActivateWidget` (which made things worse: Back jumped to the row and the D-pad could not leave it - the game's rows
are not activated). A live diff of our row against Exit Game showed every reflected property identical and the maps
correct, yet Down on Exit Game produced not one ProcessEvent on any widget: the native subsystem rejected the press
before consulting anything.

**What was actually true.** The subsystem takes a navigable's parent, handle and map ONCE, when the widget is
constructed (added to a panel); later edits to those properties are invisible to it, and nothing reflected shows that.
Setting our row's parent, handle and map BEFORE adding it, and taking Exit Game out of its panel with
`RemoveFromParent` and putting it straight back (constructed again, its Down entry now leading to ours; slot layout
copied across, order kept) made the D-pad reach the row and return. Proven by the owner 12:5x.

**The check.** When a live object's reflected state is correct and a native system still ignores it, suspect a copy
taken at a lifecycle point (construct, activate, register) rather than a live read - and re-run that lifecycle point
(re-add, re-activate) instead of editing more properties. A diff that finds nothing is itself the evidence. Entry
7825 (SLS) is the same family: re-activation after a re-add.

## offsetof through std::array's operator[] points a settings row at the wrong member - CCM's framing rows read and wrote the camera style (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** CCM's settings table names each INI key's member with `offsetof(Values, member)`. The per-context
framing rows used `offsetof(Values, fmGroups[3].side)` with `fmGroups` a `std::array`. Under MSVC that expression goes
through `operator[]` (a function call, not a built-in subscript) and every framing row resolved to offsets 0-12 - the
members `enabled`, `cameraStyle`, `fBlockTurnSeconds` and `fSpellTurnSeconds`. Save wrote those four values into every
[Framing.<Context>] section (0.00 / 0.20 / 1.40 and bOwn=1 everywhere); ccm.drive Framing.* wrote into them; the next load
would have put 0 into the camera style. The start-up check that compares Values{} with the table's defaults DID say so -
thirty "compiled default ... a build defect, report it" errors at the top of the first log - but only as log lines, and
the handoff for that build did not ask for the log's first lines to be read. The tester then reported the symptom as
"the sneak context doesn't apply" and as offset stacking.

**Do instead.** Never take `offsetof` through a container's `operator[]`: use a C array for an indexed member, and
`static_assert` the indexed offset against `offsetof(array) + i * sizeof(element) + offsetof(element, field)`. A settings
table must check at start that no two rows share bytes and, if any do, refuse to read or write the INI at all (a table
that points at the wrong member corrupts the player's file). A start-up self-check that finds a build defect must stop
the thing it guards, not only log - and every handoff after a settings change asks for the first log lines. Also: a
warning must fire on the failure, not on a normal condition near it - CCM's "the game re-wrote the camera offset 38
times a second" fired on the game resetting its own value every frame, which is harmless, and sent the tester looking
for stacking that the numbers (base + offset, exactly) ruled out.

## A UObject kept by object-array slot AND pointer still went stale - a freed widget's slot and address were both reused, and the dead one passed every liveness check (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** HUD Position Manager keeps each HUD widget across frames as `ue::Handle` (the pointer plus its
FUObjectArray index; Get() asks the slot whether it still holds that pointer). The Level text this mod creates on the
layout's Overlay was made at 15:45:43, before the owner's save had loaded; the load rebuilt the HUD, the old layout and
the text were garbage-collected, and the engine handed the SAME address and the SAME array index to another object of
the same size. The handle said "alive", Apply measured whatever full-screen widget now lived there (rect 0,0 x
1920x1080, so the sliders' range collapsed to 0 %), and Find() saw `created && Get()` and never made a new text. Nothing
logged, because every check the code had was passing; the owner reported "the level widget position settings are stuck
at 0 %". A live search of every WBP_AltarTextBlock_C in the object array (285 of them) found none that was ours - the
first evidence.

**Why it looked right.** Slot-plus-pointer is the check the other mods use and it had never failed; the assumption was
that a reused slot would hold a different address. UE's allocator hands freed blocks of one size class back first, and
the object array's free list hands the freed index back first - so a widget destroyed and a widget of a similar class
created in the same rebuild get both back together, routinely, not by chance.

**Do instead.** A handle to a UObject compares three things at Get(): the slot's pointer, the object's class, and its
FName (the 8 bytes, index and number) as recorded at Set(). CommonLibOB64's FUObjectItem has no SerialNumber to lean on.
And when a "found" element's geometry is the whole viewport, treat that as "this is not the widget I think it is"
before anything else. The check that would have caught it sooner: a mod-created widget should be looked up by name in
the object array once after every HUD rebuild and the count logged.

## Oblivion Remastered's PlayerCharacter singleton exists at the main menu with no character - asking it for an actor value there hangs the game (2026-09-29)

**What happened.** HUD Position Manager's "Length follows the resource" read the player's health, magicka and fatigue
through [code removed] once a second from the HUD tick. The HUD tick
runs from the first frame the layout exists - the main menu included - and the owner's layout had the length link on.
At 23:08:54, seconds after launch and before any save was loaded, the game took an access violation reading address
[value removed] inside its own code, called from `LinkedLength` (TestBench's crash record, symbolized against the PDB with
dbghelp: [source reference removed]). The game froze instead of closing. The earlier sessions never hit it because the length link
was only turned on in game.

**Why it looked safe.** `GetSingleton()` returned a non-null player, and every other read the mod made from it at the
main menu (`GetLevel`, the `skillAdvanceCount` member) came back without crashing - the skill count read -1, which was
the tell that no character was loaded. A virtual that walks the actor-value owner is a different matter from a plain
member read.

**Do instead.** Treat the player as present only when `menuMode == 1` and `player->parentCell != nullptr`; before that,
keep the last known value (or the neutral one). Gate rule `or-player-actor-values-need-a-placed-player` now fails the
package of any Oblivion Remastered plugin that calls `GetActorValue` / `GetActorFloatValue` after
`PlayerCharacter::GetSingleton()` without a `parentCell` check. Also: a crash record's module offsets turn into source
lines with the system's dbghelp.dll (SymLoadModuleExW at a fake base + SymGetLineFromAddrW64) - no extra tool needed.

## Oblivion Remastered's compass HostileData lists only actors IN COMBAT - who can detect the player lives in each NPC's HighProcess detection list at [value removed] (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** HUD Position Manager's first sneak detection indicator placed its marks from the HUD view model's
`HostileData` (the compass's red enemy ticks), shown while the vignette's `bSneaking` was set. The owner reported "I
dont see the sneak detection widget". Live reads showed `bSneaking` true and the reticle's `SneakDetectionLevel` moving,
but `HostileData.num` was 0: it lists only actors in combat with the player, so sneaking past guards, the case the
widget exists for, drew nothing.

**Why it looked right.** The damage direction indicator uses the same list and worked, because a hit implies combat.
The data source was chosen for the widget that happened to be built first.

**Do instead.** Read detection from the engine itself. `MobileObject::currentProcess` ([value removed]) of the player is a
HighProcess, and its `BSSimpleList` at [value removed] names the actors around the player. Each of those actors' own HighProcess
(the same vtable as the player's - lower process levels are skipped) has the same list of the actors IT detects. Its
entry whose first qword is the player carries the detection level at [value removed] (u8: 0 lost, 1 unseen, 2 noticed, 3 seen)
and a signed value at [value removed]. Both were seen moving live, as prison guards looked toward or away from the player.
Position is `TESObjectREFR::data.location` ([value removed]). The direction relative to the view is atan2(dx, dy) minus the
compass's `CompassDirectionValue`. Both are Oblivion headings, clockwise from north; Oblivion heading = UE yaw + 90.
Read it fault-guarded, a few times a second, not every frame. The check that would have caught it sooner: before
building on a view-model array, read it in the exact situation the feature is for (here, sneaking near non-hostile
NPCs) and confirm it is not empty.

## A per-tick UE call with a cached controller as its world context crashed the game on quit - the controller outlived its world, and a slot-checked handle still said it was fine (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** Minimap Menu crashed as the owner quit to the main menu (01:49:42; EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading
[value removed] inside the game, rcx 0, called from `minimap::Layout()` through `WidgetLayoutLibrary::GetViewportSize`). `Layout()`
ran every 500 ms whatever the game was doing, and passed the cached player controller as `WorldContextObject`. During a
quit the controller object is still in its object-array slot, with the same name and class, until garbage collection
runs. The world and viewport behind it are already torn down, so the engine read through a null world pointer.

**Why it looked fine.** The controller was held the safe way: by slot and pointer, checked through the slot every tick
(entry 8027's lesson). That check proves only that the OBJECT is still there. Nothing about a world-context object's
world is checked by it, and a tick that runs behind menus reaches exactly the moment when the two part.

**Do instead.** A call that takes a `WorldContextObject`:
- runs only in gameplay (menuMode == 1) unless it truly must run behind a menu;
- refuses a context object that is dying: object flags BeginDestroyed, FinishDestroyed, PendingKill or Garbage, or
  internal flags Garbage, Unreachable or PendingKill;
- goes through a fault-guarded ProcessEvent (`Call::RunGuarded`, `__try` / `__except`) so a torn-down world costs one
  skipped call, not the game.

Gate rule `or-world-context-calls-are-guarded` refuses a package whose source sets `"WorldContextObject"` and then
calls a plain `.Run()` within the next few lines. Minimap Menu, Camera Configuration Menu and Improved Wheel Menu were
fixed the same day.

## A rounded-box brush does not clip a MATERIAL in Oblivion Remastered - Minimap Menu's round map became a turning square; nested turned clip panels make the circle (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** In Minimap Menu's circle shape, the game's local map (a material, M_LocalMapUI, on its own image)
showed its square corners outside the round frame. The panel clips to its own square, and the map image is larger than
the panel and turned about the player. The first fix sized the image to the panel, chose the visible part of the map
through the brush's UVRegion, and set the brush's DrawAs to RoundedBox with the half-height radius - the same thing
that makes the parchment (a TEXTURE brush) round. In game the owner saw "a square that rotates the entire frame": the
material drew as a plain square, and turning that panel-sized square turned the whole minimap.

**Why it looked right.** A rounded box does round a texture brush in this game (the parchment, the frame), and a UE5
material brush drawn as a rounded box was assumed to get the same shader. It does not here: the material's own pixel
shader draws, and nothing clips it to the rounded shape. The hypothesis was built on the texture case and never
checked against a material before it shipped to a test.

**Do instead.** To clip anything - a material included - to a circle in UMG without a mask material, nest clip panels:
N CanvasPanels, each filling its parent, each `ClipToBounds`, each turned 90/N degrees more than the one outside it
(render transform, pivot 0.5, 0.5). Slate clips a turned widget to its turned rectangle (stencil clipping), and the N
clips intersect in a regular 4N-sided shape that holds the inscribed circle; at N = 8 it is within about a pixel of a
330 px circle. Turn the innermost panel back by the sum of the others, so its content is laid out untouched. Before
building on a brush's DrawAs for a material, try it on that material in game first.

## The licence rules never looked at an Oblivion Remastered mod - their markers named only CMake/vcpkg projects, and every OBSE64 plugin builds with xmake (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** Asked whether the licence gate had been run on the Oblivion Remastered mods, the audit found that
the gate's licence rule for repo text (`repo-shipped-text-never-calls-the-mod-mit`) is keyed on a vcpkg.json or
CMakeLists.txt naming GPL-3.0 - so every xmake-built OBSE64 plugin was skipped ("repo has no ... matching"), every
package, silently. And no rule checked that a linked permissive component's notice ships at all: Ultimate Combat
Redux 1.0.0 was released without spdlog's MIT notice (spdlog comes in through CommonLibOB64, never named in xmake.lua),
Improved Wheel Menu linked MinHook (BSD-2) and nlohmann/json without theirs, and Camera Configuration Menu had no
dist\LICENSE or notices file.

**Why it looked covered.** Every package gate run printed "PASS every rule clear". A "skip" line reads like "not
applicable" - it was "not looked at".

**Do instead.** When a rule is keyed on a build-system marker, list every build system in use (CMake+vcpkg for SKSE,
xmake for OBSE64, Python for MO2 plugins) and include them all. Check a component's notice by its copyright holder's
line, which only the licence text carries (Gabi Melman, Tsuda Kageyu, Niels Lohmann, Omar Cornut) - a changelog mention
of the name must not satisfy it. Gate rules added the same day: or-linked-spdlog-keeps-its-notice,
linked-minhook-keeps-its-notice, linked-nlohmann-json-keeps-its-notice, linked-imgui-keeps-its-notice; the MIT rule's
marker now includes xmake.lua. The check that would have caught it sooner: read a gate run's SKIP lines for a new
build system the first time it is packaged.

## The packager seeded an Oblivion Remastered mod's package from the Skyrim mod of the same name - it chose its seed by display name alone (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** Packaging HUD Position Manager 1.0.0 for Oblivion Remastered (repo HUDPositionManagerOR),
package-mod.ps1 took the newest existing package named "HUD Position Manager" as its seed - the SKYRIM mod's 1.0.1 - and
the new package came out with that mod's FOMOD (Common\, Line-17\, Line-SE-AE16\, fomod\) beside its own
OblivionRemastered\ tree. The packager only warned "the newest existing package is 1.0.1, which is not older than the
requested 1.0.0"; the package gate passed every file rule. It was caught by listing the folder.

**Why it looked fine.** Rule 10 gives an Oblivion Remastered mod the plain name, so two games' mods can share a display
name (Apocrypha Menu Framework already did, but its versions and FOMOD suffix kept the seeds apart by luck). The seed
step never asked which game a package was for.

**Do instead.** A seed must be the same game's package: package-mod.ps1 now reads the mod's registry entry (game
OblivionRemastered, or an OblivionRemastered pluginDir) and seeds only from a package with - or, for any other mod,
without - an OblivionRemastered\ tree. Gate rule or-package-carries-no-skyrim-installer (kind one-game-per-package)
fails any package that holds an OblivionRemastered\ tree beside fomod\, Line-17\, Line-SE-AE16\, Common\, SKSE\, Data\
or Interface\. When two games' mods share a name, list the package folder after packaging.

## OpenRGB "lost" its profiles after a restart - OpenRGB 1.0's own Windows service came up with an empty profile folder, and the window became its client (2026-09-30)

**Symptom.** After the BIOS update's restart the owner opened OpenRGB and every profile (Blue, Green, Red) was gone -
"we fixed this once already". The profile files were still in %APPDATA%\OpenRGB\profiles, untouched since 2026-09-25.

**Cause.** OpenRGB 1.0's installer registers a Windows service, "OpenRGB" (LocalSystem, Automatic,
C:\Program Files\OpenRGB\OpenRGB.exe). It keeps its OWN settings in C:\Program Files\OpenRGB\service_config (OpenRGB.json,
profiles\, logs\). When the service runs, the OpenRGB window started by the user becomes a network client of it (its log
shows only "[NetworkClient] Requesting controller ID n") and lists the service's profiles - an empty folder. The service's
logs show it ran on 2026-09-25 21:56 and then not until the 2026-09-30 restarts (06:55, 08:46), which is why the profiles
"disappeared" only now. It detected every device (ENE DRAM x2, the mainboard board, the Corsair Lighting Node Core); only
the profiles were missing. Copying into Program Files needs administrator rights, which Claude's shell does not have.

**Do instead.** Put the profiles where the service reads them: copy %APPDATA%\OpenRGB\profiles\*.json into
C:\Program Files\OpenRGB\service_config\profiles (an elevated copy - the owner in Explorer), reopen OpenRGB, and set
"Load profile on service startup" if a colour should apply at boot. Check which instance is running first:
`Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter "Name='OpenRGB'"` and the parent of OpenRGB.exe (services.exe = the service).
Leave Windows Dynamic Lighting off (the 2026-09-26 finding: it overrides the RAM and board lights).

**Resolved 2026-09-30 (elevated session).** Copied Blue/Green/Red.json into service_config\profiles (SHA-256 matched), and set
ProfileManager.service_startup_profile = {enabled: true, name: "Blue"} in service_config\OpenRGB.json (backup: OpenRGB.json.bak-20260930).
Two traps: PowerShell's ConvertFrom-Json refuses this file (the detector list has keys differing only in case - 'GPU'
and 'Gaming OC'), so edit it with Python's json; and STOP the service before editing, then start it - a plain Restart-Service can
let the service write its settings back over the edit on shutdown. The new log lists 'Found file: Blue.json/Green.json/Red.json'.
Then the profiles listed but the MOTHERBOARD ignored them: the service lacked %APPDATA%\OpenRGB\Configuration.json, the file that
holds user-set zone sizes (mainboard JRAINBOW1/2 = 40 LEDs each), so it saw those headers at 0 LEDs and the profile's board entry
(82 LEDs) no longer matched. Copying Configuration.json into service_config (service stopped) fixed it. The service needs ALL THREE:
profiles\, OpenRGB.json's ProfileManager, and Configuration.json. Check over the SDK (openrgb-python, port 6742): zone LED counts.

## A fix proven in one Oblivion Remastered mod stayed in that mod - AMF's System row still asked a FREED page "are you alive" by reading it, and crashed on a loadout swap (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** The owner equipped the second loadout of Simple Loadout System and the game crashed. The UE crash
report blamed no loadout code: [code removed] from `systemrow::Tick()`,
reading 0x...EBC - offset [value removed] (`internalIndex`) past a 16-byte-aligned heap block. The System row kept the System page,
its row and the row above as raw `UObject*` across frames and checked them each tick with `IsLive`, whose FIRST step read
the object's own slot index. The loadout swap rebuilt the menus, the collector freed the page, and the liveness check
itself dereferenced freed memory.

**Why it looked fine.** IsLive compared the slot with the pointer, which reads like a weak-pointer check, and it passed
every earlier session because freed UObject memory usually stays mapped. HUD Position Manager had already met the same
class (entry 8032, the day before) and built `ue::Handle` - slot index, class and FName recorded while live, the slot
asked before the object is touched - but the fix lived in that mod alone; AMF's copy of the pattern never got it.
The crash was also first read as Simple Loadout System's, because that was what the owner was doing.

**Do instead.** An engine object kept past the frame it was found in is a `Handle` (AMF: `reflect::Handle`), never a raw
pointer checked later. A liveness check never reads through the pointer it is checking unless guarded. When a lesson like
8032 lands in one OR mod, grep the other OR mods for the same pattern (`IsLive(` on a global or member) the same day.
Read the crash report's call stack before naming the mod: the action the player took is the trigger, not the culprit.

## The version gate read every Nexus ID in Skyrim's section - linking the Oblivion Remastered pages recorded two 2016 Skyrim mods as our "working" versions (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** Linking the owner's eight Oblivion Remastered Nexus pages ([id removed]-5668, found through the v2 GraphQL
API filtered by game and uploader) with `version-gate.ps1 -Action link` reported versions that matched nothing of ours -
UVC 2.0.0, Weightless 1.1.0, Minimap "removed", HUD Position Manager 1.21.0 "wastebinned" - and the Nexus-is-the-floor
logic wrote UVC 2.0.0 and Weightless 1.1.0 into the ledger as WORKING. `Get-NexusPublished` hardcoded
`/v1/games/skyrimspecialedition/`, so each ID was another author's Skyrim mod from 2016-17. The first link (Simple
Loadout System, 5666) looked right only because that Skyrim mod also reads 1.0.0. The HPM link also landed on the
Skyrim mod's registry key (`HUDPositionManager`, not `HUDPositionManagerOR`).

**Why it looked fine.** The tool said `ok` for every link and the versions were plausible numbers; nothing compared
the page it read with the mod it was linking.

**Do instead.** A Nexus ID means nothing without its game section: the registry carries `nexusDomain` (inferred from a
repo's `dist\OblivionRemastered` tree when absent), and `link` / the Nexus sync refuse a page not uploaded by
ApocryphaRealm and print the page's NAME, so a wrong ID or section fails loudly instead of writing the ledger. Read the
name back on every link. The bad registry links were reverted from git and the two false ledger rows removed.

## A name two games share sent the finalize tools to the other game's mod - the Oblivion AMF 1.0.5 finalize rewrote the SKYRIM framework's Nexus folder and deleted its zip (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** Finalizing Apocrypha Menu Framework 1.0.5 (Oblivion Remastered) through the new `finalize-mod.ps1`,
two tools resolved the display name "Apocrypha Menu Framework" - which the Skyrim framework also carries - to the
SKYRIM mod. `pre-finalize-check.ps1` matched the Skyrim registry entry first (caught: the dry run showed CMake 1.9.9).
`sync-nexus-distro.ps1` called `Resolve-DistroFolder` without a game and took `Skyrim - Apocrypha Menu Framework`: it
set that page's "This package is" line, its notes counter and its banner pill to 1.0.5, copied the Oblivion zip in,
and `Remove-Item -Force`d the Skyrim 1.9.9 FOMOD zip. The same run's prune step would also have recycled the Skyrim
`Apocrypha Menu Framework 1.8.1.zip` (caught before it ran). Restored from `10. finalized mods` and by reversing each
edit; `nexus-distro-sweep.ps1` reads the Skyrim folder CURRENT again.

**Why it looked fine.** Each tool had been proven on SLS, Tween Menu and Minimap Menu that evening - names only one
game uses. `Resolve-DistroFolder` already took a game; nothing passed one.

**Do instead.** A tool that finds a mod by name is handed the registry KEY (unique) or reads the GAME from the package's
contents (`Get-PackageGame`) and refuses a folder of another game. Now: `finalize-mod.ps1` passes the key to the check
and prunes only releases of the package's game; `sync-nexus-distro.ps1` reads the game from the package, refuses when it
cannot, refuses a folder of another game, and keeps the current version's optional downloads (`<Mod> X.Y.Z - SDK.zip`).
Dry-run first on any mod whose display name another game's mod shares.

## Typing into a web form box without reading it first spliced text into the middle of the owner's existing permissions (Nexus, 2026-09-30)

**What happened.** Applying the owner's custom-permissions text to Ultimate Combat Redux's Nexus page, the first screenshot
showed none of the three permission options selected, so the box was taken for empty. "Write your own (custom)" was
already selected further down, its box holding 729 characters of credits (Kramer7046's permission, Cosmic's animations).
A click put the caret mid-sentence and the typed text landed inside "His permissions ex|plicitly allow". Nothing was
saved: the inserted span was selected by script and deleted with a real Delete keypress, which restored the exact text.

**Why it looked fine.** The visible part of the page showed no selection; the form's lower half was off-screen, and a
script query for checked radios returned none because the control is custom-drawn.

**Do instead.** Before typing into any field on someone's live page, read the field's current value (a script read of
the textarea) and act on what is there: an empty box gets the text, a filled one is reported, not appended to. Also from
the same session, Nexus's new upload form: a scripted `.value` fill does not reach its React state (a changelog vanished
on a step change) - type with real keystrokes; the description is SCEditor (`sceditor.instance(ta).val()`), and closing
a tab with unsaved changes hangs the extension on the beforeunload guard - restore the field and save, or ask.

## package-gate.ps1 run on its own skipped every page rule - it looked for the distro folder by the pre-rename name (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** Testing the short-description rule after moving the summary into `short-description.txt`, the gate
reported `skip [page-summary-fits-nexus-field]` even for a 431-character summary. Line 73 joined
`11. Nexus distro\<Mod>`, the naming from before the 2026-09-29 `<Game> - <Mod>` prefixes, so a gate run without
`-DistroDir` found no folder and skipped every page-text rule silently; `pre-finalize-check.ps1` passes the folder
explicitly, which hid it.

**Do instead.** Resolve distro folders only through `distro-names.ps1` (`Resolve-DistroFolder` with the package's game
from `Get-PackageGame`), never by joining a name. A rule test must include a case that has to FAIL - a skip reads like
a pass.

## Item Explorer's live Nexus file read "1.0.10" - it was already the 1.1.1 build under a version number that never exists (2026-09-30)

**What happened.** Asked to post Item Explorer 1.1.1, Claude found the 13.6 MB zip over the Chrome extension's 10 MB
upload cap and began planning an upload through the Nexus v3 API. The page's changelog for "1.0.10" already began
"Version 1.1.1 ... Version 1.1.0", which gave it away: the live file was 14,270,747 bytes, the same as the local
`Item Explorer 1.1.1.zip`, and the v1 `md5_search` endpoint matched its MD5 to that file. The build had been posted on
2026-09-20 with a hand-typed version ("1.0.10" cannot exist under rule 6); nothing needed uploading.

**Do instead.** Before uploading a release, compare the live main file with the local zip (size from
`/v1/games/<domain>/mods/<id>/files.json`, then `/v1/games/<domain>/mods/md5_search/<md5>.json`). If they match, fix
only the label: the file's ⋮ menu > Edit > File version, with "Update mod version to match" ticked. The v3 API's
`PUT /mod-files/{id}` changes only the name, so it cannot fix a version. A version typed into the Nexus form is
checked against the distro zip's name before saving.

**The leftover changelog entry.** A Nexus changelog entry is keyed by its version string, and the editor reaches it only
through a file that currently carries that version: its version box is locked and an empty entry cannot be saved, so an
entry can be corrected but not deleted or renamed (the API only adds entries). To correct the orphaned "1.0.10" entry,
the file was set to 1.0.10 for a moment with "Update mod version" unticked, the entry was rewritten from the file's
⋮ > Edit changelog, and the file was set back to 1.1.1. Wait for a dialog's Save to finish before the next click: a
click sent while the spinner ran typed into the still-open changelog box.

## Driving and filming Oblivion Remastered without the owner: what reaches the game, and what a clip needs (2026-10-01)

**What happened.** The owner left Claude to test Ultimate Combat Redux and Improved Wheel Menu alone and asked for video,
because motion does not show in stills. Most of the first half hour went on inputs that never arrived:
- TestBench `pad` and the ViGEm virtual DualShock 4 did nothing in gameplay. Steam Input sits in front of XInput, and
  with the owner's own pad connected the game listened to it alone. TestBench `key` posts window messages, which the
  menus accept and gameplay ignores.
- TestBench `console` said "typed into the game console" for additem/equipitem that never ran. Its `close` left the
  console open, and every later click went into the console, not the game.
- `re.additem` refuses weapons (type 33) and ammo (34) as "not an item".
- A bow that would not draw had no arrows equipped. "[BowCharge] attack released with no draw running" was the tell.
- `iwm.pad` triggers are BYTES: "rt":1 is a trigger barely touched (the log said "max RT 1", out of 255).
- The first clips were washed out: Windows HDR is on for the desktop, so an 8-bit desktop grab (ddagrab) of an SDR game
  comes out flat. The 16-bit grab is scRGB with SDR white at 6.0 (480 nits).

**Do instead.**
- Keyboard and mouse: `scripts\sendkey.py` (SendInput, scan codes; `seq` for held timelines).
- The wheel's pad: `iwm.pad press` (laid over the pad reads on the game thread).
- Console commands: `scripts\orcmd.py` (KismetSystemLibrary::ExecuteConsoleCommand through ue.call).
- Clips: `scripts\gamevideo.py` (ffmpeg gfxcapture - Windows Graphics Capture of the game WINDOW only: correct colours,
  nothing of the desktop), with `gameclip.py` / `iwmclip.py` wrapping record + inputs + contact sheets.
- Tool gaps to fix in TestBench: re.additem for weapons/ammo, and the console tool's execute/close.

## Oblivion Remastered fixes an action's animation speed when the action STARTS - writing its Duration mid-action looses the logic early and leaves the animation (and the state) hanging (2026-10-01)

**What happened.** UCR's Quick Shot had to shorten the bow draw. Three levers failed in turn: writing the draw action's
`DrawDuration` (the Blueprint recomputes it, and it is only a copy of the animated action's Duration); setting the bow
form's `Speed` (never read on this path - 1.47 s every time); and cutting `pawn.CurrentAnimatedAction.Duration` on a
tap. The last one made the arrow leave at 0.19 s while the draw animation kept playing at full length, the draw state
never ended, and the next attack press fired a second arrow (the owner: "it would immediately fire an arrow before ...
the animation even plays. And then it would leave the bow in the arm").

**Why.** An OR action plays through `StateMachinePlayAnimatedAction:PlayAnimatedAction(..., DesiredDuration, ...)`
(the bow draw passes the constant 0.0 = the clip's own length). The main AnimInstance stores `{Duration, Index}` per
action tag ([value removed]); when the action layer's Start state is ENTERED, native code sets
`VLayerCharacterAnimInstance.AnimLayerPlayRate` ([value removed]) = clip length / Duration. After that, nothing re-reads the
Duration - so a mid-action write changes when the action completes, not how fast it animates. There was no anim
montage to retime (GetCurrentActiveMontage stayed None for the whole draw).

**Do instead.** Shorten an action by its `DesiredDuration` at the moment it starts (UCR 273a1c7's QuickDraw re-points
the native wrapper's single call so it can change that float for the player's bow draw - a Blueprint's call into a
native static UFunction does not pass through ProcessEvent), or write the layer's `AnimLayerPlayRate` directly together
with a matching Duration. Before choosing a lever, read how the engine times the thing (the action/layer chain), not
just which fields look like durations. Skyrim's "rapid shot" mods are no guide here: they play separate short clips and
fire the arrow from a script marker.

## Swallowing a controller's Blueprint input event did not stop the game's native action - "swallowed (ok)" proved nothing (2026-10-01)

**What happened.** To cancel a bow draw without sheathing, UCR's plugin swallowed `ReadyItemInput_Pressed` and
`ToggleDrawWeaponPressed` at ProcessEvent during the draw and logged "swallowed" every time. The owner: "it just
sheathed the weapon normally". The draw's action exited 18 ms after the swallowed press. The cancel it called instead
(`OnUndrawBowReleased`, then `Interrupt` on the attack behaviour) was also wrong: the first was traced as itself starting
the sheathe, and the second could never run because `Behavior_AttackBehaviorBase_C` does not update during a bow draw.

**Why.** Those controller BP events are notifications raised by native Enhanced Input handling; the sheathe is decided
natively from the input action itself. Blocking the BP event left the real path untouched. And the trace that "proved"
`OnUndrawBowReleased` sheathes was taken while the swallow was active, so the swallow may have shaped the evidence.

**Do instead.** Prove a block by what the game does next (the action exits or not, the weapon state), never by the
blocker's own success line. Before building on a trace, check whether something of ours was altering the run it
recorded. To find what really starts a native action, log the calls in the window before it enters (UCR 273a1c7 logs
every controller call in the 300 ms before the draw/sheathe action enters) or read the state machine's transition
conditions.


**Amended later the same day (UCR e5bc5eb's offline read of the executable).** The "notifications" conclusion above was
wrong. `ReadyItemInput_Pressed`, `ToggleDrawWeaponPressed`, `OnUndrawBowReleased` and `OnAttackRequestPressed` are
registered Final|Native|Private (flags [value removed]; a Blueprint event such as ReceiveTick reads [value removed]) and Enhanced Input
calls them by name through ProcessEvent - so swallowing one DOES stop its body. The first swallow failed because F /
controller X is mapped in `IMC_Game_Combat` to BOTH `IA_Game_Combat_ReadyItem` and `IA_Game_Combat_UndrawBow`, and only the
ready-weapon handlers were swallowed: the sheathe came from `OnUndrawBowReleased`, which that build did not swallow (and
called itself as its "cancel"). The lesson stands in its general form - prove a block by what the game does next - plus:
before concluding an input event is "only a notification", read its function flags, and list EVERY action the key is
mapped to in the active mapping contexts.
## A "read-only" TestBench probe crashed the owner's game - ue.struct walked a UEnum as if it were a struct (2026-10-01)

**What happened.** While the owner was playing, a build agent ran `ue.struct {"path":"/Script/EnhancedInput.EInputMappingRebuildType"}`
to read an Enhanced Input type. The path was a UEnum; TestBench walked it as a UStruct's field list and hit an access
violation ([offset removed], "unreadable FField [value removed]"). The game died at 03:53:42; the owner lost his play since the
last save, and MO2 was left with Root Builder's deployed copies in place.

**Why it looked safe.** The probe changed nothing, so it was filed under "read-only - allowed while the owner plays". But
a reader that trusts an object's type dereferences whatever that type implies; reading can crash as surely as writing.

**Do instead.** Tools that walk reflection (ue.struct, ue.props, ue.tree) must check the object's class (UStruct/UClass
via IsA) and guard each field read, refusing anything else with an error. Until a tool is proven to refuse bad input,
treat its probes as risky while the owner plays: probe paths you have already seen it handle, and do unfamiliar
reflection work offline (the pak dumps through CUE4Parse/uejson) instead of on the live game. After a crash, do not
install into Root Builder mod folders until MO2 has closed and cleaned up (the deployed copies would be copied back).

**Fixed (TestBenchOR 3b5eb4c, primary session, 2026-10-01).** The root was `StaticFindObject<UE::UStruct>`: the template
argument is a cast, not a check, so any path came back "as a struct". Now `UEReflect::IsStruct` (a live object whose
class chain has `Struct`) gates every walk; `UEReflect::OwnFields` is the one ChildProperties walk (refuses a non-struct,
reads each FField's links under SEH after `Readable`); supers go through `SuperOf`; ue.struct finds a path untyped and
refuses a non-struct with its class chain. `tools/probe-safety.py` checks the source (no typed StaticFindObject on a
caller's path, no ChildProperties walk outside OwnFields) and, with the game up, that an enum, a package and a CDO are
refused while a ScriptStruct and a Class are read. The rule generalises: a typed lookup (`StaticFindObject<T>`, a cast
of a user-given address) is a claim about the type, never a check of it.

## An agent worktree inside a repo is a whole second copy of it - the version gate and the package gate both read it as the mod (2026-10-01)

**What happened.** Finalizing Improved Wheel Menu 1.0.0 (repo PerfectedWheelerOR), `version-gate.ps1 -Action bump` refused
with "a version location appeared since registration: .claude\worktrees\agent-...\xmake.lua set_version literal", and
after that was fixed `package-mod.ps1`'s gate failed the package on `or-reflect-selfcheck-never-latches-not-found` -
matched in `.claude\worktrees\agent-...\src\Reflect.cpp`, an old copy of the file whose real version had been fixed days
earlier (bb9a132). A sub-agent started with `isolation: worktree` leaves `.claude\worktrees\<agent>\` inside the repo:
a full checkout, excluded from git (`.git\info\exclude`) but not from the scripts' recursive file walks.

**Do instead.** Every recursive walk of a repo's files skips `\.claude\` the way it skips `.git` and `build`
(version-gate.ps1's `$EXCLUDE_RE`, package-gate.ps1's five repo-source scans - .MD f2288a9). A gate hit on a path under
`.claude\` is never the mod's own code: fix the walk, do not "fix" the source.

## Moving every package into per-game folders: what the migration and the tie-breaks taught (2026-10-01)

**What happened.** The owner asked for packages to sit under a folder named like the mod's distro folder (`<Game> -
<Mod>`) after Oblivion Remastered's HUD Position Manager 1.0.1 collided with the Skyrim mod's own "HUD Position Manager
1.0.1" (package-mod refused; with -Force it would have deleted Skyrim's release; version-gate `record` compared the
Oblivion build with Skyrim's DLL). A sub-agent moved 321 folders and zips (rules v2.8.0, .MD 835e12b). Its findings:
- A content sniffer that will MOVE data needs a stronger test than one that only labels it: `Get-PackageGame` counts any
  `scripts\` folder as Skyrim, so the Pipeline Kit (docs plus a scripts folder) read as Skyrim. The migration required a
  real Skyrim marker (SKSE, Data, Interface, meshes, textures, a FOMOD, a plugin, a DLL) and left the rest in place.
- An auto-guessed input must never break a tie: sync-nexus-distro picked the shortest matching repo name when none was
  given, and that guess silently chose Skyrim's HUD Position Manager. Only a repo the caller names may decide now; two
  games' packages without -Game is a stop ("pass -Game").
- `powershell -File script.ps1 -Only 'a','b'` passes ONE string, not an array: gate-sweep matched nothing and printed
  "every distro package clears every gate rule" after checking nothing. Use `-Command` or `&`, and treat a pass that
  touched zero items as a failure.
- The test-build install can change between a plan and its run: an expected gate hit did not happen because another
  session had installed the build meanwhile. Read the instance before predicting a gate result.
- Staging only your own hunks in a file another session has also edited: `git apply --cached` of a `--no-index` diff
  failed on a CRLF file; building the blob as HEAD plus one's own change, `git hash-object -w` and `git update-index
  --cacheinfo` worked.

## TestBench re.additem crashed the owner's game - it calls AddObjectToContainer on the UE game thread, the thread the engine's own trap refuses (2026-10-01)

**What happened.** The owner asked for a shield to test Wonger's Shield on Back. Claude called TestBench `re.additem
{form id [id removed]}` while he played. The game died at once: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION writing address [value removed] at
[offset removed], stack TestBench!REProbe::AddItem ([source reference removed]) <- GameThread::Pump
<- HookedProcessEvent (TestBench-crash-2026-10-01-07-25-59.log; the owner pasted the same report). That address is
already explained in Improved Wheel Menu's TesThread.h (2026-09-29): the remaster runs the TES simulation on a thread
of its own, and the engine's equipment / container path compares GetCurrentThreadId() with the id it stored and does a
DELIBERATE null write when they differ. re.additem runs on the UE game thread (ProcessEvent pump), so it can never be
safe - it worked once on 2026-09-29 only by luck of the path taken.

**Why it was missed.** The library had an entry naming re.additem's gaps (weapons/ammo refused) and saying console
commands go through `scripts\orcmd.py`; Claude did not grep the library for "additem" before acting in that area.

**Do instead.**
- Items into the player's inventory: `scripts\orcmd.py` (ExecuteConsoleCommand - the console queues the command for
  the TES thread), or ask the owner to type `player.additem <id> <n>` himself. Never re.additem until it is fixed.
- Any Gamebryo write (equip, unequip, add/remove item) from a plugin or tool: post it to the TES thread
  (PerfectedWheelerOR\src\TesThread.cpp pattern), never the UE game thread.
- FIXED 2026-10-02 (TestBench CHANGELOG): `src/TesThread.h/.cpp` - the main loop's per-iteration call hooked on
  first use, tasks in a shared_ptr, skipped once their caller times out; re.additem registers through
  `TesThread::Wrap`. Any NEW TestBench tool that writes Gamebryo state registers through it too.
  Proven in game 18:04 the same day: re.additem ok on the TES thread (11 ms wait), no crash.
- Before any TestBench call that WRITES game state while the owner plays: grep this index for the tool's name.

## Nexus pages answer HTTP 403 to WebFetch and curl - read them in the built-in browser pane; a comments page past 1 silently returns page 1 there too (2026-10-02)

**What happened.** A research sub-agent reading the Skyrim QuickLoot pages and classic Oblivion's Loot Menu page for a
port spec got 403 from Nexus on WebFetch and on plain curl (rule 35 notes curl with a browser User-Agent getting through
for the request hub's pages; for mod pages it did not). The built-in browser pane loaded every page.

**Do instead.** For reading a Nexus mod page's user-facing text: the built-in browser (navigate, then read
`document.body.innerText`); for a page's changelogs, click its "Changelogs" element first, then read. The Nexus API
(`secrets.md` key, nexus_files.py) remains the way to read a mod's description and file list when the page itself is not
needed. Comment paging is unreliable in the pane as elsewhere: asking for page 2 returned page 1 again - use page 1 and
the stickies, and say so in the report.

## Nexus description editor: Save stays disabled after a scripted val() unless a real keystroke lands in the editor AND the editor then loses focus; the click only focuses it when a screenshot came first (2026-10-02)

**What happened.** Adding the Pipeline Kit link to 33 live Nexus descriptions through Claude in Chrome, the edit was
set with `sceditor.instance(ta).val(new)` and made "dirty" with a real click into the editor plus Ctrl+End, space,
Backspace. On the first page Save enabled; on the next four it never did. `document.activeElement` was BODY: the
click had not focused the editor iframe. The working pages were the ones where a screenshot had been taken just before
the click (the screenshot brings the tab to the foreground; a background tab's click does not focus the iframe). Even
with focus, Save enabled only after the editor blurred - SCEditor reports its change on blur.

**Do instead.** Per page: navigate; set the value by script; take a screenshot (scale 0.1 is enough); click into the
editor; Ctrl+End, space, Backspace; then `document.activeElement.blur()`, wait ~1 s, confirm `val()` is still the
intended text and Save is enabled, click Save, and verify the PUBLIC page (`/<domain>/mods/<id>?tab=description`,
`cache:'no-store'`). The scripts can live in the tab's `sessionStorage` and run via `new Function` to keep batches small
(Nexus's CSP allows it); clear them afterwards. If the extension disconnects mid-batch, the batch keeps running in
Chrome - watch the tab URL, do not re-send until it has finished, and make every step idempotent (skip a page whose
text already has the change). Also learned: the live page text can lag the distro file by whole sections (25 of 33
pages had no "Support section" at all) - insert relative to the live text, never assume the distro's structure is live.

## Oblivion Remastered: `As<RE::TESBoundObject>()` is null for EVERY item, item names are LOC_FN_ keys, and AMF's "game language" is Windows' (2026-10-02)

**What happened.** Researching the Item Explorer port, three facts turned up that each look harmless in source:
1. CommonLibOB64's `As<T>()` / `Is<T>()` compare `T::FORMTYPE` exactly (`[source reference removed]`), and
   `TESBoundObject` declares no FORMTYPE - so `form->As<RE::TESBoundObject>()` returns null for a sword, a potion,
   anything. TestBench met it on 2026-10-01 and switched to `form->Is(<the 13 item FormTypes>)` + `reinterpret_cast`
   (`TestBenchOR\src\[source reference removed]`); Simple Loadout System's test-only `loadouts::AddItem`
   (`[source reference removed]`) still has the broken gate - the fix stayed in one mod again (the entry on AMF's freed page).
   Base-class components go through `RE::oblivion_cast<...>` (the RTTI cast), which does work.
2. `TESFullName` on OR holds a localisation KEY (`LOC_FN_Arrow1Iron`), not text. The player-facing name comes from
   [code removed] - a
   ProcessEvent call, so UE game thread only. AMF page callbacks run on the RENDER thread: resolve on the game-thread
   tick, cache UTF-8, never resolve from a page.
3. AMF OR's font atlas adds the framework language plus a "game language" that is really the Windows display
   language (`ApocryphaMenuFrameworkOR\src\[source reference removed]`), not the game's UE culture - game-supplied text in a
   script the Windows language does not cover would draw as `?`.

**Do instead.** Gate items with `Is(...)` over the explicit FormType list; resolve OR names on the game thread before
ImGui sees them; when a page shows game text, check the culture with `KismetInternationalizationLibrary` against
AMF's language line. (Found by the read-only research sub-agent for `4. plans\item-explorer-oblivion\research.md`.)

## A link to paid modding content went onto 33 Nexus pages before anyone read Nexus's anti-solicitation policy (2026-10-02)

**What happened.** Asked to add a link to every mod page, Claude added it to all 58 distro pages and all 33 live pages, verified every one - and checked nothing about whether Nexus allows it. The owner then asked for the policy to be checked. Nexus allows donation links but its Anti-Solicitation Policy forbids offering files, updates or modding-related services in exchange for money. The line came out again the same day.

**Why it looked fine.** The owner had asked for it, and the page already carried a donation link - the difference between a donation link and a link to paid modding content was not looked for.

**Do instead.** Before putting anything on a public page that points at money, read the platform's own policy for that kind of link and say what it allows before posting.

## Closing Oblivion Remastered unattended: "qqq" through orcmd.py does nothing; CloseMainWindow ends it cleanly within about a minute (2026-10-02)

**What happened.** After the Item Explorer Build 1 test, `orcmd.py "qqq"` returned ok and the game kept running for 50 s:
orcmd.py sends through UE's `KismetSystemLibrary::ExecuteConsoleCommand`, and `qqq` is an Oblivion console command, not
a UE one. `Process.CloseMainWindow()` then closed it - not within its first 45 s of polling, but before the next call a
minute later; MO2 exited by itself and Root Builder emptied the game's plugin folder (a clean exit - no leftovers to
move by hand, unlike after a crash).

**Do instead.** Close OR with CloseMainWindow and wait up to ~2 minutes before anything harsher; a force-kill leaves
Root Builder's deployed files in the game folder. Also: OR's OBSE logs are under the OneDrive-redirected Documents
(`<HOME>\OneDrive\Documents\My Games\Oblivion Remastered\OBSE\Logs`), not `<HOME>\Documents` - a wait
loop on the wrong path burned three minutes.

## The health gate said STOP and the game launched anyway - the gate and the launch were chained with ";" in one PowerShell call (2026-10-02)

**What happened.** For the Item Explorer preview probe, one PowerShell call ran `health-gate.ps1 | Select-Object -Last 1;
mo2-launch.ps1 ...`. The gate returned exit 2 (STOP - the day's share of the weekly usage was spent) and printed only its
last line, "gate cost ... exit 2 (STOP)", but `;` runs the next command regardless, so MO2 and the game started. The
game was closed again (CloseMainWindow) before any probing.

**Why it looked fine.** Two earlier launches the same day used the same chained line and the gate said GO both times,
so the chain had never been tested against a STOP; trimming the output to its last line also hid the reason.

**Do instead.** Run the gate as its own call and read its verdict before launching or building - or chain with an
explicit check ([code removed]). A STOP from usage pacing
means: finish the step in hand, save, idle until the next 15:00 slot unless the owner calls a burst day.

**Same evening, a second lesson:** CloseMainWindow sent to Oblivion Remastered about 20 s after launch - still loading,
before the main menu - left it on a black screen, "Not Responding", for over five minutes; it had to be force-ended
(MO2 then closed normally and Root Builder still cleaned the game folder). Close OR only once it has reached the main
menu or a loaded save; during the load, wait.

## Two posting snags on CCM 1.0.2: the distro sync left "release tag v1.0.1" as the link's label, and the live Nexus description indents with a non-breaking space (2026-10-02)

**What happened.** After `finalize-mod.ps1` synced the distro folder, nexus-page.txt's Source line read
`This package is v1.0.2 ([url=.../releases/tag/v1.0.2]release tag v1.0.1[/url])` - `sync-nexus-distro.ps1` rewrote the
version and the link but not the link's LABEL, and the gate's page-version row passed because the "This package is
vX.Y.Z" text matched. Then, editing the live description, three of four replacement strings matched nothing although
they read identically: the live SCEditor text indents continuation lines with U[offset removed] + space (Nexus converts a pasted
leading double space), while nexus-page.txt has two plain spaces.

**Do instead.** After a sync, grep the page for the OLD version string anywhere (`grep -n "v<old>"`) - not only the
"This package is" line - and fix sync-nexus-distro.ps1's Source rewrite to cover `release tag vX.Y.Z` labels (queued).
For a live-description edit, match with a fallback that maps "\n  " to "\n\u00a0 " (and write replacements the same
way), and refuse to set anything unless every replacement matched exactly once.

## Release screenshots taken while the owner's monitor was off came out 1024x768 (4:3) - the desktop falls back when the screen is off, and nothing in the game can render past it (2026-10-01)

**What happened.** Capturing Apocrypha Menu Framework 2.0.0 for its Nexus page with the owner at work, every in-process
capture was 1024x768 although Njordlinger Test runs at its native resolution borderless. Windows reported the desktop as 1024x768
(the monitor was off - no display to read a mode from), and the game's window follows the desktop. A 1920x1080 window
in SkyrimPrefs was clamped to the desktop; SSE Display Tweaks' Borderless + BorderlessUpscale + Resolution=1920x1080
logged "Resolution override: (1024x768)" and rewrote its own INI with that value. At 1024 wide the owner's fTextScale
1.5 also clipped the menu names. The owner's verdict on the shots: *"those pictures are at the wrong aspect ratio or
something. They don't look right. So wait until I turn the monitor back on for you to take the screenshots."*

**Do instead.** Before any capture meant for a Nexus page, read the desktop size
([code removed]). If it is not the owner's 16:9 screen, functional captures
(proof for the ledger) are fine, but the page's screenshots wait for the monitor - say so, do not post. Changing the
Windows display mode is a system setting and is not an option. Every capture-time change to the test profile (text
scale, theme, layout, Display Tweaks, SkyrimPrefs) is backed up first and restored when the game closes.

## A new release tripped Defender's cloud ML ("Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.C!ml") hours after posting - 1.9.9 passes, 2.0.1 does not, no code reason (AMF 2.0.1, 2026-10-02)

**What happened.** A Nexus user's Windows Defender quarantined Apocrypha Menu Framework 2.0.1's Line-17 DLL as
Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.C!ml the morning it was posted. VirusTotal: both 2.0.1 DLLs 1/71 (Microsoft only, B!ml / C!ml).
A same-day re-scan of the published 1.9.9 is 0/67, so Microsoft's model did not change - it scores the new file. Local
Defender with current definitions finds nothing in either DLL. pefile shows one new import (CRT round) and no new
process / memory / hook / network APIs. "!ml" is Defender's cloud machine-learning verdict on new, unsigned, rarely
seen files - the same reputation pattern Dragon's Eye Minimap hit on 2026-08-26.

**Do instead.**
- After posting a release, look up its DLL hashes on VirusTotal (`GET /api/v3/files/<sha256>` publishes nothing; the
  session scratchpad's vt_check.py does it).
- A Microsoft-only `!ml` hit is answered with a false-positive submission (microsoft.com/wdsi/filesubmission, the
  owner's Microsoft account) and a reply naming the evidence - never a code change made to dodge a classifier.
- Write-up and the ready text: `2. Mod Types\bug reports\Apocrypha Menu Framework\2026-10-02 - Defender Wacatac ml
  detection\findings.md`.
- Code signing is the durable fix (the owner's call - it costs money).

## A FOMOD's optional texture choice was never made - Security Overhaul Extra Locks drew untextured locks in Njordlinger's lockpicking screen (2026-10-02)

**What happened.** The owner saw a texture problem in the lockpicking interface. po3_LockVariations.log named the lock
swap of the moment: ImpJailDoor01 -> [asset path removed], from "Security Overhaul SKSE - Extra
Locks" (Nexus 126119). The model's textures (`[asset path removed]`)
were in no enabled mod. install-log.jsonl had recorded the install PARTIAL with 31 textures missing. The archive's FOMOD
keeps them in `textures - 1k|2k|4k` folders as Optional plugins, so install-from-nexus.py's path-suffix match
(`textures\...`) never found them. Apostasy, the list it copied, had never chosen any of them either. 11 lock models
(imperial, dawnguard, chests, farmhouse, noble chest, nordic snow, orcish, vampire) were affected.

**Fix.** Re-downloaded the main file (the archive was gone from the downloads folder) and installed `textures - 2k` as
the mod's `textures`. Verified that every texture the model names now resolves to that mod.

**Do instead.**
- When an asset looks wrong in game, read the log of the mod that swapped it (Lock Variations, Base Object Swapper,
  DBVO...) for the exact file, then resolve that file's textures against the profile's enabled mods (the session
  scratchpad's lock_tex.py does it).
- A PARTIAL line in install-log.jsonl is a lead, not noise: 127 Njordlinger mods carry one (audit queued as its own
  task).
- install-from-nexus.py should map FOMOD folder sources (`<folder source="textures - 2k" destination="textures">`)
  before declaring a file missing.

## The owner took 10 screenshots for "the new banner" and got ONE banner - a set of shots he takes for a page is a set of banners that replaces the old ones (AMF 2.0.1, 2026-10-02)

**What happened.** Asked to "take a picture or take multiple pictures for the new banner for AMF", the owner took ten 4K
Steam screenshots himself, one per feature (separators open, groups folded, settings, controls, help, the on-screen
keyboard, Chinese, the menu list, framework settings, the System-tab window). Claude made one banner from one shot,
posted it beside the six old banners, and left the old ones up. The owner, twice: *"the banners are not using the new
pictures"*, then *"use all 10 pictures that I made to replace the ones that are there. So the old banners shouldn't be
there aside from the one that has the six themes on it"*, and *"why would i take so many screenshots if i didnt want
you to use them for the banner?"*

**Do instead.**
- Screenshots the owner takes for a page are ALL used: one 1920x1080 banner per shot, each in the approved layout (the
  whole picture in a 16:9 pane, a feature line and a tagline).
- They REPLACE the page's older banners that show the same things. Back up with nexus-media-backup.py first, then
  delete. Keep only what he names (here the six-themes comparison).
- If which old images to keep is unclear, ask once - but make every shot into a banner without asking.
- Script: the session scratchpad's make_201_banners.py.
- **Nexus gallery mechanics.** Titles are set per tile from its "..." menu -> Edit title.
  - Scripted menu clicks hit a stale menu item and titled the WRONG tiles.
  - A batch of title edits typed into a dialog that had not closed, which garbled one title.
  - A coordinate click after the layout shifted opened a "Delete image" confirm (cancelled).
  - What held: screenshot before each menu click; clear the box by script; type; read the value back; save; read the
    tile caption; press Escape before the next tile.

## An MO2 plugin fitted the start-up splash "for the next start" - MO2 actually loads plugins BEFORE it reads splash.png, so the owner saw a small splash for nothing (MO2 Splash Fit, 2026-10-02)

**What happened.** MO2 Splash Fit was built in the belief that MO2 reads `splash.png` before any plugin loads. It
therefore fitted the file from the main window's monitor (`onUserInterfaceInitialized`), for the NEXT start. The
reference note said "Plugins initialise later". The owner had tested 1920x1080 and then gone back to its native resolution. On the
next start the 1536x864 splash showed in the middle of the screen. The owner: *"The image that appeared just now was a
lot smaller than the screen."* Reading `moapplication.cpp` v2.5.2 line by line shows the opposite order:
`m_plugins->loadPlugins()` is at line 272 and `MOSplash splash(...)` at line 316, in the same `doOneRun()`. A first fix
looked for the live `QSplashScreen` in `init()` and found none, because it does not exist yet. That is what exposed the
order.

**Do instead.**
- Before designing around WHEN MO2 does something, read the order of the calls in the function itself, not a summary.
  Write the line numbers into the plugin's MO2-REFERENCE.md.
- In MO2 2.5.x a plugin's `init()` runs before the splash, before OrganizerCore setup and before the main window. A file
  MO2 reads at start-up (`splash.png`) can be prepared in `init()` for the SAME start.
- MO2 centres the splash on `[Geometry] MainWindow_monitor` from `ModOrganizer.ini` (an index into
  `QGuiApplication::screens()`, else primary; settings.cpp `centerOnMainWindowMonitor`). Read that key in `init()`;
  there is no window yet.
- A "written already, skip" state file must also check the real file. MO2 recreates a missing `splash.png` from the
  game plugin, and an author may replace it.

## A live Nexus page carried ANOTHER mod's description - Civil War Starts showed the Skyrim AMF text, and an anchored-replace check said 'no match' instead of saying why (2026-10-02)

**Symptom.** Updating Alternate Perspective Civil War Starts' description for 1.0.6, none of the four anchored
replacements matched, the editor held 23,783 characters, and its version line read "v1.8.7". The first check of the
public page said the text was fine - it had parsed the wrong element (the first of several selectors matched the "About
this mod" box, not `.mod_description_container`).

**What it was.** The stored and published description of 192064 WAS the Skyrim Apocrypha Menu Framework's, from an
earlier session's edit. Nothing in the pipeline compared a live description with its own page.

**The checks, now standard.** (1) Before an anchored edit, read the live text's first sentence and compare it with
the distro `nexus-page.txt`; a 0-match on every anchor means the wrong text, not a changed one. (2) Read the public
description from `.mod_description_container` only. (3) After a session that edits descriptions, sweep every page:
fetch `/<domain>/mods/<id>?tab=description`, take the container's opening, and set it beside the page title (done
2026-10-02 for all 35 pages - only 192064 was wrong). The fix was the whole distro page text set through SCEditor
`val()` and saved; the AMF text stays in AMF's own distro folder.

## Oblivion Remastered stops reading XInput when no controller is connected - an iwm.pad test needs WM_DEVICECHANGE, and its end looks like the owner pressing buttons (2026-10-02)

**Symptom.** Testing Improved Wheel Menu 1.0.1 with TestBench `iwm.pad` steps: after one tap worked, every later
`iwm.pad state` answered "the game thread did not answer in 3 s (no controller reads)", queued steps never ran, and
TestBench's own `pad` counter stayed 0. Earlier the same run, the wheel closed 1.5 s after the tap with no `pad:` line and
the Character / system menu opened by itself - read at the time as the owner at the controls.

**What it was.** With no physical controller, Unreal's XInput interface stops polling a disconnected pad and polls
again only after a device-change notification. A plugin's injected test step makes the pad read as connected while it
runs; when the queue ends, the pad reads disconnected, the game releases every button (the latched wheel closes) and
opens its pause/system menu for the lost controller. Nobody else was pressing anything.

**How to test from now on.** Queue the whole sequence in ONE `iwm.pad press` (with a trailing idle step), then post
`WM_DEVICECHANGE` ([value removed], wParam 7 = DBT_DEVNODES_CHANGED) to the game window so it polls; read the log after. Expect
the system menu when the queue ends - close it with the TestBench `key` tool (Escape). A Steam Deck's slow wheel open
is reproduced with the console's `t.MaxFPS 20` (restore with `t.MaxFPS 0`). Loading a save: `key` Enter at the title,
Enter on Continue, Enter on the confirmation (the owner, 2026-10-02).

## Every frame capture came back black - AMF's in-process capture and a gamevideo clip - while the overlay was drawing on screen; it was the AMD driver, not the page (2026-10-03)

**Symptom.** Testing the AMF SDK example page in Skyrim: `amf.process op=capture` wrote its native resolution PNGs whose every pixel
was (0,0,0), three times; a `gamevideo.py record` clip came out 48 bytes (ffmpeg ddagrab + h264_amf), and the AMD
software raised its own bug-report prompt. The owner, watching the screen: "I saw AMF pop up over the main menu" and
"AMD just said that there is a bug report. So it looks like your screenshot issue is actually an AMD driver issue."
`mcp__gamelink__see` returned a picture, but it is the game's frame from BEFORE AMF's Present hook (entry 2280), so no
overlay can appear in it.

**What went wrong in the reasoning.** A black capture was first read as "the page did not draw" or "the monitor is off".
An all-zero image is a capture failure, not a page result - a real frame always has some non-zero pixels.

**Do instead.** Check `PIL.Image.getextrema()` on any capture before reading it; all zeros = the capture path failed.
**2026-10-08 (the owner: "when you get a black screenshot, you try the other screenshot methods because there are
multiple"):** go to the next method first - `scripts\desktop-grab.ps1` (DPI-aware GDI grab of the screen) showed the FLICK
page with AMF's overlay at once while three in-process captures were black; the full order is in PREFLIGHT. Only when
every method fails, prove drawing from data instead: a one-time log line in the drawing code (the SDK example logs its first draw and
whether it shared the framework's ImGui), `amf.menu op=state`, and the owner's eyes when he is at the screen. Stop any
ffmpeg left running after a failed clip (`gamevideo.py stop`, then prockill ffmpeg).

## vcpkg's stock imgui port at the usual baseline is 1.90.2 - AMF pins 1.90.8 through its own overlay port, and a consumer built without it was rightly refused (2026-10-03)

**Symptom.** The Skyrim AMF SDK example (vcpkg.json with imgui + docking-experimental at baseline 8d3649ba, the same
baseline as AMF) logged "Dear ImGui not shared, drawing nothing": AMF::UseFrameworkImGui() refused it.

**Cause.** The baseline's imgui port is 1.90.2. AMF does not take imgui from the baseline - `cmake/ports/imgui` (and
`cmake/ports-17/imgui`) is an overlay port pinning 1.90.8 docking. The header comment I had written ("the framework's own
baseline gives 1.90.8") was wrong; the version check caught it, which is what it is for.

**Do instead.** Before claiming which version a vcpkg dependency resolves to, read
`build/<preset>/vcpkg_installed/<triplet>/include/<lib>.h` of the project that already builds, and look for an overlay in
`cmake/ports*`. The SDK example now ships AMF's imgui overlay port, and AMF.h says so.

## esp-audit failed DBReV.esp on a quest's ANAM - in QUST, ANAM is the next alias ID, a counter, not a FormID (2026-10-03)

**Symptom.** plugin-gate refused to launch with Dragonborn ReVoiced 1.5.2 installed: "QUST [id removed]: ANAM points at
[id removed], which no record in this file defines" (a 0-master ESPFE).

**Cause.** esp-audit's FORMID_SLOTS treats every ANAM as a reference. In QUST records ANAM is "next alias ID" (uint32).

**Fix.** esp-audit.py: `NOT_REFS = {(b"QUST", b"ANAM")}` exempts (record, subrecord) pairs that share a reference
signature but hold none (backup esp-audit.py.bak-qust-anam-20261003). When the gate fails on another author's plugin
that loads fine for thousands of users, check the subrecord's meaning in THAT record type before believing the gate.

## A consumer window's BlockUserInput cannot decide who gets the input - the stock SMF header defaults it to true, so a play-time overlay would have locked the player out (AMF 2.0.4, 2026-10-03)

**Symptom.** AMF 2.0.4's first build gave a mod's window the cursor and input when it was open with BlockUserInput
set (RaceMenu Atelier works only that way). StepUpOnto SKSE's play-time "NPC Perf" overlay also has BlockUserInput
true - the stock header's `AddWindow(render, doesWindowPauseGame = true)` default - so with it shown, all game input
went to ImGui during ordinary play.

**Fix.** The gate also requires that the window drew, last frame, at least one top-level ImGui window WITHOUT
`ImGuiWindowFlags_NoMouseInputs` (probe: `amf.menu op=state` consumerWindows[].submitted). A pure display overlay
never takes the input. StepUpOnto's overlay does accept the mouse, so it takes the input while shown - the owner:
"that's nothing new for an overlay menu". Test any input-routing change with every AddWindow mod the list has open, not
only the one in the bug report.

## Releasing a COM object another module may still hold a raw pointer to - AAOS freed XAudio2 engines Dragonborn ReVoiced kept, and its next line crashed (2026-10-03)

**Symptom.** phbd01: crash switching headphones to speakers; ntdll `inc [operand removed]` under XAudio2_7[value removed]
(CX2Engine::CreateSourceVoice taking a deleted critical section) under AutoAudioOutputSwitch.dll HookCreateSource,
called by [offset removed] from the Papyrus thread.

**Cause.** AAOS held the game's old engine across a switch and released it after the rebuild; DBReV had cached the
engine pointer at startup without a reference. Reproduced exactly in game: DBReV's first line after any switch calls the
OLD engine from [offset removed].

**Fix (1.0.5).** Engines the game lets go are retired - referenced for the rest of the session, stopped - and calls on
them from other threads are refused with XAUDIO2_E_INVALID_CALL; DBReV then hands the line to the game's playback.
DevBench `aaos.control op=foreigncall` reproduces the pattern without DBReV. **Rule:** when a hook makes you the owner of
an object other modules can see (a shared vtable, a game global), assume someone kept a raw pointer: retire, never
