free, and log which modules call it.

## The owner's PC froze during a 1.7.104 boot proof - a startup message box, a spinning TextInputHost and an AMD driver fault together; the card came back on code 31 after the hard reset (2026-10-03)

**Symptom.** "The computer seems frozen", then "I can't even move the mouse to close the AAOS error screen". The boot
proof had launched Steam 1.7.104 Test; the 1.7 test mod still held the pre-rename ApocryphaAutoAudioOutputSwitch.dll, so
AAOS 1.0.4+'s guard raised its modal message box during plugin load and the game sat behind it (wj-boot-proof had to
force-close it). At the same time TextInputHost.exe was spinning one core (2.9 s CPU per 3 s; 35 h accumulated) and,
on the next launch, MO2 crashed inside atio6axx.dll (AMD's OpenGL driver), the Snipping Tool crashed and Game Bar hung.
After the owner's hard reset the GPU came up with device error 31 (driver not loaded); a second normal restart
cleared it.

**Do instead.** Before a boot proof, list the test mod's folder for an old-named DLL (an install over an old folder
adds files, it does not remove them) - a guard's message box at load looks exactly like a hang. If the owner reports a
freeze: check for a spinning TextInputHost (restart it - prockill, Windows relaunches it), then the System/Application
logs for AMD driver faults, and stop launching anything until `Get-PnpDevice -Class Display` shows the card OK. A
device error code (31/43) is fixed by the owner (restart, then a driver reinstall), never by Claude.

## A locked Windows session cannot be brought to the front - no screenshot, no SendInput; posting F12 to the game window does not trigger Steam's screenshot (2026-10-03)

**Symptom.** With the owner at work, an Oblivion test needed the page on screen: AppActivate returned true but the
foreground stayed ShellExperienceHost (the lock screen), sendkey.py refused ("the game is not the window in front"),
and TestBench `key` F12 (a posted WM_KEYDOWN) produced no Steam screenshot.

**Do instead.** While the session is locked, test only through DevBench/TestBench tools that act inside the process
(state reads, `set` ops, forced states such as HPM's forceCombat) and leave anything that needs eyes or real input -
slider feel, layout, wrapping - for when the owner is back; say so in the changelog's Tested section rather than
calling the build working.

## Nexus's new edit form keeps Save disabled after a scripted description change - SCEditor's insert('') marks it changed, even in a hidden tab (2026-10-03)

**Symptom.** On games/<game>/mods/<id>/edit/general the description is SCEditor; `sceditor.instance(ta).val(text)` changes
the text but both Save buttons stay disabled. A real keystroke typed into the editor enables Save, but keystrokes need
the tab visible and the editor focused - with the PC locked (`document.visibilityState` "hidden") they never arrive,
and clicking the editor by a find() ref once navigated the tab away to the homepage, losing the unsaved edit.

**Do instead.** `inst.val(newText)`, then `inst.insert('')` (fires the editor's value-changed path, which the form
listens to), `inst.updateOriginal()`, check [code removed], then click the enabled Save by
script. Works with the tab hidden. Re-open the edit page and compare the saved text before calling it done. Not every time: on 2026-10-03 (AMF 2.0.6) insert('') left Save
disabled, and inserting text through inst.insert() put stray markup and a leading newline into the description, which then
had to be stripped by hand. What enabled Save was ONE real keystroke from the Chrome computer tool - click inside the editor,
`End space BackSpace` - which worked although document.visibilityState read "hidden" (screenshot the tab first: if it
captures, it takes keys). Never insert() visible text to provoke the form; check val() is byte-identical before Save. Patch
by anchors (each checked to occur exactly once) rather than pasting a whole page, unless the live page is behind the
distro by more than the anchors cover (AAOS's live page was still on 1.0.3's text).

**2026-10-08 (AMF 2.1.6, tab in the BACKGROUND behind the game):** the React-field path alone (`val(TEXT)`, then the
textarea fiber's `onChange(TEXT)` / `onBlur()`) left Save enabled and the save request returned 200 - but it saved only the
version field; the reopened page still held the old description. What saved it, still in the background: `inst.val(TEXT)`,
`inst.insert('')`, `inst.updateOriginal()`, THEN the fiber's `onChange(TEXT)` and `onBlur()`, then the Save button by script.
Wrap `fetch` first and read the `/mods/save` request body (`includes('<a phrase only the new text has>')`) - it tells you
before the reopen whether the description went out. SCEditor drops one newline before a `[/spoiler]`; harmless.
A save can come back **520** (Cloudflare) and store nothing - the same session's next save of the same text, done the
same way, came back 200 and stuck. Always reopen and check; on a 520 just repeat the save.

## A script clicked the last menu button of the WHOLE gallery and deleted the new banner instead of the old one (Nexus media editor, 2026-10-03)

**Symptom.** Replacing Item Explorer's main banner by script: the "card" for the old image was found by walking up
from its <img> to the first ancestor with a button and "by " in its text - which was the container of every card, so
`[...card.querySelectorAll('button')].pop()` opened the LAST card's menu (the just-uploaded banner) and Delete removed
it. Then a second "Set as thumbnail" click hit a disabled item from a menu left open on another card.

**Do instead.** Scope a card as the nearest ancestor that contains exactly ONE gallery image; abort if none. Pick menu
items that are enabled and nearest to the button just clicked. Before a Delete, assert the target card is not the
thumbnail and that the new image IS; after it, list the gallery to confirm what remains. Back up the page's images
first (nexus-media-backup.py) - that is what made this mistake recoverable.

## install-test-build put an Oblivion Remastered package BESIDE the mod folder's Root\ - the game would have kept loading the old DLL (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** HUD Position Manager for Oblivion Remastered 1.0.2: the package (OblivionRemastered\Binaries\... at
its top) was installed with install-test-build.py into "test HUD Position Manager", a Root Builder mod folder whose
files live under Root\. The script copied the tree to the folder's top level and reported "every package-owned file
matches" - true of the copy it made - while Root\...\HUDPositionManager.dll stayed the pre-bump build. The package
gate caught it ("installed-build-is-the-package"); a hash of the Root\ DLL showed the mismatch.

**Do instead.** install-test-build.py now installs into Root\ when the mod folder has Root\ and the package does not
(--no-root to opt out), and prints that it did. After any OR install, hash the DLL under Root\ against the package
before launching.

## A race-type row in RaceMenu's list is not always a race - Apprentice files classes and traits there, and a replacement UI that calls ChangeRace on them changes the race (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** The owner: Apprentice - A Class Overhaul's classes showed in RaceMenu Atelier "mixed with the race
category". Reading RaceMenu's lists live (TestBench `menu action=gfx`, added for this): Apprentice appends one
`type 1` (race) entry per class and trait to `racePanel.itemList.entryList`, filed under its own categories
(`filterFlag` 2^29 classes, 2^30 traits; races are 2), with `isClass` / `isTrait`, the key in `callbackName`, and its
class NUMBER in `raceID`. It replaces the panels' `onItemPress` to record a pick. Atelier drew every type-1 entry in
one race grid and called `ChangeRace(raceID)` itself - choosing "Agent" (raceID 0) would have made the character an
Argonian and recorded no class.

**Do instead.** In any UI that replaces RaceMenu's: a race-type entry whose filterFlag lacks the Race bit belongs to
the category it is filed under, and a click on it goes through the movie's own `onItemPress({index, entry})` -
whatever mod owns that handler records the pick - never a direct `ChangeRace`. Read the movie (TestBench
`menu action=gfx name="RaceSex Menu" path=...`) before reasoning about what a mod injects.

## TestBench could not read a menu's Scaleform data - `menu action=gfx` added rather than a one-off dump in the mod under test (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** Working out what Apprentice injects into RaceMenu needed the live entryList/categoryList.
TestBench's `menu` tool could only list, open, close and answer message boxes.

**Do instead.** `menu action=gfx name=<open menu> path=<AS path>` (TestBench 3f28748): any variable of an open
menu's movie as JSON - depth (default 2, max 6), from/count to page an array, fields to keep only some members.
Use it for every SWF-backed menu question (RaceMenu, SkyUI, HUD) instead of reasoning from source or dumping
from the mod being built (rule 64's amendment).

## The game's translation table (BSScaleformTranslator) cannot be read through CommonLib on 1.5.97 - a find() misses every key and iterating it crashed the game; read the mod's own Interface\Translations file (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** AMF's experimental MCM Helper loader (branch exp/mcm-loader) translated `$keys` through the
game's own table, [code removed].

1. The first try built a `BSFixedStringW` key and called `find()`. Every key missed: TrueHUD's
   `$TrueHUD_EnableActorInfoBars_OptionText` drew raw, though TrueHUD_english.txt was loaded.
2. The second try iterated the map to copy it. It read `[value removed]` and crashed the game the moment the page
   drew (crash-2026-10-04-08-59-07.log, `[source reference removed]`).

CommonLibSSE-NG 3.7's layout of that map does not match this runtime.

**Do instead.** Read the file the game itself loads for a plugin: `Interface\Translations\<plugin>_<language>.txt`.
- The format is UTF-16LE with a BOM, one `$KEY<TAB>text` per line.
- Read it with `RE::BSResourceNiBinaryStream`, so a BSA-packed file is found too. Read it once at load on the main
  thread, with English as the fallback.
- The language comes from the game's `sLanguage`.

A file format other mods depend on is a stable contract; a reverse-engineered engine struct is not. A struct read that
"just misses" (step 1) is the warning sign that the layout is wrong, not that the data is absent.

## An MCM Helper mod may apply its settings ONLY in OnConfigClose - writing the value and sending OnSettingChange saves it but the mod ignores it until the next load (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** The experimental AMF MCM loader wrote TrueHUD settings through `MCM.SetModSettingBool` and then
sent `OnSettingChange(id)`, which is what MCM Helper's own menu sends per control.
- The value reached MCM Helper's store; `MCM.GetModSettingBool` followed it.
- TrueHUD did nothing.

Its script (and those of True Directional Movement and Precision, all by ersh1) is `Event OnConfigClose() native`.
The DLL re-reads every setting when SkyUI's menu closes, not per setting.

**Do instead.** Mirror SkyUI's lifecycle, not just MCM Helper's per-control event:
- `OnConfigOpen` when a mod's page is entered;
- `OnConfigClose` when it is left or the menu closes;
- `OnSettingChange` for each change;
- a scripted change with no page open plays the whole visit (open, change, close).

**Verify by an effect, not a proxy.** A log-line counter (TrueHUD's playerWidget resolve errors) stayed flat even
after the fix. What settled it was TrueHUD's Recent Loot popup:
- off through AMF, then `player.additem f 111` - no popup;
- on, then `additem 222` - "Septim (222) RECEIVED".

The DevBench `papyrus` tool (`call MCM.GetModSettingBool`) reads MCM Helper's live store directly.

## A Papyrus call dispatched from native code is NOT upcast - pass a script object typed as the PARAMETER's script, or the VM refuses the call and returns None (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** The experimental AMF MCM loader called SkyUI's `SKI_ConfigManager.UnregisterMod(SKI_ConfigBase)` and
`RegisterMod(SKI_ConfigBase, string)` with each mod's config script object.

- Every call came back `None`, and SkyUI's list did not change. Three argument shapes failed the same way:
  1. a bare `Variable::SetObject(obj)`;
  2. the object typed as its own script (`obj->GetTypeInfo()->GetRawType()`);
  3. the quest form packed by `PackValue`.
- A no-argument call on the same object (`GetVersion`) returned 4, so the call path itself worked.
- Only Papyrus.0.log (turned on for one run) named the cause: `RegisterMod(SKI_ConfigBase a_menu,string a_modName)
  received incompatible arguments! Received types (TrueHUD_MCM,string) instead!`.

Compiled Papyrus would upcast TrueHUD_MCM to SKI_ConfigBase; a native dispatch does not.

**Do instead.**
- Type the argument as the parameter's script: `vm->GetScriptObjectType("SKI_ConfigBase", info)` then
  `var.SetObject(obj, info->GetRawType())`. That passed.
- Read every result through a callback: `None` means the VM refused the call.
- When a native Papyrus call "does nothing", turn on `[Papyrus] bEnableLogging=1` for one run before guessing again. The
  VM writes the exact refusal there. Back the profile INI up first and restore it after.

## SkyUI's config manager ignores RegisterMod/UnregisterMod while its Journal is open - they return -2 in the BUSY state (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** `SKI_ConfigManager` enters `state BUSY` from `OnMenuOpen` to `OnMenuClose` of the Journal. In that
state `RegisterMod` and `UnregisterMod` `return -2` and change nothing. A hide switch flipped from AMF while it was opened
from the Journal's System row would silently do nothing.

**Do instead.**
- Read the result. -2 means busy: retry every few seconds until it answers.
- Count a mod as hidden only when SkyUI returns a slot (>= 0) or -1 (not in the list).
- Verify from the Journal's own movie (`menu action=gfx`, `_root.ConfigPanelFader.configPanel._modList._entryList`),
  not from your own counter. The counter said 33 hidden while SkyUI still listed all 83.

**Related, the clean way to keep a mod out of SkyUI's list.** `UnregisterMod(config)` empties the slot but leaves the
config's `_configManager` set. `SKI_ConfigBase.OnConfigManagerReady` returns early when [code removed], so
the mod never re-registers. The manager re-announces itself every 5 s, then every 30 s, and still there is no "MCM:
Registered N new menu(s)" notification. `RegisterMod` puts it back.

## SkyUI's MCM pages never load in Njordlinger Test - Papyrus does not run while the Journal is open there, with or without our code (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** During the AMF phase-3 test, SkyUI's Mod Configuration list opened (83 mods), but choosing a mod never
filled its page list. `_root.ConfigPanelFader.configPanel._subList._entryList` stayed at `$size 0` for over a minute.
With the Journal open, a DevBench `papyrus call Game.GetGameSettingFloat` timed out ("VM stalled?"). The same call answered
at once after the Journal closed, and our own queued `OpenConfig`/`SetPage` finished at that moment too. The first suspect
was our new `UI.InvokeStringA` forwarder. Two controls cleared it:
1. The forwarder was taken out live: the stall was the same.
2. A fresh launch with `bLoadSkyUIScriptMenus=0`, so the forwarder was never installed: the stall was the same.

The owner, the same day: MCM menus are "so unreliable in game", which is why he wants them as AMF pages.

**Do instead.**
- Before blaming a change for a SkyUI MCM failure in this list, run the same steps with the change never installed, not
  only removed live. A live removal cannot clear a VM that is already stuck.
- The SkyUI inventory does the same (SLS test, 2026-10-04): a Papyrus `EquipItem` sent while it was open timed out,
  and nothing was equipped once it closed. Equip with the menu closed, then reopen it.
- Drive Papyrus-backed tests with the Journal CLOSED. AMF's pages work there because AMF does not stop Papyrus. A test
  that needs SkyUI's own MCM in Njordlinger cannot pass until the Journal stall itself is found.

## Giving SkyUI's MCM list "back" with RegisterMod for every config adds menus that were never there and undoes other mods' hiding - give back only what you hid (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** AMF's after-load pass, with its hide switch off, sent `SKI_ConfigManager.RegisterMod` for every config it
knew. The aim was to recover menus hidden in an earlier session. Honed Metal's config had `_configManager` set but was not
in SkyUI's list, and the call ADDED it (result 1). Every later call returned -1. `RegisterMod` returns -1 when
`_configCount >= 128`, and that check comes BEFORE the "already registered" check, so -1 does not mean "not there". The
same pass would also re-add entries that MenuMaid2 hides through the same `UnregisterMod`.

**Do instead.** Keep a ledger of what AMF itself unregistered (a slot >= 0 came back), outside the save:
`SKSE\Plugins\ApocryphaMenuFramework\McmHiddenInSkyUI.txt`. Send `RegisterMod` only for ledger entries. Remove a ledger
entry only when the give-back returns a slot. A -1 on give-back means SkyUI's list is full: keep the entry and warn.

## CommonLib NG's Actor::GetGoldAmount faults on SE 1.5.97 every time, not only during loading - count the gold in InventoryChanges yourself (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** HUD Position Manager 54c3053 read the player's gold for a new widget through
`PlayerCharacter::GetGoldAmount()`. It crashed reading `[operand removed]` (rcx [value removed]) in CommonLib [source reference removed], the
`IsGold()` check inside `GetInventory`. The first crash came on the load screen, and this entry first blamed a load race:
the HUD advancing before the save's inventory was rebuilt. **That was only half right.** Main Agent's re-run of the same
SE build faulted again 2 s AFTER kPostLoadGame (crash-2026-10-04-12-12-14) with the SAME [value removed] pointer. Counting the
gold entries of `player->GetInventoryChanges()->entryList` directly, behind an SEH guard, read 72 with no fault, matching
STB's gold widget. So the garbage comes from GetInventory's other half, the base-container (TESContainer) walk. A pointer
that is the same on every run is a layout mismatch between CommonLib NG 3.7 and SE 1.5.97, not a timing problem.

**Do instead.**
- On SE 1.5.97 builds, do not call `Actor::GetGoldAmount` / `GetInventory`. Count the gold yourself from
  `GetInventoryChanges()->entryList` (the gold form is [value removed]), behind an SEH guard.
- Keep the load gate as a second guard: never read a save-rebuilt structure from a per-frame HUD hook before
  kPostLoadGame / kNewGame, or while "Loading Menu" is open.
- **The general lesson:** when the same bad pointer comes back on every run, suspect a struct layout before suspecting
  timing. Re-run once after the timing you suspect has passed, before writing the cause down.
- To map crash offsets to lines: `.MD\scripts\symbolize-crash.py <dll> <offset>...`, with the DLL's PDB beside it.

## A switch that gives SkyUI its MCM menus back gave nothing back - the ledger trusted RegisterMod/UnregisterMod results that came back None (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** AMF's "take those mods out of SkyUI's list" kept a ledger of the menus it hid, so that turning the
feature off would give exactly those back. An entry was written only when UnregisterMod returned a slot (>= 0). In
Njordlinger, every result of an 84-call pass came back None ("SkyUI call returned no int, none=true"), so the ledger
stayed empty. Switching the feature off then sent 0 RegisterMod calls: the menus stayed out of SkyUI, which is the exact
failure the owner had asked to be checked. On a stripped-down profile the same calls returned real slots. The result
depends on the list, so it is not a contract.

> **Amended later the same day: the cause in Njordlinger was MCM Unlocked (Nexus 180186, v2.0.1), not the size of the
> list.** Its `[asset name removed]` wins in Njordlinger Test and has NO `_modConfigs` / `_modNames` arrays: the
> registry lives in its DLL, behind GetConfigBase / GetConfigCount / GetModIDFromConfigID / GetModNameFromModID. Reading
> `_modConfigs` therefore finds nothing on such a list. The "judge from `_modConfigs`" rule below is right only for
> stock SkyUI; under MCM Unlocked, membership has to be read through its natives. MCM Helper also handles a third
> layout ("Barzing": `_MainMenu` plus `_modConfigsP<n>`). Before reading a manager's arrays, check which manager script
> actually wins in the list.
>
> **And Menu Maid 2 (found by Main Agent the same night, with MCM Unlocked off):** its loose `[asset name removed]`
> wins in Njordlinger. It HAS a `_modConfigs` array, so it passes for stock SkyUI. But it keeps the real list in its
> DLL (`MenuMaid2.PluginsAmount()` = 82) and copies it into `_modConfigs` only when the Journal opens. Read at any
> other time, the array is empty, so AMF's hide switch takes nothing out. **The presence of an array does not prove
> the array is live.** Detect the manager by its own script (`MenuMaid2`, `MCMUnlocked`) before trusting its arrays.

Three more ways to the same failure were found while fixing it:
- The script-menu give-back skipped every target while its own switch was off.
- The after-load pass returned early when both loaders were off.
- An MCM Helper menu could not be found once its loader had been off since the game started.

**Do instead.**
- Record the intent BEFORE the call: a menu you are about to take out is yours to give back.
- Judge every outcome from SkyUI's own `SKI_ConfigManager._modConfigs` (compare the object pointers). A ledger entry
  leaves only when the array shows the menu back.
- The give-back path must work with every switch off, after any load, and from the ledger line alone.
- Prove it with the full round trip on a minimal profile: hide, save, reload, switch off, then read SkyUI's own array
  (DevBench `amf.mcm op=skyuilist`). Repeat once with the switch turned off in the INI while the game is closed.
- An empty `_modConfigs` slot is an object-typed None that `Variable::IsNoneObject()` does not report. Test
  `GetObject()` for null instead.


## ImGui's Win32 backend sizes the display from the game WINDOW, but the overlay draws on the swap chain's IMAGE - they differ whenever the game renders smaller than its window (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** Soulsthat (2560x1440) reported AMF's menu clipping at the right and bottom, the right side before the
left, and tooltips cut off near the edge. ImGui_ImplWin32_NewFrame sets io.DisplaySize from GetClientRect; everything
ImGui draws lands 1:1 on the back buffer. With a lower render resolution scaled up in a borderless window (SSE Display
Tweaks BorderlessUpscale, Auto Resolution's PreSSEDisplayTweaks fRatio, an upscaler) the window is bigger than the image,
so "the centre of the screen" sat right of and below the image's centre and every clamp to the display ran past the
image. Reproduced in Njordlinger with Auto Resolution fRatio 0.5 (a 1600x900 image in a its native resolution window); our own
desktop never shows it because there the two are equal. Note: Auto Resolution REWRITES SSEDisplayTweaks.ini's Resolution
at every start, so a test has to change fRatio, not that INI.

**Do instead.** In any ImGui overlay on the game's swap chain, set io.DisplaySize from IDXGISwapChain::GetDesc's
BufferDesc after the Win32 NewFrame, and log once when it differs from the window. Mouse input that comes from window
coordinates must then be scaled by image/window as well (AMF's cursor is its own, accumulated deltas, so it needed no
scaling). Fixed in AMF main 3584465.


## A plugin's globals cannot be found by editor ID on SE 1.5.97 - look them up by form ID in their plugin, and first check the plugin actually LOADED (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** HPM's Survival Mode bars read the need globals (Survival_HungerNeedValue ...) with
TESForm::LookupByEditorID: every lookup came back empty. Switching to TESDataHandler::LookupForm(local id,
"ccQDRSSE001-SurvivalMode.esl") also came back empty - and so did Papyrus GetFormFromFile and GetLightModByName,
because in the HPM Minimal profile the plugin had never loaded: GetLightModCount was 2 (SkyUI_SE.esp and
TestBench.esp, both ESL-flagged .esp files) with ccqdrsse001-survivalmode.esl and _ResourcePack.esl ticked in
plugins.txt. Two causes stacked: the editor-ID map does not hold these forms on 1.5.97, and the plugin was absent.

**Do instead.** Read a plugin's globals by form ID in the plugin (take the local ids from the file itself - a GLOB
walk of the .esl gives EDID, form ID and default value in seconds). Before blaming the lookup, ask the running game
whether the plugin is there: Papyrus Game.GetLightModCount / GetLightModName(i) / GetLightModByName for a light
plugin, GetModByName for a full one. A ticked line in plugins.txt is not a loaded plugin.

## gamewatch.ps1 start launches a background frame RECORDER - against the owner's standing ban on continuous capture (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** Following PREFLIGHT's in-game line ("level 1 gamewatch.ps1 start"), the HPM test started
gamewatch, which printed "recorder started ... at 2 fps". The owner had banned background game-screen recording on
2026-09-29 (the no-background-game-screen-recording memory); the preflight line predates that and was never changed.
It was stopped (gamewatch.ps1 stop) within a minute.

**Do instead.** For an in-game look, take single frames on request: gamelink `see` / `step`, or `gamewatch.ps1 snap`.
Never `gamewatch.ps1 start`. A standing ban recorded in memory outranks an older procedure line - and the procedure
line is corrected the same day (PREFLIGHT amended 2026-10-04).

## A fade multiplier on a clip whose owner TWEENS its own alpha compounds to 0 - set that clip's alpha outright instead (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** HPM's fade engine follows each clip's own alpha as the base and writes base x multiplier. On the
vanilla sneak eye (HUDMovieBaseInstance.StealthMeterInstance) the fader read 0.625 while sneaking, yet the clip's
_alpha read 0. The HUD's own script fades the eye by reading _alpha back and stepping it each frame: every frame it
started from our already-multiplied value, so base x 0.625 was taken again and again until it reached 0. Static clips
(the compass, the crosshair) followed the multiplier exactly.

**Do instead.** On a clip whose owner animates its alpha by read-modify-write, take "full control" while you manage
it: write an absolute alpha (100 x the fade), and give the clip back to the owner (stop writing) when your mode does
not apply - HPM's eye mode holds it only while the player sneaks. A multiplier is safe only on clips whose owner writes
absolute values or none. When a faded element reads lower than the fader says, suspect a tween before the maths.

## A TestBench papyrus call that "returned null" had been REFUSED - a whole number sent to a Float parameter is an Int, and native dispatch does not convert it (2026-10-04)

**What happened.** In HPM Minimal, TestBench's `papyrus` tool ran `Actor.DamageActorValue("Health", 40)` and
`Form.SendModEvent("HPM_SetElementHidden", "Compass", 1)`. Both answered `{"called":true,"returned":null}`, and neither
did anything: health stayed at 100, and HPM's ModEvent sink (which logged SkyUI's events) never saw the event. In the
same session AddItem, EquipItem, GetActorValue and GetItemCount worked through the same tool.

**Cause.** TestBench built every argument from its JSON shape: [bytes removed] and `1` became Int Variables. `afDamage` and
`afNumArg` are declared Float. Compiled Papyrus would convert an int literal; a native `DispatchMethodCall` does not. The
VM refused the call, but its callback still fired with an untyped None, which the tool reported as a normal void
result. Papyrus.0.log (logging on for that run) named it at the same seconds as TestBench.log's invocations:
`Type mismatch for argument 2.` / `Type mismatch for argument 3.`, both with an empty stack. Every call that worked took
only Int / Bool / String / Form arguments. Same family as the upcast entry above (native dispatch converts nothing).

**Why it was convincing.** `called: true` with `returned: null` is exactly what a void function returns, so a refused
call and a successful one looked identical. The other calls through the same tool worked, so the tool looked sound.

**Fixed in TestBench** (`13. testbench\TestBench\src\Papyrus.cpp`, commit 3d000b6): JSON numbers are built as the
DECLARED parameter type (whole numbers into Float, whole floats into Int, 0/1 into Bool, ints into a declared Float[]).
Every argument and the argument count are checked against the function before dispatch, so a mismatch fails 400 with
the argument named. The response carries `returnType`, plus a warning when a non-void function comes back untyped None.
Proven in HPM Minimal: DamageActorValue 40 -> health 100 -> 60.25; 0.35 still passes unchanged; SendModEvent ... 1 hid
the compass (HPM logged the event) and 0 gave it back; fractional-for-Int, number-for-String and too-many-args each fail
400 by name.

**Do instead.** Read `called: true, returned: null` from a native dispatch as "maybe refused", not "done": check the
effect, or turn on `[Papyrus] bEnableLogging=1` for one run. The VM writes the refusal there and nowhere else. A tool
that builds Papyrus arguments must type them from the function's declared parameters, not from the caller's literals.

## `Variable::IsNoneObject()` tests for a None TYPE, not a None value - an object variable set to None reads as holding an object (2026-10-04, AMF 2.0.9, Soulsthat)

**What happened.** AMF's script-MCM discovery took a SkyUI config only when `_configManager` passed
`IsObject() && !IsNoneObject()`. Soulsthat's list was missing 16 script menus (CBBE 3BA, moreHUD, T.N.G., Wyrmstooth ...).
The first fix accepted a config whose `_initialized` was true, and added a "registered" flag built from the same check.
In game the flag read 48 of 48 registered, even right after SkyUI's own `SKICP_configManagerReset`. TestBench's new
papyrus `var` action read moreHUD's `_configManager` as None at the same moment.

**Cause.** CommonLibSSE-NG: `Variable::IsNoneObject()` is `varType.IsNoneObject()`, and that is [code removed].
It is true only for a variable whose TYPE is None. Papyrus `_configManager = none` leaves an OBJECT-typed variable with a
null pointer: `IsObject()` is true and `IsNoneObject()` is false. So the check said "holds a manager" for every
object-typed None, and dropped only a None-typed one (`SetNone()`, storedType "none"). A config past SkyUI's 128 limit
or a late one can hold either form. The same fact was already in this library, but as the last bullet of the SkyUI
give-back entry, which a topic grep for IsNoneObject / None value did not surface.

**Why it was convincing.** The name reads as "is this a None object", and the check compiled and ran without a warning.
Most configs really were registered, so the wrong check and the right one agreed in every earlier test.

**Do instead.** A Papyrus object variable "holds something" when `IsObject() && GetObject()` (pointer non-null). Treat
`IsNoneObject()` as a type test only. To see how a variable is stored, ask the object: TestBench `papyrus`
[code removed] returns `value` and `storedType`. With
`"set"` (and `"noneType": true`) it writes the state a bug report describes, so the fix is proven on that exact state
rather than on whatever the test list happens to hold.

## TestBench's combat doctrine presses F10, and in Njordlinger Test F10 opens Immersive Equipment Displays - "no doctrine box opened" (2026-10-04, HPM real-blow test)

**What happened.** The HPM hand-off's "blow" step called TestBench `playerbot {order:"class", name:"paladin"}`. It
returned 504, "F10 was pressed but no doctrine box opened within 6 s (is AutoCombat.dll loaded? is a game loaded?)",
twice. Engage then pursued a placed wolf and never struck, so no damage number appeared. A single frame showed IED's
editor window open on the left of the screen.

**Cause.** AutoCombat's doctrine box is reached with F10 (spliced). In Njordlinger, F10 belongs to Immersive Equipment
Displays (DEFAULT-KEYS.md), and IED is enabled in Njordlinger Test (modlist lines 380-382). TestBench's README assumes
IED is off in the Test profile, which no longer holds. The first attempt also ran behind Alternate Perspective's "Done
Writing" box, which can reappear once after the first accept and pauses the game.

**Why it was convincing.** The error names AutoCombat.dll and "is a game loaded?", which points away from a key
clash. The bot's pursuit worked, so the setup looked half right.

**Do instead.** Before a TestBench combat step, check that F10 isn't owned in the profile: untick the IED mods for
that run and restore them after, or give TestBench a doctrine path that doesn't go through F10. After New Game through
AP, check `menu action=list` for messageBoxOpen again a few seconds after the first accept.

**Same day, the retry.** With IED unticked, F10 hit a SECOND owner: a world-map mod's "Select World Map (1/1)" message box (Skyrim / Shivering Isles / Solstheim / Soul Cairn / Tamriel / Wyrmstooth / Cancel) opened first, and TestBench answered 409, "the open message box is not AutoCombat's doctrine box". AutoCombat's box was QUEUED behind it. Cancelling the map box (`menu action=accept index=7`) brought the doctrine box up, and `accept index=0` (Berserker) set it. Engage then landed hits within ~3 s: HPM's "-4" and "-10" over the wolf. So in Njordlinger, work through the boxes F10 opens with `menu describe` / `accept` until the doctrine box shows.

## Nexus's new media editor leaves earlier gallery menus open in the page - a "Delete" found by text belonged to the wrong image (2026-10-04, AMF banner)

**What happened.** On AMF's Nexus page (new editor, /games/<game>/mods/<id>/edit/media), I opened the ⋮ menu of the new
2.0.9 banner and used "Set as thumbnail". Then I opened the ⋮ menu of the old 2.0.1 image, asked Claude in Chrome's
`find` for the "Delete" menu item, clicked it, and confirmed. It deleted the NEW banner. The old one became the
thumbnail again.

**Cause.** The editor's Headless UI menus stay in the DOM after use. Two `[role=menu]` panels were present at once, the
stale one from the earlier card and the one just opened. `find` returned the first "Delete" it saw, which belonged to
the stale panel. The confirmation dialog doesn't name the image, so nothing showed the mistake before it was final.
Nothing was lost only because the banner was on disk, and the old images had been archived first.

**Why it was convincing.** The click went to the card I meant to delete, a menu opened, and its items read the same.

**Do instead.** Drive each gallery card by its own list item: find the `li` whose title (and image URL) match, click
that card's options button, then take the menu from `document.getElementById(button.getAttribute('aria-controls'))`
and click the item inside THAT element. Read the gallery list back (title + image id) after every delete. Keep the
archive-first rule (nexus-media-never-delete-without-archiving).

## TestBench keyboard taps (input action=tap) did not reach Skyrim in Njordlinger Test - sneak and weapon-draw never happened (2026-10-05, HPM A2)

**What happened.** An HPM hand-off tapped Left Ctrl (scan 29, 120 ms) to sneak and R (19) to ready a bow through TestBench
`input {action:"tap", device:"keyboard"}`, with the game in front. HPM's context never showed sneak, and IsWeaponDrawn
stayed false with the bow equipped, so two crosshair checks "failed". The same run's real middle and left mouse
buttons (Windows mouse_event) did reach the game: TDM locked on, and the bow drew once the weapon was out.

**Cause (not isolated).** The taps were acknowledged, but the game acted on none of them. Whether the tap is too short for
these controls, or the keys are rebound or consumed in this list, was not tested further.

**Why it was convincing.** The tool answered without error, and the failing checks read like HPM bugs: "sneaking, crosshair
not hidden".

**Do instead.** Drive a game STATE through Papyrus when the state is what's under test: `Actor.StartSneaking()` (it
toggles), `Actor.DrawWeapon()`, `SheatheWeapon()`. Before blaming the mod, confirm the state actually happened
(IsSneaking / IsWeaponDrawn). Real mouse_event clicks go only behind a foreground check that SkyrimSE is the front
window. With that, the same checks all passed (A2 retry).

## A user's MO2 deprecation warning named a call the current release no longer makes - the line number matched an OLD version, and the Nexus audit never looked at the page (2026-10-05, MO2 Custom Filters)

**Symptom.** VICKORTY posted MO2's warning `[deprecated] onModStateChanged in _on_ui [plugins\MO2CustomFilters.py:222]`.
The hand-off asked for line 222 to be moved to the Dict form, with a new version, a finalize and a post.

**What was true.** The released 1.0.5 has no `onModStateChanged` at all; it dropped every mobase callback to stop MO2
closing on mod toggles. In tags v1.0.0-v1.0.4, line 222 is `self._tabs = _FilterTabs(self, window)` inside `_on_ui`.
MO2 names the plugin's OUTERMOST frame, and the subscription itself sat in `_FilterTabs.__init__` around line 348.
Both Nexus pages (skyrimspecialedition 192713 and the Modding Tools page, site 2362) serve 1.0.5, uploaded after the
final 1.0.5 issue. So the user runs an old version, and the answer is "update", not a new build.

**Why it went unseen.** The registry had `nexusModId: null` for MO2CustomFilters, and `nexus-version-audit.py` mapped
only the Skyrim and Oblivion Remastered folder prefixes. Every "MO2 - " distro folder read NO DISTRO FOLDER, so no MO2
page had ever been compared with its folder.

**Do instead.** Before changing code over a reported file:line, read that line at each released tag
(`git show vX.Y.Z:file`) and in the version the page serves (`files.json` upload times against the commit times). Then
fix the code only if the CURRENT release still has the call. Fixed the same day: the page is linked (`version-gate.ps1
link -NexusModId 192713`), and the audit's `domain_ok()` lets an "MO2 - " folder match a page in any section.

## A Qt dialog cannot be narrower than its widest child - four sentence-long labels without word wrap held the Modlist Manager wider than MO2 (2026-10-05)

**Symptom.** The owner: *"the mm plugins popup window is wider than mo2 and wont let me adjust its width"*. In 1.1.2
the narrowest the dialog could go was 1,591 px; 1.1.3 made it 2,041 px with a longer Rules-tab explanation and one more
button on its row.

**Why.** A QLabel without `setWordWrap(True)` is as wide as its whole text, and a dialog's minimum size is its widest
child's. The Review, Rules and Settings tabs and the order line each held a sentence on one line. `resize(1100, 720)`
also opened the dialog at a fixed size, whatever the size of MO2's window. Nothing failed, so no test noticed: the
offscreen checks looked at what the dialog DID, never at how wide it was.

**Measuring it.** Qt's offscreen platform has no system fonts and measures text far wider than MO2 draws it. Under it
the dialog read 4,676 px, and setting Segoe UI changed nothing. With `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows`, never showing the
window, `minimumSizeHint()` gives the real figure.

**Do instead.**
- Wrap every label that holds a sentence: the manager's `_note(text)` helper, or short lines broken with `\n`.
- Open a dialog no larger than its parent window and screen.
- `tools/check_dialog_width.py` measures the narrowest width with real fonts and fails above 760 px. It fails on 1.1.2
  and 1.1.3 and passes on the fix (682 px).
- Gate rule `mo2-plugin-long-labels-wrap` refuses a QLabel holding a literal of 100+ characters, or a multi-line one
  without line breaks, in any MO2 plugin of ours.

## A backup of a mod's player folder copied only its top-level files - the Presets\ subfolder was overwritten by the test run (2026-10-05, AMF banner reshoot)
**What happened.** Before a long AMF screenshot run in Njordlinger Test, I backed up the owner's AMF files with
`cp "$O"/*.ini "$O"/*.txt`. That took User.ini and the three Mcm*.txt files, but not `Presets\`. The run's MCM sort
saved its undo point as `Presets\Before MCM sort.ini`, overwriting the owner's own (from his sort at 04:35). It had to be
rebuilt from an older User.ini copy, which matches his file only if he changed nothing before sorting.
**Do instead.** Back up a mod's whole player folder recursively (`cp -rp "$O"/. backup/`), list what the backup holds, and
compare it with the folder before the run starts. A feature that writes a file on use (a sort's undo preset, a learned
map) writes into the player's folder during any test that presses it.

## A dxgi.dll proxy beside the exe no longer reaches the game when the exe takes DXGI from NVIDIA Streamline - read the exe's imports before choosing a proxy or hook (Witcher 3 Remastered, 2026-10-05)

**What was found.** Planning AMF for The Witcher 3 Remastered (5.0), the obvious route was the one every 4.04-era native
mod used: a `dxgi.dll` proxy in `bin\x64_dx12` (witcher3-vr, RED3ext). Its users report it "doesn't work of course" on 5.0.
The exe's import table shows why: `witcher3.exe` 5.0 imports neither `dxgi.dll` nor `d3d12.dll`. `CreateDXGIFactory/1/2`
and `D3D12CreateDevice` come from **`sl.interposer.dll`** (NVIDIA Streamline), which loads the real modules from System32
by full path. A `dxgi.dll` in the game folder is then only picked up by some vendor DLLs (libxess, FidelityFX), never by
the game's own swap-chain path.

**Why the old answer looked safe.** It worked for years on the same game, and on Oblivion Remastered the DXGI factory
hook worked by name. The game's binary changed underneath it, and nothing in a folder listing shows that.

**Do instead.** Before choosing a loader or render hook for a game, read the exe's import table (pefile, `dumpbin
/imports`) and the imports of the DLLs beside it.
- Choose the proxy name from what the exe really imports, and check it isn't a KnownDLL. On Witcher 3 5.0 that is
  `dinput8.dll`.
- Hook the module the game's calls actually resolve to. AMF-W3 loads System32's `dxgi.dll` by full path and hooks its
  exports.
- Delay-load `dxgi.dll` in your own DLL, so a proxy in the game folder is never bound by your static import.
  Research: `4. plans\amf-witcher3\RESEARCH-web.md` 1.1.

## A posted F12 never reaches Steam's overlay hotkey, and a DPI-unaware game's client coordinates are not the capture's pixels (Witcher 3 TestBench, 2026-10-05)

**What happened.** Building TestBench for The Witcher 3 Remastered, keys are delivered inside the game process (a posted
`WM_INPUT` resolved by the exe's own `GetRawInputData` import, plus `WM_KEYDOWN`). Escape, F1 and typing all reached the
game and AMF with the game in the background, so the first `steamshot` simply posted F12 the same way. Steam wrote
nothing. The overlay's hotkey does not read keys through the exe's import or the window's message queue.
Separately, the first client crop cut the frame to its top-left two thirds: the game is DPI-unaware (it renders
2133x1200 and Windows scales the window to its native resolution at 150 %), so `GetClientRect` / `ClientToScreen` from a normal
thread answered in logical units while Windows Graphics Capture delivers physical pixels.

**Do instead.**
- Trigger Steam's screenshot through the game's own `steam_api64.dll`: `SteamAPI_SteamScreenshots_v003()` then
  `SteamAPI_ISteamScreenshots_TriggerScreenshot()`. That is exactly the F12 path: the overlay captures in its Present hook,
  and the file lands in `Steam\userdata\<id>\760\remote\<appid>\screenshots`. Check `IsScreenshotsHooked` first (when the
  game hooks screenshots, Steam hands the request to the game instead).
- Before a pixel crop or a click from a screenshot, measure the window from a per-monitor-aware thread
  (`SetThreadDpiAwarenessContext(PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2)`), keep the game's own logical client size for its input, and carry
  the ratio (`client_scale`) with every capture. A click taken from a capture is `capture_px / client_scale`.
- A capture that has to show an overlay is taken of the presented WINDOW (Windows Graphics Capture), never inside a Present
  chain whose hook order is unknown (entry 2308). That one choice made TestBench's capture independent of AMF's, Steam's and
  Streamline's hook order.

## Steam's F12 screenshot missed the overlay because inline hooks on dxgi's Present run last-hooked-first - write the vtable SLOT of the object the game holds and the overlay draws before every inline hook (Witcher 3 Remastered, 2026-10-05, proven in game)

**What was asked.** The owner: Steam's own F12 screenshot must show the AMF window, with no repeat of Oblivion Remastered,
where the capture missed the overlay.

**Why it missed.** AMF, Steam's overlay and any other overlay all MinHook/detour the same function body,
`IDXGISwapChain::Present` in dxgi.dll. Inline hooks chain last-installed-first. Steam reads the back buffer for its
screenshot as its hook is entered. When Steam hooked after AMF, Steam ran first and AMF drew afterwards, so the image
had no menu. The order depends on load timing, so it can't be fixed from inside the dxgi hook.

**What fixed it.** Hook one level OUT, at the object the game itself calls:
- find the module the exe imports `CreateDXGIFactory*` from (its import table; `sl.interposer.dll`, NVIDIA Streamline, on
  Witcher 3 5.0);
- hook those exports;
- on the factory they return, write the vtable SLOT for `CreateSwapChain`/`CreateSwapChainForHwnd`, as a plain pointer
  write under `VirtualProtect`, not an inline hook;
- on the swap chain it returns, write slots 8 (Present) and 22 (Present1).

The game's call goes through the slot first, so AMF draws before the call reaches Streamline, dxgi and every inline hook
on dxgi. It draws into the REAL dxgi swap chain, which was recorded by the dxgi-level hook nested inside the creation
call. The dxgi-level hook stays for queue capture and ResizeBuffers, and draws only while the outer path has not, so a
frame is never drawn twice.

Main Agent's run: `ISteamScreenshots::TriggerScreenshot`, which is the F12 path, saved an image containing the AMF
window. The log showed "the call lands in sl.interposer.dll".

**General form.** Order between inline hooks on a shared function is not yours to choose. A vtable slot of an object
the caller holds is always dispatched before the function body, so put "must run first" work there. Caveat: when there
is no proxy and the slot belongs to dxgi's own class, an overlay that finds Present by reading a dummy swap chain's
vtable AFTER your write would hook your detour instead. Prefer the proxy's slots when one exists.

## A saved window size came back as `inf` and the next opening filled the whole screen - the display size is [value removed] while the game is minimised or driven in the background (AMF Witcher 3, 2026-10-05)

**Symptom.** In Main Agent's second launch, `amf.menu op=open` opened the window over the entire client area. The INI
held `fHotkeyX=inf` (and Y, W, H).

**Cause.** The window geometry is saved as fractions of `ImGui::GetIO().DisplaySize`. TestBench drives the game in the
background, where the client rect, and so the display size, is [value removed]. The divide gave inf, the "moved" check passed, and
inf was saved. `IsSet()` checked `>= 0`, which inf passes.

**Fix.** Never save while `display.x/y < 1`. `IsSet()` now requires `std::isfinite` on every field, so a bad value
already on disk reads as unset.

**General form.** Any value normalised by a window or screen size must be guarded against the zero size a minimised or
background window reports. A validity check on a float must reject non-finite values, not only negative ones.

## Witcher 3 mod-menu labels are hashed keys - .w3strings format, the key hash, and why a CSV's ;meta[language] line can't be trusted (AMF Witcher 3 M4, 2026-10-05)

**Keys.** The keys a mod's settings menu (`bin\config\r4game\user_config_matrix\pc\*.xml`) uses for its labels:
- `panel_<each displayName segment>`;
- `option_<Var displayName>`;
- `preset_value_<Option or Preset displayName>`;
- `preset_<group path with . as _>`.

`panel_Mods` lives in the game's own `content\content0\en.w3strings`.

**The key hash.** `h = h*31 + c` over the UTF-16 units of the LOWER-CASED key, with no seed (Java's `String.hashCode`).
A CSV's `key(hex)` column is this hash. Rows that have only the hex need it to be matched at all, as in Friendly HUD.

**.w3strings.**
- Header: "RTSW", u32 version, u16 key1.
- Then three bit6-counted sections:
  - entries: `id^magic`, offset, length;
  - keys: hash, `id^magic`;
  - the text buffer: UTF-16 for v162-163, UTF-8 for v164.
- A trailing u16 key2.
- `(key1<<16 | key2)` maps through a fixed table to a `magic`; mods' files all carry the English key.
- The text XOR key starts at `(magic>>8) & [value removed]`. Each unit is XORed with `(length+1)*key`, then the key rotates left
  by 1 (16-bit).
- Some files claim v162 but hold UTF-8. Detect them by where the buffer ends.

Decoder: `src/ModMenusParse.cpp` (`ReadW3Strings`). It was written from the MIT-licensed Witcher3StringEditor's format;
the GPL readers were not read. It was verified 100% against every CSV/w3strings pair in the Witcher MO2.

**CSV language.** Friendly HUD's `cn.csv` and `zh.csv` both say `;meta[language=en]`. The encoder template is copied
between files unchanged, so the FILE NAME decides the language and the meta line is only a fallback. Trusting the meta
line put Chinese page names on an English menu. CSVs also come as plain `key|text` under an `;idspace=` header (More Gold
and XP).

## Rewriting a JSON rule file through json.load/json.dumps flipped all 1012 lines and turned two `\ufeff` escapes into literal byte-order marks (gate-rules.json, 2026-10-05)

**What happened.** Adding four names to one rule's `exemptMods` by `json.load` then `json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`
produced a whole-file diff:
- the file indents by 2;
- it is LF, and a CRLF guess made it worse;
- `ensure_ascii=False` turned the BOM rules' escaped `"\ufeff"` patterns into literal invisible U+FEFF characters. That
  is the very defect those rules forbid in package text.

**Do instead.** For a one-row change to a hand-formatted file, edit the text. If a round-trip is unavoidable:
- match the original indent and line ending, read from the committed bytes (`git show HEAD:<file> | xxd`);
- keep `ensure_ascii=True`, or re-escape any non-printing character;
- check `git diff --stat` before committing. A one-row change must show a handful of lines.

## Under Mod Organizer 2 a plugin's own module path is its REAL mod folder - game data looked up relative to it is missing; take game paths from the exe (AMF Witcher 3 1.0.1, 2026-10-05)

**Symptom.** AMF's mod-menu reader found 0 menu files: "could not list C:\Tools\The Witcher 3
MO2\mods\Apocrypha Menu Framework (W3 M1 test)\bin\config\r4game\user_config_matrix\pc". AMF's own themes and translations
loaded fine, so the path code looked correct.

**Cause.** The M1.1 fix made every path relative to the .asi (`GetModuleHandleEx(FROM_ADDRESS)` +
`GetModuleFileName`), because the game's working folder is `bin\`, not `bin\x64_dx12`. Under usvfs the module reports where
the file REALLY is, which is the mod's own folder. Its own files are there; the game's folders and other mods' files are
not.

**Fix.** Build game paths, and the framework's data folder too, from `GetModuleFileNameW(nullptr)`, the exe. The exe sits
in the game's real folder, and listing paths there from inside the process goes through the virtual folder, so every
mod's files appear merged. A manual install has the plugin beside the exe, so both resolve the same there.

**General form.** Inside an MO2-launched process, three paths are three different things:
- the working folder: whatever the launcher set;
- the plugin's module path: its real mod folder;
- the exe's path: the game folder, merged by the VFS.

Choose deliberately. Anything that must see other mods' files goes through the exe's path.

(Found by Main Agent's TestBench run. The same run proved that the DX12 game writes mod-menu values to
`dx12user.settings`, which with MO2 profile-local settings is the profile's copy, seen in-process at the Documents path.)

## A "pad gate leak" was the test pad connecting on every press - log the gate's callers before redesigning the gate (AMF Witcher 3, 2026-10-05)

**CORRECTED the same day.** The diagnosis below ("the game reads through GetProcAddress") was WRONG, and the fix built on
it fixed nothing. The caller log added in the next build showed that, with the menu open, the game's only pad reads were
through its import slot ([offset removed]) and every one returned a neutral pad. The game still moved because
TestBench's virtual pad existed only while a button was down. Each press was also a pad CONNECT, and the game reacts to
a pad connecting on its own: from the main menu that opened the Rewards screen. Its first idle state also reused the
pressed state's packet number, so the release was never seen. Both were fixed in TestBench (59c3f91), and the gate held.

**Lesson.** Before rebuilding a gate on a theory about the caller, log the callers: module and offset, slot, thread, and
what the gate returned. One run would have shown the gate was working. And a virtual input device must behave like a
real one: plugged in and idle before the first press, and every state change with a new packet number. The wider gate
(below) was kept as cover for a second controller or another reader.

**The original (wrong) analysis, kept for the record.**

**Symptom.** With AMF open, two D-pad Down presses from TestBench's virtual pad moved AMF's selection AND the game's main
menu (it went into CDPR's Rewards screen). The virtual pad is an inline hook on `XINPUT9_1_0!XInputGetState`, which is
exactly where a real pad's data comes from, so a real controller leaks the same way.

**Cause.** AMF's gate replaced only the exe's IMPORT SLOT for XInputGetState. witcher3.exe 5.0 also carries the names
`xinput1_4` and `xinput1_3` (wide) and `XInputSetState`/`XInputGetCapabilities`, none of them imported: it loads XInput
itself and calls through GetProcAddress, so it never touches the slot.

**Fix.**
- Keep the slot gate.
- Also MinHook `XInputGetState` at the function in every XInput DLL the game has loaded. GetProcAddress follows
  forwarders, so dedupe by address.
- The slot gate's underlying call and the framework's own reads use the trampoline.
- A thread-local "framework read" flag makes every gate pass the framework's read unchanged, whatever path it takes
  (e.g. Steam Input's hook in the slot, then into an inline gate).

**General form.** A grep of the exe's IMPORTS is not a list of its call paths. Before trusting an import-slot hook to
cover a function, search the exe for the DLL and function names as strings, ASCII and UTF-16. A name that appears
without an import means a dynamic path; gate at the function.

## Wording-pass lessons (sub-agent, AMF Witcher 3, 2026-10-05)

- **git can't show a translation-file diff.** It treats UTF-16 LE files as binary, so `git diff --stat` shows only byte
  counts and can't prove a small change. Decode `git show HEAD:<file>` and the working file, and compare BOM, line count,
  line endings and exactly which keys changed.
- **AMF's INI comments live in two places.** `settings::Save()` rewrites the whole INI from string literals in
  Settings.cpp. A wording fix in the shipped INI alone is undone the first time a player changes a setting, so fix the
  writer too.
- **Port leftovers are not only game names.** Help text can name a control the port no longer has ("Settings -> Log
  level"). Check each UI reference in help text against the controls the page actually draws.
- **A TR()-default-matches-English-file check scans every TR() in src**, including files that were off limits for
  editing: their keys live in the same translation files.

## Porting the Skyrim AMF's settings and UI to the Witcher 3 build: four traps (sub-agents' lessons, 2026-10-05)

- **A settings migration into "User.ini holds only what differs" must compare against the COMPILED defaults.** Builds
  before User.ini saved the player's changes into the shipped INI itself. Read with the new rule, those values look like
  the defaults and nothing carries over. Compare each shipped-file value with the compiled default instead (equal to the
  shipped INI by rule 16), move the differences into User.ini, then restore the shipped file. Otherwise the next save
  drops them and the next update loses them.
- **A widget built on `ImGui::InvisibleButton` draws no nav highlight at all.** "The highlight on a toggle is too faint"
  was really "there is none". Such a widget must call `ImGui::RenderNavHighlight` itself to get the frame a slider gets.
- **A comment describing behaviour is not evidence of it.** The Witcher build's comments said the window moved by its
  top bar, while `ImGuiWindowFlags_NoMove` made that impossible. Check the code path, not the comment.
- **`translation-coverage.py` reads `TR("` inside comments too**, so a placeholder comment must not contain one.
  Conversely, a key passed to `TR()` through a table (`TR(kGroups[i].trKey, ...)`) is invisible to the script and needs
  its lines added by hand.

## A button that closed the game instantly with nothing logged: a std::mutex taken twice on one thread throws, and the uncaught throw in the frame ends in std::terminate (AMF Witcher 3 1.0.3, 2026-10-05)

**Symptom.** Clicking the Mod menus tab's "Sort into categories" button killed the game at once, 2 of 2 times. There
was no line in AMF's log, no TestBench crash record (no vectored-handler exception), and no WER event or dump. The SAME
sort run through the DevBench op worked, and so did the tab's Undo button.

**Cause.** `DrawSettingsTab` held `g_importLock` (a `std::mutex`) for the whole tab, and the Sort button called
`SortIntoCategories`, which locks `g_importLock` again. On MSVC, locking a non-recursive `std::mutex` the thread already
owns throws `std::system_error` (resource_deadlock_would_occur). Nothing catches it inside an ImGui frame called from
the Present hook, so `std::terminate` runs and the process is gone before any logger flushes. The op path and Undo
never held the lock, which is what made the button path the only one that died.

**Fix.** Scope the lock to the part of the tab that needs it, and release it before calling anything that takes it.
Wrap work triggered from a frame in a try/catch that logs.

**General form.** An instant exit with no log, no dump and no vectored exception is std::terminate or a fast-fail, not
an access violation. Look for an exception leaving a frame callback; a re-entered `std::mutex` is the usual source.
When one path works and another doesn't, list the locks each path holds when it calls the shared function.

## Four ImGui/Witcher 3 overlay traps from the AMF 1.0.3 runs (sub-agent's findings, 2026-10-05)

- **One child window shared by every page keeps stale nav memory.** ImGui's `FocusWindow` restores that window's last nav
  item and rect, so the first press after switching pages is scored from the OLD page's position. On a short page
  nothing moved; on a long one the highlight jumped near the end. When nav enters the pane or the page changes, clear
  the remembered item and rect and call `NavInitWindow(force)`. Tag tab items `NoNavDefaultFocus` so the fresh start lands
  on a control.
- **ImGui handles Escape/B and closes popups INSIDE `NewFrame`.** An "Escape closes the menu" check made after NewFrame
  sees the press but not the popup it just closed, so the whole menu closed with a dropdown open. Read the popup state
  before NewFrame.
- **The Witcher 3 never repaints a thin band round its swap-chain image**: about 17 px left/right and 11 px top/bottom of
  2133x1200. Overlay pixels drawn there persist in every back buffer, with the menu closed too, until the game restarts.
  Keep overlay windows and popups out of the outer ~2.5 % (`DisplaySafeAreaPadding` for popups, a clamp for windows).
- **After a mouse click, ImGui ignores A/Space/Enter until a directional move.** The clicked item already is the nav item,
  but activate keys are read only while the highlight is shown. Show the highlight when an activate press arrives with it
  hidden.

## The Witcher 3 didn't fill the screen and a Steam toast flickered bottom-right: the exe is DPI-unaware, so at 150 % scaling it runs at 2133x1200 - Borderless can't go higher; use the game's own Full Screen (2026-10-05, corrected)

**Symptoms.** The owner saw the game picture not filling the its native resolution screen, and a notification bottom-right
"disappearing and reappearing about every quarter of a second". He changed the game's display settings and restarted,
but nothing changed.

**What was true.**
- witcher3.exe 5.0 is DPI-unaware. With Windows at 150 %, it sees a 2133x1200 desktop, so its resolution list stops
  there (`[Viewport] Resolution="2133x1200"`), and Windows stretches the window up to the full screen.
- The game never repaints a thin band round its picture (see the earlier entry). Steam's "Access Steam features from the
  overlay" toast was drawn mostly below the screen, into that band. Each of the 3 back buffers kept a different leftover
  copy, so six grabs 0.25 s apart showed it at a different height almost every time.
- AMF's log ("swap chain ...: 2133x1200") proved the in-game change hadn't taken.

**Fix (corrected the same day).** The first fix written here was wrong.
- Wrong fix 1: the per-exe compatibility flag (HKCU\...\AppCompatFlags\Layers, value = witcher3.exe's path,
  `~ HIGHDPIAWARE`). It is NOT applied when Mod Organizer 2 starts the game. The process still reported DPI awareness 0,
  with parent ModOrganizer and no `__COMPAT_LAYER`.
- Wrong fix 2: AMF making the game DPI-aware at its entry point (`bDpiAware`, built into 1.0.5). The owner turned it
  down: *"This isn't the kind of feature that should be built into AMF. At, at most, I'd want to build a separate
  mod"*. It was removed before any release.
- What actually happened: the owner's settings from before the Remastered setup (March 2026) ran
  `FullScreenMode=2` (Full Screen) at `Resolution="its native resolution"`. The fresh 5.0 settings came up as `FullScreenMode=1`
  (Borderless) at 2133x1200, written by the game itself; no session wrote them. In Borderless a DPI-unaware game is
  limited to the desktop Windows shows it (2133x1200), so the its native resolution pick was refused and it fell back to 1024x768.
- Fix: in the game, set the display mode to Full Screen, then its native resolution. Or edit `[Viewport]` in the MO2 profile's
  dx12user.settings with the game closed. AMF had no part in it: it never touches the window size, display mode or
  fullscreen state.
- Lesson: before building a fix into a mod, compare the game's settings with the owner's last known-good copy (the
  setup backups) and ask whether the problem belongs to the mod at all.

**Knock-on effects.**
- Test tooling tuned to the scaled window (TestBench's client_scale, AMF's edge band at 30 px of 1200) changes to native
  coordinates.
- A test that restores dx12user.settings from a backup must keep the new Resolution.

**Diagnosis tools.** One DPI-aware desktop grab (`SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(-4)` + PIL `ImageGrab`), the game
window's rect, and a short burst of the corner (six grabs, 0.25 s apart) - no background recorder.

## A crash on frame generation's present thread was blamed on an overlay drawing from the game's thread - wrong: frame generation presents through the hooked proxy, so the overlay already ran on that thread (Witcher 3 AMF, 2026-10-05, corrected)

**Symptom.** Witcher 3 Remastered with AMD FSR frame generation on, Full Screen at its native resolution:
- the game ran for a few minutes, then crashed with [value removed] at user32[value removed] (reading [value removed]), under dxgi's Present;
- the record came from TestBench, and RED's CrashReporter took the foreground;
- the owner saw a frozen screen he couldn't leave (witcher3 Responding=False until it was killed).

**What was true.**
- RED's minidump (`AppData\Local\REDEngine\ReportQueue\<run>\Witcher3.dmp`, read with the `minidump` Python package)
  gave the crashing thread's start address: `[offset removed]`, frame generation's
  present thread.
- Frame generation presents the real dxgi swap chain itself, real and generated frames alike, on its own thread and
  with its own queue. The queue AMF captured at that swap chain's creation was frame generation's (the log shows a
  different queue at each frame-gen switch).
- AMF drew from the game-facing Present, on the game's render thread, into that same dxgi swap chain:
  GetCurrentBackBufferIndex, GetBuffer and ExecuteCommandLists on frame generation's queue, while frame generation's
  thread was inside Present on it. A dxgi swap chain is not free-threaded.
- AMF's frames in the stack scan (imgui.cpp lines) were stale slots. The live chain was frame-gen thread -> Discord's
  hook -> Steam's hook -> dxgi. "r13 = the swap chain AMF follows" proved nothing either: any crash in that Present has
  it.

**CORRECTION (the same evening).** The race below never happened. After the fix, frame generation was on ("108 FG" on
screen), yet AMF never logged the foreign presenter. FFX's present thread presents through the Streamline proxy that AMF
hooks as game-facing, so `hk_OuterPresent`, and Render, already ran ON frame generation's thread, with dxgi's Present
nested inside it. The 19:44 crash (user32 in dxgi's Present under Discord's and Steam's hooks, full screen) is
unexplained. The detection below stays as a guard, but it fixed nothing here.
- Lesson: a fix built from a thread hypothesis needs its log line seen firing before it is called the fix. Ask which
  thread enters the HOOKED path, not just which thread crashed.

**Fix as first written (AMF-W3 1.0.5, a guard only).**
- When the dxgi-level Present of the inner swap chain arrives NOT nested inside the game-facing Present (thread-local
  `t_inPresent` false), mark it foreign-presented.
- From then on, draw only there, on the presenting thread and its queue, and skip the game-facing draw. The menu is on
  top of generated frames too.
- Reset the flag at every new dxgi swap chain.
- Render takes a try-lock, so two presenting threads never build two ImGui frames at once.
- Engine calls are unaffected: Red3 runs from the game's message pump (Tick), never from Present.

**Do instead.**
- An overlay that hooks above an interposer (Streamline, a frame-generation proxy) draws into the inner swap chain only
  from the thread that presents it.
- Check which thread reaches the inner Present before drawing there from the outer one.
- For a game crash, read the dump's crashing-thread START ADDRESS first: it names the owner of the thread in one line.

## A Witcher 3 settings group with displayName="hidden" still shows in the game's Settings as an empty row - hide it with visibilityCondition="hideAlways" (AMF Witcher 3, 2026-10-05)

**Symptom.** The owner's screenshot of the title screen's Settings: an empty, selectable row between KEY BINDINGS and
VIDEO.

**What was true.**
- AMF's `bin\config\r4game\user_config_matrix\pc\ApocryphaMenuFramework.xml` holds two internal settings: the game-menu
  entry's open request and the intro switch.
- It copied the game's `hidden.xml` shape, `displayName="hidden"`. But the options menu
  (`igmOptions.ws`, about line 309) leaves out only the group whose **id** is `Hidden`, plus groups
  `IsGroupVisible` reports invisible. The display name does nothing, so AMF's group got its own nameless row.
- The game's own way to hide a whole group is `visibilityCondition="hideAlways"` on the `<Group>`, used on
  `NewHorseControls` and `RemasterCombat`. Scripts still read and write those vars normally (GetVarValue in
  btHorseRidingManager.ws, climbProbe.ws).

**Fix.** `<Group id="ApocryphaMenuFramework" displayName="hidden" visibilityCondition="hideAlways">`. AMF's mod-menu
reader now also drops whole hideAlways groups, as the game does.

**Do instead.** Before shipping a user_config_matrix XML for internal settings, check how the game's menu script FILTERS
groups, not just what its own hidden file looks like. Copying a file's shape copies none of the special-casing keyed on
its id.

**Not ours, same screenshot.** The garbled mod entries (`▮▮=▮Z▮▮L…`) and the `>▮` "Mods" label came from pre-Remastered
string files: the AMF test fixture's eight mod menus, and modMenuStrings (Nexus 3650, 2019).

## A WitcherScript @wrapMethod over an EVENT takes the event's bool return - a bare "return;" stops the whole script compile (AMF Witcher 3, 2026-10-05)

**Symptom.** The game stopped at its script-compile screen with `Error [modapocryphamenuframework]local\apocryphamenuframework.ws(97): Unable to convert from 'void' to 'Bool'`. That line was a `return;` in `@wrapMethod(CR4RecapMoviesMenu) function OnConfigUI()`. The game's own hundreds of "not marked as abstract" warnings are normal and harmless.

**What was true.** `OnConfigUI` is declared `event` in the game's script, and events return a bool. A wrapper written as `function OnConfigUI()` takes that return type: falling off the end compiles (the game's own event does it), but `return;` is void.

**Do instead.** In a wrapper over an event, every early exit returns a value (`return false;`). Before shipping a wrapper, look up whether the target is declared `event` or `function`, and what it returns. A compile error in any mod's script stops the game at start-up, so test the script in the game (or in REDkit's compiler) before handing a build over.

**Amendment, 2026-10-06 (Item Explorer Witcher 3, preview probe) - no access modifier on a wrapper.** Wrapping CR4GuiManager's `private function Update` with `@wrapMethod(CR4GuiManager) private function Update(...)` stopped the compile: "syntax error, unexpected TOKEN_PRIVATE, expecting TOKEN_FUNCTION". The wrapper is written `function Update(...)` whatever the target's access - it wraps a private method fine. The build had gone out without a dry compile; Item Explorer's tools/dry_compile.py (REDkit, the PowerShell agent's recipe) reproduces the game's exact error, and its package.ps1 now refuses a build that does not compile.

**Amendment, 2026-10-14 (Witcher Gear Overhaul, Griffin set bonus) - one wrappedMethod call per wrapper.** A wrapper of `W3PlayerWitcher.GetSetBonusTooltipDescription` with [code removed] in one branch and [code removed] at the end stopped the dry compile: "[461]: Could not find function 'wrappedMethod'" - line 461 was the SECOND call; a wrapper with one call (IsSetBonusActive) compiled. Do instead: pick the argument in a local variable and call `wrappedMethod` once ([code removed]). Topics: witcher3, scripts.

## An SEH guard does not make a fault harmless in Witcher 3: the game's own crash reporter fires first and the game hangs - and an engine (overrideGroup) setting written at start-up faults (AMF Witcher 3, 2026-10-05)

**Symptom.** The owner saw two crash-reporter windows. The second came from AMF: its log said "engine bridge: SetVarValue
faulted - the bridge is off for this session". The guard had caught the access violation ([offset removed],
reading [value removed]), yet RED's CrashReporter came up and the game (witcher3 3488) hung until it was killed.

**What was true.**
- The write was AMF's loading-recap switch. Its sync hook set the hidden overrideGroup var `LoadingScreen/Debug`
  `DisableVideos` about a second after the game's config was readable, in every session, because the engine does not
  keep that debug group between sessions.
- Later in a session the same write works: the owner's own flip about 20 s in. At start-up, the override path reads
  through something not created yet.
- Plain vars in AMF's own group were written at run time without trouble.
- The game's crash handling sees the fault before AMF's SEH frame does, so "guarded" calls still crash-report.

**Fix (AMF-W3 1.0.0).**
- The framework's game script applies the setting when the main menu opens (`@wrapMethod(CR4CommonMainMenuBase)`
  OnConfigUI), reading a plain mirror var that AMF keeps equal to the switch.
- AMF writes the engine var only on an in-session flip, and the settings sync makes no write in its first 30 s.

**Do instead.**
- Treat every engine call from AMF on Witcher 3 as one that must not fault: a guard is a log line, not protection.
- Write engine-level settings (overrideGroup) only once the game is well up, or let the game's own script do it at a
  known point (the main menu), never from a timer at start-up.

**Amendment, 2026-10-06 (Item Explorer Witcher 3, first run) - a PLAIN var faults at start-up too, and this entry was not
looked up first.** AMF 1.0.2's new `AMF_SetGameVar` (lent to other mods) wrote as soon as the bridge resolved. Item
Explorer cleared its own plain hidden var `ItemExplorer.GiveRequest` 2 s into boot: SetVarValue faulted at the same
[offset removed] reading [value removed], and this time the game hung before its window appeared (Main Agent killed it). So the
"plain vars were fine" line above holds only for writes made at run time; at boot ANY SetVarValue can fault. I wrote the
export without grepping this library for SetVarValue, although ModMenus.cpp's own 30 s hold sat beside it in the same repo.
Fixed in AMF d52fba6: every write from another mod is queued and made only once the game is settled (bridge up 30 s and
the game's menu shown once via ApocryphaMenuFramework.GameMenuOpen, 120 s fallback) and only for a var the game reads back.
**Do instead:** any new path into SetVarValue (an export, a hook, a tool) goes through that settled gate; reads are safe
from the first ready frame, writes are not.
- A setting the engine doesn't persist must be re-applied every session, at a safe moment.

## Nested pad gates: only the OUTERMOST gate of a read may judge and blank it - judging at both ends leaked a held Start after close, judging at the innermost leaked the D-pad with the menu open (AMF Witcher 3, 2026-10-05)

**Symptoms.**
- 1.0.5 (both gates judged): pad Start closed AMF, and the game opened its world map.
- 1.0.0 first fix (only the innermost judged): with AMF open, the D-pad used potions in the game (the owner watching
  Main Agent's run).

**What was true.**
- One game read of XInputGetState passes through the import-slot gate (outer). That calls Steam Input's hook, which
  calls the XInput DLL, which hits AMF's inline gate (inner).
- Other layers sit between them and add buttons of their own: TestBench's virtual pad, and Steam Input's state.
- When both gates judged, the inner zeroed the still-held Start during the post-close settling. The outer then saw zeros,
  took them for "every button up" and ended the settling, so the next read passed Start through.
- When only the innermost judged, whatever the layers above it added went through the outer gate untouched.

**Fix.** A thread-local depth counter around each gate call. Only the gate at depth 1 (the outermost, the one the game
called) runs ApplyGate, so one judge sees the full state that will reach the game.

**Do instead.** With several hooks on one input path, decide which single layer is the judge: the outermost, the last
thing before the caller. Every other layer passes through untouched. Test a gate change with BOTH leaks in mind: a
press while the menu is open, and the press that closes it.

## Witcher 3 5.0's own UI font can be read from the install at run time - bundle entries are [value removed] bytes, zlib only, the font is a DefineFont3 inside a CR2W-wrapped CFX movie (AMF Witcher 3, 2026-10-05)

**Context.** The owner wanted AMF in the game's font. The font is not a file. It is "PF Din Text Cond Pro", in
`fonts_en.redswf` / `fonts_ru.redswf` inside the 5.0 bundles, mapped from the `$NormalFont` slot by
`gameplay\gui_new\fonts.xml` in xml.bundle. Shipping it would copy CDPR's asset, so it is read from the player's own
install. The proof is `ApocryphaMenuFrameworkW3\tools\fontreader` (DESIGN.md plans the C++ port).

**What was true.**
- **Bundles.** A 5.0 bundle's file entries are **[value removed]** bytes, not the pre-5.0 [value removed]. Every one of the 365,866 entries
  is zlib or stored: no LZ4, snappy or doboz is needed. The CRC32 is of the uncompressed data. The 16-byte hash is
  neither MD5, and isn't needed.
- **The movie.** A `.redswf` is CR2W holding a u32 length, then "CFX" (Scaleform's compressed SWF), then zlib. Find the
  movie by its signature: menu `.redswf` files carry more data after it.
- **The glyphs.** The fonts are DefineFont3 (tag 75). SWF quadratic curves map exactly onto TrueType glyf contours,
  provided each contour is reversed after the y flip.
- **Coverage.** fonts_ru is a strict superset of fonts_en (Latin plus Cyrillic and Greek), so take PF Din from fonts_ru.
- **Rendering.** The game renders it heavier than stb_truetype does.

**Do instead / watch for.** Check a built font with `stbtt_InitFont` before adding it to the ImGui atlas: one font
stb rejects fails the WHOLE atlas build, and every font is lost. Read, never write, the game folder. Fail soft: AMF
keeps its own font and logs why.

## A stylesheet frame on MO2's list rows ran out into the indent on every other mod: Qt draws the ::item rule again across an ALTERNATE row; a row frame needs alternation off and :first/:middle/:last pieces (Skellige MO2 Theme, 2026-10-05)

**What happened.** The Skellige MO2 theme draws The Witcher 3's menu frame (outer line, inner line with stepped corners)
round the hovered and selected rows with `border-image` on `QAbstractItemView::item:hover` / `:selected`. In MO2's mod
list the frame looked right on some rows and ran out to the left on others; the owner: "it's every other mod". MO2's views
have `alternatingRowColors` on, and on an alternate row Qt paints the row panel with the item rule as well, across the
whole row including the indent, so those rows got a second frame with its own left end. Three things found on the way,
each seen in a capture of the running MO2:
- a tree row is painted one cell at a time, so a frame per item gives one frame per column; Qt sets `:first`, `:middle`,
  `:last` and `:only-one` on view items, so the art comes in four nine-slice pieces;
- `border-width` on an item shrinks its content rect only while the rule applies, so the text jumps on hover. Taking the
  border back with negative `padding` keeps it still. A side padding on EVERY item moved MO2's tick box but not the name;
- with `@2x` copies of the nine-slice art beside the 1x ones, a 150% render cut the stepped corners apart; 1x only drew
  them whole.

**Do instead.** For a per-row decoration in an MO2 theme: `qproperty-alternatingRowColors: false` on the views (harmless
when both shades are the same colour), pieces by `:first/:middle/:last`, negative padding equal to the border width, and
judge it on the running MO2 with the mouse over several neighbouring rows, not one (`4. plans\witcher3-mo2-branding\
theme-round.ps1` builds, installs and captures; MO2 reloads a changed stylesheet while it runs).

## Moving an MO2 instance left the owner's Taskbar Groups entries pointing at the old folder - a click did nothing; the group caches each icon as MD5(shortcut path).png (Witcher 3 instance, 2026-10-06)

**What happened.** After the Witcher 3 instance moved to `C:\MO2\The Witcher 3` and the old folder was deleted, the
