owner clicked "Witcher 3 MO2" in his Taskbar Groups "MO2" group and nothing opened. The move had updated MO2's own files,
w3-tb.ps1, the gate rules and the memories, but not his launchers. The group's shortcuts live in
`%APPDATA%\Jack Schierbeck\taskbar-groups\Links\<group>\*.lnk`, its entries in `config\<group>\ObjectData.xml`, and its
icons in `config\<group>\Icons\` as `MD5(utf-8 full .lnk path).png` (256x256). A second entry ("MO2 (C:\MO2)") was
stale from the Minimal Skyrim move the same day.

**Do instead.** When an MO2 instance or a tool moves, sweep every launcher that can point at it: the taskbar pins
(`Quick Launch\User Pinned\TaskBar`), the Taskbar Groups links, Start menu and desktop shortcuts. Test each `.lnk`
target exists. To change a group entry, keep the `.lnk` path (the cache name depends on it), edit its target and icon,
overwrite the cached PNG, and restart `Taskbar Groups Background`.

## Some labels from our own .w3strings showed as "##key" and others from the same file worked - the key table must be sorted by hash (Unbind Vanilla Controls W3, 2026-10-06)

**Symptom.** Main Agent's 1.0.0 run: the Key Bindings page showed `##uvc_choice_up` and `##uvc_choice_down`, while
"Sailing - Stop / Reverse" (`uvc_boat_reverse`) from the same `en.w3strings` showed in words. No other mod or game file
carried those ids or key hashes.

**What was true.** Every game `.w3strings` has its key table (hash, id) sorted by the hash, unsigned; ours was written
in id order. The game binary-searches the table. A simulated binary search over our 1.0.0 file found exactly
`uvc_boat_reverse` and `uvc_horse_jump` and missed the rest, which matches what the run showed. Our own reader built a
dictionary, so the round-trip check passed.

**Why it looked like something else.** Some labels worked, so "the game does not load mod string files" was ruled out
at once, and a clash with another mod looked likelier. A partial failure from one file points at the lookup, not the load.

**Do instead.** When writing a binary format the game reads, copy the ORDER of its own files as well as the layout:
check sorting of every table in a game file before writing one. A reader that builds a map cannot catch an ordering
defect; test with the game's own lookup (here a binary search) or in game. `tools/w3strings.py` now sorts the key
table by hash.

## "AMF loaded in every test, so MO2 supplies dinput8.dll" was wrong: the test launcher copied the loader into the real game folder before every run (Witcher 3, 2026-10-06)

**What happened.** Asked whether AMF Witcher 3 needs Root Builder, I answered no: Root Builder was not installed in the
instance and AMF had loaded in every test from `mods\...\bin\x64_dx12\dinput8.dll`, so I concluded MO2's virtual folder
supplied the loader. Main Agent corrected it: `tools\w3-tb.ps1 launch` copies AMF's loader into the REAL
`...\The Witcher 3\bin\x64_dx12\` before every launch ("loader placed: ...dinput8.dll") and removes it on quit, because
the first runs (2026-10-05) never loaded it through the VFS - Windows loads dinput8.dll beside the exe before usvfs hooks
in. AMF's own README already said the file had to be a real file. The owner chose Root Builder and a 1.0.1 repackage.

**Do instead.** "It worked in every test" proves the TEST setup, not the install path. Before claiming how a file reaches
the game, read the launcher that ran those tests (w3-tb.ps1, game-relaunch.ps1, mo2-launch.ps1) and the mod's own
README for a step that puts files in place by hand. A loader DLL the exe imports (dinput8, version, winmm, dxgi proxies)
is a real-folder file under MO2 unless Root Builder (or the launcher) puts it there. Related memory:
verify-by-design-claims-from-source.

## A Bash call blocked by a PreToolUse hook runs NONE of its commands - an edit chained into it was reported done but never happened (AMF Witcher 3 page text, 2026-10-06)

**What happened.** One Bash call ran a Python edit of the AMF Witcher 3 `nexus-page.txt` and, in the same command, a heredoc
for `notes.txt`. The bash-backslash-guard hook blocked the call over the heredoc's backslashes; I rewrote only the heredoc
part as a script and ran that. The page edit, which had been in the blocked call, never ran - yet notes.txt (and my
report to the owner and Main Agent) said the page was rewritten. Main Agent found the old Installation and Requirements
still there after finalizing and rewrote them.

**Do instead.** A hook block means the WHOLE call did not run. After any blocked call, re-run every step it contained, not
only the one the hook named - and before reporting an edit, read the file back (one grep for a line the edit adds).

## Witcher 3 inventory: the hint bar's A equips the grid's selected item through the SCRIPT (OnInputHandled -> the item context), not through the inventory movie - a control added to the menu must deactivate the context (SLS Witcher 3, 2026-10-06)

**What happened.** Simple Loadout System's column inside `panel_inventory` took the pad while focused and set the item
grid's module `focused = 0`. Every A on a box still equipped the item the ARMOR grid had selected beside the column, and
the switch then stored it ("Medium armor 11" / "Light armor 04"). Two fixes aimed at the movie failed: unfocusing the module,
then a stage listener at priority 100 in both phases that swallowed every press. The owner's screenshot showed why: the
grid kept its selection and tooltip, and the hint bar still offered that item's actions. The hint bar is the COMMON menu's
(another movie); its A reaches the inventory script as `CR4InventoryMenu.OnInputHandled`, which calls
`m_currentContext.HandleUserFeedback` - the grid's item context, whose primary action equips. Nothing in the inventory movie
sees that path. (First written here as "the unfocused grid's list acts on A" - wrong; corrected the same night.)

**Do instead.** A control added to a W3 menu that owns the pad while focused does what the menu does for the player-stats
panel (`OnPlayerStatsShown` / `OnPlayerStatsHidden`): `m_currentContext.Deactivate()` on entering, `ActivateContext(...)` +
`UpdateContext()` on leaving, and a `@wrapMethod` on `OnInputHandled` that does not pass it on while focused; block the
movie's tooltip (`_contextMgr.blockTooltips(true, true)`). And when a fix aimed at one layer fails twice, look at a frame
of the screen before the next guess: the hint bar named the real owner of the button.

## A D-pad press that set a binding also changed the Controller Scheme tab - one pad press reaches a Scaleform menu as more than one input event (UVC Witcher 3, 2026-10-06)

**Symptom.** The owner, on the controller rows under Settings > Controller Scheme: *"if I press the D-pad to bind or unbind it
from a slot, then it changes the context to a different context from like combat to horse riding"*. The list waited for a
button, took the D-pad press, wrote the binding - and the page's tabs moved too.

**What was true (by the code path).** The list marked the event handled while waiting, but the wait ENDED on the first event
of the press. The W3 input delegate turns a pad button into more than one event for the same press (the button's code, and a
navigation equivalent - Left/Right for the D-pad - that the module's own tab handler reads), so the event after the one that
completed the change found nothing waiting and went to the tab handler.

**Do instead.** When a Scaleform control finishes something on a pad press (a capture, a clear, a toggle), swallow input for a
short window after it (UVC: 250 ms, `getTimer()`), not only the event that triggered it. Test captures with the D-pad and the
shoulders, the buttons the page itself navigates with.

## ResetGroupToDefaults on a probe's hidden group of three INPUTPAD rows reset the player's WHOLE input mapping to vanilla (UVC Witcher 3 probe 3, 2026-10-06)

**What happened.** Probe 3 step D called `CInGameConfigWrapper.ResetGroupToDefaults('UvcPadProbe3')` to see whether a reset
brings a cleared row back. Main Agent found about 300 lines of the owner's input.settings back to vanilla: attacks, Sprint,
Cast Sign, the radial menu, the swords - every control edit he had made. His pre-probe copy (hash-matched) was put back.

**What was true.** The input groups' values ARE the game's one input mapping; resetting any input group rebuilds that
mapping from the defaults, not only the group's own rows. A probe group's name limited nothing.

**Do instead.** Never call ResetGroupToDefaults on an input group in a mod or a probe (gate rule
`w3-no-reset-group-to-defaults` refuses a package that does). A "reset" of our own restores only our rows, one by one. A
probe that can change the player's bindings is written to touch only the actions it names - read every call in it for that
before handing it over. The same probe seemed to settle that a pad row set to IK_None takes a button again - WRONG: that was a
read-back only, and the file was wiped before anyone looked (see "An INPUTPAD write lands only when..." below). Pad-family
keys no PC pad sends (IK_JcmsRightStickScroll, IK_Gesture_DoubleTap) read back IK_None - read-backs are not evidence.

## Two INPUTPAD rows naming the same action: a write to the second changed nothing (UVC Witcher 3, 2026-10-06 - by the evidence)

**Symptom.** The "Swords" row (SteelSword;SilverSword) set to X wrote no line; Draw Steel (SteelSword;OilSteel) and Draw
Silver (SilverSword;OilSilver) had written X fine the run before. Probe 3 "ruled out" the cleared state - on a read-back.

**Most likely (revised by probe 4).** The swords' pad lines were IK_None, and a pad write from IK_None never reaches the
file (entry below). The overlap may also matter; the one-action-one-row check stays either way.

**Do instead.** One action, one row, on every page we generate: `gen_menu.py` refuses a controller action named by two rows.

## Nexus's new upload form does not save edits made in a BACKGROUND Chrome tab - the description, tags and dropdowns need the tab in front (SLS Witcher 3 post, 2026-10-06)

**What happened.** Posting Simple Loadout System (witcher3/13663) through Claude in Chrome while another session's tab
was the active one in the only Chrome window: `document.visibilityState` was "hidden". The draft dialog, file upload and
file fields worked, but the SCEditor description set through `sceditor.instance(...).val()` never reached the form (Save
stayed disabled; the saved page kept the 623-character template), the tag buttons I clicked did not stick, the
third-party and permission pickers would not open from clicks, and screenshots timed out. Main Agent, whose tab was in
front, pasted the description, re-added the two tags and published in minutes.

**Do instead.** Before editing a Nexus page, check [code removed] in the tab; if it is hidden,
ask the session (or the owner) whose tab is in front to switch, or hand the page to it - never leave two sessions on one
draft. Read back every section from the saved page (description length, tag list) before calling a step done. Dropdowns
in a hidden tab can be opened by clicking their button from page JavaScript and choosing the `[role=option]`, and the
permission radios are `span[role=radio]` taking a dispatched pointer/mouse sequence - but the description editor needs
real input in a visible tab.

## An INPUTPAD write lands only when the action's current pad key is an Xbox key - IK_None or a PS4 key never changes again, and the read-back lies both ways (UVC Witcher 3 probe 4, 2026-10-06)

**Symptom.** The owner unbound Sprint, Sprint Toggle and Summon Horse on the controller with UVC's clear (IK_None); every
rebind afterwards showed the new button in the menu and the log, and the game did nothing. input.settings still held
IK_None. Probe 4: CameraLock RS -> IK_PS4_OPTIONS read back IK_None but LANDED in the file; IK_PS4_OPTIONS -> RS read back
RS and did NOT land.

**Cause, as far as the evidence goes.** The pad writer finds the action's existing lines by a key the current pad layout
knows; IK_None and keys of another layout are not found, so nothing is replaced. GetVarValue reports what was asked, not
what was written.

**Do instead.** A controller binding is proven only from input.settings after the game saved - never from a read-back
or a log of our own. Never clear a pad binding to IK_None or to another layout's key through SetVarValue. Rows already
stuck are repaired in the file with MO2 and the game closed, exact lines, backup first.

## Witcher 3 5.0 loads a mod's gameplay XML only from paths its .reddlc names - and a loot table re-declared in a DLC file ADDS to the game's table of that name (Witcher Gear Overhaul research, 2026-10-06)

**Question.** Witcher Gear Overhaul needs ~800 new abilities (run-time stat top-ups) and 20 weapons in the random relic
loot, without replacing any game file (whole-file overrides clash with every other gear mod).

**What was true (read from the game's and installed mods' files; sub-agent report
`4. plans\Witcher 3 Gear Catalogue\research-dlc-defs-and-loot.md`).**
- The engine does NOT scan `dlc\<x>\data\gameplay\`. It loads definitions XML only from the paths a `.reddlc`
  (CR2W `CDLCDefinition`) lists in `CR4DefinitionsDLCMounter` / `CR4DefinitionsNGPlusDLCMounter`
  (`definitionXmlFilePath`): one file, or a directory ending in `\`. Ship both `abilities\` and `abilities_plus\` (or
  `items\` / `items_plus\`) - every vanilla DLC and every installed DLC mod does. Item Levels Normalized's .reddlc is
  1262 bytes with two mounters: the shape to clone. 5.0 moved the vanilla DLC into `content\content0\bundles`
  (dlc0/ep1/bob.bundle); mods still use `<game>\dlc\<folder>\content\blob0.bundle`.
- A `<loot name="X">` in a DLC definitions file with only new `<loot_entry>` rows merges into the game's table X: CDPR's
  dlc1 re-declares `_store__Griffon_merchant` with its 11 new items only, and six installed mods extend monster,
  crafting and shop tables the same way. The random relic tables (`_uniqe_weapons_epic_dungeon_skelige` (sic),
  `_unique_weapons_epic_dungeon_nml`, `_loot_monster_treasure_uniq_swords`, `_treasure_q4`) give every entry
  `chance="-1"` (read as an equal share - inferred, the roll is native).
- Scripts cannot see which loot table a container uses (only the rolled items), so a script-side loot addition has to
  guess; the XML merge needs no script.

**Do instead.** New abilities, items or loot for Witcher 3 go in the mod's own DLC folder with a .reddlc naming them -
never a replaced game XML. Test one new ability in game (AddItemCraftedAbility, then GetItemAbilities and the tooltip)
before building on it: that DLC-defined abilities join the global table is inferred from ep1's runewords, not proven
for a mod.

## A Witcher 3 weapon effect with an apply chance of exactly 0 ALWAYS applies - and the chance belongs to the ability that holds the effect, not the item (Witcher Gear Overhaul research, 2026-10-06)

**What was true (5.0 scripts).**
- `CInventoryComponent.GetItemBuffs` ([source reference removed], a script function) builds each hit's effects: for
  every ability on the item, its OWN `buff_apply_chance` (times how often that ability is on the item) goes to the
  effect sub-abilities (`<BleedingEffect is_ability="true"/>` ...) inside that same ability. Each effect then rolls on
  its own (`RandF() < chance`, [source reference removed]).
- `W3DamageAction.AddEffectInfo` ([source reference removed]): [code removed] - a 0 chance
  becomes 100 %.
- `desc_*chance_mult` attributes are display only (the character stats panel reads them); the roll never does.
- A crafted ability with a NEGATIVE buff_apply_chance does not cancel the item's base effect - it adds a second entry
  that never fires. A min..max range is rolled per item.

**Do instead.** A status-chance affix is its own ability: one effect sub-ability, `buff_apply_chance` with min = max and
never 0, plus the matching `desc_*chance_mult` for the tooltip. To remove or convert an existing effect, wrap
`GetItemBuffs` and edit the list it returns (or RemoveItemBaseAbility and re-add the stats) - a negative chance does
nothing.

## A Witcher 3 launch that sits on "Compiling scripts (parsing file N/M)" with no CPU is a hidden compile-ERROR dialog, not a hang (overnight combined run, 2026-10-06)

**What happened.** Two launches in a row stopped at the splash with "parsing file 1298/1554" (then 1249/1553), 0 % CPU,
TestBench answering. Read as a hang, and the first one was blamed on the newest native mod (Item Explorer) and the
usvfs log's "thread N never released the mutex". Both wrong: the usvfs line is in every W3 run, the good ones too.
The game had opened its "The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Script Compilation Errors" dialog (#32770) BEHIND the splash.
TestBench's capture shows only the game window, so the dialog never appeared in a capture. Its Edit control held the
one error (a mod used `state`, a WitcherScript keyword, as an identifier).

**Do instead.** After every W3 launch, run `w3-tb.ps1 compiled`: it finds that dialog by title, prints its text, and
ends the game through the dialog's own Exit Application button (exit code 2). Enumerate the game's top-level windows
before calling anything a hang; a frozen splash counter with an idle CPU means the dialog is up.

## A whole Witcher 3 test run stopped at the script compile because a local variable was named `state` - WitcherScript keywords include ordinary words (Witcher Gear Overhaul 1.0.0, 2026-10-06)

**Symptom.** Main Agent's overnight run: `Error [modwitchergearoverhaul]local\witchergearoverhaulvalues.ws(70): syntax
error, unexpected TOKEN_STATE, expecting TOKEN_IDENT, near 'state'`. Every other mod in the set compiled; the run waited
for a fixed package.

**What was true.** `state` (state machines), like `entry`, `latent`, `saved`, `editable`, `timer`, `event`, `out`,
`quest`, `reward`, `single`, `cleanup`, `autobind`, `hint`, `defaults`, is a WitcherScript keyword and cannot name a
variable, parameter or field. The build was handed over with no compile at all, and one error anywhere stops the game at
start-up for every mod. The relaunch then failed at the TYPE-CHECK stage on three more mistakes: writing a field added
to CR4Game through `theGame` ("Left hand side is const" - theGame is a const handle; write it from an @addMethod(CR4Game)
setter), one exec function calling another ("Cannot call exec function ... from scripts"), and a generated 792-case
switch ("memory exhausted, near '.'" - the parser's stack; split it into functions of ~40 cases).

**Do instead.** Dry-compile every Witcher 3 script build before handing it over - REDkit compiles offline (the PowerShell
agent's recipe): copy `content\content0\scripts` to a scratch tree, lay the mods' `Mods\<mod>\content\scripts` over it
(reverse-alphabetical, lowest priority first), and from `<REDkit>\bin\x64_RedKit` run
`wcc_lite.exe compilescripts "<tree>\" -agreetoterms`; success prints "Success! Scripts cooked", failures
"[Error][WCC] [<line>]: ..." without a file name. Vanilla alone takes ~30 s. Witcher Gear Overhaul's
`tools\dry_compile.py` does all of it and its package script refuses a build that fails. Also: keep names off the keyword
list, keep string joins starting with a string (`"" + NameToString(n)`), and check each wrapped method exists as a
script method with the same signature (wrapping `final` methods works: installed Nexus mods do it).

## Witcher 3's GetItemsWithTag does not list every item carrying the tag - and WitcherScript's only text-to-name route is a settings var id (Item Explorer Witcher 3, 2026-10-06)

**Symptom.** Item Explorer's script found items by their localisation key, and, for the items that share a key, among the
items of one of their tags. Three shared-key items (Blunt Bolt, Arbitrator_crafted, Crossbow 2) were never found, even
after a scan of every tag the item definitions use: 214 calls, 17,766 names, and none of the three among them.

**What was true.**
- `GetItemsWithTag('bolt')` returned 7 names; the definitions give 16 items that tag. `'Weapon'` returned 955 on one call
  and 754 on the next, in the same session.
- `GetItemNameFromLocalisationKeyName` answers with ONE item per shared key, sometimes another category's
  (item_name_crossbow_1 gave q603_circus_crossbow), and `None` for some keys (item_name_blunt_bolt).
- WitcherScript has no StringToName. `CInGameConfigWrapper.GetVarName(groupIdx, varIdx)` and `GetGroupName(groupIdx)` DO
  return names built from the ids in user_config_matrix XML.

**Do instead.**
- Never treat GetItemsWithTag as a complete list (vanilla uses it only for fuzzy sets like transmog).
- To turn arbitrary text into a name, ship a hidden settings group whose var ids are the names you need (generated from
  the data), then walk it with `GetVarName` and compare `NameToString`. Item Explorer's ItemExplorerNames.xml does this,
  with 5122 vars generated by tools/gen_names_xml.py.
- Diagnose script lookups in a test run by putting what was tried into the answer the native side logs: what the key
  gave, the inputs read back, the result sizes. One run then settles the question.

## Witcher 3 weapon damage read as 0 while the tooltip showed 236-305 - CalculateAttributeValue is base * mult + add, so a base-only stat comes out 0 (Witcher Gear Overhaul 1.0.0, 2026-10-06)

**Symptom.** Main Agent's run 5: the grade-damage table logged "base 0.[id removed], per level 0.[id removed] -> Common 0 ... Witcher
0" and every ordinary sword's "game damage" read 0, while the same swords' tooltips showed real numbers.

**What was true.** `CalculateAttributeValue(att)` ([source reference removed]) returns `att.valueBase * att.valueMultiplicative +
att.valueAdditive`. Weapon damage (`SlashingDamage`, `SilverDamage`) is a BASE value with no multiplier on the item or
in its definition, so it multiplies by 0. The game itself reads an item's primary stat field by field
(`GetItemPrimaryStat`: base, else mult, else add), and computes a hit from the ACTOR's summed attribute, whose multiplier
is non-zero (actor.ws GetTotalWeaponDamage). A wrapper that "adds graded - own" with own from CalculateAttributeValue
would have added the whole graded damage on top of the game's.

**Do instead.** Read an item's or a definition's flat stat as `valueBase + valueAdditive` (or the field the game's own
code reads), never through CalculateAttributeValue. To change a hit, change it by (new base - old base) * the actor's
multiplier. In WitcherScript a struct field cannot be read off a call result (`GetAttributeValue(x).valueBase` is a
compile error) - store the struct in a variable first.

## Rolling a Witcher 3 loot table from script on the player's inventory yields nothing - AddItemsFromLootDefinition only ATTACHES a table (Witcher Gear Overhaul 1.0.0, 2026-10-06)

**Symptom.** A test action that called `inv.AddItemsFromLootDefinition('<table>')` on the player's inventory 300 times
added 0 items; adding `inv.UpdateLoot()` after it still gave 0.

**What was true.** The game uses AddItemsFromLootDefinition on NPCs at spawn (encounterInitializers.ws) to attach a table
to their inventory; the items are rolled later by `UpdateLoot()` in containers and on death (container.ws, btTaskDeath.ws).
The player's inventory never rolls. There is no script API to read a loot table's entries.

**Do instead.** To roll a table in a test, use a container: the game spawns its own "lootbag" (`LoadResource("lootbag")`,
a W3ActorRemains) for dropped items - spawn one with PM_DontPersist, attach the table to its inventory, UpdateLoot, count,
destroy it. Otherwise check loot at a real chest that uses the table.

## WaitIdle before a Release is not enough in an overlay: the frame being built may already show the texture - free it after THAT frame's fence (AMF Witcher 3 3D preview, 2026-10-06)

**Symptom.** Item Explorer's 3D item card rendered and turned fine; pressing Close crashed the game, with AMD's bug-report
tool and the game's CrashReporter, no TestBench record and no TDR event: a fault inside the driver.

**What was true.** The card is drawn during the page callback: it adds the preview's texture to THIS frame's ImGui draw
list, then the Close button (later in the same frame) calls AMF_PreviewRelease. Release did WaitIdle and freed the
target, its descriptor slot and the model at once. WaitIdle only covers frames already submitted; the frame still being
built was submitted afterwards and read a destroyed resource through a descriptor that pointed at nothing (or, with the
slot reused, at something else). AMF's ReleaseTexture had the same shape.

**Do instead.**
- In a renderer where consumers draw during the frame, never free on request: queue the free, tag it with the fence of
  the next frame submitted, and free when that fence has passed (AMF Overlay.cpp g_deferred / RunDeferred). Descriptor
  slots go back to the free list only then too. When a frame records nothing, tag with the last fence signalled.
- Test the release path, not only the draw path: re-enact "record the frame, release, then run the frame" in a loop under
  the debug layer with GPU-based validation, and keep a free-at-once mode that must fail (AMF tools/preview_test loop /
  loop-now: loop-now died with [value removed] on the first cycle, loop ran 40 cycles clean).

## A Root\ folder meant for MO2's Root Builder deploys in Vortex as <game>\Root\... and the ASI loader never loads - ship a FOMOD that asks where the loader goes; Vortex's Witcher 3 offers only admin symlinks when Documents and the game are on different drives (AMF Witcher 3 1.0.3, 2026-10-06)

**What happened.** AMF Witcher 3 1.0.2 shipped its ASI loader (dinput8.dll) in Root\bin\x64_dx12 for Root Builder.
Vortex has no Root concept: it deploys the folder as it is, so the loader lands in <game>\Root\bin\x64_dx12 and the
game never loads AMF. The 1.0.2 page worked round it by sending Vortex users to a separate winmm loader.

**What was true.**
- Vortex runs a FOMOD before its own Witcher 3 installers (fomod priority 10; witcher3menumodroot 20, mixed 25, tl 30,
  content 50, dlc 60 - read from the bundled game-witcher3 index.cjs.map). One FOMOD question - "Vortex, or installing
  by hand" (bin\x64_dx12), "Mod Organizer 2 with Root Builder" (Root\bin\x64_dx12), "I already have an ASI loader"
  (none) - serves every manager; `tools\fomod.py` turns the staged package into it and `package.ps1` runs it.
- Proven 2026-10-06 in Vortex 2.8.0 with the real 1.0.3 package: loader symlinked into bin\x64_dx12, game started from
  its own folder with no MO2 - AMFLoader attached, loaded the .asi, the overlay drew.
- Vortex's Witcher 3 support offered only "Symlink Deployment (Run as Administrator)": the extension's
  witcher3menumoddocuments mod type deploys to Documents\The Witcher 3, which is on C: (OneDrive) while the game is on D:;
  a hard link cannot span drives, so hard links drop out for the whole game. Run unelevated, Vortex then raises a UAC
  prompt (consent.exe) on a staging-folder change and on every deploy - and its renderer stops answering DevTools
  until the prompt is gone. Started from an elevated shell, Vortex switches itself to plain symlinks with no prompt.
- Vortex claims nxm:// links on first start and, when that is switched off in Settings > Download, DELETES
  HKCU\Software\Classes\nxm instead of restoring the previous handler. MO2's nxmhandler.exe (it routes to every
  instance in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ModOrganizer\nxmhandler.ini) has to be written back by hand.
- Windows PowerShell 5.1's Compress-Archive writes backslash entry names; build installer zips with Python zipfile and
  forward slashes.
- Vortex's CLI takes `--install-archive "<absolute path>"` (sent to the running instance); its window is driven over
  `--remote-debugging-port` (DevTools), where screenshots are in device pixels (1.5x here) and elementFromPoint wants
  CSS pixels.

**Do instead.** A mod whose loader must be a real game-folder file ships as a FOMOD with the loader choice, not a Root
folder alone. Test a Vortex route in Vortex itself, with the game started from its own folder, and read the loader's
and the mod's logs. After installing Vortex, put the nxm handler back.


## A New Game in a test profile went into the vanilla Helgen cart although Alternate Perspective was ticked - the profile had "Base Game DLC Content" (the DLC .esm files) off (AMF 2.1.3 repro, 2026-10-07)

**Symptom.** Reproducing KnightQueen1's AMF freeze in profile MCM Minimal, the TestBench StartNewGame delegate dropped
the player into the vanilla cart ride. The owner: "You made a big mistake by loading the vanilla scripted start. Every
test instance for Skyrim is supposed to have alternate perspective installed for you to use."

**Cause.** AP was ticked, its plugin active, and JContainers loaded. AlternatePerspective.esp overrides MQ101. But
"Base Game DLC Content", the Njordlinger mod that supplies Dawnguard.esm, HearthFires.esm and Dragonborn.esm (Stock
Game holds only Skyrim.esm and Update.esm), was off in that profile. Papyrus.0.log said `File "Dawnguard.esm" does not
exist or is not currently loaded`. AP's start scripts failed on the missing DLC records, and the vanilla MQ101 ran.

**Why it was convincing.** Every check made on AP itself passed: ticked, plugin `*`-active, requirement loaded, its
translation read in skse64.log. The missing piece was a different mod, and nothing in AMF's or SKSE's logs pointed to
it. Only the Papyrus log did.

**The check.** `.MD\scripts\new-game-start-gate.py` now runs in game-relaunch.ps1. It refuses a profile with Base Game
DLC Content, Alternate Perspective or JContainers off. After StartNewGame, take one frame before any test step: a cart
means stop. When a start mod "does nothing", read Papyrus.0.log for missing-file lines before anything else.

## Nexus edit form in a HIDDEN Chrome tab: call the description editor's React onChange with the new text - Save enables and the save sticks (AMF 2.1.3 post, 2026-10-07)

**What happened.** Patching AMF's live description (190114) with the tab hidden (`document.visibilityState` "hidden",
screenshots timing out): `sceditor.instance(ta).val(new)` + `insert('')` + `updateOriginal()` and a real
`ctrl+End space BackSpace` from the Chrome tool all left both Save buttons disabled; clicking Save twice saved nothing
(the reloaded editor still held the old 35,260 characters).

**Do instead.** Set the text with `inst.val(new)`, then find the editor's React component from the textarea - its
`__reactFiber...` key, `.return.return` - and call its `memoizedProps.onChange(new)` and `onBlur()`. Save enables at
once, in a hidden tab. Before clicking it, compare the form's value with the new text on the fiber's `alternate`
([code removed]; the fiber read first can be the stale copy), then click Save by script and
re-open the edit page to read the saved text back. Patch by anchors, each checked to occur exactly once, keeping the live
U[offset removed] indents.

## A WitcherScript annotation on a player STATE needs the state's class name `<owner>State<state>` - `@wrapMethod(Combat)` does not resolve (Camera Configuration Menu W3 probe, 2026-10-07)

**What was true (REDkit wcc_lite compilescripts over the 5.0 scripts, a probe mod).** `state Combat in CR4Player` is
compiled as the class `CR4PlayerStateCombat`. `@wrapMethod(MountTheVehicle)` failed with "@wrapMethod cannot wrap
'MountTheVehicle::OnGameCameraPostTick' because the class 'MountTheVehicle' is not defined", and so did `Sailing`; with
`CR4PlayerStateExploration`, `CR4PlayerStateCombat`, `CR4PlayerStateSailing`, `CR4PlayerStateMountTheVehicle` and
`CPlayerStateDismountTheVehicle` (that state is declared `in CPlayer`) all five compiled. The compiler reports only some
failing annotations per run, so an earlier run that listed only two errors did NOT mean the short names of the others
worked - change one thing, recompile, until "Success!".

**Do instead.** Annotate a state as `@wrapMethod(<owner class>State<state name>)`, the owner being the class in the
state's `state X in <owner>` line. Dry-compile until the build is clean; never read a partial error list as a pass.

## Root Builder put an OLD AMF loader into every Witcher 3 launch: it copies files the run left in the game folder into overwrite\Root (2026-10-07)

**What happened.** w3-tb.ps1 launch copies AMF's dinput8.dll into the REAL bin\x64_dx12 (MO2's VFS cannot supply it at
process start) and its quit removes it. But Root Builder (copyfiles=**) treats any file that appeared in the game
folder during a run as the game's output and moves it into MO2's `overwrite\Root\` when the game exits - and deploys
everything in overwrite\Root into the game folder at EVERY later launch. A loader from 2026-10-05 sat there and ran
instead of the current one; a MO2 Force-load test was spoiled by it (the game imported that copy, the forced one never
attached).

**Do instead.** After a run, look in `overwrite\Root\` for anything our tooling placed: w3-tb.ps1 quit now moves its
own loader (identified by the AMFLoader string) and AMFLoader.log from there into an instance `_backup-*` folder. When a
loader change seems not to take effect, compare the hash of the dinput8.dll the game actually loaded (AMFLoader.log's
folder) with the build.

## package-gate.ps1 took the FIRST registry entry with the package's display name - a Witcher 3 package was checked against the Oblivion repo (Camera Configuration Menu W3, 2026-10-07)

**Symptom.** `package-gate.ps1` on `7. current test builds\Witcher 3 - Camera Configuration Menu\Camera Configuration Menu 1.0.0`
failed 15 rules, all about `dist\OblivionRemastered\...` files: "the repo ships ...CameraConfigurationMenu.ini but the
package has no file of that name", and every translation "is not the repo's dist\OblivionRemastered\..." file.

**What was true.** With no -RepoPath, the gate walked version-registry.json and stopped at the first entry whose
displayName equalled the package's name. Two games now share display names on purpose (version-gate `rename` allows it
per game: HUD Position Manager, Simple Loadout System, Apocrypha Menu Framework, Camera Configuration Menu), and the
Oblivion entry came first. The package's game was already known (`$pkgGame`, from its "<Game> - <Mod>" folder) and used
for the distro folder and the previous release - not for the repo.

**Fix.** Among several entries with the name, the one whose `Get-ModGame` equals the package's game wins.

**Also learned, same run.** A Witcher 3 `.asi` has no VERSIONINFO unless the build adds one, and `version-gate -Stage
package` then cannot bind the number to the binary (`Find-BuiltDll` looks for *.dll only - pass `-Dll <package>\bin\x64_dx12\<mod>.asi`).
CCM W3 compiles `src\Version.rc` with CCM_VMAJOR/VMINOR/VPATCH defined from xmake's set_version (on_load), so the
FileVersion is the gate-issued number.

**Do instead.** Any tool that maps a mod NAME to a registry entry must disambiguate by game when names repeat across
games. Give every new W3 .asi a version resource from its first build.

## A Witcher 3 mod menu whose string table holds only the BARE displayName keys shows made-up labels - the menu looks up panel_ / option_ / preset_value_ (Simple Loadout System W3, 2026-10-07)

**Symptom.** The owner: in AMF, Simple Loadout System's menu name read "SLs". Its XML: `<Group displayName="Mods.sls_menu">`,
`<Var displayName="sls_menu_count">`, `<Option displayName="sls_count_4">`; its .w3strings held `sls_menu`,
`sls_menu_count`, `sls_count_4` - bare.

**What was true (the game's igmOptions.ws, read 2026-10-07).** The group label is `"panel_" + <segment>`, a var's is
`inGameMenu_TryLocalize("option_" + displayName)`, an option's `"preset_value_" + displayName` unless the var carries the
`customNames` tag (the game's own camera options do, which is why they use bare `menu_*` keys). A missing key shows as
`##<key>` in the game's menu; AMF W3's reader looks up the same prefixed keys and otherwise builds a name from the id
(Humanize). The earlier entry above ("Witcher 3 mod-menu labels are hashed keys") lists the prefixes - SLS's generator
was written without them.

**Fix.** gen_strings.py writes the prefixed keys as well (the bare ones stay: the script reads `sls_loadout` etc.).

**Do instead.** For every displayName in a W3 user_config_matrix XML, the string table needs `panel_<each group segment>`,
`option_<var displayName>` and `preset_value_<option displayName>`; check by reading the .w3strings back for those exact
keys, not the bare ones.

## The texture.cache key is the h*31+c hash of the lower-cased path - NOT FNV-1a 32 (Witcher Gear Overhaul Kaer Morhen relocation, 2026-10-07)

**What was true.** The research sub-agent hashed every entry name of the game's and Dhubleidd's texture.cache: the key at
entry offset 0 equals Java's String.hashCode over the lower-cased path (the same hash as w3strings keys) for 79/79 of
Dhubleidd's and 22,374 of the game's 25,486 entries, and FNV-1a 32 for none. relocate_curv.py (Yennefer Outfits) had
rekeyed with FNV-1a 32; Main Agent fixed it and confirmed 18/18 on its cache. The cache FOOTER checksum is FNV-1a 64
(mip table + names + entries), as relocate_curv had it.

**Do instead.** Rekey a relocated texture with h*31+c of the lower-cased new path, and assert the hash against a few
untouched game entries before writing (tools/relocate_kaer_morhen.py does).

## Witcher 3 HUD: holding a module up with its own fade-in means it never fades again once you stop (2026-10-07)

**What happened.** HUD Position Manager W3's "Always visible" held faded modules up by calling the module's own
ShowElementFromState(true) whenever the game started a fade-out. That sets the module's _shown flag and removes its
update timer, so the game counts it as shown. When the owner switched Always visible OFF, nothing faded: a module with
nothing new to show (full health, no fight) gets no OnUpdate, so no new fade-out timer - every widget stayed up for good.

**Do instead.** Whatever holds a HUD module up must also LET GO explicitly: on release, by its display state
(getState()): "OnUpdate" -> SetUpdateTimer() (fades the usual 3 s after), "Hide" / "OnDemand" ->
ShowElementFromState(false), "Show" -> leave it. Better still, in a module class you build into, override
ShowElementFromState and record the game's own wish before holding, so release can return to exactly that
(hud_wolfstatbars does this per part). Test the OFF switch, not only the ON switch.

## Witcher 3 under MO2: a NEW Mods\mod<name> folder is not loaded until mods.settings lists it - the game did not add it (2026-10-07)

**What happened.** Witcher Gear Overhaul's Kaer Morhen fix shipped a second game mod folder, Mods\modWitcherGearOverhaulArt
(meshes, textures, icons). Main Agent told the owner the game adds new mod folders to mods.settings by itself at start-up.
It did not: the profile's mods.settings (MO2 profile-local, C:\MO2\The Witcher 3\profiles\Default\mods.settings) was not
rewritten at the 08:22 launch, the folder had no [section], and nothing from it loaded - the gear stayed invisible for a
whole test run. Secondary found it by reading the file.

**Do instead.** A package that adds a new Mods\mod<name> folder either (a) puts its content into a folder mods.settings
already lists, or (b) is installed with MO2 closed by a step that adds the [mod<name>] Enabled=1 Priority=<n> section to the
profile's mods.settings (CRLF kept) - as YenneferLatexBattlesuitW3\tools\install_mo2.py does. After the install, check
the section is there; never state that the game will pick it up on its own.

## A NEW Mods folder in the Witcher 3 MO2 profile is not loaded until mods.settings lists it - the game does not add it (Witcher Gear Overhaul Kaer Morhen fix, 2026-10-07)

**Symptom.** Second Kaer Morhen run (08:22): everything from the DLC worked (definitions, names, grades, the item
templates - they hid Geralt's body in the inventory preview), but nothing from the new Mods\modWitcherGearOverhaulArt
loaded: no mesh, no texture, no icon from its texture.cache.

**What was true.** `C:\MO2\The Witcher 3\profiles\Default\mods.settings` lists every Mods folder with Enabled / Priority;
Main Agent adds each install's line by hand (its backups show it). It had no [modWitcherGearOverhaulArt] line, and the
file had not been written since before the launch: the game did not add the new folder. Every static check had passed
(imports resolve, buffers present, texture keys reproduce Longclaw's and ours), which is why the files were blamed first.
The first run's failure was a different one: the same art packed at game-style paths inside the DLC's own bundles,
where every working mod keeps only its dlc\<id>\ paths.

**Do instead.** Put a mod's game-path files in a Mods folder that mods.settings already lists (Witcher Gear Overhaul's own),
or have the installer add the line. When a whole folder's content is missing in game, check mods.settings before the files.
Ship a load probe (LoadResource per kind of file, with a game file as the control) so the next run says which link breaks.

## WitcherScript string literals have NO backslash escape - a depot path is written with single backslashes (Witcher Gear Overhaul load probe, 2026-10-07)

**Symptom.** The Kaer Morhen load probe logged "0 of 8 load" - its control, a game mesh, too - and printed every path with
doubled backslashes ("dlc\\dlcwitchergearoverhaul\\data\\...").

**What was true.** WitcherScript keeps `\` in a string literal as it is; the game's own calls read
`LoadResource("gameplay\templates\signs\pc_igni_proj_cone.w2ent", true)`. The probe had been written C-style
(`"dlc\\dlc..."`), so it asked for paths with two backslashes, which do not exist.

**Do instead.** Write depot paths in .ws with single backslashes, the way the game's scripts do; when a probe reports, check
its control first - a failing control means the probe is wrong, not the files.

## The Witcher 3 Mod Manager (and Relapse's Mod Manager Redux on top of it) never installs bin\x64_dx12 - and takes a FOMOD's XML for menus (2026-10-08)

> **Corrected 2026-10-11 (install-route test, `4. plans\amf-w3-install-routes-2026-10-11.md` and its evidence folder):**
> the heading holds for **TW3MM 0.10.5** only. It installs `Mods\mod*` and the menu XMLs and skips all of
> bin\x64_dx12 silently (source read, and its install code run against a sandbox copy of the game). **RMMR 2.4 DOES
> install bin\x64_dx12**: the .asi, AMF's data, and INIs merged key by key. Disable and uninstall remove what it
> installed, and it backs up and restores an existing dinput8.dll. What neither manager installs is AMF-W3 1.0.3's loader, because the FOMOD keeps it
> at `loader\dinput8.dll` and neither reads FOMODs. Both also drop the fomod's info.xml / ModuleConfig.xml into
> user_config_matrix\pc. With the loader copied into bin\x64_dx12 by hand, AMF loaded and opened in game after both
> managers' installs. With RMMR's files alone, the menu entry is dead. That matches bineko's and Sylaous's reports.

> **Contested 2026-10-07 21:30 (the same user):** after following the by-hand route below the menu
> entry still does nothing, and they say their W3MM "does install bin files" - everything in the archive goes straight
> into the game folder. So the reading of Systemcluster's fetcher.py does not match their build (Relapse's Redux may
> differ), and W3MM was NOT the cause of the dead menu entry. Treat the list below as one W3MM build's behaviour only;
> the dead entry is still open (same symptom as bineko's invisible-menu report - see the AMF-W3 1.0.4 diagnostic build).

**What happened.** A user installed Apocrypha Menu Framework (Witcher 3) and Item Explorer with Relapse's Mod Manager
Redux (a visual fork of The Witcher 3 Mod Manager). It warned it "could not safely merge" user_config_matrix\pc\info.xml
and ModuleConfig.xml, and in game the AMF menu entry showed but clicking it did nothing.

**What was true** (read from W3MM's own scanner, Systemcluster/The-Witcher-3-Mod-manager src/core/fetcher.py, and run
over our real archives):
- It installs ONLY: mod* folders with a content folder (into Mods), dlc folders, EVERY *.xml anywhere in the archive
  except input.xml (into bin\config\r4game\user_config_matrix\pc, AND it adds each to dx11filelist.txt / dx12filelist.txt),
  bin\config\base\*.ini, and key/setting lines scanned out of every *.txt not named readme.
- Nothing under bin\x64_dx12 (our .asi, AMF's data, translations) and no loose loader dll is ever installed. So a
  native mod's script and menu XML land and its native half never does - the AMF game-menu entry is script-only, so
  it shows and does nothing.
- A FOMOD's fomod\info.xml and fomod\ModuleConfig.xml are taken for menu files (installed and listed in both filelists).
- The *.txt scan reads translation lines such as "[Skin] [Log]", "[ ] [ ]", "[*]", "[quest]" as empty input.settings
  sections and adds them to the player's input.settings (empty sections; harmless but clutter).

**Do instead.** For a Witcher 3 mod with a native part, a W3MM install cannot work; the page says so and gives the
by-hand route (copy Mods and bin into the game folder, the loader into bin\x64_dx12, never the fomod folder). A user who
already used W3MM uninstalls it there first (that removes the stray XMLs and their filelist lines). Pure-script mods
(no bin\x64_dx12) install fine with it, as long as the archive has no fomod folder.

## "Couldn't call RaceMenu" from an SKSE plugin = RaceMenu's Papyrus scripts never linked: the instance had NO SKSE scripts, and RaceMenu wants the scripts of the exact SKSE build (2026-10-07)

**What happened.** Testing NPC Preset Applier (NPA) under AMF 2.1.4 in the AE 1.6.1170 test instance, NPA's "Save my
look" said it couldn't call RaceMenu, and the portrait batch crashed (SkyrimSE[offset removed], a null VM object). The VM's
CharGen type held only DeleteFaceGenData, although RaceMenu.bsa carries the full [asset name removed]. It looked like a path
mismatch between NPA and RaceMenu.

**What was true.** Papyrus.0.log (needs bEnableLogging=1 under [Papyrus] in the profile's Skyrim.ini): `Cannot open
store for class "ColorForm"`, then `Unable to link type of variable "_hairColor" on object "RaceMenu"` and `Unable to
bind script RaceMenu ... base types do not match`. ColorForm is an SKSE script. The instance had no SKSE scripts at
all - the game root's Data\Scripts held 0 loose .pex and no MO2 mod shipped them - so every RaceMenu script that names
an SKSE type failed to link and its functions were missing from the VM. With the 2.2.6 scripts added, RaceMenu then
showed "SKSE script version mismatch detected (72) expected (73)": it checks the scripts against the running SKSE
build, so the scripts must come from the SAME archive as the DLL (2.2.8 here).

**Do instead.** A test instance's SKSE is ONE MO2 mod holding both halves: Root\skse64_loader.exe +
Root\skse64_<runtime>.dll (Root Builder) and Scripts\ from the same archive. Before reading a RaceMenu / CharGen /
NiOverride failure as a mod bug, grep Papyrus.0.log for "Cannot open store" and "Unable to link".

## Root Builder restores the game root's original files when MO2 closes - a file copied into the root by hand is silently undone (2026-10-07)

**What happened.** SKSE 2.2.6 in `<MO2>\AE 1.6.1170 Test Game Root` was replaced by hand with 2.2.8 (2.2.6
renamed .bak-2.2.6). The next launch ran 2.2.6 again and NPA was refused ("fatal error occurred while loading plugin").

**What was true.** The instance runs Root Builder (copyfiles=**, autobuild=true). It backs the root up on first build
and, on MO2 exit, "Clearing deployed files" then "Restoring files from backup" - putting its backed-up 2.2.6 files
back over the hand copy. mo_interface.log shows it, and a "Could not delete file ...bak-2.2.6" warning on every exit.

**Do instead.** Never edit a Root Builder instance's game root by hand. Put the file in a mod's Root\ folder and let
Root Builder deploy it. Check `ModOrganizer.ini` for RootBuilder\ keys before touching a root.

## A SkyrimSE.exe stuck in kernel teardown keeps its SKSE log files open - NPA then fails to load on every launch ("fatal error"), and other plugins log to *.log0 (2026-10-07)

**What happened.** After NPA loaded once on SKSE 2.2.8, the next launch refused it again with "fatal error occurred
while loading plugin", and NPA.log was 0 bytes. skse64.log had been empty for hours (SKSE wrote skse64.log0).

**What was true.** An earlier SkyrimSE (pid 26180) had been stuck for an hour in teardown: one thread, wait reason
Unknown, 1,538 handles still open - prockill, taskkill and Stop-Process all fail on it. It still held NPA.log,
skse64.log, skee64.log and seven other plugin logs. NPA's spdlog rotating sink renames NPA.log on start; the rename
throws on the held file and SKSE reports it as a fatal load error. The Restart Manager API (RmGetList) names the
holder in one call.

**Do instead.** When a plugin's log is 0 bytes and the plugin is "disabled, fatal error", check who holds the log
(RmGetList, or try opening it with share None). Close just the held handles from outside: enumerate the process's
handles (NtQuerySystemInformation class 64), keep FILE_TYPE_DISK ones whose path matches, and DuplicateHandle with
DUPLICATE_CLOSE_SOURCE (scratchpad close_remote_handle.ps1 did it for 13 handles; the plugins then loaded and logged
normally). Only a reboot ends the process itself.

## A PowerShell 5.1 inline `(if ...)` in an expression emptied the AE test profile's modlist.txt while MO2 started - and MO2 then emptied plugins.txt and loadorder.txt (2026-10-07)

**What happened.** A one-line profile edit built the new modlist with an `if` used as a value inside an expression.
PowerShell 5.1 does not accept `if` as an expression there; the pipeline produced nothing, the empty result was
written to modlist.txt, and MO2 (launched in the same command) read the empty list and wrote empty plugins.txt and
loadorder.txt.

**Do instead.** Profile edits go through a script file that refuses to write when the line count changes and when MO2
or the game runs (scratchpad ae_profile_only.ps1 is the pattern); never in a one-liner chained to a launch. Keep a
.bak of modlist.txt, plugins.txt and loadorder.txt before every edit.

## TestBench's `input` tool (BSInputEventQueue) crashes the AE 1.6.1170 game on any key; `bench.input` is the safe one (2026-10-07)

**What happened.** Several AE test runs died without a clear cause while keys were being sent with the devbench
`input` tool. Switching to `bench.input` (InputBench: the press spliced into the input event list ahead of the
plugins, device keyboard|gamepad|mouse) ended it; it also drives AMF's controller navigation with real gamepad codes

**Do instead.** In the AE instance press keys and buttons only with `bench.input`. A vanilla message box (Survival
Mode, RaceMenu's error box) ignores spliced keys and buttons; `amf.menu op=open` still opens AMF over it. Also:
`skee` console commands run through the devbench console crash skee64 (no console target) - not a valid way to test
RaceMenu presets.

## AMF never sent SKSE Menu Framework's menu and frame events - a mod doing its work in them (NPC Preset Applier's portrait maker) waited forever with no error (2026-10-07)

**What happened.** NPA's window drew under AMF, but "Generate missing" portraits started and never finished. Nothing
in any log said why.

**What was true.** SMF 3 dispatches four events from its render hook: 1 open, 2 close, 3 before-render (before ImGui's
NewFrame), 4 after-render (after the draw). Mods register for them (RegisterEventPriority) and NPA steps its portrait
batch from them. AMF exported the registration and stored the listeners but never fired anything.

**Do instead.** AMF fires them where SMF does (Renderer.cpp PresentHook: open/close on the edge of its menu or a
blocking mod window, before-render after the D3D ready gate, after-render after RenderDrawData). When adding SMF
parity, compare BEHAVIOUR (what SMF calls and when), not only the export list - a stored callback that is never called
passes every export check.

## An ImGui button whose label shows its state (+/-, A-Z/Z-A, "(13)") became a new item on every press - A worked once, then did nothing until the highlight moved off and back (AMF 2.1.5, 2026-10-07)

**What happened.** The owner, testing 2.1.5 by controller: a folded separator "will not let me unfold it until I select
a different separator", and the Filter word's +/- button would not cycle "without switching with the D-pad down to
something else and then reselecting". The A-Z switch and the MCM key buttons had the same fault, unreported.

**What was true.** ImGui makes an item's ID from its label. `"+##state"` still hashes the "+" (only `###` resets the
hash), and a label that changes with the state (`Name  (13)` folded, `Name` open; `PushID(label)` in widgets::Toggle)
makes the pressed item vanish and a new one appear. The nav highlight keeps the old ID, so the next A activates
nothing. A mouse click re-hovers the new item and hides it - it shows only on the controller.

**Do instead.** Any widget whose visible text depends on its own value gets a fixed ID: `"<text>###name"` (works for
PushID too). When reviewing a controller fix, grep for widgets built from a ternary or a value string.

## Setting UI::numPausesGame to 0 under the open journal froze Skyrim on the spot - never take another menu's pause count (AMF 2.1.5, 2026-10-08)

**What happened.** A converted MCM page (Atlas Map Markers) never loaded while AMF was open, because its scripts wait
while the game is paused. Letting go of AMF's OWN pause count while a page's script call waited fixed it for AMF opened
on its own (F1). Opened from the journal's System row the journal's count still held, so the next build also took the
journal's count away (numPausesGame = 0, given back after). The game drew no frame after that line, stopped
responding, kept the owner's mouse cursor hidden, and had to be killed.

**What was true.** A pausing menu's count is that menu's state, not a number to borrow. With the journal open and
numPausesGame at 0 the engine hung at once, before the give-back could run (the render thread that would have asked
for it never ran again). A DevBench probe had shown a plain Papyrus call answering with the journal open; that did
not mean a page's own scripts would, and it said nothing about what lowering the count would do.

**Do instead.** Only ever add and remove the one count AMF itself holds (g_pauseHeld). For a script that needs the
game unpaused while a game menu is open, change how the menu is opened (close the journal first), never the count.
Before trying any change to engine pause/menu state on the owner's live game, try it on a test launch first - a hang
there takes his cursor with it.

## package-mod -Force after its own prune had no seed left and wrote a flat package with no README, LICENSE, NOTICE or fomod (Carryweight on Level Up 1.0.7, 2026-10-08)

**What happened.** The first `package-mod.ps1 -Mod CarryweightOnLevelUp` run built 1.0.7 seeded from the 1.0.6 test
build, then its end-of-run prune removed the 1.0.4 and 1.0.6 test builds (both already finalized). After a code fix, a
second run needed `-Force` to overwrite 1.0.7: it deleted the old 1.0.7 first, found no package left in
`7. current test builds` to seed from, and fell back to the canonical flat layout - the DLLs landed in Line-17 and
Line-SE-AE16, but Common\, README.txt, LICENSE, NOTICE.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and fomod\ were gone. The package gate
caught it (license-file-is-the-gpl-text, notice-file-present, readme-carries-the-version).

**Do instead.** For a repackage of the same version, seed from the finalized previous release
(`10. finalized mods\<Game> - <Mod>\<Mod> <prev>`), not from a `-Force` overwrite: copy it, swap the DLL/PDB pairs per
line, retarget README / fomod\info.xml / Common\CHANGELOG.md. Read the README's "Version" headings while retargeting -
Carryweight's 1.0.6 README labelled the 1.0.4 language note and the 1.0.5 relicense both "1.0.6", and a blind replace
would have renamed 1.0.6's notes to 1.0.7.


## install-test-build.py never removes a file the new package dropped - the old art layers kept drawing in game (AMF 2.1.6, 2026-10-08)

**What happened.** AMF 2.1.6 stopped shipping the selectable controls' `-edge.png` layers (and the scroll bar's old
`-track` files). `install-test-build.py` copied the new package over the MO2 mod folder and read back every file the
package owns - but the 39 files the package no longer had stayed in the folder, and AMF found and drew them: the frames
the owner had asked to remove were still in game. Nothing reported it; the read-back only checks what the package ships.

**Do instead.** After installing a build that REMOVES assets, move every file under the mod's own asset folders that the
package does not contain out of the MO2 folder (to a dated backup, never a hard delete). The one-off that did it this time
is `.MD\scripts\prune-stale-mod-assets.py` (AMF paths set at its top: package tree vs `mods\<Mod>\...\assets`; moved 39). Fold it
into `install-test-build.py` as a `--prune-stale <subfolder>` step and add a gate row the same day (backlog item).

## desktop-grab.ps1 captures the HDR desktop about 2.2x too bright - saturated colours clip, greys look right (AMF 2.1.6, 2026-10-08)

**Symptom.** A switch drawn in (76,175,80) green read back (169,255,171); the Skyrim theme's gold headings (216,194,122)
read pure white; greys (153) read about right. The owner's own Steam F12 screenshot of the same menu had the true colours.
`amf.process op=capture` came back black (the AMD capture fault), so desktop-grab was the only working capture.

**Cause.** The desktop grab samples the HDR desktop and maps it to SDR without tone mapping - roughly x2.2 linear, clipped.

**Do instead.** Use desktop-grab for SHAPE and LAYOUT only. Never judge or report a colour from it; ask the owner for a
Steam screenshot, or sample a known reference colour in the same grab first and say how far it is off.

## A converted SkyUI script menu that 'never loads' on a loaded save is usually its own mod still starting up - Honed Metal answered only after a couple of minutes (AMF 2.1.6, 2026-10-08)

**Symptom.** Honed Metal's (and Heavy Nordic Armor Crafting Tweaks') AMF page sat on "Loading"; AMF's script queue logged
`"OpenConfig (Honed Metal)" has not finished after 15 s` again and again, even with the game unpaused and AMF closed for
30 s. On a NEW game Claude saw it open instantly once its script logged "INITIALIZED"; the owner then saw it load after
waiting a couple of minutes on his save.

**Cause.** The mod's own start-up: Honed Metal waits `iLoadingDelay` (7 s, real time outside menus) and then loads its
settings on every load; with ~100 mods' scripts starting at once ("VM Overstressed" on screen) its script answers nothing
until that is done. Not AMF - the script-menu code is unchanged since 2.1.5.

**Do instead.** Before debugging a "won't load" script menu, check how long since the load and whether the overlay says
VM Overstressed; give it two minutes. The Nexus page's Installation section now tells players to wait a couple of minutes
after a new game. (Fixed alongside: AMF re-paused the game 3 s into a script call, which guaranteed a 15 s stall when
"pause while open" was on - it now stays unpaused until the call ends or the cut-off.)

## An SKSE Menu Framework mod laid out with SameLine(<pixels>) puts its control ON its label at a big text size - fixed in AMF's SameLine export, not per mod (Show Player In Inventory, 2026-10-08)

**Symptom.** Show Player In Inventory's sliders covered "Offset X" and its bind button sat on "Rotate Button" (AMF at
its native resolution, text 1.5). Its source: [code removed]
- a pixel column sized for SMF's small text. (It is an SMF mod; its newer GitHub source has moved to FLICK's API - read the
source of the INSTALLED version.)

**Do instead.** Not a theme or fill problem (a transparent field was tried and reverted). `tools/harden-cimgui.py` now
routes the `igSameLine` export through `amf_ConsumerSameLine` (ConsumerSurface.cpp): the column is kept when the label fits;
when it would land on the label the next item starts after it. Consumers only; AMF's own code calls ImGui directly.

## Two Witcher 3 mods' menu labels could show each other's text - both had taken .w3strings idspace 7715, each as "the next one after the last I knew of" (New Game Plus Max Level / HUD Position Manager W3, 2026-10-07)

**What happened.** New Game Plus Max Level's test page and Square Minimap (now HUD Position Manager W3) were written in
parallel and both set `ID_BASE = 2117715000` - each generator's docstring said "next to" the previous mod's idspace. With
both ticked, ids 2117715001-2117715004 existed twice and one mod's labels could take the other's text. Nothing caught
it: each mod's own `gen_strings.py --check` round-trips only its own file.

**Fix.** NG+ moved to 7717 (2117717000 + n; Multi Companion had already reserved 7717 for it and taken 7718). A scan of
every `.w3strings` under `C:\MO2\The Witcher 3\mods` with `tools/w3strings.py read_ids` showed no id in 7710-7719 used by
two mods afterwards.

**Do instead.** Before choosing an idspace for a new Witcher 3 mod, grep `ID_BASE` across `6. current wip mods\*W3\tools`
AND scan the installed mods' string tables for the range - never take "the one after the last I remember". Taken on
2026-10-08: 7712 UVC, 7713 SLS, 7714 Witcher Gear Overhaul, 7715 HUD Position Manager, 7716 Yennefer Outfits, 7717 NG+ Max
Level, 7718 Multi Companion; next free 7719.

**Side lesson (versioning).** `version-gate.ps1 -Action reopen` refuses while a `vX.Y.Z` tag exists, even a LOCAL one in
a repo with no remote, and tells you to bump - but the owner's rule (memory github-release-waits-for-nexus) is that an
unposted version keeps its number and its tag moves. For an unpushed local tag: note the commit, `git tag -d`, reopen,
and re-tag after the version is recorded working again.

## A Witcher 3 mod replaces the game's files BY PATH from its own Mods\mod*\content bundles - a tool that reads only content0 shows vanilla where the player sees the mod (Item Explorer W3 1.0.1, 2026-10-07)

**Symptom.** The owner: Item Explorer's 3D card drew the vanilla Kaer Morhen armour while Geralt wore "[Remastered]
Dhubleidd Gear - Kaer Morhen Gear"; then "I still don't see the boots, gloves, and trousers for Kaer Morhen armor" -
Witcher Gear Overhaul renames them in its own DLC.

**Cause.** The reader indexed only `content\content0\bundles\*.bundle`, `content0\texture.cache` and `content0\*.w3strings`.
The game reads a depot path from the highest-priority source that has it: mods (`Mods\mod*\content\*.bundle` and
`texture.cache` - only folders whose names start with "mod"), then `dlc\*\content`, then content0. Mod order: `Documents\The
Witcher 3\mods.settings` (Enabled=0 skips, lower Priority wins; the owner's is empty), then folder names in ASCII order, the
first winning. Under MO2 the game process sees the profile's ticked mods through the VFS, so `GameRoot\Mods` and `\dlc` just
work. Item definitions come from every source's `gameplay\items\*.xml` (mods' DLC: `dlc\<name>\data\gameplay\items\`),
merged in load order with `on_conflict="extend"`; names from every source's `<lang>.w3strings`, highest priority first.

**Three format traps found on the way (all mods built for the original game):**
- bundle compression **4 and 5 are both an LZ4 block** (5 = LZ4 HC, same decoder); the reader only knew zlib;
- **texture.cache version 6** (original game) has the same 52-byte entries and block chain as 5.0's version 7 - accept both;
- **bundle TOC entries are [value removed] bytes** in the original game (u32 0, size, stored, offset, u64 time, 16 zero, crc,
  compression after the md5) vs [value removed] in 5.0. A TOC can be a multiple of both (6080 bytes) - pick the layout in which EVERY
  entry has a name, compression <= 5 and offset+stored inside the file.

**How it was proven offline.** A stand-in game folder in the scratchpad: a junction `content` -> the real content folder,
junctions `Mods\modX` / `dlc\dlcX` -> the MO2 mods' own folders; run model_test / catalog_test on it and compare with the
real game folder (Starting Armor 15515 verts with Dhubleidd vs 12485 vanilla; WGO names). **Remove such junctions with
`rmdir <junction>` before the scratchpad is cleaned** - a recursive delete that follows reparse points would delete the
real mods.

**Rule.** For Witcher 3 (and any game with path-overriding mod archives), a tool that shows game data resolves every path
the way the game does - all sources, the game's order - or it shows the wrong thing for exactly the players who mod.

## An ImGui window that must never take the controller highlight: NoNav + NoFocusOnAppearing, hand the focus back on any click, and own the pad's B with SetKeyOwner - ImGui's nav cancel reads B only when nobody owns it (Item Explorer W3, 2026-10-07)

**Asked.** The owner: the item card "view only ... the controller navigation should not leave where it's at" - View or
"Show the selected item" opens/updates the card while the highlight stays on the row.

**What it took.** (1) Window flags `ImGuiWindowFlags_NoNav | ImGuiWindowFlags_NoFocusOnAppearing` (no `SetNextWindowFocus`).
(2) Each frame, if the card window is focused (a mouse click) and `!IsAnyItemActive()`, `FocusWindow(pageWindow)` - after a
drag of the model ends, not during it (FocusWindow clears an ActiveId in another window). (3) B: with the highlight in the
list, ImGui's `NavUpdateCancelRequest` (in NewFrame) took B and moved the highlight out of the child window before page code
ran. It checks `IsKeyPressed(ImGuiKey_NavGamepadCancel, 0, ImGuiKeyOwner_NoOwner)` (1.90.8), so the page calls
`SetKeyOwner(ImGuiKey_GamepadFaceRight, ownerId)` every frame while a card is open, reads the press with
`IsKeyPressed(key, ImGuiInputFlags_None, ownerId)` to close the card, and sets the owner back to `ImGuiKeyOwner_NoOwner`
once it is closed - the next B leaves the list as before. Ownership set this frame applies from the next NewFrame.

**Rule.** To stop ImGui's own navigation acting on a pad button, OWN the key (key ownership), don't race it after the
fact - by the time page code runs, NewFrame has already acted.

## A shader embedded by a CMake configure-time step is NOT refreshed by build.bat - the DLL keeps the old HLSL until configure runs (Local Map Upgrade 1.3.3, 2026-10-08)

**Symptom.** After editing `shaders\ISLocalMap.hlsl` (MIN_ALPHA), `build.bat` linked a new DLL, but
`include\ISLocalMap.hlsl.h` - the string the DLL embeds - still had the old text.

**Cause.** `make_includable()` in CMakeLists.txt writes the header with `file(COPY_FILE ... ONLY_IF_DIFFERENT)` at CONFIGURE
time; `cmake --build` (build.bat) does not reconfigure for a changed .hlsl because the .hlsl is not a configure input.

**Fix.** Run `configure.bat` (and `configure17.bat` for the 1.7 line) after changing the .hlsl, then build; check the header
holds the new text before packaging. A version bump also needs a reconfigure (CMakeLists project VERSION).

**Rule.** When a build embeds a generated source, find WHEN it is generated; a successful link proves nothing about it.

## Two edit-tooling traps: the Write tool drops the spaces of whitespace-only lines, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less UTF-8 .ps1 as ANSI (2026-10-07)

**Symptom 1.** A Python edit script written with the Write tool asserted an anchor containing a blank line that, in the
source file, held four spaces; the anchor never matched (count 0) - the Write tool had saved the script's blank line empty.
**Do instead:** anchor on non-blank lines only, or make the edit with the Edit tool directly on the file.

**Symptom 2.** `package.ps1` (UTF-8, no BOM, written from Python) compared README text containing "·" (U[offset removed]); PowerShell 5.1
decoded the script as ANSI, the literal became mojibake and the README line was "not found". **Do instead:** keep .ps1
files ASCII - build such characters with `[string][char][value removed]` - or save them with a BOM. Check:
`python -c "print([c for c in open(p,encoding='utf-8').read() if ord(c)>127])"`.

## Hosting another mod's own ImGui tool in AMF: OAR and IED each run their OWN ImGui context on the SAME game call sites as AMF; OAR has an open/close API, IED does not, and OAR's bEnableUI=false installs no UI at all (research, 2026-10-07)

Full study: `4. plans\amf-2.1.5\imgui-tool-menus-feasibility.md`. The facts most likely to be needed again:
- AMF, Open Animation Replacer and Immersive Equipment Displays all `write_call` the same sites: present
  `75461/77246 [value removed]`, D3D creation `75595/77226`, input `67315/68617 [value removed]`. The trampolines chain in DLL load order
  (alphabetical); the last installed runs first, so while OAR's window is open OAR hands AMF an EMPTY input list.
- Each links its own ImGui statically (IED: its author's fork "1.86 WIP"; OAR: 1.89.6; AMF: 1.90.8) - separate GImGui,
  incompatible structs: drawing them INSIDE an AMF window is not feasible without rebuilding them against AMF.
- OAR exports `RequestPluginAPI_UI` (interface V3: OpenMenu / CloseMenu / ToggleMenu / IsMenuOpen /
  SetSuppressMenuHotkey); IED exports only the SKSE entry points (open it by splicing its ToggleKeys, reliable only with
  `OverrideToggleKeys=true`).
- With `OpenAnimationReplacer.ini [UI] bEnableUI = false` (the owner's Njordlinger, via "Open Animation - No Main Menu
  GUI") OAR installs no UI hooks - OpenMenu would open nothing. `bShowWelcomeBanner = false` hides the banner instead.
- Neither tool can be navigated with a controller.

## A Nexus page's public Images tab lists one page of images - a backup built from it missed 26 of AMF's 50 gallery images (2026-10-08)

**What happened.** Before replacing AMF's gallery, the backup URL list was read from `?tab=images` on the public page:
24 images plus the header. The media editor (`/games/<game>/mods/<id>/edit/media`) showed 50. The other 26 would have
been deleted unarchived if the editor's count had not been checked first.

**Do instead.** Read every image URL from the media editor's tiles (the tile's React props hold `image.url` and
`backendId`), compare the count with the editor's gallery, and only then run nexus-media-backup.py. The same props hold
`image.file.name` for tiles uploaded in that session: that is how uploads are matched to their files, because Nexus
ignores the file name and titles every upload "No title". The editor's own requests, captured by hooking fetch, are
`media/images` with `edit-title`, `set-gallery-visibility` (show:0 hides from the gallery and the URL keeps working),
`set-primary` and `delete`, then `media/save`; `media-editor-helpers.js` wraps them. The Chrome tool's output is cut
near 1,000 characters (and some URL-like text is blocked), so read long lists in slices.

## Pictures with loading="lazy" inside a closed details element never loaded in the artifact viewer on the owner's PC - fine on his phone (2026-10-08)

**What happened.** The AMF demo artifact showed broken images on PC in every drop-down; the phone was fine. Removing
lazy loading and setting `src` when a drop-down opens fixed the first symptom. The owner's PC tab had also been open
a long time. Flattening the image folders made no difference: nested paths were served too.

**Do instead.** In artifact pages, load pictures for hidden sections on demand (`data-src`, set on the toggle event)
rather than relying on lazy loading, and if a viewer still shows broken images, have the owner reload with Ctrl+F5
before changing paths.

## A tool that copies session transcripts into new files copies the secrets the owner pasted into them - a login token reached an archive-sweep digest in plain text (2026-10-08)

**Symptom.** The archive sweep's `session-digest.py` wrote everything the owner typed in each archived session into a
digest file. The batch 5 checking agent found a complete Claude login token on line 10 of one digest: the owner had
pasted it into a chat on 2026-09-25 while setting up his login.

**Cause.** The extractor treated "what the owner typed" as safe to copy because it is his own text. But owners paste
credentials into chats (tokens, keys, passwords), and a transcript is the one place every such paste survives. Any
derived file - a digest, a report, a cache - multiplies the copies, and a later reader (a sub-agent, a commit, a share)
spreads it further. The safety classifier then correctly refused a grep that would have printed part of the token.

**Fix.** `session-digest.py` redacts anything shaped like an API key, OAuth token or JWT before writing (`SECRET_RE`),
the digests were regenerated (1 redaction), the sweep reports and the skill-scout cache were scrubbed with the same
pattern without printing any match, and the checking agents are told never to copy a credential. The owner was asked
to confirm the token was revoked.

**Rule.** Any tool that copies text out of transcripts, logs or chats redacts secrets at the point it writes, and its
checks report counts, never matches. Never search for a secret by printing it.

## When a tool refusal's error text is mangled, isolate the operation - never infer the cause from the truncation (2026-09-12, saved 2026-10-08)

*Owed since 2026-09-12: five attempts to save it were refused, and its text survived only in that day's handoff. The
2026-10-08 archive sweep found it.*

**Symptom.** A script writing to LOGIC-LIBRARY.md was refused with `Remove-Item on system path ''D:\Claude' is
blocked`. The truncated `'D:\Claude` looked like decisive evidence of a word-split at the space in the project root,
so an entry was drafted asserting exactly that - and the call meant to save it refused identically, falsifying the
explanation within one tool call. A second theory (any `Remove-Item` poisons the whole script) was drafted next, and a
later script with no `Remove-Item` refused too. Neither survived.

**Cause.** What is established, and deliberately nothing more: a script doing ONE simple thing to a file under the
project root succeeds; `AppendAllText` and `Directory::Delete` both work as the sole operation; the refusals came from
scripts doing several things at once. The precise trigger was never pinned down.

**Fix.** Writes went through one-operation scripts. Entry "Gotcha: a command refused as touching a system path..."
(2026-09-11) now carries a caveat that its mechanism is unproven.

**Rule.** Treat a truncated value in an error as an artefact of the reporting, not a clue; isolate one operation per
script until the refusal reproduces; keep a write you care about out of any script that also deletes or rewrites in
place, because a refusal is all-or-nothing and silently loses the rest; and never write a mechanism into this library
until it has been demonstrated - a wrong entry here is worse than none, because it is the file every future session
trusts. The only reason a false mechanism did not land here permanently is that the save kept failing: luck, not
process.

## A propose-then-apply tool that re-runs its proposal on --apply overwrites the reviewed input; a verbatim script handed to a low-level agent is proof-run by its author first (pipeline restructure plan, 2026-10-08)

**Symptom.** The memory-topics tool written into `STEPS.md` step 0.7 for a Haiku agent has two phases: `--report`
proposes topics per memory into a JSON the main session edits, then `--apply` writes the reviewed JSON into the
memory files. Run end to end on six copied memories, `--apply` stopped at the first file with "no topics decided" -
although the JSON had been edited to give that file a topic.

**Cause.** The proposal code sat at the top of the script unconditionally, so the `--apply` invocation regenerated
the proposal JSON before reading it, discarding the review. It looked right because each phase was correct on its
own; the defect was in what ran BEFORE the apply branch, and a reader following the apply branch never saw it. A
Haiku agent handed the script verbatim could not have debugged it: its instruction was "create the file and run it".

**Fix.** The proposal write is guarded (`if "--apply" not in sys.argv`). Found only because the author extracted the
three verbatim scripts from the plan and ran them on real data before hand-over; the other two (the reference
counter, the distro golden harness) ran clean.

**Rule.** Two rules. (1) A tool with a review step between two phases must never regenerate the reviewed artefact in
the second phase; the test is "edit the proposal, run apply, confirm the edit landed". (2) Any script written out
verbatim in a plan for an agent that cannot debug it is run by the plan's author first, on real data, with its
output pasted beside it - the plan is not finished until that run exists. One proof run of three scripts found one
defect; the agent would have reported a failure the main session could not have explained from the plan text.

## Nexus's new edit UI: a file's "File options" description is a React field whose visible textarea is a decoy - typing, form_input and native setters all "save successfully" and change nothing; set it through the parent component's onChange(value) (2026-10-08)

**Symptom.** Adding an incompatibility note to the main file's description on skyrimspecialedition/190114 (the owner:
"add the note ... to the files options in the Nexus page"). The dialog at `/games/<game>/mods/<id>/edit/files` ->
More actions -> Edit -> Toggle file options shows a 255-character Description box. Typing into it with real keys,
`form_input`, and the React native-setter-plus-input-event trick each left the box showing the new text; "Save file"
answered "File saved successfully."; the public Files tab still carried the old text. Three saves, no change.

**Cause.** The dialog holds TWO textareas. The visible one (95 px, `maxlength=255`, no React props) is a plain
element the page syncs by its own means; the real field is a `display: none` textarea with React props
(`ref`, `defaultValue`) whose PARENT fiber carries `onChange`, and that handler is `e => a("description", e)` - it
takes the VALUE as its argument, not an event. Nothing done to either textarea reaches that handler, so the
component state never changed and Save wrote the old state back. The "25/255" counter never moved either, which was
the one honest signal and was read as "a static label" instead of "state unchanged".

**Fix.** From the hidden textarea's `__reactFiber$` key walk `.return` to the first `memoizedProps.onChange`, call it
with the string, then click Save; verify on the PUBLIC Files tab (`?tab=files`), not by reopening the dialog, which
re-renders from the same stale store and showed the old text even after a real save. Saved on the fourth attempt.

**Rule.** On a React form, a success toast proves the request was sent, not that the state carried the edit - verify
on a fresh public read. When a counter or any derived display does not move after an edit, the state did not change,
whatever the box shows. And when the visible control has no React props, look for the hidden one that has them and
call its handler with what the handler's source says it takes (`h.toString()` is one line and settles it).

## A rename swept as plain text rewrote the owner's quoted words in five memories (pipeline restructure 9.1a, 2026-10-09)

**Symptom.** After `LOGIC-LIBRARY.md` was renamed `PAST-MISTAKES-LIBRARY.md`, a sub-agent replaced "logic library"
with "past-mistakes library" in every memory file, as the step told it to. Five memories then quoted the owner as
