saying "make that your specific past-mistakes library" - words he never said - and the memory about the NEW catalogue
now claimed the new PAST-MISTAKES-LIBRARY.md "catalogues logics", the opposite of what it records.

**Cause.** The step treated a name as a string. A memory holds two kinds of text: our prose, which should follow a
rename, and the owner's quotations (`*"..."*`), which are a record of what he said on a date and must never change.
It also mixed two meanings of the old name: "the mistakes file" (renamed) and "the logic catalogue" (which keeps
the old file name). A blind replace cannot tell either difference, and the step's own check (files changed, counts)
measured the sweep, not its meaning.

**Fix.** The main session restored the five quotations to the owner's words and rewrote the catalogue memory by hand;
the governing documents were then swept with a script that changes the prose name only OUTSIDE `*"..."*` spans, and
a scan for the new name inside quotation spans confirmed zero left.

**Root cause:** the plan specified the rename as a text substitution without separating quoted record from current
prose, because no tool or rule marks a quotation as immutable.

**Rule.** A rename or wording sweep over memories, rules or records leaves the owner's quotations untouched: replace
outside `*"..."*` spans only, and after the sweep scan the quotation spans for the new name (the count must be zero).
When a name changes meaning (here: the old file name passes to a new document), list each sentence that names it and
decide it by hand - those are a handful, and they are exactly the ones a blind replace gets wrong.


## A build that copies live files by path broke silently when the restructure moved them behind stubs; the kit nearly shipped retired-path stubs and literal byte-order marks (Pipeline Kit 1.0.2 rebuild, 2026-10-10)

**Symptom.** Asked to update the Pipeline Kit in its distro folder, `build_kit.py --check` failed on
"rewrite did not match in version-gate.ps1". The 2026-10-09 restructure had moved every script into a kind folder
(`scripts\gates\`, `release\`, `ops\` ...) and left a 4-line RETIRED-PATH stub at each old path. It had also turned
four documents into 3-line "moved" pointers and renamed the mistakes library. The build read every one of those old
paths. It failed on the first rewrite only by luck: a script with no rewrite would have shipped its stub, which calls the
owner's absolute `D:\` path. Once the build was ported, the package gate failed on five interior U+FEFF characters. They
were literal in the LIVE `gate-rules.json` (the two BOM rules' own patterns) and in this library's prose about entry 9578.
The kit is the only package that ships those files.

**Root cause:** the build named its sources by remembered path, not by role, and had no check that a source was the real
file. A restructure that keeps old paths working through stubs makes a path-based copier read the stub without any error.

**Fix.** The build (ported by a sub-agent) now finds each script at its real location, mirrors the live layout, ships the
resolver with rosters filtered to what the kit carries (identity values become placeholders), and FAILS on any
RETIRED-PATH stub or "moved" pointer document. Its leak patterns now match doubled backslashes (`[\\/]+`), because a single
`[\\/]` let `D:\\...` inside string literals through. `sanitise()` writes any interior U+FEFF as the `\ufeff` escape. The
live `gate-rules.json` was fixed the same day at the owner's go-ahead (1.0.1: the two patterns written as the escape, by
a text edit, never json.dumps; the four package-script-passes rows pointed at `gates\`). Other lessons from the port:
a resolver copied into `dist` takes the folder above `dist` as its root, so any build step that calls it runs in a staged
`<tmp>\.MD`; a self-test that installs a memory folder must point USERPROFILE at its temp folder.

**Rule.** Anything that copies live pipeline files out (a kit, a package, an export) asks the resolver for each source
and refuses a stub or pointer file it reads. After any restructure, rebuild every such export the same day.


## A kit that leaves the machine shipped the owner's name in capitals, reused a number after packaging, and listed hashes no member could match (Pipeline Kit 1.0.2 -> 1.0.3, 2026-10-10)

**Symptom.** An outside review of the 1.0.2 zip, pasted in by the owner, found three things. (1) "It took the owner proposing
it twice" in PAST-MISTAKES-LIBRARY.md. (2) Two different zips both called 1.0.2: the 2026-10-08 build, already packaged
in its distro folder, and the 2026-10-10 rebuild. (3) 71 of 103 MANIFEST.json hashes did not match the shipped files.

**Root cause:** (1) the name substitution and the leak scan both matched `\b<owner-name>\b` case-sensitively, so an emphasis
spelling passed both. (2) The rule that an untested number is reused was applied to a build that had already gone
into a distro folder. The rule is written for test builds that never left the machine, and a member cannot tell
two zips with the same number apart. (3) The manifest hashed the live SOURCE file, before sanitising, under a key
that read as the shipped file's hash.

**Fix.** 1.0.3: substitution and leak scan match the name in any capitalisation. A new gate row,
`shipped-text-carries-no-owner-name` (`[pattern removed]`, spelled so the rules file does not carry the name), fails
any package; it hits the 1.0.2 package and clears 1.0.3. MANIFEST.json gains `files` (every file's hash as shipped,
124/124 verified) and renames the pre-sanitising hash to `source_sha256`, with an `_about` line. A new number was
issued.

**Rule.** A privacy match is case-insensitive in both the substitution and the scan. Once a build has been copied into a
distro folder (or anywhere a person could take it from), any rebuild gets a NEW number, even if the ledger still says
untested. Every hash a package ships describes the shipped bytes, or it is labelled as describing something else.


## The event log could count gate refusals but never say what caught them, and stopped recording finalizes when finalizing moved into a script (2026-10-10)

**Symptom.** An outside review of `pipeline-events.jsonl` (pasted in by the owner, for a summary statistic of what the gates
prevent) found all 463 `gate-FAIL` events carried an empty note and the same fixed evidence string. The log could
say "236 distinct builds refused", but not which of the 103 rules refused them, and not whether a refusal was a real catch
or the gate run on an unfinished build. Checking that claim showed a second gap: the last `finalized` event was
2026-09-22, although releases were finalized after that through finalize-mod.ps1 (2026-09-30). (The review's other
claim, that logging stopped on 2026-10-06, was wrong. Its copy was older; gate events run to 2026-10-09.)

**Root cause:** the log write recorded THAT a transition happened, not WHY, because the script's own results were never
passed to it. When finalizing moved from hand steps (caught by the filesystem watcher) into finalize-mod.ps1, nobody
added the event write to the script that now performed the transition.

**Fix.** pre-finalize-check.ps1 writes one token per failing check into the note: `gate-rules:<id>` for each package-gate
row that hit, `rule <n>: <check>` for its own checks. A run on Perfected Wheeler 1.4.0 logged the version gate's refusal
and four rule IDs. finalize-mod.ps1 records `finalized` as its last step, through a resolver lookup that cannot fail a
finished finalize.

**Rule.** An event a script writes carries the reason with the outcome, so every statistic can be computed from the
log alone. When a transition moves into a new script, that script writes the event; check the log for the event's
last date after the move.


## Repackaging a two-line FOMOD with package-mod.ps1 seeds from an old flat package and prunes the previous FOMOD; changelog.ps1 cannot tell two repos sharing a ledger key (MIT-label sweep, 2026-10-10)

**Symptom.** Rebuilding Local Map Upgrade 1.3.3, Dragon's Eye Minimap 1.7.4 and CNO 1.1.7 so their DLLs say GPL
(sub-agent, 2026-10-10). Running package-mod.ps1 again on LMU's existing two-line FOMOD produced a package seeded from
the 1.2.9 FLAT package: no LICENSE, no NOTICE, no fomod folder. Its own prune then sent the 1.3.2 FOMOD out of
7. current test builds, so repack-fomod.ps1 could no longer find its default previous package. For DEM, package-mod passed
the ledger key "DragonsEyeMinimap" to changelog.ps1, which matches two repos (the SMF one and the original), so the
changelog check failed. With no `dist\README.txt`, repack-fomod copied the repo's README.md (a bare title) over the
player README. And `version-gate -Action status -Mod X` ignores -Mod.

**Root cause:** package-mod.ps1 picks its seed package by name pattern and was written for flat packages. The two-line
FOMOD layout (Common / Line-SE-AE16 / Line-17) came later, and nothing tells package-mod which layout is current.
changelog.ps1 resolves a repo by ledger key, and the key is not unique.

**Fix (this time).** Copy the previous FOMOD to the scratchpad first, then run repack-fomod.ps1 with it as `-Previous`.
Pass `-Mod DragonsEyeMinimap-SMF` to changelog.ps1. Add a real `dist\README.txt` (DEM, commit 9c9cd87).

**Rule.** For a mod whose current package is a FOMOD, repackage with repack-fomod.ps1 `-Previous <last FOMOD>`, never
package-mod.ps1. Keep a copy of the previous package before any packager runs, because its prune can remove it. The
package-mod layout detection, the changelog key ambiguity and status -Mod are open fixes (to-do list, 2026-10-10).


## The distro one-zip rule hard-deleted an optional download at finalize; release scripts used Remove-Item where finalize's own prune used the Recycle Bin (AMF-W3 1.0.4, 2026-10-11)

**Symptom.** finalize-mod.ps1's distro sync for AMF-W3 1.0.4 removed the 1.0.3 "No Installer" optional zip (built that
night) with `Remove-Item -Force`. It was gone, not in the Recycle Bin. The release agent rebuilt it byte-identical
from the same sources. nexus-upload.py would also have picked the No Installer zip as the main file had it not been
moved aside.

**Root cause:** sync-nexus-distro.ps1 and nexus-distro-sweep.ps1 enforce "one zip, the newest" with a hard delete. Their
optional-file exemption only covers optional zips of the CURRENT version, so an older optional zip counts as stale.
finalize-mod.ps1's own prune already used the Recycle Bin. The release scripts had never been checked against rule
50 (never delete unprompted) as a class.

**Fix.** Both distro scripts and package-mod.ps1's same-name rebuild now send files to the Recycle Bin.
`scripts\tests\test_release_scripts_recycle.py` (pre-commit) fails on any Remove-Item / IO Delete / rmdir in
`scripts\release\*.ps1`, unless the line is marked `# in-assembly` (a copy inside the package being built right then)
or touches a temp path.

**Rule.** A release script that clears old files sends them to the Recycle Bin. A new deletion site in scripts\release
fails the test until it is marked or changed. Optional downloads of an older version are rebuilt alongside the new
release (rebuild the No Installer zip from each new AMF-W3 version).


## Witcher 3 test gotchas from AMF-W3 1.0.5: `entry` is a WitcherScript keyword, the recent-saves list is not newest-first, run saves sync to the cloud, and an owner autosave is not a clean test save (2026-10-11)

**What happened.** Porting AMF Skyrim's feature set into AMF-W3 1.0.5:
- (1) The "here only" script named a local `entry`. That is a WitcherScript keyword (like `state`), and the game's script compile stopped on it.
- (2) Per-save settings were stored under the wrong save, because `GetRecentListSG` is not ordered newest-first.
- (3) The run's own test saves were deleted locally but came back from the cloud sync. They must be deleted in the game's load list too.
- (4) Loading the owner's newest autosave crashed twice at [offset removed]. Falsification: the same crash with AMF's new save/load hooks removed. Then a clean load of the Nexus 12404 save with only AMF ticked. The cause was the save plus a mod set broken by the 5.0.2 patch (Bug Fixed Fast Travel and Minimalist Witcher Senses fail the compile), not AMF.

**Root cause:** an assumed API order and an assumed identifier set, never checked against the game. And a test fixture (his save) that carried state from mods the run had changed.

**Do instead.** Rename locals away from WitcherScript keywords. Sort the save list by time yourself. Delete a run's saves in game and locally, and count them before and after. W3 save tests load the Nexus 12404 save (`ManualSave_6b4a7_7ea48c00_5a9df13`) through LOAD GAME, with only the needed mods ticked (memory w3-tests-use-nexus-12404-save, amended 2026-10-11).


## Retargeting a Nexus changelog entry by editing its version field deleted the newer entry (AMF-W3 credit change, 2026-10-11)

**What happened.** To change a contributor's credit name in the 1.0.4 entry of AMF-W3's Nexus changelog tab, a
sub-agent found the editor would only open the newest entry (1.0.5). It changed that entry's version field to 1.0.4
in the page's code and saved. Nexus then wrote the 1.0.5 entry's lines into 1.0.4, appended to the old ones, and
deleted the 1.0.5 entry. The live changelog lost 1.0.5 and showed 1.0.4 twice over. Restoring it needed the owner's go-ahead.

**Root cause:** the version field is the entry's KEY, not a label. Changing it saves the text under another version,
and the original entry is gone. The editor's limitation was worked around instead of reported.

**Do instead.** Edit a Nexus changelog entry only through the editor control for THAT version. If the editor will not
open it, stop and report. Never change an entry's version field. Before any changelog save, keep the full current
changelog text (changelog.txt in the distro folder) so it can be restored. After each save, read the public changelog
back.


## "Missing UnknownPlugin = old FLICK header" also matched mods that are not FLICK-header consumers, and an old header has 31 table orders, not one (AMF 2.1.8, 2026-10-11)

**What happened.** 2.1.8 was to host mods built against an old FLICK header (2.1.7 refused them by the absence of
`"UnknownPlugin"`), with the brief: an old-ITool adapter for "era A" (before 2026-05-28) and an old-order table for "era
B" (before 2026-06-08). Walking all 107 commits of FLICK's `src/FUCK_API.h` showed the brief's two-layout picture was
wrong: there are **31 different table orders** before 2026-06-08 (23 of them in era A, 9 in era B), three older ITool
layouts, two unreleased later breaks, and nothing in a DLL says which order it was built with. Separately, a scan of every
FLICK-using DLL on the machine found **Risa's All In One Menu**: it calls `RequestFUCK` through its OWN client struct and
carries no `"UnknownPlugin"` - a rule "no UnknownPlugin -> hand it the old table" would have handed a current client an
old-order table, a crash the rule itself caused. And Simple Timed Block's FLICK page, once hosted, was hidden by AMF's
one-entry rule (it also registers an SMF page), so the page could not be tested without a new driving op.

**Why it looked right.** One historical marker (UnknownPlugin, added with PluginName on 05-28) did split the ITool
layouts, so it was natural to assume the table split the same way at one date. The marker was proven on the mods that
were known to be FLICK consumers - never on the DLLs that merely ask for FLICK.

**Do instead.** Classify by POSITIVE evidence per module: "UnknownPlugin" = current; the header's own Connect() line
("Connected to FUCK API version {}") without it = an old FLICK header (order unknown -> answer RequestFUCK with nothing,
the header's own "FLICK not installed" path); neither = a client of its own (current table). Host an old build only when
its exact header is proven - for Simple Timed Block: its source's submodule pin (StyyxUtils 8919775 = FLICK 27e3db1's
162-slot table), RTTI (9-entry vtable), and the slot indexes its code calls reading as one coherent page in that order
and as nonsense in the neighbouring ones - and match the build by its PE header (time stamp, image size, entry point).
`RequestFUCK` picks the table by `_ReturnAddress()`'s module. The history, the proof and the scripts are in
`4. plans\amf-flick\ABI-HISTORY.md` and `abi-tools\`.

Two smaller ones from the same run:
- **A FLICK mod calls `SetTooltip` after every control without checking hover** (FLICK shows it for the item before it).
  Answering it with ImGui's unconditional `SetTooltip` left the LAST call's text over the page all the time. A host's
  answer must follow the original's semantics, not the ImGui function of the same name.
- **`nexus-upload.py` checked the md5 lookup immediately and reported "md5 found False -> CHECK THE PAGE"** without
  recording the version posted; the md5 search found the file ~40 s later. Wait for the md5 (poll a few minutes) before
  calling an upload unverified; record `posted` by hand with the evidence when the tool gave up early.
**Root cause:** A historical marker that split ITool layouts was assumed to split the table order the same way, and it was proven only on mods known to be FLICK consumers, never on DLLs that merely ask for FLICK.


## A sub-agent launched the game on a profile another session was using, because "nothing is running" is not "nobody holds it" (AMF themes, 2026-10-11)

**What happened.** The Powershell Agent session announced a long Skyrim screenshot run on "Njordlinger Test" from about 17:00. Between two of its launches, at 19:51, this session's theme sub-agent saw no Skyrim and no MO2 running, passed health-gate, installed a draft AMF build into that profile and launched it. The stop message reached it minutes later. The game crashed at 19:55 (in an AMD frame-generation thread, cause unproven). The draft build sat where the other session's next launch would have captured it. The sub-agent restored the folder from its own backup, and a hash check proved the restore. The profile's settings.ini and initweaks.ini had no backup.

**Root cause:** the launch gates check running processes, not ownership. A session between launches holds the instance without any process to show it. And rule 69 (one launcher, one combined run) was not applied: the sub-agent was briefed to test in game itself.

**Do instead.** Game tests go through the launcher session (rule 69; the owner, 2026-10-11: "the main agent does the launches"): hand it the build plus a TEST-HANDOFF.md. Never brief a sub-agent to launch on a shared instance. Before ANY write to an instance, back up every file a launch rewrites (including the profile's settings.ini and initweaks.ini), not only the mod folder. To-do: an instance lock file that the launch gates read (a session announcing a run writes it).

## A build-path fix measured on the flags would have passed twice while the artefact still leaked: a quoted VCPKG_CXX_FLAGS path was cut at its first space, and a reused PDB kept its old user-folder records (AMF 2.1.9 rebuild, 2026-10-12)

**What happened.** The new gate rows `shipped-files-carry-no-user-folder` and `shipped-dll-carries-no-project-root`
refused every Skyrim package. The fix went into one shared place, `.MD\scripts\build-env\` (TEMP / TMP outside the
user profile, and a vcpkg overlay triplet with `/d1trimfile` so CommonLibSSE-NG's own sources compile trimmed). Two
things that looked done were not:

* **The first triplet set `VCPKG_CXX_FLAGS` to `"/d1trimfile:<path>"`.** The configure log showed the flag, and the
  path contains spaces ("Claude output", "6. current wip mods"). vcpkg passes the value as a `-D` argument through its
  parallel-configure ninja file, which stripped the quotes and cut it at the first space: CommonLibSSE-NG's
  `build.ninja` read `/d1trimfile:D:\Claude` and nothing after. Fix: a chainloaded toolchain
  (`toolchains\windows-trim-paths.cmake`) that includes vcpkg's `windows.cmake` and calls `add_compile_options`, which
  takes the flag as one argument; plus `VCPKG_LOAD_VCVARS_ENV ON`, because a chainloaded toolchain otherwise makes
  vcpkg skip the MSVC environment ("No CMAKE_C_COMPILER could be found"). Inside the toolchain,
  `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` is unset when CMake re-reads it from `CMakeSystem.cmake`; `CMAKE_PARENT_LIST_FILE` (vcpkg.cmake)
  names vcpkg's scripts folder reliably.
* **After the rebuild, both DLLs were clean but the PDBs still held 254 and 199 user-folder strings**, all
  `...\AppData\Local\Temp\lnk{GUID}.tmp` with many different GUIDs although TEMP now pointed outside the profile.
  link.exe had updated the EXISTING PDB and kept the module records of earlier links. Deleting the DLL and PDB and
  relinking gave 0.

**Do instead.** Verify on the artefact, never the command line. For a path flag, read the compile line the build tool
actually wrote (`build.ninja` FLAGS) and count the strings in the built DLL and PDB with the gate rows' own patterns.
A path with spaces does not survive vcpkg's flag strings; give it to CMake as a list argument. The first build of a
repo in a new environment deletes the old PDB before linking (rule 45, PREFLIGHT).
**Root cause:** The path fix was verified on the command line (the configure log showing the flag) instead of on the built artefact, so a flag cut at its first space and a reused PDB with old records went unseen.


## A gate row overrode an owner-named exception: the A-Z sort tick box was turned into a switch because checkbox-is-a-toggle flagged it, though the code comment said the owner asked for it (AMF 2.1.9, 2026-10-12)

**What happened.** The owner reported a tick box on Simple Timed Block's page (rule 32: switches, never tick boxes). While fixing that, Main Agent also told the rebuild agent to turn the Mods row's alphabetical-sort tick box into a switch, because the package gate's checkbox-is-a-toggle row flagged it. The source carried a comment that the owner had asked for a tick box there by name; the agent followed the gate and said so in its report. The owner, 2026-10-12: "It was indeed supposed to be a tick box next to a toggle." It cost a revert, a third rebuild and a second launch in the last hour before the 07:00 post.

**Root cause:** a general rule (and the gate that enforces it) was treated as outranking a specific, owner-named exception recorded in the code. A gate row has no way to carry an exception, so the only way to pass it was to change the control.

**Do instead.** When a gate flags code whose comment cites an owner request, the comment is evidence of an exception: ask the owner before changing it, and record the ruling as an exemption marker carrying his quote and date, which the gate row honours. A general rule never silently overrides a specific owner ruling.


## A control drawn with art lost its outline: the art path skipped ImGui's border, no shipped box, button or tick box part had an edge layer, and faces are the panel colour - Norden - Black's buttons were invisible (AMF next after 2.1.9, 2026-10-12)

**What happened.** The owner, on AMF Skyrim's Norden - Black: "the button faces don't have any kind of outline at all, even a basic one." The theme's border (#8E9396 on #000000, contrast 6.8) was fine. AMF's ImGui art hook replaces RenderFrame for boxes, buttons and tick boxes with the theme's art part and returns true, so ImGui never draws its border; only a part with an `-edge` layer drew a line, and no shipped box, button or tick box part has one. Every face is the panel colour at rest (kRoleBoxes = Background), so on a black panel a black plate with no line is simply not there. Other themes hid it because their plate art's shape or the panel's tone happened to show.

**Root cause:** a replacement drawing path took over ImGui's whole frame, fill AND border, while the art only ever supplied the fill. The look was checked theme by theme by eye, never as a rule ("every control has a visible outline").

**Do instead.** When a hook replaces a widget's drawing, list everything the original drew (fill, border, nav highlight) and keep each part the replacement does not supply. AMF's DrawPlate now draws ImGui's border line (Border colour, at least 1 px) whenever RenderFrame asked for a border and the part has no edge layer; switches get the same; theme::Apply keeps the Border colour at least 2.0 contrast against the panel and faces (else the text colour). Gate row `theme-control-outline-visible` (`gates\theme-outline-gate.py`) fails a shipped AMF theme whose border would not show.


## A click shorter than a frame lost its release: CommonLib's IsUp() needs a held time, and the game's release of a button let go before its next poll carries none (AMF next v3, 2026-10-12)

**What happened.** The v3 in-game run clicked AMF's MFM switch with real mouse input at a 60 ms gap: 30 ms holds 4 of 4, 20 ms 3 of 4, 10 ms 0 of 5. Every lost click logged its press in AMF's drain and never its release, and there was no "held to the next frame" line. The v2 and v3 fixes had both worked on the DRAIN (one change per button per frame, carry ahead of newer input) - the release never got that far. AMF's input hook keeps transitions only, `IsDown() || IsUp()`, and CommonLib defines `IsUp()` as value 0 AND heldDownSecs above 0. The game's mouse device polls DirectInput once a frame and stamps a release with the time it SAW the button held, so a button let go before the poll after its press (under about 11.6 ms here) is released with heldDownSecs 0: neither IsDown nor IsUp, filtered out.

**Root cause:** a filter built on a library predicate whose definition carried an extra condition (a held time) that the transitions-only intent did not need, and two rounds of fixes aimed at the next stage without first asking where the missing record stopped.

**Do instead.** When an event is "logged at one end and never at the other", find the LAST place it was seen and the first filter after it, and read that filter's predicates in the library's own header before changing anything downstream. A button release is its value going to 0 for a button whose press was passed on (AMF `InputFrames.h` ButtonEdge / FedButtons). Model the device's timing offline and run the OLD code beside the new as a control: the model reproduced v3's numbers (10 ms lost in every poll phase, 20 ms in about a third, 30 ms never) before the fix was trusted.

## A theme switch that set a few style sizes over a scaled style undid the scale: rebuild the whole ImGui style each time (AMF next v3, 2026-10-12)

**What happened.** After cycling themes, Norden - Black came back with tighter window padding; a relaunch fixed it. Start-up ran theme::Apply (WindowPadding 34) and then `ImGuiStyle::ScaleAllSizes(UI scale)` once; every later Apply wrote WindowPadding back as 34 unscaled over a style whose spacing stayed scaled (56 at 1800p). Another file had even grown a workaround that recognised "34 unscaled after a theme switch".

**Root cause:** the style was treated as two things - a scaled base built once and theme values patched in later - while ScaleAllSizes is a one-shot multiplication, so any value written after it is unscaled.

**Do instead.** A function that sets part of a shared mutable style must either own the whole of it or none of it: build the style from ImGui's defaults, set the theme's values, scale once, every time (AMF `ThemeStyle.h`), and check offline that a switch through every theme and back is byte-equal to a fresh load. A workaround that detects a second state of the same value is a sign the state should not exist.

## The rules reached 2.10.0: a minor bump kept its own arithmetic while only the build step was collapsed into the version gate, and the gate's shape check looked at the patch digit alone (rules 2.9.1 -> 2.10.0, 2026-10-09; found 2026-10-12)

**What happened.** Rule 6's arithmetic says the minor rolls at .9 and the major rolls at x.9.9, so a `.10` never exists in any position. The rules archive holds `CLAUDE-v2.10.0.md` through `CLAUDE-v2.10.9.md`, ten revisions over 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-12. The series then stepped to 3.0.0 by itself today when the build digit reached 9 under a minor of 10. The 2.10.0 stamp came from step 2.6 of the restructure (rule 70 added, commit 7ad0064): `rules-version.ps1 -Action bump -Level minor` from 2.9.1. Every earlier minor jump in the archive (2.4.9 -> 2.5.0 ... 2.8.9 -> 2.9.0) was a build step rolling at .9, so the minor branch had never been run from an x.9 before.

**Root cause:** The 2026-09-12 collapse to one arithmetic (entry "version numbers kept going wrong ... seven implementations") moved only the DEFAULT (build) branch of `rules-version.ps1` and `docs-pipeline.ps1` onto `version-gate.ps1 -Action nextnumber`. Their `minor` and `major` branches still do their own sums: `'minor' { $newMinor++; $newBuild = 0 }` in rules-version.ps1 and `'minor' { return @($maj, ($min + 1), 0) }` in docs-pipeline's Step-Version. Neither caps the minor at 9, and `nextnumber` has no level input to delegate them to. The gate's `Assert-Shape` then let 2.10.x through nine times, because it refuses only `Build -ge 10`; the minor digit is never checked. Two half-collapsed implementations plus a gate that checks one of three digits is the same class as the 2026-09-12 entry, one layer down.

**Do instead.** A collapse to one tool is finished only when every BRANCH of every consumer calls it: grep each consumer for the arithmetic operator (`++`, `+ 1`) after the collapse, not just for the call. Give `version-gate.ps1 nextnumber` a `-Level` (minor: x.9.z -> (x+1).0.0, else x.(y+1).0; major: (x+1).0.0) and make both document tools delegate all three levels. Extend `Assert-Shape` to refuse `Minor -ge 10` the way it refuses `Build -ge 10`, so a wrong number cannot survive its next step. Topics: versioning, gates, powershell, rules.
**Root cause:** The earlier collapse to one version arithmetic moved only the build branch onto the shared gate, leaving the minor and major branches with their own unbounded sums, and the gate's shape check looked at only one of the three digits.

## A key SendInput sends is proof only for mods that read Windows keys: F13-F15 never reached OAR, Community Shaders or IED, which read the game's own input events - and a splice inside AMF's load-time hook would reach no other plugin's hook (AMF 2.2.0, 2026-10-12)

**What happened.** AMF 2.2.0's "AMF holds this key" wrote F13 / F14 / F15 into Open Animation Replacer's, Community Shaders' and IED's configs and pressed them with SendInput. Every offline check passed (each config written, read back by the mod's own reader, restored byte-exact), and before the relaunch each Open still worked - because it still pressed the mods' OLD keys. After the relaunch none of the three opened, from AMF's button or from a real SendInput F13-F15 (scan code or virtual key), while TestBench's bench.input - a ButtonEvent spliced into the list PollInputDevices dispatches - opened all three on DIK [value removed]-[value removed]. OptiScaler, on F16 by SendInput, did open: it reads Windows keys. The same run found IED's F15 was also Community Shaders' CS Editor key, and Root Builder copying OptiScaler.ini back at every launch, which quietly undid the switch.

**Root cause:** the design assumed "a key the config names is a key SendInput can deliver" without asking which input path each mod reads. Windows' F13-F15 do not arrive in the game's DirectInput, so for a mod that reads the game's input events the delivery was never possible; the offline proof covered the file half and none of the delivery half, and the pre-relaunch test exercised the old keys only.

**Do instead.** Classify every key target by the input path it reads (game input events vs Windows keys) and press it on that path - AMF now injects game-event keys itself (Input.cpp, the game-key injector). An injector that splices events must sit OUTERMOST on the call it hooks: a splice inside AMF's own hook, installed at load by a plugin that loads first, reaches only hooks installed before it (none); bench.input worked because it installs at kInputLoaded. AMF installs its injector by an SKSE task on the game thread when the main menu first opens. Before writing a key into another mod's config, read every config's bindings and refuse a key that one press could share (`hostcore::Clashes`), and treat a backup beside a config that no longer carries AMF's key as "something put the file back" rather than fighting it. A held-key feature is proven only by a press after the relaunch that reads the new config.


## The Nexus "1.0.5" file of MO2 Custom Filters was the 1.0.4 package - "the user runs an old version" was right about the code and wrong about why (2026-10-13)

**Symptom.** lillianneee (12 Oct, MO2 2.5.2) still saw `[deprecated] onModStateChanged in _on_ui [plugins\MO2CustomFilters.py:222]` "using version 1.0.5". The 2026-10-05 entry above had answered the same warning with "the user runs an old version - the answer is update", because the repo's 1.0.5 registers no mobase callback and line 222 sits in `_on_ui` only in v1.0.0-v1.0.4.

**What was true.** Both Nexus pages (skyrimspecialedition 192713 file 809492, site 2362 file 10088) list their MAIN "1.0.5" file at 30,388 bytes - the exact size of the ARCHIVED 1.0.4 file, and of the 1.0.4 package rebuilt from tag v1.0.4 with the same zip settings (that rebuild also matches the Nexus 1.0.3 size to the byte). The real 1.0.5 zip in the distro is 31,933 bytes, and Nexus's md5 search finds it on neither page. So everyone who downloaded "1.0.5" got 1.0.4 - the warning AND the mod-toggle crash 1.0.5 fixed. Control on MO2 2.5.2: the 1.0.4 file reproduces the user's warning at :222 word for word; the repo file logs nothing.

**Why it went unseen.** The 10-05 check compared the page's VERSION LABEL and upload time with the commits, never the uploaded BYTES. The label was right; the file under it was not. The ledger's "posted" record for 1.0.5 is a backfill with `sha256: null`, so nothing held the posted file's identity.

**Root cause:** "posted" was proven by a label - the page's version string and upload time - and a backfilled ledger row with no hash; nothing tied the bytes on Nexus to the zip in the distro, so a wrong file under the right label passed every check.

**Do instead.** When a report contradicts the release, compare the posted archive itself with the distro zip: `files.json` `size_in_bytes`, and `games/<domain>/mods/md5_search/<md5>.json` for the local zip. A label/version check is not evidence of what was uploaded. Fixed as 1.0.6 (the 1.0.5 code under a new number, so an update reaches everyone with the mislabelled file). Proposed gate (not built): `nexus-version-audit.py` fails a page whose newest file's size differs from the distro zip of that version.

## "Two entries vanish from the Mods list in Chinese" - both were in the list, 150 rows from where the test looked: a menu name that follows the game's language is a newcomer to an order saved in another language (AMF 2.2.0 final5, 2026-10-13)

**What happened.** The final5 run switched the game to Chinese over a player profile whose custom order was saved with English names. The Mod Function Menu (registered as "模组函数菜单") and "精准度 - 局部伤害 (MCM)" were reported missing: not seen at the bottom of the list, and "in mods[] but not in displayOrder" by DevBench `op=state`. In English both showed. The suspects named before any test were the sort, grouping, search, ImGui IDs and text-width culling.

**What was true.** AMF's list code (source/Personalization.cpp), compiled offline and fed that run's 278 registered names and the player's User.ini, lists both: rows 158 and 159 of 291, the last two loose mods, directly above the first separator ("Combat"). The order is kept by registered NAME; both names follow the game's language (MCM titles from the mod's translation file, the MFM entry from AMF's translation), so in Chinese they are names the saved order never held. A newcomer is inserted at its A-Z place among the loose mods, and a CJK name's place is after every Latin one. The "not in displayOrder" reading could not be reproduced and was most likely a text match on re-encoded tool output. The same run's control: unchanged HEAD code gave the same rows.

**Root cause:** a "vanished" report was taken as a drop because the place the entry should be was assumed (its English position, or the end of the list), and the list was checked by string-matching CJK text in tool output rather than by the list's own indices.

**Do instead.** Before chasing a "missing row", run the list builder offline on the run's own inputs (the registered names from the log's "first page registered for" lines and the player's INI) and print where every entry lands: `tools\list_order_check.bat <names> <User.ini>` does this for AMF. In game, match `displayOrder` rows to `mods[]` by `index`, not by a non-ASCII string. A language switch over a saved custom order moves every language-following name to the end of the loose mods - say so in a test plan that switches language. Fixed alongside: names were lowered byte by byte with the CRT's locale-dependent tolower; include/ListCore.h folds whole UTF-8 characters with no locale for the sort, search and Filter. Topics: amf, cjk, testing, ui.


## A requested feature was parked for a later version instead of folded into the open one (AMF 2.2.0 slider wheel, 2026-10-13)

**What happened.** At about 22:00 on 2026-10-12 a Nexus suggestion (the mouse wheel nudges sliders, from HadToRegister) reached Main Agent while AMF 2.2.0 was open and unposted, with nine hours to the 07:00 release. Main Agent filed it for the version after 2.2.0 to avoid another rebuild, and asked the owner whether he wanted it sooner. He did not see or answer the question. At 05:00 he hit the missing feature in game: "It was supposed to have already been built and installed ages ago... Why wasn't this already built?"

**Root cause:** the standing rule that a requested feature goes into the open version (memory full-set-means-one-release-not-a-roadmap) was traded for release-night caution, and the trade was put to the owner as a question instead of being decided by the rule.

**Do instead.** A feature request that arrives while a version is open is built into that version straight away, unless the owner says otherwise. Release-night risk is handled by testing it, not by deferring it; ask only when the feature would genuinely not fit before the release.


## A Witcher 3 EIAB_Sprint lock moves the camera: the game treats Geralt as indoors and switches to the close indoor camera (Loot on Hover W3, 2026-10-13)

**What happened.** Loot on Hover held sprint off while its window was up with `thePlayer.BlockAction(EIAB_Sprint, ...)`, beside its jump, roll and attack locks. The owner then reported that the camera zoomed in every time the window popped up. This was first suspected to be a vanilla loot-popup "focus" camera.

**What was true (read from the 5.0 scripts).** No popup or container code touches the camera. `CPlayer.PlayerTick` sets `movementLockType = PMLT_NoSprint` whenever EIAB_Sprint is blocked. The Exploration state's `OnGameCameraTick` then runs `UpdateCameraInterior`, the indoor camera: 1.5 m distance, -10 degrees pitch. jumpCamera.ws and locomotionDirectController.ws read the same lock as "in an interior" too. So the lock does more than block a button: it is the game's own indoors switch.

**Do instead.** Never block EIAB_Sprint (or EIAB_RunAndSprint) just to hold a button off. Wrap `CR4Player.CanSprint` and return false instead. More generally, before adding an action lock, grep the scripts for every reader of that lock (`IsActionAllowed( EIAB_x )`) and not only its button. Topics: witcher3, witcherscript, camera, input.
**Root cause:** An action lock was used just to hold a button off, without checking that the game reads the same lock elsewhere as its indoors switch.


## The gate was used as the test: 233 same-station re-runs of the finalize gate, 163 of them refusals (straight flow, 2026-10-13)

**What happened.** The Pipeline Flow artifact drew every recorded event of every version in the order the pipeline
intends (Fable Advisor Agent, 2026-10-12). It showed the finalize gate run again at the same station 233 times (163
refusals, 183 of all re-runs under two minutes apart; fail then fail 159 times, fail then pass 51), 198 loops from
"distro synced" back into the finalize gates, and 119 versions synced to the distro straight from "proved working",
skipping the gate and the finalize. The causes were in the tools, not in the sessions alone: finalize-mod ran the gate,
moved and zipped, synced the distro, then ran the gate again, tolerating two rows "only the sync can fix" on the first
run; pre-finalize-check's -SyncNexusDistro and hand runs synced text outside finalize; and nothing stopped a refused gate
from being re-run blind on the same inputs.

**Root cause:** the gate was being used as the test - run, read the refusal, try again - instead of the refusal sending
the work back to test and fix. The owner, 2026-10-12: "No station repeats before the reason for its failure is fixed.
The gate is not the test."

**Do instead (built 2026-10-13, three gates that refuse, rule 34's shape):**
- A: `sync-nexus-distro.ps1` refuses outside finalize (exit 3) unless the version is already finalized (rule 10).
- B: `finalize-mod` runs one straight order - text sync, ONE gate event, tag, move and zip, distro zip with a hash
  post-check (no second gate run) - and the Recycle Bin clean-up moved out to `post-release-prune`, fired by the first
  recorded posting (rules 21, 23, 3).
- C: a refused gate is not run again on an unchanged input fingerprint (exit 3 with the stored reasons); `-Force -Reason`
  is the only, recorded, way past (rule 34).
Acceptance: re-run the flow artifact on events after 2026-10-13 - finalize-gate repeats only with a changed
`refs.inputs`, no distro-to-gate loops, no working-to-distro skips. Reports: logs\steps\SF-A, SF-B, SF-hashes, SF-C.
Topics: release, finalize, gates, distro, versioning.

## A package seeded from an older release than the last one: a folder named "<Mod> X.Y.Z FOMOD" is skipped as a seed, and new dist files landed at the FOMOD root (SLSC 1.0.3, 2026-10-13)

**What happened.** Simple Loadout System for Controller 1.0.3's first package failed gate row
`fomod-delivers-every-file-of-previous` eleven times: the eleven translation files 1.0.2 installed were not reachable by
the 1.0.3 installer. package-mod had seeded from 1.0.1, because the 1.0.2 test build's folder is named
"Simple Loadout System for Controller 1.0.2 FOMOD" and the seed pattern only accepts "<Mod> X.Y.Z". 1.0.1 predates the
translations, so package-mod's "everything in dist ships" step copied `dist\Interface\Translations` to the package ROOT,
which a FOMOD never installs (it installs Common\ and the chosen line folder). The seeded README.txt was 1.0.1's too.

**Root cause:** the dist-copy step assumed the package root is the install root; in a FOMOD package it is not.

**Do instead:** package-mod now puts a new dist file under Common\ when the package has fomod\ModuleConfig.xml and
Common\, and removes the empty root SKSE\ left by the flat-copy removal (.MD commit, 2026-10-13). After packaging, read
the "seeded from" line: when it is not the last release, compare README.txt with the repo's README.md. The gate row
already catches the missing files.
Topics: release, packaging, fomod, translations.

## A HUD setting that "does nothing" on a settings page was parked as an INI-priority bug - the value reached the movie only once, in its constructor (Compass Navigation Overhaul 1.1.7, 2026-10-13)

**What happened.** On 2026-10-10 the quest list's Position X/Y sliders in Compass Navigation Overhaul's settings page
moved nothing on screen. The finding was recorded as "it was saved to Norden UI's copy of the INI, which takes
priority", and the fix was parked as "read and write the INI copy that actually wins". That explanation could not
produce the symptom: the plugin reads and writes the INI through one game-folder path, and Mod Organizer 2's virtual
file system resolves that path to the same winning copy (Norden UI's tuned one) in both directions - and neither copy's
file date had changed, so no save had landed anywhere that night. The real cause was in the code: Position X/Y and Max
height reach the HUD movie once, as arguments to the QuestItemList movie's AS constructor when Infinity UI patches the
HUD, and nothing ever sent them again, so a slider changed only a C++ variable until the next start.

**Why the wrong answer looked right.** A second copy of the INI was visibly present with different values, and a rule
about virtual-file-system writes (rule 16, the Norden skyhud.txt entry) was fresh in mind. The killing condition - "if
the INI copy were the cause, the slider would still move the list live, because the page changes the variable directly"
- was never written down.

**Also learned.** Norden UI ships its own QuestItemList.swf, which overrides ours when it wins, so a new AS function in
our SWF would not exist in the movie players actually run. The live move therefore calls the movie's OWN constructor
again (both SWFs have the same script: decompiled with FFDec 2026-10-13), after putting the clip back at its starting
_x/_y and keeping its `entries` array.

**Do instead:** for any setting that "does nothing" in game, first trace where the value reaches the game (grep the
variable's every use) before blaming files; a value used only in an init path is not live. When another mod can replace
the movie we drive, drive only what both movies share.
Topics: ui, settings, mo2, process.
**Root cause:** The cause was named from a plausible file-priority story before tracing where the setting's value actually reaches the game, and no killing condition was written for that hypothesis.

## A Witcher 3 load sync in the player's OnSpawned never logged - thePlayer (and GetWitcherPlayer()) is still NULL there on a save load, and the sync's guard returned silently (Kaer Morhen Gear 1.0.0, 2026-10-13)

**What happened.** Kaer Morhen Gear's `@wrapMethod(W3PlayerWitcher) OnSpawned` called a sync that began
[code removed]. The inventory-open sync logged every time; the load sync never once. Witcher Gear
Overhaul's "values (load)" sync is the same shape.

**What was true.** On a save load the global `thePlayer` is not yet set while the player entity's OnSpawned runs.
Runtime evidence, not source: Multi Companion's CR4Player.OnSpawned wrap logs `"Found Player: " + thePlayer` and the
2026-10-13 20:00 scriptslog reads "Found Player: NULL when spawning ... player.w2ent". `GetWitcherPlayer()` is only
`(W3PlayerWitcher)thePlayer`, so it is NULL too. The guard had no log line, so the failure was invisible.

**Do instead.** Inside the player's own events use `this` (`GetInventory()`), never `thePlayer` / `GetWitcherPlayer()`.
Every early return in a sync or hook logs why (rule 14) - a silent guard turned a one-glance diagnosis into a missing
line nobody could explain.
Topics: witcher3, scripts, logging.
**Root cause:** A guard in a player spawn event relied on a global that is still NULL there on a save load, and because the early return logged nothing the failure was invisible.

## Inflated Witcher 3 item values were blamed on another mod's switches - the test save was New Game+, and the game's own NG+ item scaling explained every number (Kaer Morhen Gear, 2026-10-13)

**What happened.** On the owner's new test save, the Kaer Morhen swords showed 1201-1469 / 1552-1898 and the armour
800 / 315, against the expected 775 / 1025 and 300 / 115. The silver range matched the Manticore sword's, and Witcher
Gear Overhaul's "Highest damage" and "Our values" switches were all on, so the report and Main Agent blamed WGO, and a
fix agent was briefed to make WGO leave the items alone.

**What was true.** The save is New Game+ (Geralt level 100). Vanilla `inventoryComponent.ws` OnItemAdded calls
IncreaseNGPItemlevel on every weapon or armour piece without an Autogen tag, adding one autogen_fixed_* ability per level
above 30 (+8 steel, +10 silver, +5 chest, +2 the other pieces). With 70 levels this gives 775+560, 1025+700, 450+350
and 175+140 exactly (the armour base is KMG's own NG+ value). WGO's log said "our values on 0 item(s)". The Manticore
match was a coincidence of numbers.

**Why the wrong answer looked right.** A matching number and a switch with a fitting name looked like proof. Nobody
checked the save's game mode or tried to break the inflated numbers down before naming a cause.

**Do instead.** Before blaming a mod for wrong Witcher 3 item stats, check whether the save is NG+ (player level, NGP
lines in the scriptslog) and try to break the difference down by the game's per-level steps. Read the other mod's own
log line for the item before suspecting it.
Topics: witcher3, testing, scripts.
**Root cause:** A matching number and a fitting switch name were taken as proof, without checking the save's game mode or breaking the inflated values down by the game's own per-level steps.


## A release was posted with its description still in the old plain-text format: every page check read facts, none the layout (Simple Loadout System W3 1.0.1, 2026-10-14)

**What happened.** Simple Loadout System (Witcher 3) 1.0.1 was finalized and uploaded on 2026-10-14 with every gate
clear. The owner then saw the page: "it looks like Simple Loadout System's description wasn't updated with the new
template like it was supposed to have been." Its nexus-page.txt was still the old plain-text sections - no header cards,
no feature drop-downs, no quote panels - although the standard layout has been the rule since 2026-10-08.

**Why nothing caught it.** nexus-upload.py posts only the file and its changelog, never the description;
sync-nexus-distro.ps1 only rewrites version references, the notes counter, the banner pill and the zip; finalize-mod
never compares the description with the template; and the thirteen page rows in gate-rules.json all check FACTS in the
text (version line, credit link, chat server invite, summary length, stale names). A page could pass every one of them in
the old format. Measured that night: about 25 of 65 distro folders were still plain text (the Oblivion Remastered and
Witcher 3 mods, a few Skyrim ones); pages built by hand in the layout keep it in nexus-description-X.Y.Z.txt.

**Do instead.** Gate row `page-is-in-the-standard-layout` (kind page-layout, 2026-10-14) refuses a package whose live
description source - the newest nexus-description-X.Y.Z.txt, else nexus-page.txt - has fewer than 3 quote panels, 1
drop-down or 3 pictures. A first release or a release of a plain page now builds the layout (nexus-page skill) and has
the owner review the preview BEFORE finalize. Topics: nexus, release, gates, pages.

---
**Root cause:** Every page check and gate row tested facts in the description text and none tested its layout, so an old plain-text page passed all of them.

## A Papyrus script slot passed IsObject() and still crashed AMF - type and value are separate words, and GetObject() writes a refcount through the value (AMF Skyrim 2.2.1, 2026-10-17)

**Topics:** amf, papyrus, crash, skse, threading

**Symptom:** a user crash on a NEW GAME in `mcmloader::scripts::Discover()`: `[instruction removed]` with rdi = [value removed],
while reading SKI_ConfigBase's `_configManager` on the dormant "SLA Config" quest (SexLabAroused.esm).

**What was true:** the code did `manager->IsObject() && manager->GetObject()`. The slot's TYPE word said object, but its
VALUE word was still garbage (odd, misaligned), because Discover runs as an SKSE task on the main thread while the
Papyrus VM is still setting up or writing that script on its own threads (on a big list it stays busy for minutes).
`GetObject()` returns a BSTSmartPointer copy, and the copy raises the refcount at [value removed] through the bad pointer.

**The check:** a type check is not a validity check. Judge a VM-owned pointer slot from its raw words (null, 8-byte
aligned, user-mode, committed per VirtualQuery) BEFORE any smart-pointer copy, and treat "unstable" as "retry on a
later pass". Prefer reading VM data on the VM thread. Sibling of entry 10 (null checks vs a bad code address).
Side notes: including <Windows.h> after CommonLib turns GetObject into GetObjectW (add `#undef GetObject`).
package-gate's built-after-source check compares every DLL against the newest source, so touching one source
means relinking all outputs.

---
**Root cause:** A type check was treated as a validity check, so a VM-owned slot whose value word was still garbage was copied through a smart pointer that wrote a refcount through the bad pointer.

## w3-tb.ps1 quit pressed CONTINUE at the Witcher 3 main menu, loaded a save, and the autosave rotated out an old one (WGO 1.0.0 test abort, 2026-10-18)

**Topics:** w3, testbench, save, quit

**Symptom:** an aborted test's `w3-tb.ps1 quit` sent Up then E while the game sat at the main menu, which pressed CONTINUE: the newest save loaded, the game wrote a new autosave and rotated the oldest autosave out. The pause menu then ignored Up/Down, and the forced close crashed (Crash Reporter held MO2 open).

**What was true:** quit's key sequence assumes the pause menu is open. It isn't safe at the main menu. Escape opens the pause menu only on every other press (send vk 27 down/up, not the key name "Escape").

**The check:** capture the screen before `quit` and only send it from the pause menu; at the main menu, use the menu's own Exit. Back up gamesaves before any W3 launch (that backup restored the rotated autosave here). Pass `-RootBuilder` to `quit -Force` and use `kill -RootBuilder` after a forced exit, or dinput8.dll is left in bin\x64_dx12.

---
**Root cause:** The quit script assumed the game was at the pause menu and sent its key sequence without first checking the screen, so at the main menu it pressed CONTINUE.

## WitcherScript rejects `!(SomeClass)x` - negating a cast is a syntax error (WGO 1.0.0, 2026-10-18)

**Topics:** w3, witcher, script, ws

**Symptom:** wcc_lite stops with a syntax error on a line like [code removed]. Two build agents hit it independently in one night.

**The check:** cast into a local first ([code removed]). Also: wrap a method once per mod - call new code from the mod's existing wrapper instead of adding a second wrapper of the same method.

---
**Root cause:** WitcherScript does not allow negating a cast expression, a syntax rule that was not known to the build agents when they wrote the condition.

## A stat ability added to a slotted W3 mutagen item leaked 0.05 spell power per slot cycle (WGO 1.0.0, 2026-10-18)

**Topics:** w3, witcher, wgo, script, mutagen

**Symptom:** slotting the Basilisk monster mutagen added +0.10 spell power instead of +0.15; unslotting removed 0.15, so every cycle lost 0.05.

**What was true:** WGO's "WGO MM" ability was put on the mounted skill-mutagen item with AddItemBaseAbility. The item's own stats and ours did not come and go as a pair: slotting applied only ours, removal took ours plus the item's base 0.05.

**The check:** never hang a stat ability on a mounted mutagen item. Put it on the player and recount the copies against the slots at every slot change and sync. A slot/unslot test must run at least two cycles and assert start equals end.

---
**Root cause:** A stat ability was attached to a mounted item whose own stats come and go separately, so slotting and removal were not symmetrical and nothing counted the copies against the slots.

## A set bonus was designed around enemies landing critical hits - in W3 5.01 enemies never crit (WGO armour sets, 2026-10-18)

**Topics:** w3, witcher, wgo, design

**Symptom:** Mag Deira's planned 4-piece ("weakened enemies cannot land critical hits on you") had nothing to act on: 5.01 only rolls criticals when the player attacks. A second 4-piece (Ofieri: "runeword effects 50% stronger") had no single strength value to raise, since each runeword reads its own attribute in its own place.

**The check:** before a design is agreed, check in the 5.01 scripts that its trigger can actually happen and its effect has one place to act. Design-stage review should include a "can this fire?" pass. A "ran out" status check must also require a finite duration, or endless effects (over-encumbered) count as running out.

---
**Root cause:** A set bonus was designed before checking in the game scripts that its trigger could ever happen and that its effect had one place to act.

## LMU's map border drew nothing for a week - img:// loadMovie can't load loose DDS, and a disabled code path's log line was read as the cause (LMU 1.3.3, 2026-10-18)

**Topics:** lmu, scaleform, swf, ui, logging

**Symptom:** the Local Map Upgrade border was blank on the first map open and a garbled "img" placeholder on the second. A log line ("screen (1500,812)-(6500,3625)") looked 2.5x off and was blamed for a week.

**What was true:** that log line came from a diagnostic path the placement never used (`kUseExtentsForPlacement=false`). The real cause: the border was built with Scaleform `loadMovie("img://...")` of loose DDS tiles, which `img://` never resolves (it only finds images the game registered in memory), and DrawMapBorder runs once per map open, so its single placement pass ran before anything loaded.

**The check:** before trusting a number in a log, confirm the code actually uses it. Don't rely on `img://` for loose files; draw from embedded data or the clip drawing API. Don't assume a "per frame" comment is true - check how often the function really runs. Nexus comment edits go through WysiBB: set `wbb.$body.html(wbb.getHTML(T, true))` then submit, or the old text is saved silently.

---
**Root cause:** A number in a log line was blamed without confirming the code path that printed it was used, and the loading method was assumed to resolve loose files and to run per frame without being checked.

## Ragdoll "flying corpses" read from unsettled bodies; TestBench key presses queued while the game was unfocused fired together (Perfected Wheeler 1.4.0, 2026-10-18)

**Topics:** wheeler, testbench, physics, build

**Symptom:** early runs showed corpses moving up to 1290 units with the wheel open at slow time; a control run moved 209 units with no wheel at all. Separately, a stray OpenWith dialog stole focus, two queued bench.input presses fired at once on refocus, and the game crashed in vanilla code.

**What was true:** the bodies had not settled before measuring. With a stationary baseline, corpses moved 0.0 units with the wheel open. Also: SSE Display Tweaks' DynamicMaxTimeScaling rewrites fMaxTime every frame, so a one-off fMaxTime fix would be overwritten anyway.

**The check:** wait for a stationary baseline and run a control before reading any ragdoll displacement. Check the foreground window before sending TestBench input. Build in the shared build environment from the start (a build outside it embedded the machine's folder in the DLL/PDB and failed rule 45).

---
**Root cause:** Ragdoll displacement was read before the bodies had settled and without a control run, and key presses were sent without checking that the game window had focus.

## An outfit replacer recorded "working" never looked at the NPC - outfit overrides don't reach actors an existing save already dressed (Jarl Ulfric Armor Replacer 1.0.1 -> 1.0.2, 2026-10-18)

**Topics:** replacer, esp, outfit, npc, testing

**Symptom:** a user on an existing save reported Ulfric still in vanilla clothes. 1.0.1's "working" record only proved the plugin loaded (items visible in Item Explorer).

**What was true:** the game reads an outfit record only when an actor is first set up; a save that already dressed Ulfric keeps his old clothes. 1.0.2 adds a start-game quest that re-dresses him once if he still wears vanilla.

**The check:** "working" for an armour/outfit replacer means reading the NPC's worn items on BOTH a new game and an existing save. Any outfit replacer needs a runtime re-dress step for existing saves.

---
**Root cause:** The working record proved only that the plugin loaded, never that the NPC's worn items changed, and the fact that outfit records are read only at first actor setup was overlooked.

## "No markers in inns" was a UI replacer's art file overriding the add-on's icon table everywhere (Local Map Item Markers 1.0.1, 2026-10-18)

**Topics:** lmim, local map, marker, swf, ui, testing

**Symptom:** reported as no item markers inside inns. The game accepted all 71 markers, but 60 clips were null.

**What was true:** LocalMap.ExtraMapMarker.IconTypes (in IconDisplayExtensionArt.swf) had 6 entries; Norden UI / Norden UI Black / LMU all ship that file, and whichever wins drops the add-on's icon types 6-9 - indoors and out. The 1.0.0 test profile had no UI replacer, which hid it. Quest items looked missing because alias-reserved refs carry the Deleted flag until the quest fills the alias.

**The check:** read the class/data the failing code indexes from the running game before trusting where the symptom was reported. Never keep an add-on's own data in a shared art file a UI replacer may ship - patch statics from your own swf. Test UI mods with a UI replacer above them. install-test-build does not remove files a new package dropped; clean them by hand.

---
**Root cause:** The failing symptom was assumed to be where it was reported (inns) instead of reading the data the code indexes from the running game, and the add-on kept its own data in an art file a UI replacer can override; the test profile had no replacer to expose it.

## Norden UI Black's recolour skipped the dialogue box: a "neutral greys only" rule misses hued slate that reads as panel; the packager reverted the fix; a headless PC can't show 16:9 UI (2026-10-19)

**Topics:** norden, ui, swf, colour, packaging, testing

**Symptom:** the dialogue box stayed slate-blue in the black theme. After the fix, the first package silently carried the old 1.0.3 dialogue files back in.

**What was true:** the box comes from [asset path removed] drawn in Norden's slate (42,52,57 / 91,103,109); the recolour only darkened greys with channel spread <= 3. build-fomod.py's carry-over from the installed folder overwrote the new files (same class as "the packager seeds from the previous release"). With the owner's monitor off Windows reports 1024x768, the stage is 4:3 and Norden's 16:9 dialogue UI is off-screen - unphotographable.

**The check:** when a recolour rule exempts "hued accents", list which accents are really panels. Diff the built package against the source after packaging. Check the screen/stage size before relying on game frames; a visual check may need the owner's display. Don't load a save written with a plugin that is now disabled (DBReV -> MenuMaid2 crash).

---
**Root cause:** A recolour rule exempting hued accents did not consider that some hued colours are panels, and the built package was not diffed against the source, so the packager's carry-over reverted the fix.

## Five first packages failed the path gates because find-msvc.bat never called the shared build environment (2026-10-19)

**Topics:** build, msvc, find-msvc, gate, packaging, paths, lmu, lmim, dem, civil-war-starts, wheeler

**Symptom:** the first packages of Local Map Upgrade, Local Map Item Markers, Dragon's Eye Minimap, Civil War Starts and Perfected Wheeler all failed shipped-dll-carries-no-project-root and shipped-files-carry-no-user-folder - after a full build and package each time.

**What was true:** each repo's find-msvc.bat lacked the lines that call the shared build environment (MODS_BUILD_ENV), so the build used the profile's TEMP and an untrimmed cached CommonLib, baking the build machine's paths into the DLL and PDB. The older row build-env-hook-reads-the-saved-variable only checks the registry fallback of a hook that is already there and skips a file with none, so nothing looked at the missing hook.

**The check:** gate row build-env-hook-present-in-find-msvc fails any repo whose find-msvc.bat lacks MODS_BUILD_ENV (skips repos with no find-msvc.bat); test scripts/tests/test_build_env_hook_present_gate.py. Fix: copy find-msvc.bat from HjerimStart, delete the repo's build\ folder, rebuild. Check a new C++ repo's find-msvc.bat before its first build, not after its first package.

---
**Root cause:** The existing gate row checked only a build-environment hook that was already present, so a find-msvc.bat with no hook at all was never examined before the first build.

## Screenshot-run "bugs" were mostly not bugs - check a capture-run observation against live data before building a fix (2026-10-19)

**Topics:** testing, capture, triage, unbind, ysgramor

**Symptom:** the 2026-10-11 page-capture run logged four Skyrim bugs. On checking: Unbind's "missing" ITEMS/IN MAP sections are off-screen on a wider-than-screen sheet; its blank controller sheet only happens with an injected (fake) pad; Ysgramor's body "inside stone" lies in the casket and was just unlit; the B-key clash came from the owner's own Wheeler setting. A CPC "arrow keys do nothing" item is likely the same class (TestBench keys don't reach every menu).

**The check:** treat a capture run's visual observation as a lead, not a bug. Before any fix, read the mod's own data (rows ops, refs, positions), test with real input (SendInput / virtual pad) and real light, and compare with the mod switched off. Mark the result in the to-do entry either way.

---
**Root cause:** Visual observations from a capture run were treated as bugs without checking them against live data, real input and a control with the mod off.

## The release check read a FOMOD's nested file mapping as "never installed", and a package layout was bent to suit it (Norden UI Black 1.0.4, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** gate, package-gate, fomod, install, installed-build, norden-ui-black

**Symptom:** Norden UI Black 1.0.4's finalize was refused: installed-build-is-the-package said the test folder "has no Extras/RaceMenu Atelier/RaceMenuAtelier.dll - the package was never installed there", although the FOMOD installs that file to SKSE/Plugins and it was there. The package was reshaped (one top-level "RaceMenu Atelier" folder installed with destination "") only to satisfy the check.

**Root cause:** the row compared each package file to the same relative path in the mod folder, flattening only Line-*, Common, Languages and top-level single-name folders. A file or nested folder that ModuleConfig.xml sends elsewhere was never mapped, and an option the player did not choose would also have read as missing.

**The check:** the row now reads fomod/ModuleConfig.xml (required files, each option's files, conditional installs), maps every file and folder source to its destination, and judges a covered file at its mapped destination only for options that are installed (an option counts as installed when any file it places exists). Test scripts/tests/test_install_gate_fomod_mapping.py. Package layouts are not to be bent to fit a gate; fix the gate. Packages with no ModuleConfig.xml are judged as before.


## Three quiet traps met building Perfected Wheeler 1.4.1 (2026-10-20)

**What happened.** Building Wheeler's weapon-type slots toggle, a sub-agent hit three tools that fail without saying so.
(1) install-test-build.py takes the mod FOLDER NAME as its second argument; given a full path it installed the files and
then reported the mod as disabled. (2) The version gate only writes CMakeLists.txt for Wheeler-Refined, so the package
README's "..., version X.Y.Z" line kept 1.4.0 and the package gate's README check failed; the packager rewrites only a
line of the form "Version X.Y.Z". (3) translation-coverage.py reports "Wheeler-Refined draws no translated text", so
rule 66 is never checked for this mod; its settings rows are drawn from dMenu descriptor JSONs in English.

**Do instead.** Pass install-test-build.py the folder name. Give Wheeler-Refined a registry location for its README
version line (open). Treat a "draws no translated text" result as a coverage gap, not a pass: the new row's strings were
added to all eleven Wheeler_*.txt files by hand through $WeaponTypeSlotsName / $WeaponTypeSlotsDesc. Topics: wheeler,
install, versioning, translations.

---
**Root cause:** Three tools failed silently (a folder-name argument, a version line the gate does not update, a coverage check reporting no translated text), and an empty or quiet result was read as success.

## A side effect inside a wrapped permission query that the game polls on a timer repeats forever (WGO Magic system, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, witcher, script, ws, sound

**Symptom:** after loading a save with Magic below one cast, the "no adrenaline" sound (gui_no_adrenaline) played about ten times a second until Magic regenerated.

**Root cause:** the wrapper treated a permission query as if it were the moment of the player's action; it never asked who calls the query and how often.

**What was wrong:** the wrapper of `CR4Player.HasStaminaToUseSkill` played the sound and flashed the pips (`IndicateTooLowAdrenaline`) whenever it answered "refused". That function is a permission QUERY, and the game polls it: `playerWitcher.ws` OnSpawned starts a 0.1 s timer (`UpdateGamepadTriggerEffect`) that asks it every tick. A query answered "no" on a timer meant a sound ten times a second.

**Do instead:** a wrapper of a query (`Can*`, `Has*`, `Is*`, `Get*`) only answers, and logs rate-limited. Feedback (sound, flash, HUD message) belongs in the handler of the real input press, found where vanilla plays its own refusal sound (`playerInput.ws` OnCastSign / AltCastSign, `r4Player.ws` ProcessUsableItemsTransition play `gui_no_stamina`). Let the query only NOTE the refusal while a press handler runs, and let the press wrapper act once per press, latched until the button is released. Before shipping a wrapper of a game function, grep who calls it and from what (timers, per-frame updates, menus); if the answer includes a timer or a menu, nothing audible or visible may live in it. Sweep the mod's other query wrappers for the same mistake (WGO had none; its other queries only log once or change state idempotently).

---

## A Witcher 3 inventory "stats" hint never showed - the stats module is never selectable, so its context is never created (WGO 1.0.0, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, swf, menu, input, diagnosis

**Symptom:** a "Spend character point" button hint added in a W3PlayerStatsContext Init wrap never appeared, and X did nothing in the inventory stats panel.

**What was true:** Main Agent's first theory (vanilla updateInputFeedback clears the bindings) was wrong - that function has no callers in 5.01. The real cause: the swf's PlayerStatsModule.hasSelectableItems() returns false, so navigation never selects the "inventory.stats" module and W3PlayerStatsContext is never created. In the centered stats view CharacterRendererController.handleInput swallows every key, and script never learns the selected row - catching A on a custom row needs a panel_inventory swf edit.

**The check:** before claiming a cause from one script function, confirm it is actually called (grep its callers) and trace the swf side of menu input. A stats-list row can be ADDED from script (GetPlayerStatsGFxData wrap), but reacting to it needs the swf.

---
**Root cause:** A cause was claimed from one script function without confirming it was ever called, and the swf side of menu input, where the stats module is never selectable, was not traced.

## A scan for mods that replace a file missed every mod folder with "[" in its name - Python's glob reads brackets as a pattern (WGO build queue A1b, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, witcher, mo2, swf, python, packaging

**Symptom:** the check "does any ticked mod already replace panel_inventory?" walked `C:\MO2\The Witcher 3\mods\<mod>\**\*.bundle` with `glob.glob` and reported no hit. A second look found Simple Loadout System 1.0.4 (ticked) ships `panel_inventory.redswf` - shipping WGO's own edited copy would have silently replaced one of the two.

**What was true:** most mod folders in that instance are named "[Remastered 5.01] ...". `glob` treats `[...]` as a character class, so `glob.glob(r"...\[Remastered 5.01] Simple Loadout System 1.0.4\**\*.bundle")` matches nothing - no error, an empty list. 14 of the 19 swf replacements were in bracketed folders.

**The check:** never build a glob pattern from a folder name - walk with `os.walk` (or `glob.escape(root)` first). When a "no conflict" scan returns nothing, prove the scanner sees a known positive in the same run (here: HPM's own `hud_wolfstatbars.redswf`) before trusting the empty result.

---
**Root cause:** A glob pattern was built from a folder name containing brackets, which glob reads as a character class, and an empty scan result was trusted without proving the scanner could find a known positive.

## A regex that edited label text also matched code, and the failed run then truncated the menu XML to 0 bytes (WGO build queue A3, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, python, xml, strings

**Symptom:** a one-off script removed "(... <difficulty> ...)" parentheticals from labels in tools\tier_strings.py with a regex for "(...<...>...)". It also removed two code lines containing `(r"\t<!-- TIERS.*?<!-- /TIERS -->", ...)`; the generator then crashed inside `f.write()` - after `open(MENU_XML, "w")` had already emptied WitcherGearOverhaul.xml.

**The check:** a text fix on a source file is scoped to the lines it means (the phrase table), never the whole file; `git diff` the file before running it. A generator builds its output fully (and asserts it looks sane) before opening the target for writing - school_strings.py / unique_strings.py now assert the new XML is a string and at least half the old size first.

---
**Root cause:** A one-off regex was run over the whole source file instead of only the lines it was meant for, and the generator opened the target for writing before it had built and checked its output.

## A Witcher 3 item definition can hold <item> tags inside its own <item> block - a non-greedy regex cut the record short (WGO Viper split, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, xml, python

**Symptom:** copying the Hearts of Stone Viper gloves' record with `<item name="...">.*?</item>` produced a definitions XML that no longer parsed ("mismatched tag").

**What was true:** a `<variant>` lists the items it pairs with as `<item>Geralt Shirt</item>` inside the outer `<item>`; the first `</item>` belongs to the variant.

**The check:** cut an `<item>` record by depth (count `<item` opens against `</item>` closes) and parse every generated XML (`xml.dom.minidom`) before packing it.

---
**Root cause:** A non-greedy regex assumed an item record has no nested item tags, so it cut the record at the first closing tag instead of tracking depth.

## Enemy tiers "did nothing": the resistance step only reached resistances already above 0, and people have none - plus nothing redid the enemies already standing there (WGO fix round, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, script, diagnosis

**Symptom:** the owner set soldiers to Legendary and still killed them in one hit.

**What was true:** four things stacked. (1) `WGO_ET_Apply` added tier resistance points only where `perc > 0`; every physical resistance of a person is 0 in `opp_base_abl.xml` ConDefault, so a soldier gained nothing - the rule had been written from the monster case. (2) No armour at all, while Geralt's hits run 10,000 - 34,000. (3) The game runs `CNewNPC.AddLevelBonuses` only at spawn, `SetLevel`, difficulty and upscaling changes - a menu change, or a soldier turning hostile after spawning, never reached the enemies already present; the header promised "the start of a fight" but no code did it. (4) Hostile guards (`ENGT_Guard`, the type of many soldiers) were excluded.

**The check:** when a scaling step is gated on the target's current value, test it against the base data of EACH enemy family (people, monsters, beasts) before shipping; when a promise in a header says when something re-applies, grep for the call that does it. The fix: armour per enemy level, resistances on every entry, a 2 s sweep (`WGO_ET_Sweep`) that redoes out-of-date NPCs through the game's own `RecalcLevel`, hostile guards covered.

---
**Root cause:** The resistance step was written from the monster case and gated on a value that is zero for people, it was never tested against each enemy family, and no code did the re-apply that its header promised.

## A "same key as jump" feature tested only against the default layout - the owner's pad has jump on Y and Roll on A (WGO combat jump, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, input, script

**Symptom:** jump-and-climb in combat never fired for the owner.

**What was true:** the build only hooked `OnCbtDodge` / `OnCbtRoll` and needed them on the jump key. His `input.settings` (MO2 profile `Default`) has `[Exploration] IK_Pad_Y_TRIANGLE=(Action=Jump)` and `ExplorationInteraction`, `[Combat] IK_Pad_A_CROSS=(Action=CbtRoll)`, `IK_Pad_B_CIRCLE=(Action=Dodge)` and `IK_Pad_Y_TRIANGLE=(Action=SelectAxii)` - no press ever reached the check.

**The check:** read the owner's real `input.settings` in the profile before building an input feature, and key it on the physical key (`GetPadKeysForAction` of the target action), not on one assumed action. The fix hooks every combat action that can sit on the jump key (Roll, Dodge, Sign select, light / heavy attack, Sign cast).

---
**Root cause:** The feature was built and tested against the default input layout instead of the owner's real input settings, and was keyed on assumed actions rather than the physical key.

## Monster mutagens ran the skill-group colour bonus at LESSER size - the game reads the tier from the item's alchemy_s19 ability (WGO, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, mutagen, script

**Symptom:** a greater red mutagen showed +52 % attack power, a Water Hag (WGO: above greater) in the same slot +26 %.

**What was true:** in 5.01 the colour multiplier is applied by the CHARACTER MENU (`characterMenu.ws GetGroupBonusDescription` adds `<tier>_mutagen_color_<c>_x` x matching skills) and by Synergy (`MutagensSyngergyBonusUpdateSingle`), both picking the tier from `GetMutagenBonusAbilityName(item)` - the item's ability tagged `alchemy_s19`. Every monster mutagen carries `lesser_mutagen_color_<c>`; WGO's top-up sat on Geralt and is not multiplied.

**The check:** when a mod raises an item "above" a tier, trace every place the game reads that tier (abilities by tag, menu code that adds abilities), not only the item's stat line. The fix wraps `GetMutagenBonusAbilityName` / `...Names` for WGO monster mutagens (greater ability of the colour), re-runs the game's Synergy update at every sync, and rewrites the menu line to the real value.

---
**Root cause:** Only the item's stat line was traced, not every place the game reads the mutagen tier, so the bonus was applied at the default tier.

## Git Bash grep `$'\r'` reported no CRLF in files that were CRLF, and heredoc edit scripts with literal tabs failed to match (WGO fix round, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** python, process, git

**Symptom:** exact-text replacements of WitcherScript blocks kept failing with "count 0" although `cat -A` showed the same text.

**What was true:** the working copies are CRLF (core.autocrlf true) - `cat -A` and `grep $'\r'` in Git Bash did not show it; Python's `repr` did. Inline Python heredocs also lose or mangle tabs and backslashes (the backslash guard blocks the latter).
