**The check:** for block edits use a patch file written with the Write tool and a script that normalises CRLF to LF, replaces, and writes back in the file's own newline style (the scratchpad `patch.py` shape: `>` marks a leading tab), and check line endings with Python, not Git Bash tools.
**Root cause:** Git Bash tools were trusted to show line endings and tabs that they do not display, so exact-text replacements failed with no visible difference.


## A control holds several keys on one device: "already bound" and "is the default" checked only the first (Unbind Vanilla Controls Skyrim 1.1.2, 2026-10-20)

**What happened.** A player bound Favorites to D-pad Up and after a restart it was on Up AND Down. The game's controlmap
gives Favorites two pad buttons (Up [value removed], Down [value removed]). UVC's bind code looked only at the control's first mapping,
which after sorting was already Up, so it skipped the bind and Down stayed; the remap recorder compared the live key with
only the FIRST default key, so "Up only" read as the default and its INI line was dropped. A second trap: an empty
mapping ([value removed]) can sort before a controller key such as Y ([value removed]), so "the first mapping" is not "the bound key".

**Do instead.** Any "already there" or "is the default" check on a control compares the WHOLE set of its mappings on
that device; a bind sets exactly one mapping and empties the rest; the bound key is the first mapping that HAS a key.
Also: package-mod cannot build UVC's two-line FOMOD (no seed - it makes a flat package); repack-fomod does.
Topics: controls, unbind, input, package.

---
**Root cause:** The 'already bound' and 'is the default' checks looked at only the first of several mappings on a device, and assumed the first mapping was the bound key even though an empty mapping can sort before it.

## A Witcher 3 stats list re-sent from script kept its old right-hand card - the panel refills the card only when the selected row CHANGES (WGO character points, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, swf, menu, ui

**Symptom:** after spending a character point from the inventory pop-up, the "N / 12" lines in the card beside the "Add character points" row stayed at the old numbers until the inventory was closed and opened again, although the script re-sent the whole list (OnRequestStatsData).

**What was true:** panel_inventory's PlayerGeneralStatsPanel `set data` replaces the list's DataProvider but keeps `selectedIndex`; the card (PlayerDetailedStatsPanel.setData) is only filled from `handleIndexChanged`, i.e. on a selection change. Re-sending the data with the same row selected never fires it.

**The check:** before assuming "send the data again" refreshes a Scaleform panel, decompile the panel class (FFDec `-selectclass ... -export script`) and read what its data setter actually redraws. The fix here: after the re-send, read `mcPanelGeneralStats.mcStatsList.selectedIndex` from script and set `mcPanelDetailedStats.data` to that row's subStats (SetMemberFlashArray on the sprite, which runs the AS3 setter) - no swf edit.


---
**Root cause:** It was assumed that re-sending the data refreshes a Scaleform panel, without reading what the panel's setter actually redraws; the card refills only on a selection change.

## A Witcher 3 skill-slot list with more rows than sockets hands the extra rows to the MUTAGEN slots - CD PROJEKT RED's count always matched, so it never showed (WGO mutation slots 5-6, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, swf, menu, slots, mutation

**Root cause:** a by-index pass ahead of a by-id pass in SlotsListPreset.populateData, safe only while rows = sockets.

**What was found (before it shipped, by reading the movie):** adding skill slots 17 and 18 makes the character menu's
`character.skills.slots` list 18 rows long. `SlotsListPreset.populateData` (panel_character_dupe and the legacy movie)
first gives row i to renderer i - sockets sorted by slot id, then the four `SlotSkillMutagen` renderers - and only then
`SlotsListSkillSockets.populateData` re-matches rows to sockets by slot id. With 16 sockets in a grid (the normal grid
before the mutation system; the legacy movie; another mod's default movie) rows 17 and 18 land on two mutagen slots.
The game never hit it because its row count equalled its socket count: the mutagens got `null`, and `SlotBase.data`
ignores null, so the mutagen data survived every slot refresh.

**Do instead:** when a Scaleform list is given more data rows than the game ever sent, read the list's populate code for
an index-based pass before trusting a by-id one. Here: the movie's `setData` keeps only rows with a socket in the shown
grid and re-applies the full list when the grid switches; for movies without the new sockets the script re-sends the
mutagen list after the slot list (both menus' `UpdateAppliedSkills` wrappers).

## WitcherScript: a method call on an array a function RETURNS does not compile - "Only arrays coming from variables can be modified", even for .Size() (WGO mutation slots 5-6, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, scripts

**Root cause:** WitcherScript allows array methods only on variables; and a known library entry was not applied before writing an event wrapper.

**Symptom:** the dry compile stopped with `[line]: Only arrays coming from variables can be modified` on
[code removed]. The same build's first dry compile had stopped on a bare
`return;` inside an `@wrapMethod` over an EVENT (OnGetLockedMutationSkillSlotTooltipData) - the known entry "A WitcherScript
@wrapMethod over an EVENT takes the event's bool return", applied late.

**Do instead:** copy a returned array into a local (`slots = thePlayer.GetSkillSlots(); slots.Size()`), and in a wrapper
over an `event` never write a bare `return;` - put the work in an `if` or an `@addMethod` helper. Dry compile
(`tools\dry_compile.py`) before handing a build over, as every W3 build here does.

## A Witcher 3 mod built for 4.0x loads its bundles and texture cache on 5.0, but its collision cache and its world file do not carry over - REDkit 5.0 calls a v9 collision.cache "NOT a collision cache", and a 4.0x .w2w has none of the Remastered lighting (Kaer Morhen Fortress, 2026-10-20)

**Situation.** Kaer Morhen Fortress's second build takes "Kaer Morhen Restored To Its Ancient Splendor" (a 2024 REDkit
4.0x build) as its castle. The question was whether such a mod works on 5.01 as it ships.

**Root cause:** "the game still loads old mods" was true per file TYPE, not for the whole mod - 5.0 kept readers for
old bundles, CR2W v163 and v6 texture caches, but changed the collision cache format and added the Remastered
environment block to the world file, so a 4.0x world mod is partly current and partly not.

**What was true (each checked, not inferred).**
- **Bundles:** [value removed]-entry TOC, header version 3. REDkit 5.0's own `uncook` refuses them ("invalid headerVersion: 3
  (expected 5)"), and `upgradeBundles` wants a metadata.store beside them; our pipeline (extract with
  `w3bundle_any.py`, `wcc_lite pack`) writes 5.0 bundles with byte-identical files. The GAME reads old bundles: ticked
  Classic 1.32 and 4.04 mods in the owner's profile work.
- **texture.cache v6:** the game reads it (several ticked mods ship v6 caches).
- **collision.cache v9:** `wcc_lite optimizecollisioncache -file=<v9> -out=...` answers "Specified file is NOT a
  collision cache"; the same call on a 5.0 mod's v11 cache succeeds (the control). Treat a pre-5.0 collision cache as
  unread on 5.0 until a game test says otherwise - its new geometry may have no collision.
- **World file (.w2w):** a 4.0x world file has the same layer imports as 5.0's but none of the Remastered environment
  settings (AgX tone mapping, path tracing, remaster bloom, translucency, new grass parameters - 112 property names).
  Shipping it takes that world's lighting back to the Next-Gen look. Keep the game's 5.0 world file unless the mod's
  own world-file change (new layer entries, terrain clipmap) is needed, and say what is lost.
- **Cooked CR2W checksums:** export data CRC and table CRCs are plain CRC32 over the data and the table bytes; the
  header CRC matches no simple CRC32/FNV-1a formula over header, tables or file. So patching a cooked layer in place is
  not proven safe.
- **wcc_lite pack writes entry names as UTF-8**; a mod's ANSI name ([value removed]) comes back as C3 A9. Our readers now decode
  names as latin-1 so the byte is kept and the read-back check catches it.
- **`wcc_lite cook -mod=<folder>`** finds the files but cannot load them ("Failed to load ... - is this a resource");
  `-basedir` replaces the whole depot (fatal assert). Cooking needs the files where a REDkit project's workspace puts
  them.

- **Occlusion tiles (found the hard way, the same day):** the first build shipped Restored's four castle
  `.w3occlusion` tiles, which I had read as "emptied" from their 407-byte size - they are real Umbra tomes kept in
  `.w3occlusion.1.buffer` files (0.9-2.2 MB), computed for Restored's 4.0x world. In game the castle was "more or less
  gone ... some things floating around in midair": the tome culled every static object (sector data from every layer)
  in those tiles, while entities still drew. Fix: the game's own 5.0 no-data tile (`dataStatus EUTDS_NoData`, 384
  bytes, no buffer - 10,476 of the game's 11,520 tiles) at those paths. An occlusion tome belongs to ONE build of ONE
  world; a world mod's tiles are only right with exactly the world and layers they were baked against.
- **Materials:** Remastered 5.0 moved some Kaer Morhen meshes from pbr_vert_blend + texture arrays to pbr_std; a 4.0x
  copy of such a game mesh names textures that no longer exist. Check every import of a shipped mesh against the game's
  texture.cache, not only its bundles (KaerMorhenFortressW3 `tools\prove_offline.py`).

**Do instead.** For a pre-5.0 Witcher 3 world mod: repack its bundles, keep its texture cache, never ship its occlusion
tiles (use the game's no-data tile where its geometry changed, or re-bake in REDkit 5.0), flag its collision cache
as the top in-game risk, compare its world file's properties with the game's before shipping it, and never trust a
cooked-file patch whose header checksum cannot be reproduced. `wcc_lite optimizecollisioncache` is a cheap headless
test of whether REDkit 5.0 accepts a collision cache.

## Witcher 3 skill-grid moves follow each socket's navigation INDEX, not the nearest slot - added sockets got no controller navigation (WGO mutation slots 5-6, 2026-10-20)

**Topics:** w3, wgo, swf, menu, slots, controller

**Root cause:** the build read SearchForNearestSelectableIndexInDirection and assumed it was the move; handleInputPreset only calls it when the slot's own navigationUp/Down/Left/Right target is unselectable.

**What happened:** two sockets added to panel_character_dupe's mutation grid showed and took mouse drops, but the D-pad never reached them (owner's test). The design said moves were spatial and needed no wiring. SlotsListBase.handleInputPreset follows the timeline's per-slot renderer indexes; a -1 or a selectable target is followed as it is. Inserting the sockets also shifted the four mutagen renderers by two, so every number that pointed at a mutagen now pointed somewhere else.

**Do instead:** before claiming a Scaleform list's navigation is spatial, read the handler the MODULE actually calls (here ModuleSkillsSocketsDupe.handleInput -> handleInputPreset), not a helper that exists in the list. When renderers are added, re-point every existing navigation number at the same slot's new index and give the new ones (and their neighbours) explicit numbers - WGO's wgoWireNavigation in flash\wgo_slots.as.txt.

## "Launch when ready" was read as "launch with what is built" - the game was launched while a requested change (HPM vanilla adrenaline toggle, colours) was still unbuilt in another session (Main Agent, 2026-10-20)
**What happened:** the owner said "launch when ready". Main Agent installed the three packages that existed (WGO, KMF, HPM 1.0.1 at 4dbbdab), dry compiled, and launched. The HPM round the owner had asked for (one Adrenaline bar entry with a vanilla-look toggle, Magic blue, adrenaline red) was still with the Secondary Agent - its repo had no commit after 4dbbdab - and the launch summary mentioned that only as a side note. The owner went in game, found the straight bar and no toggle, and asked why the game was launched before the changes were ready.
**Reasoning failure:** "ready" was measured against the packages on disk, not against the list of changes the owner was waiting to test. An outstanding item owned by another session was treated as "not mine, so not blocking".
**Resolution / rule:** before a launch for owner testing, list every change the owner asked for in this round and mark each built+installed or not. If any is not, do NOT launch; tell the owner which item is still outstanding and who has it, and launch only when it lands - unless the owner explicitly says to launch without it.
**Root cause:** 'Ready' was measured against the packages on disk rather than against the list of changes the owner was waiting to test, and an outstanding item held by another session was treated as not blocking.

## A Windows bugcheck during a Root Builder deploy zeroed BuildData.json - MO2 then dies silently at "Previous build data exists, updating" (Njordlinger, 2026-10-21)
**What happened:** at 03:45 the PC bugchecked ([value removed], after an AMD driver dropout crashed Skyrim in CommunityShaders' DX12 present). Root Builder had been mid-way through its deploy for the Njordlinger Test launch. Afterwards plugins\data\rootbuilder\DModlistsNjordlingerStock_Game\1_5_97_0\BuildData.json was 51,813 bytes of zeros, and every MO2 start ended at "[RootBuilder] Previous build data exists, updating." with no process left - no error dialog.
**Reasoning failure to avoid:** treating "MO2 won't start after a crash" as an MO2 or profile problem; the profile files (modlist/plugins/loadorder, ModOrganizer.ini) were intact.
**Resolution:** with MO2 closed, move the zeroed BuildData.json aside AND move out the Root files the interrupted deploy left in Stock Game (byte-identical to their mod's Root folder, not in Root Builder's Backup) - moving only BuildData.json would make Root Builder back those leftover copies up as "originals". Both go to _backups, never deleted; Root Builder then does a clean first build. MO2 started normally afterwards. Check after any crash during a launch: an all-zero BuildData.json and leftover Root copies in Stock Game.
**Root cause:** A post-crash failure to start MO2 was treated as an MO2 or profile problem without checking the interrupted deploy's own state files, where BuildData.json had been zeroed.

## Nexus description save: SCEditor val() plus textarea input/change events no longer marks the form changed - Save quietly kept the old text (MO2 Modlist Manager 1.1.5, 2026-10-21)
**What happened:** saving the 1.1.5 description with the old recipe (sceditor val() and input/change events on the textarea) left the form unchanged, so Save stored the old text. The sticky edit had the same class of problem: WysiBB's $(textarea).bbcode(txt) only reads.
**Root cause:** the recipe assumed DOM events reach Nexus's React form state; the form only updates through the React field's own handlers, and the comment editor only through its WysiBB instance.
**Resolution:** description - call the React field's onChange(txt) then onBlur(), found by walking the textarea's __reactFiber up to the node whose props include onRequestGallery (close the preview drawer first on a narrow viewport); ALSO set sceditor.instance(textarea).val(txt), because Save posts the SCEditor's content (SLS 1.0.4, same night: onChange/onBlur alone saved the old text; close the preview drawer, which reopens on every load; a greyed Save means nothing counts as changed); verify by reopening /edit/general and comparing SHA-256. Sticky - w=jQuery(t).data('wbb'); w.$body.html(w.getHTML(txt,true)); w.sync(); dispatch keyup on w.$body[0]; Submit; read the Posts tab back on a fresh load.

## FFDec's script export is not deterministic - the same SWF exported twice gave different text for some classes, so "only my script differs" checks must compare SWF tags byte by byte (SkyUI Config Diag, 2026-10-21)
**What happened:** building an instrumented SkyUI menu, exporting the same inventorymenu.swf twice with FFDec gave different ActionScript text for CategoryList, ButtonGroup and InputDelegate, so a text diff reported changes that were never made.
**Root cause:** the check assumed decompiled text is a stable fingerprint of the bytecode; FFDec's decompiler output can vary between runs.
**Resolution:** verify edits by comparing the SWF's tags byte by byte against the original (every tag except the edited one must be identical), not by diffing exported script text.

## An edited SkyUI class inside a menu swf never ran - imported libraries ([asset path removed], inventorylists.swf) define the same AS2 class first and the class guard skips later copies (SkyUI Config Diag, 2026-10-21)
**What happened:** an instrumented skyui.util.ConfigManager was built into Norden's inventorymenu.swf and magicmenu.swf (the winning files). In game the original class ran: no log lines, and even a shortened timeout had no effect.
**Root cause:** the patch assumed the menu movie's own copy of the class is the one used. Every SkyUI item menu imports [asset path removed] and [asset path removed] before its own class code, each carries a full copy of the class, and compiled AS2 classes only define themselves if _global already lacks them - so the first imported library's copy wins.
**Resolution:** patch every copy of the class (itemcard.swf, inventorylists.swf and the menus), and have each copy log which file it came from so the log proves which one ran. Check for duplicate class definitions across imported swfs before editing any SkyUI class.


## A new settings row "did not appear": an old test mod's copy of the settings JSON won the load order (Perfected Wheeler 1.4.1, 2026-10-22)

**What happened.** Wheeler 1.4.1's new Weapon Type Slots switch failed its in-game test: not on the AMF page, not found
by its INI key. The code was right. A leftover test folder, "test dMenu NG 1.4 (AMF header test)", enabled high in the
Njordlinger Test modlist, shipped its own dMenu\customSettings\Wheeler Controls.json from 2026-09-20 (56 nodes, no new
row), and it won over ours (57 nodes). wheeler.log's census line (nodes=56) proved it. install-test-build.py's priority
check guarded only dll/swf/esp/esl/pex/bsa, so nothing warned that a higher mod overrode one of our data files.
In the same round a sub-agent installed the 1.4.1 test build into the POSTED Wheeler folder instead of a test folder,
so the posted folder carried an untested DLL for two days.

**Do instead.** A settings or data row that "does not appear" is first checked against the census the mod logs (count
what was loaded), not the code. install-test-build.py now also guards *.json (d04e6cb). A test build goes into a test
folder of its own, never into the posted mod's folder. Topics: wheeler, settings, install, mo2, amf.

**Root cause:** The test checked our code and our package but not what the VFS actually served: the install priority guard covered only binaries, so a data file from an older, higher-priority test mod could silently override ours, and test folders were never retired after their test ended.

**Resolution:** install-test-build.py guards *.json too (d04e6cb); the mod's own census log line is read first when a row is missing; test builds go only into test folders.

## A per-line FOMOD pre-selected the SE/AE DLL on every game - 1.7.104 players got "failed to open address library file" (Infinity UI 2.1.2, 2026-10-22)
**What happened:** a Nexus bug report on Infinity UI 2.1.2 (Skyrim 1.7.104, Address Library v13) showed REL/ID.h(223) "failed to open address library file". The path hash in the error belonged to the CommonLibSSE-NG 3.7 tree that only the SE/AE line links: the player had the SE/AE DLL, which the FOMOD pre-selected as Recommended whatever the game. CommonLib 3.7 treats a 1.7.x exe as SE and looks for version-1-7-104-0.bin, which AL v13 doesn't ship (it ships versionlib-1-7-104-0.bin, database format 5).
**Root cause:** the installer offered one DLL per game line without detecting the game, and the plugin had no check that its build line matched the running game before CommonLib opened the Address Library; the 1.7 line itself was fine.
**Resolution:** FOMOD gameDependency at 1.7.0.0 flips which option is recommended; each line checks the game version before SKSE::Init and loads inert with a plain "choose the other option" message; the Address Library guard added (2.1.3). Read the build-tree hash in an error path to identify which DLL a player is actually running.

## LIO reported lock-breaking as a theft (StealAlarm) - guards shouted "Stop right there" but no bounty or arrest followed (Lock Interaction Overhaul 1.0.6, 2026-10-22)
**What happened:** a Nexus user reported that breaking a lock with LIO's penalty system on made guards yell the arrest line with no bounty, fight or arrest. LIO's Alarm() called player->StealAlarm(lock, base, 1, 5, owner, true), treating the door or chest as a stolen item.
**Root cause:** the crime call was chosen by its name's resemblance instead of copying what the game itself does for the same act; vanilla's lockpicking call sites use Actor::TrespassAlarm(ref, GetOwner(ref), -1), where the third argument is a crime id (-1 = new trespass crime), not gold.
**Resolution:** Alarm() now calls TrespassAlarm(ref, GetOwner(ref), -1) so the game's own trespass crime, witnesses and bounty apply (1.1.0; the fixed "reported value" slider retired). For engine API calls, list the vanilla call sites (gamecallers.py) and copy their exact arguments.

## A standalone pre-finalize check before finalize-mod blocked the finalize on gate C (AMF 2.2.3, 2026-10-22)

**What happened.** Before finalizing AMF 2.2.3, pre-finalize-check.ps1 was run on its own as a "pre-finalize gate" step.
Run that way it does not defer distro-archive-equals-finalized-folder (the distro zip only exists after finalize), so it
recorded a refusal on that row alone. finalize-mod.ps1 then ran the gate and gate C refused: inputs unchanged since the
last refusal. The only way on is finalize-mod -Force -Reason, which the auto-mode classifier denied to a sub-agent.

**Do instead.** Do not run pre-finalize-check.ps1 by itself right before a finalize. Use finalize-mod.ps1 -DryRun for the
look-ahead (it stops before the gate and records nothing), then finalize-mod.ps1, which runs the gate once with the
deferred row. Topics: release, gates, finalize.

**Root cause:** Gate C's "same inputs as the last refusal" check counted every gate event for the mod key and version, whoever recorded it. A standalone run judged a row that can only pass after finalize writes its output, so its refusal was an artefact of running outside finalize, and finalize was compared against it on an identical fingerprint.

**Resolution (2026-10-22, .MD d07cd83):** pre-finalize-check.ps1 takes -FromFinalize, passed only by finalize-mod. Without it the run defers the finalize-output rows ("deferred - runs inside finalize") and records refs.caller = standalone. Gate C compares only with the last gate event from the same caller (events.py last --caller; no caller counts as standalone). A repeat of a refused finalize is still refused. Test: test_gate_c_standalone_never_blocks_finalize.py.

## A sanitiser that names what it removes is itself the leak (Pipeline Kit, 2026-10-22)

**What happened.** build_kit.py kept the owner's email, name, account, home and project paths and chat server invite as literal regexes so it could strip them from the kit, so the kit's own source repo carried every identifier the kit removes, in all commits and tags. Making the repo public as asked would have published them. Two package-gate rows spelled the name with a character class (hidden from a literal scan, not from a reader), and nothing checked for the email.

**Root cause:** Identity patterns were treated as code instead of private data, so they lived in a file that is versioned and shipped; no guard at push time looked for the owner's identity.

**Resolution (2026-10-22, .MD 37b5bed):** All identity patterns live only in the untracked .MD\private\identity-patterns.json (role identity-patterns); build_kit.py, the global pre-push hook (identity-scan.py) and the package-gate kind forbid-private-identity-patterns read it and fail closed without it. The kit went public as a fresh single-commit repo (ApocryphaRealm/PipelineKit); the old history stays private as PipelineKit-history. Topics: release, privacy, git.

## Editing the repo CHANGELOG between packaging and finalize made finalize refuse (Lock Interaction Overhaul 1.1.0, 2026-10-22)

**What happened.** After a clean finalize-mod -DryRun, a sub-agent flipped the repo CHANGELOG heading from "untested" to "working" and pushed, then ran finalize. Gate row shipped-changelog-is-the-repos refused: the package (built before the edit) no longer matched the repo.

**Root cause:** The status line was treated as bookkeeping outside the release inputs, but the package carries a copy of the repo CHANGELOG, so any edit to it after packaging changes a finalize input.

**Resolution:** Revert the edit so the repo matches the package again, then run finalize (no -Force). The CHANGELOG status line is flipped only after posting, together with the next repackage. Topics: release, finalize, changelog.

## A lock answers "is it free?", not "may you launch?" - five agents each launched their own run (rule 69, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** On the night of 2026-10-23 five agents each launched their own in-game test run, although rule 69 says only Main Agent launches and every other session hands its tests over for one combined run. The owner reminded Main of the rule. Separately, a sub-agent's `agent-lock register --holder ... --rename yes` renamed Main's own session ("NGTP Agent"), so no session was registered as Main Agent and the first combined-run executor was later refused by the new gate.

**Root cause:** the only launch gate was the instance lock, which refuses only while ANOTHER session holds it, so any session that found the instance free could launch; Main itself briefed sub-agents to "test in game when the lock is free", turning the rule into a queue of separate launches. A sub-agent shares its parent's session id, so it could also rename the parent.

**Resolution (2026-10-23, .MD 0547f84; rule 69 amended, rules 3.2.0):** every launcher calls `combined-run gate` and refuses without the ticket of Main Agent's open batch; sessions with a build run `test-request submit`; Main runs `combined-run start / launch / result / finish`; `register` refuses a rename without `--rename yes`, and sub-agents name their lock holder with AGENT_SESSION_NAME only. Main briefs sub-agents to return test hand-offs, never "launch when free". Topics: testing, process, sessions, mo2.

## A gate saw a file hidden in MO2 (.mohidden) as "never installed" (Norden UI - Black 1.1.0, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** installed-build-is-the-package refused Norden UI - Black 1.1.0: SKSE\Plugins\RaceMenuAtelier.dll missing from the test folder. The brief (from Main) blamed an unchosen optional FOMOD component; the folder actually held the option, with the DLL hidden by MO2 as RaceMenuAtelier.dll.mohidden, byte-identical to the package's.

**Root cause:** the diagnosis was made from the gate's message instead of listing the folder (including .mohidden files), and the gate itself only knew "present" or "absent", not MO2's hide.

**Resolution (.MD 16e020a, gate-rules 1.0.12):** a file placed only by optional FOMOD options may be hidden in MO2 and is judged by hash; required files stay strict. Test test_install_gate_mohidden_optional.py. Before explaining a gate refusal, list the real folder. Topics: gates, fomod, mo2, release.

## A new Nexus page's first file can't go through nexus-upload.py or a browser upload over 10 MB (New Game in Third Person, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** Publishing a brand-new page: nexus-upload.py only adds a version to an existing file, and the browser's uploader refused the 12.3 MB zip.

**Root cause:** the upload role was written for updates only; first files had always been small enough for the browser.

**Resolution:** create the first main file through the Nexus v3 API (POST /mod-files with mod_id), as the AMF Witcher 3 optional files were; then version-gate -Action link -NexusModId records it. Worth folding into nexus-upload.py as a "first file" mode. Topics: nexus, upload, release.


## An MO2 Python plugin passed under python.exe and failed in MO2: ModOrganizer.exe is not long-path aware (Modlist Manager 1.1.5, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** A player's Modlist Manager window came up empty with "path not found". A mod file path of 276
characters raised WinError 3 from os.path.getsize inside the plugin; nothing caught it, so the whole compute() stopped
before filling any tab, and os.walk had already been skipping folders past 260 characters without a word. Offline runs
under python.exe never showed it: python.exe is long-path aware, ModOrganizer.exe 2.5.2 has no longPathAware entry in
its manifest, so the same code fails only inside MO2.

**Root cause:** The plugin was only ever run under python.exe, which is long-path aware, while ModOrganizer.exe is not; and no per-file error handling existed, so one unreadable path aborted the whole compute().

**Do instead.** Anything an MO2 plugin reads inside mod folders goes through the \\?\ long form (as MO2's own envfs
makeNtPath does); reproduce with the process's long-path flag cleared, not under plain python.exe; one unreadable file
is reported, never allowed to abort the whole read. Fixed in 1.1.6 (_lp() helper, tools\test_long_paths.py).
Topics: mo2, plugin, path, modlist manager.


## "Every page works but HPM's" under TW3SE: a loader guess stood for a week while a run's own logs already ruled it out (HUD Position Manager W3, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** A player on TW3SE reported HPM changing nothing. The to-do entry carried an unchecked guess: HPM's
.asi is loaded only by AMF's dinput8, which the "No dinput8 (for TW3SE)" file drops. The owner's own run of 2026-10-22
04:10 had used exactly that setup, and its logs already answered it: tw3se.log `asi: HUDPositionManager.asi loaded`,
HPM's page registered, and AMF's `game var HUDPositionManager/Report` updating through play. TW3SE loads every .asi in
bin\x64_dx12 (its installation.md). The guess was wrong, so the player's fault is game-side (our Mods folder missing or
disabled in mods.settings, or another mod's HUD movies winning). Second defect found: HPM showed "In your HUD" from a
Report game var left over from a previous session - a value the game keeps proves nothing about the current one.

**Root cause:** An unchecked loader guess sat in the to-do entry and was never tested against the logs the owner's own run had already written; and HPM trusted a Report game var that the game keeps from an earlier session.

**Do instead.** Before guessing at a loader, read the logs a run already wrote (tw3se.log `asi:` lines, the AMF
game-var lines). HPM 1.0.1 now opens its log with `check:` lines (its Mods folder, its mods.settings line, any other
folder shipping its movies or hooked HUD scripts), logs the first bridge hand-off and answer at info, and clears the
stale Report at start. Topics: w3, witcher3, tw3se, hpm, loader, logs.


## A derived FOMOD kept "only recoloured files" and silently dropped the settings file that pairs with the art (Norden UI - Black 1.0.4-1.1.0, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** A player (phbd01) found inventory items "very large" with Norden UI - Black, normal with original
Norden UI on the same options. Every movie was identical to Norden's (0 differences over 874 files). Each Norden
inventory layout also installs MCM\Settings\SkyUI_SE.ini, which sets SkyUI's 3D item scale (0.7, or 0.6 for the
vertical card and Slimventory); build-fomod.py dropped every installer entry without recoloured art, so the ini never
shipped and SkyUI drew items at its own 1.5 - 2.1x to 2.5x Norden's size.

**Root cause:** build-fomod.py kept only the installer entries that had recoloured art, so the non-art files each source option installs (here SkyUI_SE.ini) were dropped, and nothing compared each option's full file list with the source's.

**Do instead.** A FOMOD derived from another mod's installer carries every non-art file each source option installs
(settings, ini, json), not only the files it changes; compare the option's full file list with the source's before
packaging. Fixed in 1.1.1. Topics: norden, fomod, package, settings, skyui.

## Shipping a mod's settings file to restore the source's values also overrides the PLAYER's own settings underneath (Norden UI - Black 1.1.1, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** The 1.1.1 fix shipped Norden's SkyUI_SE.ini with each layout. In game (batch B-20261023-192904) the
owner's Njordlinger Test had Norden UI's own SkyUI_SE.ini at scale 1.5 - not Norden's shipped values - and Black's
copy (0.6) now won, so the item drew ~2.5x smaller than the owner was used to; SkyUI's menu also saves into the
highest-priority copy, so later edits land in Black's folder. The offline fix assumed the file underneath held the
source's defaults.

**Root cause:** The offline fix assumed the file underneath held the source's defaults instead of checking the player's own copy in a real profile; a shipped settings file is user state and overrides whatever sits below it.

**Do instead.** Before shipping a settings file that pairs with art, check what the player's own copy underneath holds
in a real profile; a settings file is user state, so prefer not shipping it when the source mod already provides it
(or make it an option). Topics: norden, fomod, settings, skyui, testing.


## TestBench input in SkyUI lists and "mod off" tests in Njordlinger (batch B-20261023-192904, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** In the SkyUI inventory a TestBench gamepad D-pad up press did nothing (down worked) and the keyboard
up arrow sometimes moved two rows, so the wrong item was shot. Turning Norden UI off for a control step was refused
by the launch gate twice (it holds OxygenMeter2's only config and the fonts the active fontconfig loads).

**Root cause:** Captures relied on TestBench input moving the list selection as sent, without reading the selection back; and the control step tried to untick a whole mod that other mods depend on instead of hiding the one file under test.

**Do instead.** Select list rows by reading the selection back - Papyrus UI.GetString on
_root.Menu_mc.inventoryLists.itemList.selectedEntry.text - and step until it matches before each capture. For a
"without mod X" step in Njordlinger, hide the one file under test (backed up) instead of unticking a mod other mods
depend on. Topics: testbench, skyui, input, testing, combined-run.

## Listed to-do items as "not worked on" from their HEADINGS while the bodies said done (Main Agent, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** Asked for planned Skyrim projects not being worked on, Main listed seven items from the to-do
list's headings alone. The owner pointed out several were already done: the CNO text slider was posted in 1.2.0, the
RaceMenu Enhancer and long-help-text fixes shipped in 2.2.1 and 2.2.2, the dropdown fix in 2.2.3, and the UVC Favourite
row in 1.1.3. Their status lines had been appended to the entry bodies, but the headings were never updated.

**Root cause:** Status was read from the to-do headings alone, and the headings were stale: status lines had been appended to the entry bodies without updating the heading in the same edit.

**Do instead.** Before telling the owner an item's status, read the entry's LAST status line (and the CHANGELOG if
needed), not the heading. When an entry's status changes, update its heading suffix in the same edit. Topics:
todo, records, status.

## combined-run finish: crashes on a surrogate after restoring, and does not undo test-build installs (batch B-20261023-201147, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** finish crashed with UnicodeEncodeError (surrogate) after it had already restored the files, leaving
an empty restore report. It also left install-test-build installs in existing test folders (Wheeler 1.4.1, UVC 1.1.3,
TestBench), because it restores only files that were backed up; the executor mirrored them back from its own snapshot.

**Root cause:** finish was not safe for a surrogate character in its output, so it crashed after restoring; and it restores only files it backed up, so installs into existing test folders were never snapshotted or undone.

**Do instead.** Run finish as `py -3 -X utf8` until the script is fixed; snapshot every test folder before installing
into it and mirror it back after finish (a `combined-run backup --dir` is being added). Topics: combined-run, testing,
mo2, encoding.


## Probing a settings mod through its own control op wrote the owner's third-party files (UVC 1.2.0, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** A `uvc.control op=function` bind wrote two third-party files at once; one of them (TK Dodge AIO.ini
uDodgeKey 42 -> 1) belonged to a different row, because of a row-index bug. Only the batch backup saved the owner's file.

**Root cause:** A row-index bug in UVC's control op wrote another row's target file, and only the file under test had been backed up rather than every file the mod's adapters can write.

**Do instead.** Before probing any mod that writes other mods' settings, back up every file it could write (all its
adapters' targets), not only the one under test. Topics: uvc, testing, settings, backup.


## Staged test profiles fail the order audit without loadorder.txt and every plugin of their enabled mods (2026-10-23)

**What happened.** The Norden Menu Studio Test profile, built by a staging script, would not launch: no loadorder.txt
(the audit crashed), then Norden UI's UntarnishedUI_Subtitle.esp missing and its fontconfig needing Fonticon.swf from
Oblivion Interaction Icons. Steam F12 also silently produced no file in that profile, so its frames were too-bright
desktop grabs.

**Root cause:** The staging script wrote no loadorder.txt, did not list every plugin of each enabled mod and did not resolve the kept UI mods' asset dependencies; and nothing checked that a capture file existed in the new profile.

**Do instead.** A profile-staging script writes loadorder.txt and lists every plugin of each enabled mod, and resolves
the asset dependencies of the UI mods it keeps (fonts, icon SWFs); after the first capture in a new profile, check the
file exists. Topics: mo2, profile, testing, capture, norden.

## Closing the map with TestBench "menu close" during SkyUI's finder search leaks a text-entry count (batch B-20261023-205401, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** During the AMF keyboard test, closing MapMenu with TestBench `menu close` while SkyUI's location
finder search was active left the game's text-entry counter one higher (confirmed with a control run without AMF). PC
hotkeys and AMF's text-field detection stayed dead until a relaunch, costing an extra launch.

**Root cause:** The menu was closed by TestBench `menu close` instead of its own keys while SkyUI's search was active, which left the game's text-entry counter one higher; nothing checked that count before the next step.

**Do instead.** After any search box is opened, close the menu through its own keys (Esc/B), never `menu close`; check
the text-entry count is back to 0 before the next step. Also: UI.GetString returns SkyUI search text in a different
letter case than shown ("IRON" vs "iron") - judge text from frames or AMF state; TestBench pad D-pad Up and A/B/X never
reach game menus (Start and D-pad down do) - mark rows that need the game to see those buttons "needs owner's pad".
Topics: testbench, skyui, input, testing, amf, keyboard.

## A test teleported with `cow Tamriel 5 -3` into Whiterun's Tamriel stand-in, and the frame looked like broken terrain (batch B-20261023-220257, 2026-10-23)

**What happened.** The batch executor used `cow Tamriel 5 -3` to reach Whiterun. That cell is the low-detail Tamriel
copy of the city (walls, two WRHouse*LOD shells, flat terrain) meant only for distant viewing; the walkable city is the
separate WhiterunWorld. The frame (flat white ground, house bases cut off, player sunk to the waist) reached the owner
as a possible terrain/collision bug and cost an investigation, an interrupted batch and a closed repro.

**Root cause:** The executor assumed the Tamriel cell at Whiterun's grid was the walkable city, but it is the low-detail distant-view stand-in (the city is WhiterunWorld); the frame was reported without checking the cell's worldspace.

**Do instead.** Reach walled cities with `coc <CityOrigin>` (WhiterunOrigin, etc.) or a door, never `cow` into the
Tamriel cells under a city; before reporting an exterior visual problem, check the cell's worldspace and whether it is
a city stand-in. Topics: testing, testbench, worldspace, terrain, combined-run.

## Matching an owner's screenshot framing in game: camera, vanity, placement and horse traps (batch B-20261023-233541, 2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Re-shooting the owner's console screenshots took many tries: `player.setangle` in third person turns
the character but not the camera; the idle vanity camera took over while standing still; `tfc` plus moving the player
gave sky or empty frames; placing the player at a reference's z put them under the terrain; `player.moveto` lands
beside an object, not at its centre; an unloaded cell's ref gave "self form not found"; the player's horse walked into
frame.

**Root cause:** Each try relied on a console behaviour that does not hold: setangle in third person turns only the character, the idle vanity camera takes over when standing still, a reference's z is not safe ground for the player, moveto lands beside an object, and an unloaded cell's reference cannot be read.

**Do instead.** Use TestBench `camera setPov first` and check with `camera get`; `setini "fAutoVanityModeDelay:Camera"
99999` for the session; skip tfc in first person; place ~250 units above and let the player land; read a ref's position
with Papyrus GetPositionX/Y/Z (or the plugin's REFR DATA when its cell isn't loaded); move away and `tai` the horse.
Topics: testing, testbench, capture, camera.


## Running PGPatcher with an override mod enabled feeds the override's meshes back in as PGPatcher's input (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** PGPatcher ran with "Snowdrift Ground Snow (personal)" enabled, so its output was built from our
drift meshes; the drift builder's source paths no longer existed, and the builder deleted its build folder before
checking sources. The All Snow installer's list of generated outputs also lacked PG_1.esp, so it would have placed its
plugin after PG_1.esp. A test request stored as instance:njordlinger (lower case) started a 0-request batch.

**Root cause:** PGPatcher was run with our override mod still enabled, so it read the override's meshes as input; the drift builder deleted its build folder before checking that its sources existed, the All Snow installer's generated-outputs list lacked PG_1.esp, and the request instance was compared with case.

**Do instead.** After a PGPatcher rerun, rebuild overrides from PGPatcher's _pgpatcher_dups or their previous output
(the builder now resolves every source before writing); every installer that places plugins before the generated
outputs must list PG_1.esp; store request instances in canonical case (combined-run now compares without case).
Topics: pgpatcher, mo2, snow, plugins, combined-run.


## Two sessions staging in the same .MD index: one commit swept up the other's staged files (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** The powershell agent staged its repack-fomod fix and test, its commit was stopped by low memory, and
the batch executor's later commit of combined-run.py (7449058) included those staged files under its own message.

**Root cause:** Both sessions shared one git index in .MD, and the later commit was made without an explicit pathspec, so it committed everything staged, including the other session's files.

**Do instead.** Commit with an explicit pathspec (`git commit -- <files>`) whenever another session may be working in
the same repo, and check `git diff --cached --stat` before committing. Topics: git, sessions, records.



## combined-run result refused a short request id that start --only had accepted, and finish then wrote NOT-RUN over a real pass (batch B-20261024-004955-caa9, 2026-10-24)

**What happened.** The log clean-up batch was opened with `start --only 2d72` (a unique suffix, accepted). After the run
`result --request 2d72` printed "not in batch" without failing the next command, `finish` ran in the same call and wrote
NOT-RUN for the request, and a closed batch refuses any later `result`. The real verdict had to be appended by hand.

**Root cause:** `result` refused the short id that `start --only` had accepted (the two matched ids differently), and its "not in batch" did not fail the call, so `finish` in the same call went on and wrote NOT-RUN.

**Do instead.** Pass the FULL request id to `combined-run result`, and run `finish` as a separate call only after reading
that `result` printed "written". Topics: combined-run, testing, process.


## A text-position edit to gate-rules.json put a note into another row's id and switched the whole package gate off (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Appending a dated note to two rows' "why" text, a script searched for the first `",` after
`"why": "` - but those why values contain escaped quotes (`\"...\",`), so the search landed early and, for one row,
past the row's end: the note was written into the next row's id (distro-sticky-fits-a-nexus-comment). json.loads still
passed (the file was valid JSON), so the commit went through, but the schema check then failed and no package-gate rule
ran for about twenty minutes until a sub-agent noticed while gating Deep Snow.

**Root cause:** The edit script found the value's end by searching for punctuation (`",`), which the escaped quotes inside the why text defeated; and the only check before committing was json.loads, which proves valid JSON, not a valid rule set.

**Do instead.** Edit a JSON value by its exact serialized form (json.dumps of the old value, replaced once), never by
searching for punctuation; after any gate-rules edit, check every id still matches ^[a-z0-9-]+$ and run the package gate
once on a real package before committing - valid JSON is not a valid rule set. Topics: gates, gate-rules, json, tooling.

## Input Manager action ids are positions that go stale - a UVC bind renumbered every action (batch B-20261024-010711, 2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Binding Dodge for All through Input Manager's API made Input Manager rewrite all 56 action files and
shift every `order` by +3; BFCO NG's stored id 6 then meant "Right", so the power-attack key landed on strafe-right. The
bind also rewrote IDCache.json, which the request's Inputs backup did not cover.

**Root cause:** BFCO NG stored an Input Manager action by its position (`order`), which Input Manager renumbers when a bind rewrites its action files; and the backup covered only Inputs, not IDCache.json.

**Do instead.** Identify Input Manager actions by name through its API, never by a stored position; back up the whole
Input Manager folder (incl. IDCache.json) before any bind. Topics: uvc, input, testing, backup.


## Tool and test-harness gotchas from the 2026-10-24 backlog run

**What happened / do instead.** SSE Display Tweaks' DynamicMaxTimeScaling rewrites fMaxTime every frame, so any fMaxTime
read-back is meaningless with it on. QuickLoot's LootMenu blocks Wheeler while the crosshair is on a corpse. Steam F12
makes no file with Community Shaders off and in the minimal Norden profile - check each capture exists. steam-capture
silently failed when the out file already existed. ini-edit on a sectionless INI needs ":Key=Value" ("Section:Key"
appends a new section). install-test-build got 0 files from bash paths with doubled backslashes - use forward slashes.
Console `advlevel` is not a level-up event. `player.placeatme` bandits can kill the player before Actor.Kill lands - tgm
first. A TestBench `game load` once fell back to the main menu - confirm the load before reading results. A plugin's
masters must be checked before a request tells a run to tick it alone (BFCO NG.esp masters BFCO 3.100.2). Topics:
testing, testbench, capture, wheeler, ini, combined-run.

**Root cause:** not established in the entry - the entry collects separate tool behaviours (Display Tweaks rewriting fMaxTime every frame, QuickLoot's LootMenu blocking Wheeler, Steam F12 and steam-capture silently producing no file, ini-edit's section syntax, doubled backslashes in bash paths, advlevel not being a level-up event, placeatme bandits, a `game load` falling back to the main menu, a plugin's masters left unchecked) without a common cause.


## Modlist Manager judged a master "missing" by mod folders only, and the judgement cascaded down every dependent (1.1.5, 2026-10-24)

**What happened.** A player's 1,080-plugin list lost about half its plugins after an Apply. The plugin plan counted a
master present only if it was a base master or sat in an ENABLED MOD FOLDER; Creation Club files in the game's Data
folder (USSEP 4.3 on AE needs four), plugins installed straight into Data and Overwrite plugins all read as missing, so
each dependent was parked in Optional ESPs and the loop then parked everything built on it, link by link. Apply also
dropped every Data / Overwrite / unmanaged plugin from plugins.txt and loadorder.txt. Our own Njordlinger lists never
showed it: their CC files live inside a mod.

**Root cause:** The plugin plan judged a master present only from base masters and enabled mod folders, not the whole data directory MO2 sees (Data, Skyrim.ccc, Overwrite); the judgement cascaded down dependents without asking, and it was tested only on our own lists, where CC files live inside a mod.

**Do instead.** Judge "present" the way MO2 sees the data directory (enabled mods, Skyrim.ccc, Data, Overwrite,
loadorder.txt), never by mod folders alone; a judgement that spreads down a dependency chain lists what it will change
and why, and asks (Cancel by default), before writing anything; keep the tool's own pre-Apply backup and a one-click
undo. Test against a list shaped like a player's (AE, CC files in Data), not only our own instances. Fixed in 1.1.6
(tools\test_master_cascade.py). Topics: mo2, modlist manager, plugin, master, load order.

## Teleporting the test character by coordinates/drop killed it with falling damage - use coc (the owner, 2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Test runs placed the player at coordinates or ~250 units above a reference and "let them land" (an
earlier lesson's workaround for landing under the terrain); the owner watched the character die from falling damage.
His words: "Just use a center on cell command if you're going to teleport."

**Root cause:** An earlier workaround (place the player ~250 units above and let them land) was adopted without allowing for falling damage, instead of teleporting with coc.

**Do instead.** Teleport only with `coc <cell editor id>` (coc <City>Origin for cities). To reach a spot near an
object, coc to the nearest cell, turn tgm on, then move at ground level. This replaces the "place above and let them
land" advice. Topics: testing, testbench, worldspace, camera.

## Searching swap files by the new plant's name missed City Trees' BOS swaps: NotWL renames vanilla tree editor ids (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Palms and sunflowers stood in the eternal-winter snow. Main searched every swap/INI for the new
plants' names and FormIDs and found nothing. The swaps were in City Trees' BOS files (CT_05_WitcherPlants*_SWAP.ini,
CT_10_DiverseShrubs*_SWAP.ini) keyed on the VANILLA base - and Nature of the Wild Lands renames those bases
(TreePineShrub02 -> pine_young_lowest01_summer, TreeThicket01 -> nettle01_summer); BOS resolves both names. BOS replaces
the base at load, so Seasons' winter swaps never see the summer plant. ~11-14k wild refs were affected.

**Root cause:** The search used the new plants' names and FormIDs, but City Trees' BOS swaps are keyed on the vanilla bases, which Nature of the Wild Lands renames; it did not start from the reference's original base and every editor id that base has in the load order.

**Do instead.** For "why is X here", start from the ref's ORIGINAL base in Skyrim.esm, get every editor id it has in
the load order (overrides rename), and search swap files for all of them; read po3_BaseObjectSwapper.log for which
files loaded. BOS acts after Seasons - out-of-season BOS swaps must be hidden for a permanent-winter list. Topics:
bos, seasons, plugins, njordlinger, snow.

## A PBR base colour shipped under a non-PBR texture name rendered paper white, and noon test frames could not see it - they clip at 218 (All Snow Ground Match, 2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Layer A of "All Snow Ground Match (personal)" replaced Nordic Snow's landscape\snow01/snow01alta/
snow02/snowrocks01 (grey, BC3, mean ~107) with Faultier's PBR base colour (BC7_UNORM_SRGB, mean ~222) and Faultier's PBR
normal maps (alpha 255). Every user of those names draws them through the vanilla shader (flat FX drifts, Seasons'
multipass winter material on spruce trunks, TOTS winter meshes). Community Shaders lights a True PBR albedo at 0.65x
(PBRLightingScale, linear lighting off) and the vanilla shader at 1x with full specular from that normal alpha, so the
patches came out near white at Helgen (frame ratio 1.75 in linear light against the PBR ground). The plan had taken the
drift "before" measurement (within 1-2%) as proof - but those drifts got the PBR texture set through a TXST, and every
22f6 baseline frame was shot at noon with max pixel 218 across all frames, so bright surfaces all read ~0.98 of the ground.

**Root cause:** the plan judged "same texture = same colour" without asking which shader draws the name, and accepted
a match measured in frames whose bright end was clipped, so the measurement could not have failed.

**Do instead.** A texture under a name the vanilla shader reads is authored for the vanilla shader: tone = linear PBR
albedo x 0.65 (CS PBRLightingScale), stored UNORM like the file it replaces, its normal map's alpha kept low; the build
refuses a diffuse whose mean luma leaves its band (build_all_snow.py). Measure brightness matches in unsaturated light
(dawn/dusk/overcast, max pixel well under the frame's clip) and report max_pixel with every ratio. Topics: snow,
texture, pbr, dds, testing, capture, community shaders.

## Nexus's description save strips the line break after [/quote] when the next line starts a tag - a raw SHA check fails (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Swapping banner URLs in 18 descriptions, the SHA-256 of the saved text didn't match the edited file:
Nexus removes the newline straight after `[/quote]` whenever the next line starts with a tag, in WYSIWYG, source mode and
with the textarea set directly. Only pages without that pattern matched byte for byte.

**Root cause:** Nexus's save drops the newline after `[/quote]` when the next line starts with a tag, and the verification compared raw hashes without normalising the expected text the same way.

**Do instead.** Normalise the expected text the same way (drop "\n" after "[/quote]" when the next char is "[") before
comparing hashes, and record both hashes; don't treat that difference as a failed save. Topics: nexus, description,
verify.


## A Nexus reply drafted from a summary of the comment asked the commenter what they had already said (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Main Agent drafted a reply to a Nexus commenter (phbd01) from a summary of their comment, and the
draft asked which UI and settings they used - the comment had already said "norden ui og same options work fine". The
owner caught it before it went out.

**Root cause:** the reply answered a paraphrase. Summarising a comment drops exactly the details a reply must not ask
for again, and nothing made the drafter go back to the source text before writing.

**Do instead.** Every reply goes through role `nexus-reply`: `snapshot` re-reads the thread from Nexus and prints it,
the draft is written after that read and reviewed by the Fable session against the verbatim text, and `gate` refuses an
edited draft, a changed thread or a read older than 30 minutes (rule 10, amended 2026-10-24; nexus-page skill,
"Replying to a comment"). Topics: nexus, replies, gate.

## A test that runs git, started from a pre-commit hook, inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE and read the repo being committed (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** test_md_commit, run by .MD's pre-commit hook, created a throwaway repo but inherited git's
GIT_INDEX_FILE (and other GIT_* variables) from the hook, so its git calls read .MD's in-progress index instead. The
refusal discarded git's temporary index, so .MD was unharmed - by luck. Separately, the whole-suite pre-commit hook
(10-14 min) collided across sessions on a memory-short machine: commits killed, stale locks, sessions racing.

**Root cause:** The test did not clear the GIT_* environment variables, so under a pre-commit hook it inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE; and the whole 10-14 minute suite ran in pre-commit on a memory-short machine shared by several sessions.

**Do instead.** Any test (or tool) that runs git clears every GIT_* environment variable first. .MD commits now run
only the changed tools' tests (run-all.py --changed) and go through the md-commit role, which waits for index.lock
politely and never removes it; the full suite runs nightly. Topics: git, tests, hooks, sessions.

## A test's own SendInput presses made MO2 Agent Control report the PC "in use" (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Request 0cc8 checked MO2 Agent Control's idle-based refusal, but the executor had just sent keys
with SendInput. Those reset Windows' idle clock, so the plugin reported "in use" until 5 minutes passed. Separately,
MO2 wrote modlist.txt about 1 second after replying to set_mods, so an immediate read looked like a failure.

**Root cause:** The test's own SendInput presses reset Windows' idle clock, which the idle check reads, and MO2 writes modlist.txt about 1 s after replying to set_mods; the test waited for neither.

**Do instead.** Before any idle-sensitive check, wait 5 minutes after the last synthetic key press. Wait at least 1 s
after set_mods before reading modlist.txt. Topics: mo2, testing, input.

## The request named a version the profile did not have active (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** Request a0e4 said Norden UI Black 1.1.1, but Norden Menu Studio Test had 1.1.0 active. Acting on the
request text alone would have tested the wrong build.

**Root cause:** The version a request names was not checked against the profile's active modlist, and the two disagreed (1.1.1 named, 1.1.0 active).

**Do instead.** Read the profile's modlist before acting on the version a request names; report any mismatch as a
deviation. Topics: testing, combined-run, mo2.

## Helgen tone ratios moved with weather state and box choice (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** For c5e1, the first frame after `fw` was in a different weather state from the settled ones. At dawn,
the patch-to-ground ratio swung from 0.87 to 2.0 depending on the box, because brazier light warms the ground but not
the patch. The old 612b boxes did not fit the new framing.

**Root cause:** The first frame after `fw` was taken before the weather settled, and single measurement boxes were judged at dawn, where brazier light warms the ground but not the patch; the old boxes did not fit the new framing.

**Do instead.** Wait for two matching frames after a weather change. Pick measurement boxes per frame and report several
pairs; judge at noon as well as dawn. Topics: testing, njordlinger, screenshots.

## AMF in-process capture black for a whole launch; what reaches Atelier's ImGui popup (2026-10-24)

**What happened.** AMF's capture returned black frames for the entire launch, RaceMenu included. Separately, TestBench
pad B and synthetic mouse clicks never reached RaceMenu Atelier's ImGui popup, though real Escape, R and Enter via
SendInput did. Its Finish button always draws white (primary style), so how it looks proves nothing about focus.

**Root cause:** not established in the entry - AMF's capture returned black for the whole launch, with no cause recorded; TestBench pad B and synthetic mouse clicks do not reach Atelier's ImGui popup while real SendInput keys do; and the Finish button always draws white, so its look is no evidence of focus.

**Do instead.** In Njordlinger Test, fall back to Steam F12 (includes AMF's overlay with true colours); a desktop grab
reads bright on HDR. Drive Atelier with SendInput keys. Prove focus with done_finish_focused, not by how it looks.
Topics: testing, screenshots, amf, input.

## Two release-gate false results: a folder plugin could never pass rule 29, and a "<version>" placeholder read as an MIT label (MO2 Agent Control, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** Finalizing MO2 Agent Control 1.0.0, the pre-finalize rule 29 check compared only top-level
plugins\*.py files, so a folder plugin (plugins\<Name>\__init__.py) could never be proven installed. Separately, the
package-gate row shipped-text-never-calls-the-mod-mit matched `<Version>[^<]*MIT` case-insensitively, so a README
placeholder "<version>" followed later by "limit" counted as an MIT licence label.

**Root cause:** Rule 29's check compared only top-level plugins\*.py files, so folder plugins were never considered; and the MIT gate row's pattern was case-insensitive with no word boundaries, so a "<version>" placeholder followed by "limit" matched.

**Do instead.** Fixed in 9072db8: rule 29 now recurses into folder plugins (byte-identical, __pycache__ ignored), and the
MIT row needs a real case-sensitive <Version>...</Version> with a standalone MIT, plus word boundaries on the prose
forms. Regression tests: test_prefinalize_mo2_folder_plugin.py, test_gate_mit_label.py. Topics: gates, release, mo2.

## New Nexus page: the browser Files step attached the zip but never uploaded; the generated description duplicated Credit/Support/Source (Deep Snow, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** On the new edit UI, Claude in Chrome's file_upload attached Deep Snow's 7.2 MB zip to the Files step,
but no upload started, even with manual change/input events. Separately, the description draft from ds-1.0.0\gen_ds.py
(simplepage.build) put a full second copy of the Credit, Support and Source text inside the Compatibility spoiler; the
owner's preview image showed it too.

**Root cause:** not established in the entry - why the browser upload never started is not recorded (Claude in Chrome's file_upload attached the zip on the new edit UI, and manual change/input events did not help); the duplicated sections came from gen_ds.py's simplepage.build, and nothing checked the draft for repeated section text before saving.

**Do instead.** Create a new page's first file through the v3 API (POST /mod-files with mod_id) whatever its size -
fold this into nexus-upload.py as a first-file mode (see entry 11981). Before saving a generated description, check
that no section's text appears twice. Making a comment STICKY via Manage also locks it. When Nexus edit-page
screenshots hang, find/get_page_text still work. Topics: nexus, upload, page.

## "Recorded working" was taken as "ready to finalize": three of six finalizes refused on stale packages and unfixed rules (release batch, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** Six mods showing "working" in the ledger were sent to finalize. DEM 1.7.5's package DLLs had been
rebuilt after the record (rule 48); MO2 Bring Game To Front's record predated a behaviour change at repo HEAD; Local Map
Upgrade still called ImGui sliders directly (rule 68); HUD Position Manager failed a playbook check; Item Explorer's
package carried an older CHANGELOG than its repo. Each real finalize spends a gate run, and finalize's text step had
already bumped nexus-page.txt and the banner pill in the refused folders. UVC W3 1.0.0 had in fact been released under
another name (Modern Control Remapping 1.0.1), but its ledger key still read working/unposted.

**Root cause:** A ledger "working" record was taken as ready to finalize without checking the package against that record (rebuilt DLLs, newer repo HEAD, older CHANGELOG) or against the current rules; finalize's text step bumped page text before its gate decided; and a renamed mod's ledger key was never retired.

**Do instead.** Before a real finalize: run the stand-alone package-gate (diagnostic, records nothing); compare the
package's DLL hashes with the ledger's working record; compare the package CHANGELOG with the repo's; check repo HEAD
is not newer than the recorded build. Retire or mark posted any ledger key whose mod was renamed. Topics: release,
versioning, gates.

## Nexus informal warning: our pages disclosed AI code but not AI page media (2026-10-25)

**What happened.** Nexus staff issued the ApocryphaRealm account an informal warning for "content classification and tag
use failure", after earlier notices from staff. Rule 10 asked only for "AI-Generated Content", but Nexus separates
"AI-Generated Content" (code, UI, translations, in-game assets) from "AI Media" (promotional art, thumbnails, videos and
mod page descriptions). Every page's description and banners are AI-made, so 61 of 68 pages lacked "AI Media" and
Norden UI Black had no tags at all. Six live pages were missing from the version registry, so no audit saw them.

**Root cause:** the rule was written from one tag name and never re-checked against the site's own guideline; tags are
set on the public page, outside the edit form, so no page check read them back.

**Resolution.** Both tags added to all 68 pages and read back (4. plans\nexus-ai-tags-2026-10-25\TAGS.md). Rule 10
amended (rules v3.2.4): both tags, never "AI Assisted". Gate row distro-nexus-page-carries-both-ai-tags
(scripts\gates\nexus-ai-tags-gate.py, test_nexus_ai_tags_gate.py) fails a finalize whose page lacks either tag. The
guideline also holds the author to every claim on the page (FPS, "lighter"), so page text needs evidence for such
claims. Topics: nexus, release, page, gates.

## Finalize text step and build tools wipe or bump before the gate decides (2026-10-25)

**What happened.** finalize's text step bumped nexus-page.txt, the notes counter and the banner pill to the new version
in three distro folders before its gate refused, leaving the page text ahead of the zip. build-fomod.py and repack-fomod
remove the folder they replace (rmtree), so an old package survived only because helpers moved it away first.

**Root cause:** finalize's text step writes its version bumps before the gate decides, and build-fomod.py and repack-fomod rmtree the folder they replace without keeping a copy.

**Do instead.** Move a package folder to backups before any rebuild; check a refused finalize's distro folder for
bumped text. Tool fixes are queued (repack-fomod chip). Topics: release, packaging, tools.

## Test-design lessons from combined run 2026-10-25 (presets, DEM typed entry, MO2 stand-in program)

**What happened.** (1) AMF presets: with Remembered settings' "Remember each change made here" on, the test's script-menu
change was written straight into the preset in use, so it never showed as a difference and Load could not undo it - the
test (and the design) assumed a preset is a fixed snapshot. (2) DEM 1.7.5: typing a Scale value above the in-game cap
(0.95) applied live, re-applied every frame without settling, and crashed Skyrim in Scaleform 2/2; only values inside the
cap had been typed before. (3) A held-arrow focus pass at the main menu (13db) did not hold in game, where a "Set to
current" button sits next to the slider. (4) MO2 Bring Game To Front: Windows 11 Notepad hands its window to an
already-running process, so it cannot stand in for a game; msinfo32 works.

**Root cause:** Each test rested on an unchecked assumption: that a preset is a fixed snapshot (remembering wrote the change into it), that typed values would stay inside the cap, that main-menu focus behaviour holds in game beside other widgets, and that Windows 11 Notepad runs as its own process.

**Do instead.** Presets tests change settings while a different preset is in use (or with remembering off). Type values
above and below every slider's cap, at the main menu and in game. Test held-key focus where neighbouring widgets exist.
Use a classic Win32 program with a main window of 640x360 or more as a stand-in game. Write big DevBench results (presets
status can exceed 200 KB) to a file. Topics: testing, amf, sliders, mo2.

## Hand-built parent CELL / WRLD overrides blanked the master's data (Ysgramor's Armor addon 1.0.1, Souls to Perks 1.0.6, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** Both plugins place references in vanilla cells, so they must carry the parent CELL (and WRLD) record.
Ysgramor's generator wrote the tomb cell with only its editor ID (16 bytes against Skyrim.esm's 14 subrecords: lighting,
music, location, encounter zone...), so whenever it won, the tomb lost all of it. Souls to Perks copied Tamriel's WRLD
from a hand-picked subrecord list and dropped MHDT (45 KB of max-height data). The page texts claimed "no record of any
other mod is edited" / "without overriding anything". Separately, package-mod.ps1 carried the PREVIOUS release's plugin
into the new package (it never refreshes plugins).

**Root cause:** Ysgramor's generator wrote the parent CELL with only its editor ID and Souls to Perks copied WRLD from a hand-picked subrecord list, instead of copying the master's record byte for byte; and package-mod.ps1 never refreshes plugins, so the previous release's plugin shipped.

**Do instead.** A required parent record is copied byte for byte from the winning master (everything except per-file
data such as WRLD's OFST and RNAM); compare against what the Creation Kit (or another mod's copy) writes. Page text says
plainly that the plugin carries unchanged copies of the records its placed objects need. Gate row
shipped-plugin-is-the-repos (gate-rules 1.0.20) refuses a package whose plugin differs from the repo's dist copy.
Topics: plugins, esp, records, packaging, nexus.

## Wrapped text followed the content width once AMF's page got a horizontal scroll bar (AMF 2.3.0, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** After 2.3.0 added a horizontal scroll bar to the content pane, ImGui sized wrapped text and tab bars to
the content width instead of the window, so one wide frame kept the page wide: preset text ran off the right edge and the
Controls intro and "Controller" tab were cut off at text sizes 1.5 and 2.0.

**Root cause:** Adding a horizontal scroll bar let ImGui size wrapped text and tab bars to the content width instead of the window, so one wide frame kept the page wide; wrapping at large text sizes was not tested after the layout change.

**Do instead.** Hold the page area to the visible width when a pane can scroll sideways; test wrapping at large text sizes
after any layout change. Topics: amf, imgui, layout.

## Naked Vigilants of Stendarr: a SkyPatcher outfit mod built for the ESL file of its master, installed beside the ESP file (Njordlinger, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** The owner saw naked Vigilants of Stendarr. "Paladin of Stendarr for NPCs" (Nexus 113100, SkyPatcher)
gives VigilantOfStendarrFaction its own outfit and empties and refills the vanilla VigilantOfStendarrOutfit with armour from
"Stendarr Paladin Armor Set" (Nexus 29841) - but it was built for that mod's ESPLite file (110906, IDs [value removed]-[value removed]), while
Njordlinger had the ESP file (110905, IDs like [value removed]). Every armour reference failed; only the amulet resolved.
SkyPatcher.log said so ("[critical] Form not found: StendarrPaladinArmor.esm [id removed]"); the outfit part drops missing
items silently. A plugin patch cannot fix it, because SkyPatcher rewrites the outfit at runtime after plugins load.

**Root cause:** The SkyPatcher mod was built for the ESPLite file of its master, whose FormIDs differ from the ESP file installed in Njordlinger, so every armour reference failed; SkyPatcher drops missing outfit items silently, reporting it only in SkyPatcher.log.

**Do instead.** When an NPC looks naked or wrong, read SkyPatcher.log / SPID logs for "Form not found" first, then check that
each distributor INI's plugin|ID references exist in the installed variant of its master (ESL vs ESP files of one mod
have different IDs). Tool: 4. plans\njordlinger\vigilant-outfits\tools\verify_esplite_ids.py. Gate idea: scan SkyPatcher /
SPID / KID INIs against installed plugins at list-build time. Topics: njordlinger, outfits, skypatcher, spid, esl.

## No '= NULL' default is not 'ImGui dereferences it', and a parameter's name is not its contract (AMF 2.3.0 cimgui null checks, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** To make AMF's "every export is null-checked" claim true, tools\harden-cimgui.py had to guard every
pointer parameter of the 1,397 cimgui wrappers that Dear ImGui dereferences. Two shortcuts would each have been wrong.
(1) "No `= NULL` default in imgui.h means ImGui dereferences it": Dear ImGui 1.90.8 accepts NULL in at least 95 parameters
that have no default - FocusWindow(NULL) clears the focus, SetActiveID(0, NULL) clears the active id, PushFont(NULL) uses
the default font - so guarding them would have turned valid calls into no-ops. (2) The old generator treated every `p_*`
name as optional and skipped it: `p_selected` is optional in MenuItem but dereferenced in Selectable, and `p_data` is always
dereferenced - the 12 real crash gaps were all `p_data`.

**Root cause:** Both shortcuts read a parameter's null contract from signals that do not define it - the absence of a `= NULL` default, and a `p_*` name - instead of from the callee's own code.

**Do instead.** Decide each parameter slot from the callee's own code, never from its name or the absence of a default.
Keep the NULL-legal slots in ONE file that both the generator and the audit read (tools\imgui-null-ok.json, each entry
citing the ImGui code that handles NULL), so the two can never disagree. Topics: amf, imgui, cimgui, null-checks, gates.

## An empty-string stand-in for a null pointer is not always safe (AMF 2.3.0 cimgui null checks, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** Substituting `""` for a null `const char*` is the easy guard, but for some parameters it is worse than
the null: for a range end (`*_end`), `base` or `in_text_curr`, the "" points into unrelated memory and the callee does
pointer arithmetic between it and a real pointer; for a `mode` string passed to fopen, "" trips the CRT's invalid-parameter
handler, which ends the process. A first-parameter range begin that gets "" while its end is real builds an invalid range
(for example igImStrchrRange(NULL, end)).

**Root cause:** "" was assumed to be a safe universal stand-in for a null `const char*`, but some parameters are used for pointer arithmetic against another pointer, as fopen modes, or as range begins, where "" is invalid.

**Do instead.** Substitute only text that is read as text (labels, formats - and a format takes imgui.h's own default such
as "%.3f"). Anything used for pointer arithmetic, any mode or filename string, and a range begin gets an early return
instead; a range end is rebuilt from a proven begin (`end = begin + strlen(begin)`). Topics: amf, imgui, cimgui,
null-checks.

## The null-check audit's memory floor stalls while the game runs (AMF null-check gate, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** tools\null_check_audit.py (libclang over AMF's whole build) waits for 6 GB of free RAM and stops itself
above 2 GB. During a combined run SkyrimSE holds 10-16 GB, so free RAM sat near 2 GB and the audit - and so the gate row
amf-every-pointer-read-is-null-checked - waited for the game to close; a step's count could only be "expected", not measured.

**Root cause:** The audit's fixed free-RAM thresholds cannot be met while SkyrimSE holds 10-16 GB during a combined run, so the audit and its gate row waited for the game to close.

**Do instead.** Run the null-check audit (and AMF's package gate) when no combined run is live, or plan for the wait; say
in the report which counts were measured and which are expected. Topics: amf, null-checks, gates, memory, testing.

## "No snow in Riverwood": two saves named Save3, and Seasons keeps a season per save (Njordlinger, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** The owner saw summer Riverwood in a test game. First diagnosis (a coc sent from the main menu) was
wrong: a clean load + coc was still green. Real cause: Njordlinger Test has TWO saves named Save3 - the Prisoner save
(outdoors, Tamriel) that load.py loads by default, and a Darian save made indoors in Breezehome. Seasons of Skyrim stores
a season per save in overwrite\Seasons\Serialization.ini, writes an entry only when the player saves OUTDOORS, defaults a
missing entry to summer, and only re-evaluates on an interior door, an unset season or a save - coc uses no door. So the
Darian Save3 + coc Riverwood stays summer (snow still falls from the weather, distant peaks stay white).

**Root cause:** Saves were loaded by the bare name "Save3", which two saves share; and Seasons keeps a season per save, written only on an outdoor save, defaulting to summer and not re-evaluated by coc - so the indoor Darian save plus coc stayed summer. The first diagnosis was not checked against a clean load.

**Do instead.** Load test saves by their full file name, never a bare "Save3"; judge snow only after loading an outdoor
save with a Seasons entry, or after leaving an interior through its door. When "season looks wrong", read
Serialization.ini for the save's entry before suspecting mods. Topics: njordlinger, seasons, testing, saves.

## libclang positions are byte offsets - cutting decoded text at them hid every later `else` (AMF null-check audit, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** tools\null_check_audit.py decoded each source file and then cut the text at libclang's extents. Those are
BYTE offsets, so after the first multibyte UTF-8 character in a file (one em dash in a comment) every cut landed a little
early and the `else` branch of an if/else guard was no longer seen - reads were reported unchecked that were checked, and the
same drift could as easily hide one. The same run found that the offered helper `amf::Call` had never been through the audit:
its type `amf::detail::Caller<std::function<...>>` contains "std::function<", and the audit's whole-name search counted every
call through it as an unchecked callback.

**Root cause:** A tool that reads another tool's positions assumed characters where the producer gave bytes; and a helper was
handed to the work as "the checked way" without being run through the checker first.

**Do instead.** Cut raw bytes at libclang offsets, then decode. Run any new guard helper through the audit on a small test repo
before recommending it (tools\null_check_audit_test.py, 5 cases). Match a type by what it IS, not by a substring of its name.
Topics: amf, null-checks, gates, tools.

## A null guard on a job that holds a busy flag or a queue slot must end the job, not just return (AMF 2.3.0 null checks, 2026-10-25)
