**What happened.** Guarding the internal reads of AMF's job chains (Remembered settings, Presets, the McmScripts operation
queue) with a plain AMF_REQUIRE_VOID would have returned with the page's busy flag still set, or a queue slot still waiting,
so a "safe" null would have locked the feature until its watchdog fired (15 s for the queue). Empty "done" callbacks in
McmLoader threw bad_function_call before the guards went in.

**Root cause:** "Return early" was treated as always safe; a function that owns a piece of shared state (a flag, a slot, a
callback someone waits on) has a duty on every exit, the null exit included.

**Do instead.** On a guarded exit from a job, end the job (clear busy, call done, release the slot) and log once; replace an
empty completion callback with a logged no-op. Also: a `// nonnull:` added at the END of a line with code after a `{`
comments out the rest of that line - it silently removed four table entries in KeyboardLayouts.h with no parse error; put the
note on the line above. Topics: amf, null-checks, cpp.

## Helgen "paper-white / grey snow" was a landscape layer, not the meshes we retoned twice (Njordlinger, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** On 10-24 the bright Helgen snow patches were diagnosed as flat FX snow-drift meshes on snow01alta, and
"All Snow Ground Match" Layer A was rebuilt twice (tone 0.65, then 0.52) with retests 612b and c5e1 measuring the patches.
The owner then saw them grey under Community Shaders. Real cause: Northern Roads' Helgen mud LAND layer
(COTN_LHelgenMud) is swapped by its Seasons _WIN.ini to LDirtSnowPath01, whose Community Shaders PBR material JSON lacks
the subsurface scattering and clear coat of the ground-snow set (LandscapeSnow01Landscape); no snow01alta reference
exists within 2,500 units of the keep. The original diagnosis was never killed by its own cheapest test (untick Layer A
or click the patch with tfc), so two tone rebuilds were calibrated on a surface Layer A does not draw.

**Root cause:** The first diagnosis was never put to its own cheapest killing test (untick Layer A, or console-click the patch), so what was actually drawn there - a landscape layer swapped by a Seasons INI - was not identified before two rebuilds.

**Do instead.** Before retexturing anything that "looks wrong", identify what is actually drawn at that spot: console-click
it (tfc) - a mesh selects, landscape doesn't - and check Seasons swap INIs for the winning LTEX. Run the hypothesis's
killing test (untick the suspected mod) before building on it. Fix landscape-material mismatches game-wide with a
Synthesis patcher (WinterSnowGroundMatch). Topics: njordlinger, snow, seasons, community-shaders, troubleshooting.

## A crash log's source line names the call, not the fault - and null checks never cover the engine's own reads (AMF 2.2.3 Discover crash, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** A Nolvus user's CrashLoggerSSE log put AMF 2.2.3 on the stack at [source reference removed], labelled
`SKSE::ModCallbackEvent::~ModCallbackEvent`, with the fault a `lock inc [operand removed]` on RAX = [value removed]. Read at face value it blamed an
AMF destructor. The PDB and the instruction before the return address showed `[instruction removed]` - the game's own
IVirtualMachine::FindBoundObject, asked by AMF's timed MCM discovery for "SKI_ConfigBase" on every quest; the engine walked
QuickLoot IE's MCM quest scripts and hit a type pointer reading [value removed]. The open 2.3.0 - just made fully null-checked - had the
identical call: its guards cover AMF's reads, and [value removed] is not null.

**Root cause:** A symbolised frame names the nearest symbol and the line of the CALL; the fault is in the callee. And
"every pointer we read is checked" was mistaken for "AMF cannot crash", while AMF kept handing the engine walks it does
not check, on a timer, for every quest.

**Do instead.** Map the return address with the PDB (llvm-symbolizer) and read the instruction before it before naming a
culprit. Treat an engine call made in a loop or on a timer as AMF's exposure: read the structure yourself under the engine's
lock and judge each word first (slotguard::JudgeScript, AMF 98202a3), with a one-time cross-check against the engine call.
Also: a run driver must copy the SKSE logs aside before relaunching after a crash - the S8 crash's DEM / AMF logs were
overwritten by the relaunch and half a killing condition could not be checked. Topics: amf, crash, papyrus, mcm,
troubleshooting, testing.

## A slider held active steps at ImGui's nav-tweak rate (~54/s), not the key-repeat rate (AMF 2.3.0 one-way sliders, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** AMF's one-way slider design kept a highlighted slider active while Left/Right was held so every copy of
ImGui would step it. ImGui's keyboard tweak repeats at about 0.198 s then every 0.015 s - 49 steps in a 1 s hold at 60 fps,
55 at 144 - so DEM's Offset X re-applied its minimap that often and Skyrim crashed in Scaleform (SkyrimSE[offset removed], the same
address as DEM's earlier every-frame re-apply crash). Scaling io.KeyRepeatDelay/Rate instead made DEM's own nudge add steps.

**Root cause:** "Make it active and let ImGui step it" handed the rate to ImGui's tweak repeat, which is not the key repeat,
and two readers of the same key (ImGui's tweak and the mod's own nudge) each paced it differently.

**Do instead.** Pace a held key once, at the source, for every reader (navside::HoldTweakAtKeyRepeat: DownDuration reads 0 on
the press and each 0.275 s / 0.050 s tick, 0.1 otherwise - 16 steps a second at any frame rate). Test a hold at two frame
rates and count steps, not only a tap. Topics: amf, imgui, sliders, nav, dem.

## An ESL-flagged Nexus file can be invalid on SE 1.5.97 (Immersive Gathering, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** Immersive Gathering 1.9a ships an ESL-flagged copy (Nexus file 678566) beside the plain .esp (678565).
The ESL copy keeps its FLST aaaIWCMList (the settings menu's form list) at FormID [value removed], below the [value removed] floor that light
plugins on 1.5.97 can reach, so `esp-audit --runtime 1.5.97` fails it as unreachable - the menu would silently break.

**Root cause:** The mod's ESL-flagged copy keeps a FormID ([value removed]) below the [value removed] floor light plugins can reach on 1.5.97, so an ESL-flagged Nexus file is not automatically valid for that runtime.

**Do instead.** Run esp-audit for the target runtime on every third-party plugin before choosing the ESL variant; prefer
the plain .esp when the ESL copy has FormIDs under [value removed] (it costs one full slot). Topics: plugins, esl, install, njordlinger.

## Two helpers of one session shared the MO2 instance lock (2026-10-25)

**What happened.** The lock tool identifies holders by session, so a second sub-agent of Main Agent "acquiring"
instance:Njordlinger only refreshed the first one's lock (and overwrote its purpose text) instead of refusing - two writers
could have edited the same profile. Caught by the agents themselves; nothing was corrupted.

**Root cause:** The lock tool identifies holders by session, not by acquirer, so a second helper of the same session refreshed the first one's lock instead of being refused.

**Do instead.** Until the lock is per-acquirer (sidebar chip queued), Main serialises profile writers itself: only one
helper at a time may touch an instance, others are told to wait for an explicit go. Topics: locks, mo2, sessions.

## Scaleform calls queued through SKSE AddTask raced the HUD movie on another thread (Dragon's Eye Minimap 1.7.5, 2026-10-25)
**Root cause:** AddTask runs on the game's main task queue, not the UI thread, and the code assumed it was safe for Scaleform calls; nothing gated Scaleform calls by thread.

**What happened.** Holding an arrow on DEM's Offset X crashed the game twice (SkyrimSE[offset removed] in the HUD's own advance,
then [offset removed] in DEM's getBounds with RCX=1.0f). Each slider change queued a full minimap re-apply (SetMember _x/_xscale,
getBounds, InitMap/loadClip) through SKSE::AddTask. On 1.5.97 that queue runs as its own BSJobs job beside the UI job
that advances the HUD movie, so DEM's GFx calls ran concurrently with the movie's advance; more changes per second meant
a sooner collision. The same calls from DEM's own Advance() (on the HUD thread) never crashed. AMF's new one-way held
stepping first exposed it by stepping every frame; at a normal repeat rate it still crashed, proving the race is DEM's.

**Do instead.** Never make Scaleform/GFx calls from AddTask - use AddUITask or the menu's own advance; coalesce re-applies
(DEM 1.7.6: RequestDisplayApply flag served from Advance() at most every 120 ms, never re-entrant). Gate row queued
(scaleform-calls-only-on-the-ui-thread). After any crash, copy the SKSE logs aside before relaunching - the relaunch
overwrites them. Topics: cpp, scaleform, threading, crash, dem, testing.

## A UI task that re-queues itself runs every pass in the same frame (Hjerim Start 1.0.3, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** Moving Hjerim Start's repeated Alternate Perspective menu pass from AddTask to AddUITask: SKSE runs the UI
task queue in a loop until it is empty, including tasks added during that loop, so a pass that re-queued itself would have
run all 300 passes in one frame, before Alternate Perspective had read its files.
**Root cause:** SKSE drains the UI task queue in a loop that includes tasks added during the loop, so a self-re-queuing pass had no frame boundary.

**Do instead.** A retry/poll loop needs a pacer outside the UI queue: a short-lived thread (no Scaleform on it) that posts the
next AddUITask pass only after the previous one ran, e.g. every ~16 ms with a timeout; or serve it from the menu's own
per-frame advance. Topics: cpp, scaleform, threading, skse.

## Wrapping SetFormEditorID never captured LTEX/TXST/STAT editor IDs on SE 1.5.97 (Deep Snow 1.1.0, 2026-10-25)
**Root cause:** the design assumed the game calls SetFormEditorID for LTEX/TXST/STAT, but on 1.5.97 that vtable slot is the base no-op and is never called for those types; the offline check only tested matching logic, not that names arrived.

**What happened.** Deep Snow's road-by-name rule kept editor IDs by wrapping SetFormEditorID (vtable slot [value removed]) on the
LTEX / TXST / STAT vtables, installed at plugin load. In six runs it kept 0 names: on all three vtables slot [value removed] is the base
TESForm no-op and the game never calls it for these types, even with po3 Tweaks' Load EditorIDs on. The offline check had
only tested the matching logic, not that names ever arrived.

**Do instead.** For editor IDs of form types the game discards, read them from the active plugins yourself at kDataLoaded
(walk the LTEX/TXST/STAT groups, skip others by size, map in-file FormIDs to load-order IDs incl. FE light IDs) - a
background thread, a few ms per plugin. Always add a log line counting what was captured and test that count in game.
Topics: cpp, editorid, plugins, deep snow, hooks.

## A test save made with a behaviour mod ticked crashed every load once that mod was unticked (Njordlinger Test, 2026-10-25)
**Root cause:** a shared test save was made while test-only behaviour mods were active, and nothing checked the save's plugin list against the profile before reuse.

**What happened.** Seven launches crashed seconds after loading AMFTest-Outdoor-20261025 (SkyrimSE+1234430/+1234380,
Havok/behaviour graph, bad pointer [value removed], no mod DLL on the stack). Unticking tonight's list patches, Deep Snow, TMO 1.2.1,
UVC 1.2.0 and DEM 1.7.6 changed nothing. Cause: the save was made while "test Simple Timed Block 2.3.0" and "test Kill Feed
1.1.0" were ticked for FLICK checks; batch finish unticked them, so the save's missing-content box named their plugins and the
behaviour data left in the save crashed. Ticking them again made the same save stable. Separately, Papyrus
Game.QuitToMainMenu crashed in DynamicStringDistributor.dll.

**Do instead.** Read the missing-content box / the save's plugin list FIRST when a save crashes right after load. Never make a
shared test save while test-only mods (especially behaviour or animation mods) are ticked; make test saves on the base
profile (new game via Alternate Perspective, walk out the door). Never call Game.QuitToMainMenu from tests - relaunch.
Topics: testing, saves, njordlinger, crash.

## A merge that kept records but dropped the group tree broke a plugin, and the launch gate never looked at it (Civil War Guard Armor Replacer, 2026-10-25)

**What happened.** Vigilants of Stendarr showed up naked. Civil War Guard Armor Replacer.esp had been built by merge-to-espfe.py, which read each source's records but wrote one flat top-level group per record type. That left top-level REFR/INFO groups, interior CELLs without block/sub-block/children groups, placed references cut off from their cells and dialogue responses cut off from their topics. Mutagen's overlay read refused it ("Read in data that was not a GRUP") and its full read silently dropped 74 of 1312 records. esp-audit had flagged it since 2026-09-21, but plugin-gate only checked "test *" folders and the mod sat in an "unpublished *" folder, never packaged again.
**Root cause:** merge-to-espfe.py kept records but rebuilt groups flat (no parent links), and plugin-gate only scanned "test *" folders, so the failing esp-audit result on an "unpublished *" plugin was never enforced.

**Do instead.** A plugin writer must keep each child record's parent and write the real nesting (esp_groups.py; esp-regroup repairs in place). Launch gates check every folder of ours ("test *" and "unpublished *"). An esp-audit failure on an installed plugin of ours is a release blocker, not a note. Gate row esp-records-sit-in-their-groups now fails this class.
Topics: plugins, esp, mutagen, gates, merge.

## A patch that gated every perk entry still left the chopping block opening another mod's menu (ChoppingBlockToIG, 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** the patch only addressed perk Activate entries and never checked the target FURN's own default activation (workbench type/keywords), and a scripted Activate was mistaken for proof of the perk path.

**What happened.** ChoppingBlockToIG v1 made Woodcutting Tweaks' perk Activate entries false on chopping blocks so Immersive Gathering would own them. In game a real E still opened WT's "Firewood (2)" menu: WT had also turned the block FURN records themselves into crafting workbenches (CraftingWoodchoppingBlock keyword, bench type CreateObject), and that default activation survives any perk gate. The offline check had only listed perk entries naming the target, and the earlier run's "scripted Activate spawned IG's log" had been counted as proof IG's entry works, though entry 42 says scripted Activate skips perk entry points.

**Do instead.** When taking an activation away from a mod, check the target record's own default activation (workbench type, station keywords, scripts) as well as perk entries, and evaluate EVERY winning Activate entry's conditions against the target, not just entries that name it. Never count a scripted/console Activate as evidence for a perk-entry path; test with the real input. A patch that gains a PGPatcher output as master must be re-run after each PGPatcher run.
Topics: synthesis, mutagen, perks, activation, furniture, testing.

## SPID conversion: faction filters lost other mods' guards, and NPC filters spread through templates (Civil War Guard Armor Replacer 2.0.0, 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** the filter assumed every guard carries the vanilla guard faction and that SPID NPC lines match only that NPC, when other mods reuse vanilla outfits without the factions and SPID matches template children too.

**What happened.** Moving the guards' outfits from NPC record edits to SPID. A first draft filtered by per-hold guard factions: it only ever removed guards, because Beyond Skyrim's Cyrodiil patrols and Winterhold Restored's guards wear vanilla guard outfits without the vanilla factions. Separately, a SPID line naming an NPC also catches every NPC built from it as a template, so named lines and exclusions spread further than intended. A .bak-merged plugin also hid what its 30 statics were (the weapons' first-person models, not displays) until esp-audit caught it.

**Do instead.** Filter SPID outfit lines by the NPC's starting (vanilla) outfit rather than faction when replacing an outfit; put specific lines first (first match wins in a pass) instead of relying on exclusions; only name NPCs that no differently dressed NPC is built from. Simulate the whole load order before and after (verify-spid.py: references resolve, nobody gains/loses the armour, protected groups like Vigilants unchanged). Check every shipped *_DISTR.ini against the load order before packaging.
Topics: spid, plugins, outfits, distribution, npc.

## combined-run keep on a folder did not protect a folder snapshotted with backup --dir (batch d1f8/721d, 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** keep_rules matched kept paths only against exact file paths or names, so a kept folder did not cover files already in a --dir snapshot.

**What happened.** Installing Civil War Guard Armor Replacer 2.0.0 inside a batch, the executor marked the mod folder `combined-run keep --file <folder>`, but the folder had been snapshotted with `backup --dir`; the finish dry run showed it would put the old 1.x .esp back. Keeping each changed file worked. Same night: tgm stopped stamina draining, hiding a stamina-based power-attack check; Auto Draw sheathes a drawn weapon after 6 s out of combat; TestBench's inspect position is stale for walking NPCs (use Papyrus GetPositionX/Y/Z); WASAPI loopback on this PC records silence, so audio checks need the owner.

**Do instead.** Always dry-run combined-run finish and read what it would restore before the real finish; keep individual files (or fix keep to cover --dir snapshots). Turn tgm off for any check that reads stamina; land test swings within 6 s of drawing; read NPC positions through Papyrus; leave listening checks to the owner.
Topics: combined-run, testing, tools, audio.

## A "missed" road stretch was a vanilla road mesh brought back by a later plugin, and Seasons repaints every non-winter landscape texture (Njordlinger roads / no snow under roofs, 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** the road patch only handled landscape textures; a later plugin not mastering Northern Roads re-enabled a vanilla road-chunk REFR, and Seasons' generated swap file maps every non-winter landscape texture to snow.

**What happened.** The owner saw a Riverwood stretch still cobblestone after RoadsToCobblestone. It was not a landscape texture: Northern Roads disables the vanilla road-chunk REFR 1CD8D, and Ember_Sword.esp (not mastering Northern Roads, loading later) overrides it and brings the mesh back; Convenient Bridges' patch did the same for 5 more. Separately, snow under roofs comes from Seasons of Skyrim's generated MainFormSwap_WIN.ini, which maps every landscape texture whose EditorID lacks Snow/Ice/Winter/Frozen/Coast/River to snow by material, swapping the picture by texture set.

**Do instead.** Console-click a "missed" road first: a mesh selects, landscape does not. Patch road-chunk REFRs game-wide so the newest Northern-Roads-aware override decides whether the mesh exists. A landscape texture meant to stay bare under Seasons needs its own texture set (and PBR JSON copy) plus a never-swap line in a mod _WIN.ini. A rerun script that tidies a shared output folder must only touch files it wrote itself.
Topics: synthesis, mutagen, roads, seasons, landscape, snow.

## CommonLib API differences between build lines, and tooling blind spots, found building Njordlinger 1.0 (2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** code was written against one CommonLib line's API and the translation/package tools assumed the dist\ layout, so line-specific signatures and a data\-shipping repo slipped past the checks.

**What happened.** Building the overhaul's SKSE plugin for both lines: Actor::AddPerk does nothing on an NPC (follower effects had to be ability spells); ActorValueOwner::RestoreActorValue takes 3 arguments on the SE/AE line but 2 on 1.7 (1.7 uses DamageActorValue for the negative case); IsStaggered() exists only on 1.7. translation-coverage.py and the gate's translation rows read only dist\, so a repo shipping from data\ had its eleven language files unchecked; translations-check.py read "50% faster" as a printf specifier (fixed 39c026e). package-mod picked a .NET tool's DLL from a tools obj folder until -Target was passed; a first two-line package needed make-fomod.py by hand.

**Do instead.** Give NPCs effects as ability spells, not perks; read actorState2.staggered on both lines; wrap RestoreActorValue per line. Point translation checks at wherever the repo ships its language files; pass -Target to package-mod in repos that also hold tools.
Topics: cpp, commonlib, translations, packaging, njordlinger.

## install-test-build kept shipped framework data INIs as "player settings", so changed KID/SkyPatcher data never reached the game (Njordlinger CGO, 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** install-test-build treated every existing .ini as player settings, with no distinction for framework data INIs that belong to the package.

**What happened.** Installing Njordlinger Combat Gameplay Overhaul's phase 3 build, install-test-build kept the existing NjordlingerCGO_*_KID.ini and SkyPatcher LoreTierLevels.ini because every existing .ini was treated as the player's settings. They happened to match this time, but a changed tier/set/distribution file would silently never install. Same class as entry 7378 (themes), whose fix only covered AMF's paths.

**Do instead.** Framework data INIs (names ending _KID, _DISTR, _SWAP, _WIN/_SPR/_SUM/_AUT, _FLM, _DESC, _CID, or under SkyPatcher\) are package files: replace them on install (old copy to <instance>\_install-backups\) and read them back against the package (install-test-build, .MD b02b464). A new framework means adding its suffix to DATA_INI_SUFFIXES.
Topics: install, ini, testing, tools.

## SPID never gave our gear perks to the player on an existing save, though its log showed every NPC getting them (Njordlinger CGO phase 3, 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** the design relied on SPID distributing to the player on an existing save, which SPID 7.2.1 did not do, and the test read SPID's log instead of the player's HasPerk.

**What happened.** Unique-item effects were perks distributed by SPID 7.2.1 with no filter. In game no unique effect applied: the player's HasPerk was false for every gear perk while SPID's session log listed 75 distributions, all to NPCs. Set bonuses passed only because their abilities were added by our DLL. The test had relied on SPID's log as proof of distribution.

**Do instead.** Any perk our gameplay needs on the player gets a DLL fallback that adds it at load (Actor::AddPerk works on the player only - NPCs keep SPID). Test with HasPerk on the player, not SPID's log. When two features must scale the same game setting (no entry point exists), give the setting one shared writer so neither undoes the other.
Topics: spid, perks, cpp, testing, njordlinger.

## A sprint-cost effect did nothing because Paragon zeroes the game's sprint-drain setting and drains with its own spells (Njordlinger CGO, 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** the effect scaled a game setting without first reading its live value in the target list, where Paragon had set it to 0 and moved sprint drain into its own spells.

**What happened.** Savior's Hide and the Scout's Long Legs scaled fSprintStaminaDrainMult, which ParagonPerks.esp sets to 0 (fSprintStaminaWeightMult too); Paragon drains sprint stamina with its own spells (APO_VALOR_SprintStaminaDrainSpell [id removed], horse [id removed]). Both effects silently did nothing until the shared writer also scaled those spells; even then the measured cut was 16-22% instead of 25%, so part of the drain comes from elsewhere.

**Do instead.** Before building an effect on a game setting, read that setting's live value in the target list (and which plugin overrides it); if it is 0 or overridden, find the mechanism that really drives it. Measure the effect in game against a control, not only the log line.
Topics: gmst, perks, njordlinger, testing.

## Every compiled Papyrus script we shipped carried this machine's Windows account and computer name in its .pex header (found 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** the Papyrus compiler writes user and computer names into every .pex header and no build step or gate ever inspected .pex headers.

**What happened.** The Papyrus compiler writes the compiling user's account name and computer name (and the source path) into each .pex header. A sweep found them in every loose .pex packaged before Njordlinger CGO: Civil War Final Battle Equipment 1.0.0/1.0.2, Jarl Ulfric Armor Replacer 1.0.2, Ysgramor's Armor addon 1.0.1/1.0.2, Ophyre's Honeyside - Weatherproof 1.0.0 - finalized folders that get zipped and uploaded, so released archives very likely carry the owner's account name. No gate looked inside .pex files; the user-folder row only checked paths in text.

**Do instead.** Compile Papyrus through a step that blanks the header identity fields (NJCGO tools\build-papyrus.py scrub()). Gate row shipped-pex-carries-no-build-identity (pex-header-gate.py, gate-rules 1.0.26) now refuses any package whose .pex carries a user/machine name or a user-folder source path. Loose .pex only - a script inside a .bsa is not opened yet.
Topics: privacy, papyrus, packaging, gates, release.

## Offline Mutagen staging without the Strings BSA made every localized vanilla text read empty (Stormcrown Forward, 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** the offline stage held only plugin files, so localized strings could not resolve and every vanilla text compared as empty.

**What happened.** Building a field-level forwarder over Stormcrown.esp, the offline stage held only plugin files, so every localized vanilla name and description read as empty; the diff saw them as "changed" by every overriding plugin and would have forwarded bogus text changes.

**Do instead.** When an offline Mutagen run compares localized text, hardlink the game's Strings source (Skyrim - Interface.bsa and the DLC/strings files) into the stage, or compare text only where both sides resolved. Compare fields by what the game reads (text by words, regions/keywords as sets, script properties by name, XCLC by the land-hide bits).
Topics: synthesis, mutagen, strings, plugins.

## install-test-build left files the new package no longer ships, so an old loot INI kept stones in boss chests (Njordlinger CGO, 2026-10-26)
**Root cause:** install-test-build only copied package files over the folder and its read-back only checked the package's own files, so files the package dropped were never removed or flagged.

**What happened.** After stone loot was removed from the overhaul's package, the installed MO2 folder still held the old SkyPatcher SoulStones.ini (and an old Barter script), because install-test-build only copied the package over the folder and its read-back only checked the package's own files. The game would have kept dropping stones from boss chests.

**Do instead.** An install must leave the mod folder equal to the package: files the package doesn't ship are moved (never deleted) to <instance>\_install-backups\<mod>\<time>\, keeping settings INIs, meta.ini and matching FOMOD option files; the read-back fails on any extra file (install-test-build, .MD 23add95; --verify-only repeats the check). Note combined-run finish restores its own snapshot, which can bring stale files back after a batch.
Topics: install, testing, tools, packaging.

## Backticks inside a double-quoted `python -c "..."` string were run by the shell, so the written text lost its file names (plan edits, 2026-10-26)

**What happened.** Twice in one session a plan edit was sent as `py -3 -c "... 'The proposal is `DESIGN-RETHINK.md`: ...' ..."` through the Bash tool. Bash treated each backticked span as a command substitution, ran it (`DESIGN-RETHINK.md: command not found`), and handed Python the string with the span removed. The replacement text landed in PLAN.md and STONE-CRAFTING.md without the file names, and in one case the SEARCH string also lost its backticks, so `str.replace` matched nothing and failed silently. The only signs were two stray "command not found" lines above the script's own "updated" message.

**Do instead.** Never put a backtick inside a double-quoted shell string; write the edit as a script file (the Write tool keeps backticks literal) and run the file, or use single quotes with no backticks. After any text edit that was sent through the shell, grep the target for the inserted file names before reporting it done.

**Root cause:** the same gap the bash-backslash-guard closes for doubled backslashes - the Bash tool hands text through one shell parse before the interpreter sees it, and nothing refused a double-quoted `-c` string containing backticks; the edit scripts also used plain `str.replace` without asserting the match, so a swallowed search string failed silently.

**Rule.** The backslash guard should also block a `-c "..."` string that contains a backtick (a gate rule for Main Agent to add to `bash-backslash-guard.py`); edit scripts assert every search string before replacing.
Topics: bash, tools, docs, gates.

## A combined-run result with quoted notes was split by PowerShell 5.1, failed unseen, and finish recorded NOT RUN (batch B-20261027-000506-8eac, 2026-10-27)
**Root cause:** result took notes as a command-line argument that PowerShell 5.1 splits on embedded quotes, the failure printed no clear marker, and finish silently turned a missing result into NOT RUN.

**What happened.** An executor passed `--notes` text containing quotes from Windows PowerShell 5.1; PowerShell split it into several arguments, argparse failed, nobody checked the output, and `combined-run finish` then wrote NOT RUN over a request that had actually run. Same failure class as entry 12195 (2026-10-24).

**Do instead.** From PowerShell, pass notes with `--notes-file` (UTF-8, BOM stripped) and treat a `result` call as done only when it prints `RESULT WRITTEN <id>`. Closed in the tool (.MD 2842157): `result` prints one RESULT WRITTEN line or exits 2 naming --notes-file; `finish` refuses (exit 3) while any request lacks a result unless `--allow-not-run`.
Topics: combined-run, powershell, quoting, testing, tools.


## An esp/bsa-only MCM Helper did not reproduce a "script type without the function" crash (AMF 1.7.104 report, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** The AMF crash analysis said the player's crash (DispatchStaticCall reading a null function at [offset removed]) could be reproduced by loading MCMHelper.esp + bsa without MCMHelper.dll. The repro run saved the setting ("saved by MCM Helper") and did not crash.

**Root cause:** the plan assumed that a native function with no DLL behind it would make the engine's static-function lookup fail. Papyrus links a script whose native globals are unbound, so the lookup still finds `SetModSettingInt`. Only a missing or differently named function reaches the unchecked read.

**Do instead.** To reproduce a "type exists, function missing" crash, use a script that really lacks the function (a stub .pex with other globals only). An unbound native doesn't count. State the killing condition of a repro before running it, and record it as killed when it fails rather than adjusting the hypothesis to fit.
Topics: amf, crash, papyrus, testing, troubleshooting.

## Python text-mode edit of modlist.txt wrote mixed newlines (AMF repro, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** A helper's profile-switch script read modlist.txt in text mode (CRLF turned into LF) and then split it on "\r\n". The file it wrote had mixed newlines. The helper caught it and restored the file from the batch backup.

**Root cause:** text-mode reads normalise newlines, so searching the result for CRLF found nothing, and the edit treated the whole file as one line.

**Do instead.** Edit MO2 profile files (modlist.txt, plugins.txt) as bytes: detect the file's newline, split on it, and write it back with the same newline. Read the file back before launching.
Topics: mo2, python, tools, profiles.

## A game launched behind MO2 hung at frame 0 and nothing could close it cleanly (AMF repro, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** On Steam 1.7.104 Test, one launch left MO2 in the foreground. The game stopped after the data-loaded message, at TestBench frame 0, and went Not Responding. `sendkey` refused, `AppActivate` hung and `game-close-clean` refused. AMF's fast exit was denied by the permission check, so the owner had the PowerShell Agent force-close it. The cause is not yet separated from a stub .pex in the same run.

**Root cause:** the driver acted on the game without first checking that it was rendering (frame counter rising), and the launch path does not bring the game window to the front.

**Do instead.** After launch, wait for the TestBench frame counter to rise before sending any input. If it stays at 0 with MO2 in front, bring the game window forward once. If it is still at 0 after that, report the hang straight away rather than queueing actions. Gate candidate: the launch scripts refuse to drive while the frame count is 0. Settled 2026-10-27 05:25: with the game in front the stub crashed as expected (no hang); with MO2 in front frames crawled (123 to 170 in 40 s) and a plain SetForegroundWindow returned True without moving focus - only AttachThreadInput (run2\front.py in the AMF 2.3.1 plan folder) brought the game forward. The window behind MO2 was the cause.
Topics: launch, mo2, testing, testbench, gates.

## Test teleports dropped the player into the void (combined run eacb, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** During the NJCGO run the owner watched the player fall endlessly through black space. `coc SleepingGiantInn` (the wrong cell name) landed in Winterhold, and a face-the-NPC helper then set the player's position to Thorvar's coordinates from another cell. Separately, `player.moveto` on Thorvar's ref took the player into his floorless holding cell, NJCGO_RunesmithStorage.

**Root cause:** teleport targets were typed from memory, with no check that the cell existed and the player stood on ground afterwards. SetPosition was used across cells, and moveto was aimed at an NPC whose ref sits in a holding cell until the player arrives.

**Do instead.** Use exact editor IDs (RiverwoodSleepingGiantInn). After any teleport, check the player's cell and that they're grounded before going on. Only SetPosition within the current cell, and never moveto an NPC kept in a storage cell; go to the cell where they're placed instead.
Topics: testing, console, teleport, testbench.

## The owner-presence gate never saw the owner's Steam Controller (2026-10-27)
**What happened.** The owner played with a gamepad around 05:50 while a combined run was live, but owner-real-input.json recorded his last input as 05:39, so the 5-minute idle gate would have let an executor drive the game while he was hands-on.

**Root cause:** two faults. The owner's pad is the new Steam Controller (28DE:1304), whose state arrives only on vendor page FF00 - the watcher listened only to the gamepad page, and XInput shows nothing system-wide because Steam Input feeds the game in-process. Separately, the watcher's RID_DEVICE_INFO ctypes struct was 40 bytes where Windows requires 32, so GetRawInputDeviceInfoW failed silently and every VID/PID read 0000:0000 - the Sony path, the Steam-virtual-pad exclusion and `--pads` were all quiet no-ops, and the test only checked a 'registered' string. The device in the owner's hand had been assumed (a DS4), not checked.

**Do instead.** Check the actual device first (Get-PnpDevice for the vendor IDs plus a raw-input page/usage listing) whenever the owner says a gate missed him. Assert every ctypes struct passed with a cbSize equals the Windows size, and test what the call returns, not that a tool printed something. Fixed in owner-input-watch.pyw (.MD ecad001): FF00 Valve reports decoded by fixed layout, struct asserted at 32 bytes, `last_real_input_detail` names the path.
Topics: owner-presence, gates, input, gamepad, testing, tools.

## Posted versions of our mods sat unticked in the Test profile while older ones stayed active (found 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** The owner noticed Item Explorer 1.2.0 (finalized, recorded working) was not running in Njordlinger Test - 1.1.4 and the 1.1.3 base folder were both ticked. An audit found the same for many mods (AP Civil War Starts, CWFBE, JUAR, CNO, DEM, LMU, Hjerim, Souls to Perks and more), plus duplicate versions active at once.

**Root cause:** tests tick the new build for their run and then restore the profile - a helper copied back a whole modlist.txt taken before the 1.2.0 folder existed (MO2 then re-added the folder unticked at the top), and combined-run finish restores test edits by design; a `--dir` snapshot restore also undid builds installed into shared base folders (Souls to Perks, AMF). Nothing ever made a recorded-working or posted build the profile's active version.

**Do instead.** Restores put back only the lines a test changed, never a whole earlier modlist.txt. Test installs go into a versioned `test X V` folder, not the shared base folder. When a build is recorded working, finalized or posted, tick it in the old version's position (not where MO2 put it - the top changes conflict winners) and untick the old one; a gate fails when a working/posted version is installed but unticked while an older one is ticked.
Topics: mo2, profiles, combined-run, versioning, install-test-build, gates.

## A helper repackaged AMF 2.3.1 with a different fix while 2.3.1 was mid-test (2026-10-27)
**What happened.** While AMF 2.3.1's in-game checks were running, a helper fixing an inventory D-pad defect edited AMF source and rebuilt the 2.3.1 FOMOD under the same number. The executor noticed the DLL hashes change (Line-17 [id removed] -> [id removed], SE [id removed] -> 86622753); one SE regression ran on the wrong DLL. The original package was recovered from _work\superseded-packages and the fix moved to a branch.

**Root cause:** package-mod on an open (unposted) number rebinds that number's ledger hash and replaces the package, and nothing checked whether a test request was out for that number; the helper's brief did not say AMF 2.3.1 was under test.

**Do instead.** Never package a number that has an open test request - the change goes on a branch until the number is posted, then takes the next patch number. Briefs for helpers that may touch a shared mod name the numbers under test. Gate candidate: package-mod refuses when an open combined-run request names that mod and version.
Topics: versioning, packaging, amf, combined-run, gates.

## A see-through floor you can walk over was a reverted room marker, not a missing floor (Blue Palace, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** In Njordlinger Test the owner found a strip of missing floor in the Blue Palace that could still be walked over. The floor refs and meshes were all fine.

**Root cause:** Skyrim Project Optimization's .esm loads after JK's Blue Palace Terrace in the Test profile (near the top in the main profile) and restores the vanilla size of room marker [id removed]; JK moves the doorway, so the door frame's bounds centre fell in a strip belonging to no room, and the engine skipped drawing it while keeping its collision.

**Do instead.** For 'mesh gone, collision kept' inside an interior, check room and portal markers (winners, size, position) before refs and meshes. When two plugins redraw a doorway, compare the room-marker winners too. Gate candidate: flag any room/portal marker where SPO wins over a later-edited version.
Topics: occlusion, roombounds, load-order, xedit, mutagen, cells.

## Turning a town mod off: generated landscape patchers and PGPatcher output keep its traces (GCoS off, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** Unticking The Great City of Solitude in Njordlinger Test left PG_1.esp needing it as a master, and TerrainSeamStitch and NoSnowUnderRoofs still carried GCoS-era ground. A first Mutagen strip run also failed after the profile had already been unticked, leaving it unbootable for about a minute.

**Root cause:** generated patchers copy the ground and records of whatever was active when they were built, so they keep a removed mod's data; and the profile edit ran before the risky file step. Mutagen's WriteToBinary refuses an output named differently from the plugin, and sorts masters alphabetically unless MastersListOrderingByLoadOrder is passed.

**Do instead.** After unticking any landscape or town mod, re-run TerrainSeamStitch, NoSnowUnderRoofs and any patcher listing it as a master (strip only its records - StripMasterRecords tool), and do the risky file step before touching the profile. Also: Solitude's streets are one ground mesh, not landscape - check mesh vs landscape before blaming snow patches.
Topics: mutagen, landscape, patchers, profiles, snow, solitude.

## A beam-dimming patch that edited only the lighting mod's own records left bright beams (Lux Dim Beams, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** The owner stood in the Blue Palace with bright window beams although 'Lux - Dim Beams' was active. The two throne-room beams were vanilla SlowFogBrt02 refs that Lux re-enables; the old patch changed only the meshes of nine Lux-defined beam records and loaded before ~60 Lux patches.

**Root cause:** the patch's scope was the mod's records, but a lighting mod also places, moves and re-enables vanilla bright beams; and its load position let later patches win. Separately, two helpers on the same day called `agent-lock status instance:Njordlinger` (a usage error) and read the error as 'lock free' or waited out their cap.

**Do instead.** Patch at the placed-ref level too (every ref of a bright base that the mod placed or edited) and load last. In Mutagen, GetOrAddAsOverride on a placed ref copies the parent cell from the ref's owner, not the winning cell - copy the winning cell and worldspace fields back or the patch reverts later cell edits. The lock call is `agent-lock status --instance Njordlinger`; treat any non-zero exit from it as 'unknown', never 'free'.
Topics: mutagen, patchers, lighting, cells, agent-lock.

## First public release of a private fork hit four knowable stops (RaceMenu Atelier 1.0.1, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** Releasing RaceMenu Atelier: the brief said the repo was public (it was private, and the permission check refused the visibility change, so the owner did it); the ledger's 'passed' evidence was from an earlier DLL; and the finalize gate's only run refused on the page layout, a shallow clone and two PROGRESS acknowledgements.

**Root cause:** every one was checkable before acting - visibility, the evidence hash against the ledger hash, `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`, and whether nexus-description-X.Y.Z.txt exists - but nothing ran them before the single gate run.

**Do instead.** Before a first public release: read the repository's visibility live (an owner-authorised visibility change needs the owner or a permission rule in place first), compare the evidence's DLL hash to the ledger hash, and run pre-finalize-check as a diagnostic before the one finalize gate run.
Topics: release, finalize, nexus, github, versioning.

## Items 'sent to the Recycle Bin' were purged within minutes by Storage Sense (disk cleanup, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** The owner-approved cleanup sent 71 GB of rebuildable build trees, closed batch backups and old DLL copies to the D: Recycle Bin as the reversible route; by 18:19 the bin was already empty, before the owner emptied it himself. The bin's earlier 6.6 GB went too.

**Root cause:** Storage Sense is on for this user, set to run during low free disk space with Recycle Bin clean-up, so with D: low the bin was not a holding place (likely, not proven - no event names the purge). The cleanup's bin-cap guard re-measured the bin after each send, so a purge hid the overrun.

**Do instead.** Before treating a recycle as reversible, read HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\StorageSense\Parameters\StoragePolicy (keys 01, 08, 2048) and tell the owner if the bin may be purged. Bin-cap guards keep a running total from one starting reading. Everything purged here had been approved and re-checked, so nothing unapproved was lost.
Topics: disk, cleanup, recycle-bin, machine-health.

## Cyrillic showed as ????? in RaceMenu Atelier: the framework's font, plus lossy path conversion (2026-10-27)
**What happened.** A player reported Atelier 1.0.1 shows ????? for Cyrillic. The brief asked for merged glyph ranges in Atelier's font, but Atelier owns no font atlas - it draws in the host framework's ImGui font.

**Root cause:** two parts. SKSE Menu Framework ships every non-Latin glyph set OFF (EnableCyrillic=false and the rest), so a consumer's text has no glyphs; AMF adds glyphs on demand so it is unaffected. Separately, Atelier listed preset files with std::filesystem generic_string(), which on MSVC converts through the ANSI code page and turns unmappable letters into '?'.

**Do instead.** For '?' in a menu-framework consumer, check the framework's glyph settings first - a consumer cannot rebuild the host's atlas; detect missing glyphs (FindGlyphNoFallback) and tell the player where to switch them on. Show file names via wstring -> UTF-8; hand ANSI-API code (skee) the ANSI form checked with WC_NO_BEST_FIT_CHARS / usedDefault.
Topics: imgui, fonts, translation, racemenu, unicode.

## AAOS blanked slots in the game's sound hash table and broke its chains (Bluetooth-at-startup CTD, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** A player's crash on AAOS 1.0.6 was in vanilla code (SkyrimSE 66492, the sound table's insert) with our hook only a pass-through frame on the audio thread.

**Root cause:** when a device switch could not give every playing sound a voice, AAOS's RemoveSounds zeroed table slots. The table (BSTScatterTable) is chained; a zeroed slot cuts the chain, and the engine's insert walks chains without a null check.

**Do instead.** Never write raw zeroes into one of the game's chained hash tables - remove an entry the way the table does (move the next entry up or close the chain at the previous one, keep the free count right) and verify the chains after. When a crash frame is in vanilla code, match the crashing function's offsets against our own table constants first.
Topics: crash, audio, aaos, commonlib, reverse-engineering.

## Two generated landscape patchers fed each other and left 3-4 m seams (Katla's Farm, 2026-10-27)
**What happened.** After GCoS was turned off, TerrainSeamStitch was rebuilt reading the old NoSnowUnderRoofs.esp as an input and master; NoSnowUnderRoofs was rebuilt 13 s later and won those cells, opening 5 seams at Katla's Farm (123 across Tamriel). A leftover City Trees patch (CT_70_KatlasFarm_LuxOrbis) also stayed on after its layout ESL was turned off, because its masters do not name that ESL.

**Root cause:** the rebuild order was set by script order, not by which patcher copies the other's LAND; and the leftover patch was invisible to a master check.

**Do instead.** A patcher never takes as input a patcher that loads after it and copies its records - here TSS is built without NSUR, then NSUR on top (both rerun scripts now refuse the wrong order). Backups of a live ESP are real copies, never hard links (staging folders kept with --keep-stage share the bytes). After unticking a layout or town mod, look for active plugins whose winning refs sit at that mod's positions, not only plugins that list it as a master; then scan seams across the whole worldspace (tamriel_seams.py) before and after.
Topics: landscape, patchers, mutagen, load-order, profiles.

## A release-link label with words before its version passed the label gate, and the sync never relabelled it (RaceMenu Atelier 1.1.0, 2026-10-28)
**What happened.** Finalizing RaceMenu Atelier 1.1.0, the distro text sync moved the Source link's URL to releases/tag/v1.1.0 but left its label "release tag v1.0.1", and the finalize gate passed it. A scan of every distro page found the same stale label on four Oblivion Remastered pages (Apocrypha Menu Framework, Improved Wheel Menu, Simple Loadout System, Tween Menu). Separately, the media helper's file=URL list gave tails WITH the mod-id prefix ("197089-1793...png") while fill-tokens.py adds that prefix itself, so its first run reported every new picture as 404.

**Root cause:** gate row page-release-link-label-matches-tag and sync-nexus-distro.ps1's relabel (anchor 2b) both assumed the label STARTS with the version ("]v1.7.0 on GitHub"); our newer page template writes "]release tag vX.Y.Z", which neither pattern reached. The two tools that pass image tails around disagree about the prefix and nothing states it.

**Do instead.** Both patterns now skip any words before the label's first version number (gate row note and sync comment, 2026-10-28); the four Oblivion pages are relabelled by the sync at their next finalize. When feeding fill-tokens.py from media-editor-helpers.js output, strip the leading "<mod id>-" from each tail (rma-1.1.0\urls.txt is the shape). After any distro sync, read the Source line yourself rather than trusting the version rows.
Topics: release, finalize, nexus, gates, distro.

## package-mod.ps1 packaged AMF as a flat folder without the SMF name stub; AMF's packager is tools/build-fomod.py, whose default output is the wrong folder (AMF 2.3.1 search focus, 2026-10-28)
**What happened.** Repackaging AMF 2.3.1 with `resolve.py run package-mod -Mod ApocryphaMenuFramework` wrote `Skyrim - Apocrypha Menu Framework\Apocrypha Menu Framework 2.3.1` (no FOMOD suffix) seeded from the previous package but without `SMF-Name\SKSE\Plugins\!ApocryphaMenuFramework-SMFName.dll/.pdb`; the package gate's `fomod-delivers-every-file-of-previous` refused it. Running `tools/build-fomod.py` with no argument then built the right package in the ROOT of `7. current test builds`, not in the game subfolder where 2.3.1 FOMOD lived.

**Root cause:** AMF is packaged by its own repo script (build-fomod.py stages the stub from build/relwithdebinfo-se-only and refuses a missing one); package-mod.ps1 only updates the DLLs it knows. build-fomod.py's default output predates the per-game subfolders.

**Do instead.** For the Skyrim AMF: build both lines, then `py -3 tools/build-fomod.py "<ROOT>\7. current test builds\Skyrim - Apocrypha Menu Framework\Apocrypha Menu Framework X.Y.Z FOMOD"` (it moves the package it replaces to `_work\superseded-packages`), then `package-gate -Package <that folder> -RepoPath <repo>` and `version-gate -Action gate -Stage package`. Stray packages are moved to `_work\superseded-packages\<date>\`, never deleted. Fix candidates: build-fomod.py's default output path; package-mod.ps1 refusing a repo that has tools/build-fomod.py. Also: SkyUI's SearchWidget (inventorylists.swf) has no focus or highlight state of its own - a controller focus on it has to be drawn by AMF (measure the widget with getBounds(_root) against GetVisibleFrameRect, draw on ImGui's foreground list).
Topics: amf, packaging, fomod, skyui, keyboard, inventory.

## A helper's navigate reused the owner's open Nexus edit tab and lost it (2026-10-28)
**What happened.** Analysing ModSlut, a sub-agent called Claude in Chrome's navigate without a tabId; it reused an existing tab in the group that held the owner's open 'Editing SKYHUD Settings Menu ... /edit/requirements' page, so any unsaved edits there were lost. Two other helpers the same night also worked in a reused tab.

**Root cause:** navigate without a tabId picks the first tab in the session's group, which can be one the owner or another helper is using; briefs did not say to open a fresh tab.

**Do instead.** Every browser task starts with tabs_create_mcp and passes that tabId to every call; never navigate without a tabId. Also: Chrome's Save As dialog blocks hands-off downloads (read-only for computer use) - plan for the owner's click or ask him to switch off 'Ask where to save each file', and check the last-used folder afterwards.
Topics: chrome, browser, nexus, downloads, sub-agents.

## Unbind Vanilla Controls' Controls page broke on the plain SkyUI journal (Atttomsk, 2026-10-28)
**What happened.** A player on plain SkyUI (game 1.7.104) saw the key tiles drawn faintly behind the action names, the ITEMS column cut off and '???' tiles. Our sheet had only ever been checked against Norden UI's journal.

**Root cause:** ControlsList.cpp used fixed offsets (tile x 168, 225-wide columns) tuned to Norden UI, and looked up the tile member only as 'buttonArt' - SkyUI's rows call it 'ButtonArt' and place it at x 228, and SkyUI's System page sits at a different stage x, so four fixed columns overflowed the frame.

**Do instead.** Measure layout from the movie itself (name widths via the list's own text field, tile size and row pitch from the first native row, frame width from the page's position) and fit columns to it; look Scaleform members up under every name the journal variants use. Check any journal/menu sheet against plain SkyUI as well as our own UI before release. Gate candidate: flag GetMember("buttonArt") with no "ButtonArt" counterpart.
Topics: scaleform, skyui, ui, controls, layout.


## A "settled" check counted quiet frames, so it closed mid-animation at a high frame rate - and one test profile hid it (Dragon's Eye Minimap 1.8.1, 2026-11-01)
**What happened.** A player reported the minimap appearing past the screen edge after loading hidden. The first fix re-opened the position window on Show() and looked right on the minimal profile, which runs near 50 fps. On the full list, at about 125 fps, the map stopped at 138 wide instead of 189.

**Root cause:** the window treated three frames without movement as settled, but the fade-in grows the artwork in steps about 50 ms apart. Any wait counted in frames is a wait of unknown length; it was only ever true at the frame rates it had been seen at.

**Do instead.** Wait in time for anything driven by a timeline, with one long frame capped so a hitch cannot count as quiet time. Prove a position or timing fix at two different frame rates, since a passing run on one profile says nothing about the other.
Topics: scaleform, ui, testing, dem.

## A profile tick written before the mod folder exists is dropped by MO2 - the game then runs without the mod, and the failure looks like a tool error (Dragon's Eye Minimap 1.8.1 test, 2026-11-01)
**What happened.** I ticked a new test folder in modlist.txt, install-test-build refused because the folder did not exist, then refused again on the instance lock; the launch went ahead both times and dem.control answered 404. MO2 had rewritten the line as unticked, and a later batch finish removed it as a test edit.

**Root cause:** the script chained the install and the launch without stopping on failure, and the tick was written before there was anything for MO2 to keep it against.

**Do instead.** Create the folder and install inside the batch (`combined-run with --batch B -- install-test-build`) first, with MO2 closed tick it, then launch; stop the chain on a failed install, and read the `Loading` line before judging anything. After `finish`, re-read which version each profile has ticked.
Topics: mo2, testing, combined-run.


## Researched how to build a render feature without first searching for mods that already do it (Depth First Culling, 2026-11-01)
**What happened.** The depth-first culling plan went through research notes, a staged plan and a built counter plugin. When the owner asked whether a mod already does this, one web search found Faster Objects, Skyrim Performance Solution's "Hide occluded objects" and HiZCulling-SSE, each doing the same idea.

**Root cause:** the earlier research asked how the engine works and what is feasible, and its searches were aimed at technique. Rule 24 only covered searching this project, so nothing required asking "has someone already released this?" first.

**Do instead.** Search Nexus and GitHub by what the feature does, in player words and technical words, before any design. Show the owner what exists, and test it before building. `version-gate -Action register` now refuses a new mod without `-PriorArt <file>`.
Topics: research, gates, render, new-mod.


## PGPatcher waits at a "Generation Complete" window after an --autostart run, so a script waiting for it to exit waits for nothing (unified run, 2026-11-01)
**What happened.** PGPatcher finished in 124 seconds at 23:07, then sat at its window titled "PGPatcher Generation Complete". The run script waited out its full 60 minutes for the process to exit, found MO2 still open, and stopped with the profile half restored. I reported that it was still working, reasoning that more textures meant a longer run, and did not look.

**Root cause:** the script treated the process exiting as the sign of completion, and I assumed slow work without reading PGPatcher's log, its window title or its CPU use, all of which showed it had finished an hour earlier.

**Do instead.** The run scripts now close the window when its title says Generation Complete. For any tool that seems slow, read its log and CPU first, before telling the owner it is working.
Topics: mo2, testing, pgpatcher, automation.

## Installed a mod without checking the list already had it, then told the owner it was out (Texture Downscaler, 2026-11-01)
**What happened.** I installed Texture Downscaler 2.6.1 as a new test mod without searching the profile. The list already held its own copy, 2.4.0, at 2K. Unticking mine left that one running, so I told the owner it was out while it still loaded, and a whole setup comparison ran with Skyrim Performance Solution's streaming off. SPS's own log said so.

**Root cause:** I searched by the name of what I had just added, and took the tick I changed as proof of the state in game.

**Do instead.** Before installing, search the profile and the mods folder for the DLL's name, not only the folder name. After a change that should remove something, read the running game's logs for it before saying it is gone.
Topics: mo2, testing, profiles.

## Copied a winter sibling's total stats into SkyPatcher rules, and the race's starting values were added on top (Winter Animals, 2026-11-02)
**What happened.** The rules gave each regular animal its winter sibling's health and stamina from the record's PlayerSkills fields. In game the changed records ran high: cat 440 against 340, troll 710 against 460, bear 440 against 340. The placed-creature check in the combined run caught it; the record replay could not, because it only compares fields.

**Root cause:** I took a value that reads as the total on the sibling and assumed writing the same number gives the same total. On a rule-changed record the race's Starting value is added to it: the differences match Starting[Health] and Starting[Stamina] (100/100 for snow cats and bears, 250/125 for frost trolls).

**Do instead.** For a SkyPatcher changeStats line, write the wanted total minus the final race's Starting values, then read the live value in game with getav. A cub whose wanted total is below the race's start can't reach it this way; it stays at start plus 1.
Topics: njordlinger, testing, skypatcher.

## Reading test state from fields that only update on a press (combined run, 2026-11-02)
**What happened.** Simple Loadout System's loadouts.listIndex and the list's selectedIndex read stuck during a test and looked like the list was not moving. listIndex only updates when Up is pressed, and the selectedIndex read stayed stuck too; selectedEntry.text tracked the row correctly. Also in that run: tgm is a toggle, so a second creature pass turned god mode off and the placed creatures attacked.

**Root cause:** a field that reads like live state was trusted without checking when it updates, and a toggle command was sent without reading its state first.

**Do instead.** Judge list position from selectedEntry.text. Read god mode's state before placing hostile creatures. In the inventory, favouriting through bench.input needs pad Y, keyboard F does nothing there. sqv is the quick check for a script-filled alias on a running quest.
Topics: testing, devbench.

## A sheet that looked right on the game's own journal crashed on the first remap (UVC 1.2.0, 2026-11-02)
**What happened.** An earlier run was read as UVC working with vanilla Skyrim, though its setup on the game's own journal was never reached. The first real run on that journal passed every layout number (frame fit, tiles, Xbox art), then pressing a new key after "Press a button to map" crashed the game, 3 of 3.

**Root cause:** a pass whose reasons list a setup as "not run" got read as covering that setup, and layout readings were taken as proof of function.

**Do instead.** A setup not reached is reported beside the verdict, never folded in. A controls test always exercises the remap, not only frames and rowclips.
Topics: testing, ui.

## Test harness traps from the 2026-11-02 batch: hard requirements, meta.ini, hold 6
**What happened.** Unticking Infinity UI on the 1.7 instance for a clean journal stopped the launch at a box from Dragon's Eye Minimap, because Line-17 mods with a hard requirement pass the launch gates; Local Map Upgrade and Compass Navigation Overhaul have the same check. A new MO2 folder with no meta.ini lost its tick after launch. bench.input with hold 6 moved lists two rows, which looked like CONTROLS being skipped and may explain an earlier "opens Help" reading (unproven). TestBench's loading hold made a Model Sync failure that a real main-menu load did not have.

**Root cause:** test steps changed the setup without tracing what depended on it, and a harness step was trusted as if it were a player's input.

**Do instead.** Before unticking a mod in a test, scan ticked DLLs for its name. Give each new MO2 folder a meta.ini. Use hold 1 for list moves. When a held screen fails, repeat on a real load before calling it the mod's fault.
Topics: testing, mo2, devbench.

## A sheet intercepting input only knew one journal's name for Accept (UVC 1.2.0, 2026-11-02)
**What happened.** The sheet accepted `enter-gamepad_A`, which Norden UI, Quest Journal Overhaul and SkyUI send. The game's own journal sends `enter` or `gamepad_A`. So Enter fell through to the hidden list, whose selection sat on the GAMEPLAY title row, the page called the game's StartRemapMode with "GAMEPLAY", and the key press crashed. An earlier "key did not register" on the 1.5.97 own journal was the same bug, blamed on the test tool. Accepting all three names cured it on both game versions.

**Root cause:** the input names were taken from the journals it was tried on, not read from the movie it would also run on.

**Do instead.** When a mod intercepts a menu's input, read every target journal's nav names from its SWF, and keep any hidden list unable to act. When a test tool appears to drop a key, check the mod's input path before blaming the tool.
Topics: ui, testing.

## Test run traps: INI sections, a connected pad, Steam F12 during a key capture (2026-11-02)
**What happened.** A wrong section name silently added new INI keys. With a pad connected and the gamepad setting on, real Esc and Tab did nothing in gameplay on 1.7. Steam's F12 was read as the key by a row waiting for one, which unbound a control. install-test-build took the FOMOD's Recommended option, so the 1.7 instance ran the old control map for a whole batch.

**Root cause:** each step assumed its side effects were nil: the edit tool, the input device, the capture key and the installer's default choice.

**Do instead.** Check the section first (`uLogLevel` is in [Debug], `bGamepadEnable` in [MAIN]). Read iPlatform before trusting a keyboard test. Use a desktop grab inside menus. Pass --with-option when installing to 1.7.
Topics: testing, mo2.

## A log line and a flag read as proof that a corpse was placed (Ysgramor addon 1.0.2, 2026-11-02)
**What happened.** An earlier run passed "the body works" from BodyPlaced and the script's log line. A later run read getpos: the body was at the target while the cell was unloaded, then moved about 240 units away and 200 lower once the tomb's 3D loaded, 2 of 2. Also: a filling the script did in OnInit on a start-game-enabled quest read NONE after a load; removing it let the engine's own fill hold, and the alias stayed filled through two reloads.

**Root cause:** a placement was judged by what the script said it did, not by where the object ended up after the cell loaded.

**Do instead.** Read getpos on the ref after the cell has loaded, and again after leaving and re-entering. Don't touch aliases from OnInit on a start-game-enabled quest. getgodmode isn't a console command; read god mode from tgm's own reply, and it survives a load in the same session.
Topics: testing, papyrus.

## Rolling a mod back to its Nexus build brought its bundled DLL back, and the launch gate hid why it refused (2026-11-02)
**What happened.** Putting Njordlinger Test on the posted versions reinstalled Norden UI - Black 1.1.0, whose package carries a RaceMenuAtelier.dll that then beat the real RaceMenu Atelier mod. An earlier hide existed as .mohidden, so a no-clobber rename silently did nothing and the audit failed again. game-relaunch only printed "order audit failed" with the last two lines of the audit, which do not include the FAIL line.

**Root cause:** install-test-build puts package files back over a folder's earlier .mohidden hides, and game-relaunch cuts the audit's output with Select-Object -Last 2, so the reason never reaches the caller.

**Do instead.** After reinstalling any mod that bundles another mod's DLL, run nj-order-audit.py --profile "<profile>" and read its FAIL lines before launching. Compare the visible and hidden copies and only then replace the hidden one. Gate candidate: game-relaunch prints every FAIL line from the audit.
Topics: mo2, install-test-build, gates, testing, profiles.

## Tomb steps went into combined runs against the owner's standing instruction (2026-11-02)
**What happened.** Ysgramor's addon tomb steps were queued and run in test batches although the owner said on 2026-10-25 that tomb tests of that mod are his. A helper flagged it; the last request was withdrawn and the owner was told.

**Root cause:** the memory was only reachable by topic through INDEX.md, the area was never grepped before the request was written, and test-request submit has no check for it.

**Do instead.** Grep INDEX.md for the mod before writing its test request. Give the owner a checklist for those steps. Gate candidate: test-request submit refuses Ysgramor tomb steps.
Topics: testing, combined-run, process, ysgramor.

## build.ps1 -OutRoot given a Git Bash path made an empty D:\d (2026-11-02)
**What happened.** Ysgramor's build was given a /d/... path as -OutRoot from Git Bash, and PowerShell read it as a relative Windows path, which left an empty D:\d folder.

**Root cause:** a POSIX path was passed to a Windows PowerShell script without conversion.

**Do instead.** Pass Windows paths ("D:\...") to any PowerShell script's path arguments.
Topics: build, tooling.

## A patch disabled the "duplicate" College bridge and the whole bridge vanished (Winterhold patch, 2026-11-02)

**What happened.** The Winterhold conflicts patch disabled OCW's WinterholdExtBridge01 ([id removed]) because it had the same base and position as the vanilla bridge reference [id removed]. In game the owner found the College bridge gone. OCW had given [id removed] an enable parent, so OCW's copy may have been the one drawn; the parent's state was not read.

**Root cause:** Two references with the same base and position were judged a duplicate from their placement alone; the enable parents (XESP) and the owner's plugin that had made them that way were never read.

**Do instead.** Before disabling a reference that looks like a duplicate, read the XESP of both and why the plugin placed it; anything structural (bridges, doors, paths) gets an in-game look before the owner sees it. Also list what a patch disables by name when reporting it. Topics: plugin, skyrim, mo2, testing.

## A Morthal teleport crash was a placed object with no base, from a patch built for another Fortified Morthal (2026-11-02)

**What happened.** Two crashes at SkyrimSE[offset removed] on entering Morthal showed RCX as a TESObjectREFR with "Object Reference: None". The first was blamed loosely on the terrain patch, because TerrainSeamStitch.esp appeared in the log's registers. The ref came from Fortified Morthal - Spaghetti's Cities AIO Patch.esp, whose base forms Fortified Morthal.esp does not define.

**Root cause:** A patch's references were never checked against the installed master, and a form named in a register was read as a suspect without reading which object the crash was actually on.

**Do instead.** On a crash, read the register's object first: a reference with no base means a dangling NAME. Run housecarl_check findings=errors on the plugins that edit that cell, and turn off patches whose placed objects dangle. Topics: crash, plugin, skyrim, mo2.

## A land texture change was aimed at the record while Seasons decided the picture (green ground, 2026-11-02)

**What happened.** Green ground in Solitude read as LRocks01 in the land data, and a game-wide TextureSet change was queued. Seasons' generated overwrite\Seasons\MainFormSwap_WIN.ini swaps LRocks01 to LSnowRocks01wGrass in winter, so the record change would have done nothing. Its generator also skips names with River or Coast.

**Root cause:** The land data was read as what the game draws, without checking the runtime swap layer that sits on top of it.

**Do instead.** For any ground or object look in this list, read MainFormSwap_WIN.ini first and override it with a user _WIN.ini, which loads after it and wins. Topics: seasons, landscape, snow, skyrim.

## An observe-only tool hook reused by player widgets let a keybind press also walk the menu's tabs (AMF 2.4.0, 2026-11-04)

**What happened.** On a converted MCM page, right bumper on a key row switched AMF's tab and bound nothing. The rows armed input::ArmKeyCapture, which was written for DevBench's amf.keybind and documented as recording a press without consuming it. So the press carried on to ImGui and the framework's commands, and the row then dropped every gamepad code. The fix's in-game result is still open.

**Root cause:** A testing hook whose contract was "consumes nothing" became the capture of three player-facing widgets (McmLoader, McmScripts, PrismaRedux), and only the Controls page's separate capture ever consumed. Nothing about the name told the widgets apart.

**Do instead.** When a widget reuses an input hook, read what the hook promises about consuming before relying on it, and walk one press from the hook to every reader. A capture that takes a press also needs an exit for when its widget stops being drawn, or it eats a press nobody can see waiting. Topics: amf, ui, cpp, controller.

## A MODT copied across form 40 crashed at load: flat hashes below it, a header from it on (Campfire Camp Addon, 2026-11-04)

Topics: esp, crash, process

**What happened.** The game crashed during load with the add-on's new STAT on the stack. Its build script reused OBND, MODL, MODT, MODS and DNAM from a vanilla STAT, the normal way to make a new object on a vanilla mesh. The source record was form 39 and ours form 44. The 1.5.97 MODT parser ([id removed]) reads flat 12-byte triples below form 40 and a header count from form 40 on, so the first hash was read as the count and the read ran far out of bounds. The bytes were real hashes for that mesh, the size was a tidy multiple of 12, and esp-audit passed.

**Root cause:** Only the record header says which MODT layout applies, and nothing treated the copied field as depending on its source record's form version.

**Do instead.** When copying subrecords between records, check whether the layout depends on the form version, or leave out what is optional. esp-audit's model_hash_fail, gate row esp-model-hashes-fit-their-form-version, now fails it, and esp-form44.py refuses a record below form 40 carrying these subrecords. A check like this is run across the vanilla masters and third-party plugins before it is trusted: that run caught a wrong first version (DynDOLOD.esm writes a header count of 1).

## Finalize still refuses a patch number of 10 or more after semantic versioning retired the roll-over (release batch, 2026-11-05)

**What happened.** Souls to Perks 1.0.7 was refused because its page's document counter had reached 1.0.12, and Character Progression Control 1.1.10 because of its own version number. Rule 6 retired the roll-over on 2026-10-21 and the pre-push hook's check went that day, but Test-RolloverViolations in pre-finalize-check.ps1 stayed.

**Root cause:** the rule change was applied to the hook and the version gate only; nobody searched the other gates for the same arithmetic, and no mod had reached a patch of 10 until now.

**Do instead.** When a rule retires, grep every gate for what enforced it. Until the function is removed, a release needs a dated "Gate acknowledgement" naming the exact check. Also: "recorded working" did not mean ready here either - Carryweight 1.0.8 and Character Progression Control 1.1.10 fail rows that need a rebuild, so run the stand-alone package gate before telling the owner a batch can go. Topics: release, gates, versioning.

## A "dry run" of a permanent action really did it: `Clear-RecycleBin -Force -WhatIf` emptied D's Recycle Bin (phone recycle bin page, 2026-11-05)

**Symptom.** Testing a page's Empty button in dry-run mode, the bin went from one item to none. D's bin folder changed at 08:24:09, the same second the dry run logged "nothing removed".
**Cause.** The test called the real cmdlet with `-WhatIf` and trusted that flag to stop it. The page's own result line said nothing was removed, because the text came from the flag, not from what happened. The first dry run passed only because the bin was empty then.
**Fix.** Dry-run mode no longer calls the cmdlet at all. The owner was told what was lost: one superseded Script Manager package, about 54 MB.
**Root cause:** a safety flag was treated as proof, on an action that can't be undone and that Claude isn't allowed to do, and the test's report was written from intent rather than measured from the bin afterwards.
**Rule.** A test of an irreversible action never calls the action: stub it out. Report "nothing happened" only from a before-and-after measurement. Don't run `Clear-RecycleBin` in any form.

## Told the owner a tool "is already on your PC and phone" without checking, then gave advice that could have removed his saves (OneDrive, 2026-11-05)

**Symptom.** The phone trigger was built on OneDrive, but the PC had no account signed in and OneDrive wasn't installed. Once signed in it set out to sync 47 GB, and my instruction was to untick folders, one of which holds the game's saves and INIs.
**Cause.** The folder `<HOME>\OneDrive` exists, and Documents is redirected to it, so it looked like a live OneDrive. The local test passed because it never involved the cloud. Sign-in then pulled down 56 cloud-only stubs, 47 of them in the Saves folder, and those became unreadable when OneDrive was uninstalled.
**Fix.** OneDrive was uninstalled on the owner's order; the 47 stubs in Saves were moved to `OneDrive\_removed-20261105-onedrive-stubs`, and the real files stay in his cloud. The trigger moved to a page on his Tailscale address.
**Root cause:** a design rested on an unchecked claim about the machine, tested only on the side that didn't depend on the claim, and the sign-in's effect on the folder that holds the game's data wasn't looked at first.
**Rule.** Check a service is installed and signed in (process, account) before building on it, test end to end from the far device before saying it works, and before changing any sync setting find out what's in the folder and what the change does to local copies.

## A straight-edged flooded block on a rendered map was the renderer drawing each water shape as its bounding box (World Map Render, 2026-11-05)

**Symptom.** A hard-edged pale rectangle and a blue strip across land on Skyrim's rendered map, at Earthbone Springs.
**Cause.** Each LOD water shape was filled as its bounding box, flooding a whole 4-cell tile. It looked like bad land data or a mod's cell edit, so the first reading went to the plugins.
**Fix.** Draw the shape's real triangles, on every land.
**Root cause:** the render's output was reviewed fit to screen, and nothing searched it for shapes that can't occur in terrain.
**Rule.** Search a rendered map mechanically for straight-edged blocks (`tools\right_angles.py`, built into `build_maps` and `retouch`) and look at it at full zoom before anyone else does.

## Staged fixes sat uninstalled while the owner judged old pictures (World Map Render, 2026-11-05)

**Symptom.** The owner kept reporting faults on six lands that already had fixes in staging; those lands were still 02:00-hour pictures in the game.
**Cause.** Each launch copied only the land being worked on, and "staged" read as "done" in the reports.
**Fix.** The launch gate `map-viewer-gate` compares every installed picture with what was shown, and the stage is installed whole.
**Root cause:** nothing compared the installed files with the staged ones before a launch, and each report said what was built, not what was in the game.
**Rule.** Before asking anyone to judge a build, compare what's installed with what you think is installed, and say which files are in the game.

## A compositor's denoise broke on the largest pictures only, and a colour-mask smoothing wrecked a picture (World Map Render, 2026-11-05)

**Symptom.** Half of Bruma's picture came back dark and offset from Blender; road smoothing by colour damaged Dayspring three times; an old scratch script reused by name re-damaged a staged picture.
**Cause.** The small test pictures passed and the big ones were assumed fine. Colour isn't a safe mask on a map where road, rock and shadow share tones. Scratch names like `ds2.py` were old scripts with new meanings.
**Fix.** Tiled Blender runs, smoothing at the render's source, and restoring from backup each time.
**Root cause:** results were checked on a sample smaller than the real job, and a scratch folder's names weren't checked before reuse.
**Rule.** Inspect an image process's output on the largest input at full zoom, keep a backup of what it changes, and never reuse a scratch script's name without reading what's there.

## An order to build a fix arrived after the fix had already shipped (AMF, 2026-11-05)

**Symptom.** Main Agent ordered a build of AMF commit b92ed39. That commit was already inside the posted 2.4.0, so the order would have issued 2.4.1 with no code change.
**Cause.** The order went by a helper's report saying "committed, not built". By then another session had built, tested and posted 2.4.0 from a tree that included the commit, and the report was out of date.
**Fix.** The helper checked `git tag --contains b92ed39` and the version-gate status, found it shipped, and stopped before bumping.
**Root cause:** a commit's release status was taken from a report instead of being read from the repo's tags and the version ledger right before acting.
**Rule.** Before ordering or starting a build for a commit, run `git tag --contains <commit>` and `version-gate.ps1 -Action status`. If a posted tag already contains it, there is nothing to build.
