## An install reported "equal" for a package that did not exist (install-test-build, 2026-11-06)

**Symptom.** Deep Snow 1.1.0 was "installed" for a combined run and the read-back said the mod folder equalled the package, yet the game ran the old 1.0.0.
**Cause.** The package path was wrong and the folder didn't exist. The script copied nothing, compared two empty sets and printed "read back: equal", so a check that looked like proof passed on nothing.
**Fix.** install-test-build.py now refuses a package folder that is missing or empty, before doing anything else.
**Root cause:** the read-back compared the destination with the source without first checking that the source held anything, so an empty comparison counted as a match.
**Rule.** A copy-and-verify step checks that its source exists and is non-empty before it copies. A verification that compares two empty sets is not evidence.

## A new Nexus page's header image silently didn't save (Nexus media step, 2026-11-06)

**Symptom.** On World Map Marker Filter's new page, the 1300x372 header looked uploaded but wasn't saved.
**Cause.** On the new page's Media step, the header opens an "Adding header" crop window. It needs Confirm, then Save; closing it without both drops the header with no error, so the page looked finished.
**Fix.** Confirm in the crop window, then Save, then reload the media editor to check the header is there.
**Root cause:** the posting steps treated the header like a gallery image and never read the media editor back after saving.
**Rule.** After any Nexus media step, reload the media editor (not the public page) and check that the header and every gallery image are there before moving on.

## A gate passed only after a file's timestamp was set back by hand (release gates, 2026-11-06)

**Symptom.** Walk or Run for Controller's finalize was refused by `dll-built-after-the-last-source-change` after only the vcpkg.json homepage changed. The helper reverted the content to the built state, then set the files' modified time back so the gate would pass.
**Cause.** The gate compares file modified times, not content. A reverted file still looks "newer than the DLL", so the only way through was to edit the timestamp, which is editing the gate's evidence.
**Fix.** The content really did match the build, so the release was sound, but the timestamp edit was a workaround, not a fix.
**Root cause:** the gate measures time as a stand-in for "the source changed since the build", and time can't tell a revert from a change.
**Rule.** A source-versus-build gate compares content (a hash of the source files, or the build's commit against HEAD for the files that feed the build), never modified times. Until it does, a revert is answered by a rebuild or a dated PROGRESS.md acknowledgement, never by setting timestamps.

## A config keyed by DynDOLOD.esm FormIDs went dead after a regeneration (Fires Hurt RE, 2026-11-06)

**Symptom.** 27 DynDOLOD.esm burn boxes in our Fires Hurt JSON did nothing in game.
**Cause.** DynDOLOD was regenerated on 2026-11-04, after the JSON was written on 11-03, and the regeneration renumbered its base records (POF_Campfire01Burning_DynDOLOD_BASERECORD went from [value removed] to [value removed]). Every old id now pointed at nothing, and nothing failed loudly.
**Fix.** Re-pointed each entry by EditorID with esm_lookup.py (`4. plans\fires-hurt-radius-20261106-0637\scripts\dynfix.py`).
**Root cause:** generated plugins don't keep FormIDs stable between runs, and the config stored FormIDs with no check after each regeneration.
**Rule.** Any config that names records in a generated plugin (DynDOLOD.esm, Synthesis or patcher outputs) is re-resolved by EditorID after every regeneration, and the LOD run's finishing steps include that check.

## A guessed-argument call into RaceMenu's CharGen object crashed the game (Mirrorwright run 15, 2026-11-06)

**Symptom.** A DevBench probe called `CharGen.SavePreset("MW Probe")` in the RaceSex menu; the game died at once with an access violation at [offset removed], instruction `mov dword ptr [0], [value removed]`. `CharGen.ExportHead("MW Probe")` just before it returned undefined and wrote nothing.
**Cause.** skee deliberately writes [value removed] to address 0 when a native call gets arguments it does not expect - it is a planned failure, not a memory bug. The probe guessed a one-name argument shape because the earlier getters (GetRaceSexCameraPos and the rest) had answered harmlessly, so blind calls looked safe.
**Fix.** Stop probing save/load/export calls blind; take their argument shapes from the documented interface or from observing how the menu itself calls them, and make the DevBench call op refuse those paths without a known signature.
**Root cause:** the probe tool treated every member of a native object alike; getters are read-only and safe to call with nothing, but writers (save, load, export) act on their arguments, and a guessed shape for a writer is a crash, not a harmless "undefined".
**Rule.** Before calling a native writer function (save, load, export, set) through a probe, know its argument shape from a source; a [value removed] write at address 0 in a crash log means a deliberate assert in that DLL - read it as "wrong arguments", not as corruption.

## A new package shipped the previous version inside its FOMOD installer (QuickLoot Container Merge 1.1.0, UVC 1.5.0, 2026-11-07)

**Symptom.** Two packages built the same night had the new version on their folder and DLL, but fomod/info.xml still said the previous release's number - the number a mod manager shows the player.
**Cause.** package-mod.ps1 seeds each package by copying the previous one, installer included, and replaces only the binaries; the repo's own fomod/info.xml (stamped by version-gate) was never copied in. Every other version location was gated, so the package looked right.
**Fix.** package-mod.ps1 now copies the repo's fomod/info.xml over the seeded one, or sets the seeded <Version> to the new number when the repo has none; gate row fomod-info-version-is-the-package-version (gates/fomod-info-version-gate.py) refuses a package where they still differ.
**Root cause:** seeding from the previous package carries forward every file the packager does not explicitly replace, and nothing listed which of those carry a version.
**Rule.** When a build is assembled by copying the last release, every copied file that holds a version is either regenerated or gated - check the installer metadata as well as the binary and folder name.

## A "$key" message UVC sent to the Controls page showed its "$" although the key was in UVC's own translation file (UVC 1.5.0, batch B-20261107-000625-368b, 2026-11-07)

**Symptom.** The two new Gamepad++ messages on the Controls page read "$Gamepad++ uses that button. Change it in Gamepad++ first." on screen. The keys were in Interface\Translations\UnbindControls_english.txt; the game's own "$That button is reserved." through the same ErrorText.SetText resolved.
**Cause.** The message was handed to the movie as a "$" token on the assumption that the game's translator holds the mod's own file. The movie only resolved the game's tokens, so a UVC key stayed literal. (UVC's controller graphic never hit this: its TR() reads the file itself through uvcl::Strings.)
**Fix.** SheetMessage looks a "$" token up in UVC's own loaded file (uvcl::Strings::Get) first and sends the text; a token the file lacks goes on to the movie as before.
**Root cause:** a new player-visible string was routed through a translation path that had never been shown to resolve a key from this mod's own file; translation-coverage.py only proves the key is in the file, not that the path reading it finds it.
**Rule.** For a mod's own text, translate in the DLL from the file the DLL loads, and send the movie finished text; leave "$" tokens to the movie only for the game's own keys. When a new string is added, check it on screen once (a frame), not just its presence in the files. Topics: uvc, translation, scaleform, ui.

## DLL mods shipped without a Skyrim 1.7.x build - fourteen of them, five with a Line-17 preset nobody ever built (Line-17 ports, 2026-11-07)

**Symptom.** A Nexus player on Perfected Wheeler asked for 1.7.x and was told a build was "coming soon". The inventory that followed (`4. plans\line17-ports\INVENTORY.md`) found fourteen Skyrim DLL mods whose newest package shipped only the SE/AE DLL. Five (Loading Menu Overhaul Model Sync, TK Dodge AIO, Campfire Camp Addon, World Map Render, Homeowner Starts) carried a `build-relwithdebinfo-17` preset copied from the template, and two (Deep Snow, Local Map Item Markers) had the whole ports-17 / manifest-17 / build17.bat set - yet every one of their releases went out flat. On 1.7.104 such a DLL fails as "failed to open the address library file": its CommonLib (3.7 / b93280e) calls a 1.7 game "SE" and looks for version-1-7-104-0.bin, and our own guard repeated the wrong diagnosis ("the Address Library file is missing").
**Cause.** Nothing checked that a package reaches 1.7. The scaffold came from the template, so a repo LOOKED ported; package-mod quietly made a one-line package whenever `build\relwithdebinfo-17` did not exist; and the guard only knew one reason a file could be absent.
**Root cause:** a capability (a 1.7 build) was assumed from the presence of its scaffolding in the repo instead of being checked in the shipped package, and no gate asked the package.
**Fix.** Gate row `skse-dll-package-ships-line-17` (`gates\line17-gate.py`): a Skyrim SKSE DLL package passes only with a `Line-17\` folder, or when the repo's vendored CommonLib defines `RUNTIME_SSE_1_7_*` (one DLL for all runtimes - Localized Damage, Accuracy - Localized Everything, DTD Bloodpool Patch and Beyond Mastery are already built that way on alandtse CommonLibVR 7.0+ / NG 11-13), or with the mod in the row's exemptMods and its reason in the row. Round 1 built the Line-17 DLL for Wheeler 1.6.0, Deep Snow 1.2.0, Local Map Item Markers 1.1.0, World Map Selector 1.2.0, TK Dodge AIO 1.1.0 and Campfire Camp Addon 1.0.0. Every AddressLibraryGuard touched now checks the build line first and says "this build does not support Skyrim <version>. Your Address Library is fine."
**What the ports taught (CommonLibSSE-NG 3.7 / b93280e -> 7.2.0).** `SkyrimVM::impl` is `GetVMRuntimeData().impl` (and sits at [value removed] on 1.7.99+, not [value removed]); `Renderer::GetRendererData()` -> `GetRendererDataSingleton()`; no `RE::DebugNotification` (`SendHUDMessage::ShowHUDMessage`); `BuildSoundDataFromEditorID` -> `GetSoundHandleByName`; `RestoreActorValue(kDamage, av, -x)` -> `DamageActorValue(av, x)`; two-argument `ModActorValue` -> `ModBaseActorValue`; `ToggleControls` takes a third `storeState`; `CharEvent::keycode` -> `keyCode`; `GetSlotMask()` is an EnumSet; `GetCollisionFilterInfo` takes a `CFilter&`; `ItemCard` has no default constructor; `BookMenu::OpenBookMenu` is declared but never defined (define it from `[id removed]`); `LookupActorValueByName` takes `const char*`; `LoadingMenu`'s `unk78` is `loadScreen`; `SKSEPlugin_Version`'s `UsesAddressLibrary()` / `UsesNoStructs()` take no argument; `/await` hides `std::coroutine`, which 7.2 needs; `find_package(directxtk)` must precede `find_package(CommonLibSSE)`; a submodule build that set NOMINMAX for you no longer does. And `SKSE::Init(a_skse)` on 7.2 starts CommonLib's own logger, which wipes a log the plugin opened first - pass `false`.
**Rule.** Before calling a mod "ported" to a runtime, look in the package, not the repo. A mod whose engine addresses are SE ids (`[id removed]` with one SE number, as Loading Menu Overhaul Model Sync) is not a recompile - stop and say so. Topics: line-17, commonlib, address library, packaging, skyrim.

## A wider search for "who answers" let players into houses nobody was home in (Dynamic Simple Knock 1.0.0, found 2026-11-07)

**Symptom.** A player (Kaiharu111, Nexus) was let in after knocking on houses whose owners were out, then found the inside door locked when the owner's schedule locked up.
**Cause.** After the Cruel-Sea test in 1.0.0, the resident search was widened: with nobody inside, it fell back to anyone placed in the house, then the owner, then any member of the owning faction, wherever they were. That broke the owner's own rule (2026-11-05: only someone in the house right now answers), which the file's header still stated.
**Fix.** Only a living, enabled actor in the house right now answers (plus a resident the game holds in no cell); nobody home gives "No one's home. Come back later." with Knock, Pick and Peek kept and no conversation choices; doors out are unlocked while a let-in is active.
**Root cause:** a fix for one failing test case widened a rule without re-reading the owner's stated rule it had to keep, and no test covered the opposite case (owner out).
**Rule.** When a fix widens a search or a fallback, re-read the spec it serves and add the opposite test case (the one the widening must NOT match) to the same test run.

## A camera "that doesn't follow" was a camera that never turned (Hit Detection Meter yaw test, 2026-11-07)

**Symptom.** Test 8489 recorded FAIL: every camera-yaw source stayed constant across hits after "turning the camera with the right stick", and a helper spent a rebuild adding more yaw sources and a trace.
**Cause.** gamelink's `stick` action is routed to Wheeler's input (its result carries activeWheel/open) and bench.input mouse moves do not reach the camera in this setup either: frames changed 1-2% and no yaw source moved. The yaw was constant because the view was. It looked convincing because a frame was read as "turned" without measuring the change.
**Fix.** Turn with `player.setangle z <deg>` through the console gate: the view turned 90 deg and every source moved +90 together; the markers then followed (batch B-20261107-190706-022b).
**Root cause:** the test never checked that its input had produced the precondition (the view turning) before judging the mod against it.
**Rule.** Before judging a reaction to an input, prove the input happened - a frame change figure or a state read that moved. In Skyrim via gamelink, turn the view with setangle, not the stick or bench mouse; and gamelink's stick does not move the player either (moveInput stays 0,0).

## A late default change left the FOMOD description and CHANGELOG saying the old value (Hit Detection Meter, 2026-11-07)

**Symptom.** After fRingOffset changed from +40 to -40, the FOMOD info.xml still said the ring was "just outside" Detection Meter's, and the CHANGELOG's Added line still said 40 pixels out; its 1.0.0 heading still read "untested" after the ledger recorded it working.
**Cause.** The change was made in the INI and code only; nothing re-reads the prose that quotes a default, and the CHANGELOG heading status is not synced from the ledger.
**Fix.** Wording corrected in the repo (commit 1040e23); the distro helper caught it while writing the page.
**Root cause:** prose that restates a setting's value has no check tying it to the setting, so a late change to a default is not followed into the texts.
**Rule.** When a default changes, grep the repo (info.xml, README, CHANGELOG, page text) for the old value and the words around it. Test frames for a page: also save one unannotated full-resolution frame per finding.

## An annotation comment appended to a line turned the code after it into comment text (AMF 2.3.0-2.4.0, 2026-11-07)

**Symptom.** A player's crash: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading [value removed] in ImHashStr <- ImGui::PushID <- widgets::Toggle <- imguihost::DrawSettings ([source reference removed]), right after AMF built Open Animation Replacer's menu.
**Cause.** The 2.3.0 null-check pass appended "// nonnull: constexpr table of string literals only" to the line `kNames = {`, but the first three names sat on that same line, so they became comment text. The std::array<const char*, 5> silently zero-filled entries 2-4 with nullptr; the compiler raised nothing, and the comment even claimed the table was non-null.
**Fix.** Comment on its own line, names restored, a static_assert that the entries are non-null (AMF 2.4.1).
**Root cause:** a scripted edit that appends text to existing lines was applied without a check that it left the code after it intact, and an aggregate initialiser with too few entries is legal C++.
**Rule.** An automated pass that edits source lines must append only to a line's end and diff-check that no code token moved into a comment; constexpr tables of pointers get a static_assert. Gate row cpp-line-comment-swallows-code catches the annotation case.

## An AE DLL that lists its runtimes is refused on any runtime not in the list, even with every address from Address Library (World Map Selector for Controller 1.2.0, GOG 1.6.1179, 2026-11-08)

**Symptom.** A GOG 1.6.1179 player got "WorldMapSelectorForController.dll is incompatible" at launch with the AE 1.6.1170 build, while our other AE mods loaded for them.
**Cause.** [code removed] was written as a list. The list form clears the Address Library flag, so SKSE AE accepts only the listed runtimes. Every hook already used `REL::RelocationID`, so the list was the only fault. It looked like careful coverage, compiled, passed every source gate and loaded on our SE 1.5.97 instance, which never reads SKSEPlugin_Version.
**Fix.** [code removed] (1.2.1); both rebuilt DLLs read back as Address Library.
**Root cause:** nothing read the runtime declaration out of the shipped binary, and our only test runtime (SE 1.5.97) ignores it, so a wrong declaration was invisible to every check we had.
**Rule.** Declare Address Library independence (or `add_commonlibsse_plugin` with no runtime list); a runtime list only for a plugin with real per-runtime offsets. Gate row `skse-plugin-declares-address-library-not-a-runtime-list` now reads the declaration from every packaged DLL.

## A hook on an input handler's vtable slot is dead on Skyrim 1.7 because the header's index is the pre-1.7 one (Walk or Run for Controller 1.2.0, 2026-11-08)

**Symptom.** A 1.7 player could not sprint from walk; sprint worked only with the weapon drawn (when the mod reports "running" and the game's own sprint path runs).
**Cause.** Skyrim 1.7 added two empty virtual functions at slots 4 and 5 of the player input handlers, moving ProcessButton to slot 6. CommonLibSSE-NG 7.2 still names slot 4, so `write_vfunc(4, ...)` on the 1.7 build replaced a function the game never calls. Every in-game test ran on SE 1.5.97, where slot 4 is right, so the hook looked proven.
**Fix.** The 1.7 line hooks slot 6; SE/AE keep 4 (1.2.1).
**Root cause:** we tested only on SE 1.5.97 and trusted the library header's vtable index for a runtime it was not checked against; nothing compared the index with the 1.7 binary's table.
**Rule.** For any vtable hook on a runtime line we ship, read the slot from that runtime's binary (compare the function bytes with the SE handler) instead of the header, and test the 1.7 line on the 1.7 instance. Gate row `input-handler-vfunc-slot4-wrong-on-17` refuses the slot-4 pattern; SprintOrSneakForController and TK-Dodge-AIO still carry it.

## A PGPatcher run for the Test profile sat on a hidden "Critical Error" box, and its wrapper switched the shared output back on (Wildfire removal, 2026-11-08)

**Symptom.** nj-pgpatcher-run.ps1 -Profile "Njordlinger Test" ran 11 minutes with no CPU and no log lines after "Generating the output from scratch".
**Cause.** PGPatcher showed a modal "Critical Error: DynDoLOD and TexGen outputs must be disabled prior to running PGPatcher" inside its progress window (read with UI Automation; nothing in its log). The wrapper only switches "PGPatcher Output" off, and at the end writes "+PGPatcher Output" into the profile it ran for, even where that line was "-" before (Test uses its own "PGPatcher Output - Njordlinger Test"). Its mo2-launch also left the instance lock held after MO2 exited, so the next tool was refused until agent-lock force.
**Fix.** Before the run: DynDOLOD Output, TexGen Output, PGPatcher Output and the Test output mod all "-"; the shared output folder moved aside (PGPatcher writes into mods\PGPatcher Output whatever the profile); after: new output moved into the Test mod, shared folder put back, lines reset by hand. 156 s run.
**Root cause:** the wrapper was written for the owner's profile and assumes its own starting state; a Qt modal does not show in the window title the wrapper watches.
**Rule.** For a PGPatcher run, switch off every LOD output first and read PGPatcher's windows with UI Automation when its log stops; the wrapper should restore the profile's prior +/- state rather than force "+", and release its lock when MO2 exits.
Topics: pgpatcher, mo2, skyrim, process.

## A version bump rebuilt CommonLibSSE outside the build environment, and the linker's long-lived mspdbsrv kept the user TEMP in the PDBs (AMF 2.4.2, 2026-11-08)

**Symptom.** The AMF 2.4.2 package failed shipped-dll-carries-no-project-root (vcpkg build paths in the DLL) and then shipped-files-carry-no-user-folder (lnk{GUID}.tmp under C:\Users\... in both PDBs) even after a --clean-first rebuild with TEMP set.
**Cause.** build.bat / find-msvc.bat could not run from this session (cmd refused every .bat as "not recognized"), so the build was driven from PowerShell with Enter-VsDevShell, without build-env.bat: the bump's vcpkg.json change made vcpkg rebuild every port with the stock triplet (no /d1trimfile). After setting TEMP/TMP/VCPKG_OVERLAY_TRIPLETS and reconfiguring, the ports rebuilt clean, but mspdbsrv.exe started by the first build (with the user TEMP) kept writing the PDBs.
**Fix.** Reconfigure with the build-env variables, kill mspdbsrv.exe, delete the four AMF DLL/PDB outputs, rebuild; the gate then passed.
**Root cause:** the build environment lives only in a .bat; a build that bypasses it silently loses it, and the PDB server outlives the shell that set its TEMP.
**Rule.** When building without find-msvc.bat, set TEMP, TMP and VCPKG_OVERLAY_TRIPLETS from build-env.bat first and kill any running mspdbsrv.exe before linking; scan DLL and PDB for the project root and user folder before packaging.
Topics: build, cpp, packaging, amf.

## A static ship's deck held the player but he walked out through the bow, the stern and one side - the collision had open ends and the game meets a MOPP triangle from its front only (Longship 0.1.0, 2026-11-09)

**Symptom.** In the first in-game run the player stood on the Longship's deck (z exactly the deck top) and the mast blocked him, yet walking forward or aft took him off the ends into the water, and walking to starboard took him out through the hull; port held.
**Cause.** Two faults in the script-built collision soup (one bhkMoppBvTreeShape over a bhkCompressedMeshShape, built with PyNifly): the hull surface stopped at its last station on each side with nothing across the end, and the starboard half was the port half mirrored, so its triangles faced outboard. The character controller collided with the port triangles (facing the deck) and passed through the starboard ones from inside.
**Fix.** Transverse walls close both ends; the hull surfaces and end walls go in twice, once each winding; the deck slab's top faces up. A scripted probe (tools\deck_walk_test.py: place, walk with a real W press, read player.getpos through the gated console) then showed the player contained in all four directions, unable to jump the sides, and a swimmer stopped by the hull from outside.
**Root cause:** the collision was written as visible geometry is written - one surface, mirrored for the other side - without asking which side of a collision triangle the game collides with, and without closing the volume the player walks in.
**Rule.** For walkable collision built by script: close every volume the player can stand in, make walls he can meet from both sides two-sided (or wind each side toward him), and prove it in game with a position read-back walk in every direction before calling it done.
Topics: collision, nif, mesh, havok, blender, pynifly, testing.

## A boat-seat signal read from another mod's source did not hold in game - the player's collision flag stayed on (UVC 1.6.0 Boat context, 2026-11-09)

**Symptom.** UVC 1.6.0's first build detected Oars and Sails' seated ride by "movement and activate controls off AND the player has no collision", because RowRim's SitDown calls `player->SetCollision(false)`. Seated at the helm by a real E press, op=boat showed both controls off but `collision: true`; the Boat layout never came on (request 8448 FAIL).
**Cause.** `TESObjectREFR::HasCollision()` does not read back what `SetCollision(false)` does to an actor; reading the call in the source was taken as proof of the state it leaves.
**Fix.** The rebuild reads only what the engine shows: the full ControlMap signature RowRim's SetControls leaves (movement, fighting, jumping, sneaking, activate off; menu and looking on - a scene's DisablePlayerControls also takes the menus) plus the player's height over the cell's water. Passed in B-20261109-014532-f4c9.
**Root cause:** a state was inferred from another mod's setter call instead of being read back from the object in game (rule 30).
**Rule.** When detecting another mod's state, expose every candidate signal in a DevBench op first and check each one in game before the detection depends on it. Topics: uvc, input, controls, testing, skse, cpp.

## One added collision box in a script-built ship crashed the game on loading the cell, with no Crash Logger file (Longship 0.2.0, 2026-11-09)

**Symptom.** After adding a sea-chest collision box (col_box, 0.82 x 0.48 x 0.47 m) at the helm to the Longship's MOPP soup, SkyrimSE (1.5.97, Njordlinger) died a few seconds after MorthalExterior03 loaded - twice, once before the plugin had spawned anything. Windows event 1000: access violation at SkyrimSE[value removed]; Crash Logger wrote nothing. The same box one metre further aft had loaded fine an hour earlier.
**Fix.** The box was removed (the seated player has no collision anyway); the next two loads were clean.
**Root cause:** not proven - most likely a bad MOPP tree from PyNifly's generator for that geometry. The cheap discriminating step (same build, same load; then the build without the box) was what separated it from the plugin changes made at the same time.
**Rule.** Change collision and code in separate builds when a crash is possible, and after any change to a script-built collision mesh, load its cell (not only walk it) before testing anything else. When Crash Logger is silent, read the Windows Application log (event 1000) for the fault offset.
Topics: collision, nif, mopp, havok, crash, pynifly, testing.

## TexGen's and DynDOLOD's end-of-run choice dialogs ignore BM_CLICK; UI Automation Invoke works, and a PGPatcher-wrapper lock outlived MO2 again (PGLite install, 2026-11-09)

**Symptom.** After "TexGen completed successfully", pywinauto win32 `.click()` on "Exit TexGen" did nothing (process idle at 0 CPU, MO2 still open); the same for DynDOLOD's Advanced "OK". Before that, mo2-launch for TexGen was refused because nj-pgpatcher-run.ps1's instance lock was still live after MO2 had exited.
**Cause.** These buttons sit in task-dialog / Delphi windows that do not act on BM_CLICK sent without focus; the PGPatcher wrapper does not release its agent-lock when MO2 exits (already logged 2026-11-08, not yet fixed).
**Fix.** `Application(backend='uia').connect(process=pid).window(handle=<dialog hwnd>)` then `.invoke()` on the Button ("Exit TexGen", "Save and Exit", Advanced "OK") - no focus, no real click. The stale lock was taken over with `agent-lock.py force` (own run, MO2 closed), the token passed to later launches through AGENT_LOCK_TOKENS, and released at the end.
**Root cause:** the runbook's BM_CLICK advice is true for the option windows but not for the completion dialogs; the wrapper's lock release is still missing.
**Rule.** For TexGen/DynDOLOD dialogs use UIA Invoke first; for nj-pgpatcher-run.ps1 check `agent-lock status instance:Njordlinger` after it returns.
Topics: dyndolod, texgen, pgpatcher, mo2, automation.


## A full package install replaced newer hand-made data in the test folder with the package's older copies (World Map Render, 2026-11-09)

**Symptom.** Installing the World Map Render 1.0.0 package (the map-guard DLL) replaced 97 files. The hand-smoothed map pictures from 11-05 19:31 (bsheartland.dds 111 MB) and the stage meshes were overwritten with the package's 02:xx pictures (35 MB) and older meshes. Only one stale file was backed up.
**Cause.** The test folder had been filled by hand from C:\Builds\worldmap-render\stage\data, which is newer than the repo dist the package is built from (to-do: "copy tonight's hand-smoothed pictures into the repo dist"). install-test-build.py treats the package as the truth and backs up only files the package lacks, never files it replaces. The 11-06 handoff said "Install the DLL only, never the package's pictures", but that lived in a handoff, not in the tool.
**Fix.** The stage textures, meshes and tables were copied back: diff against stage is 0, and the table md5 7d5e2d7b matches the pre-install file. Only the new DLL was kept.
**Root cause:** the installer overwrites a file in the mod folder without checking whether the installed copy is newer than, or differs from, the package's and came from somewhere else; and a "DLL only" install instruction existed only in prose.
**Rule.** Before replacing a non-binary data file whose installed copy is newer than the package's, the installer backs it up into _install-backups (or refuses without --replace-newer). A mod that may only be installed DLL-only says so in a machine-read place, its registry entry, and not only in a handoff.


## An AP menu injection took Alternate Perspective's built-in None/Random cards for a loaded menu and drew a dead card twice (AP Home Start - Winter Cove 1.0.0, Nexus report, 2026-11-09)

**Symptom.** A player on AE 1.6.1170 with Alternate Perspective 4.1 saw a faded, unclickable "Winter Cove" card twice in AP's start grid (before None and after Random); the log said "no $AltPersp_Home card ... added as a card of its own (2 card(s), 1 pass(es))", though 4.1's JSON has that card.
**Cause.** Decompiled AlternatePerspectiveMenu.swf (4.1): the MessengerMenu constructor fills `_options` with None and Random, and the JSON files are read afterwards; only when the last is read does `OptionList.setItems` push every entry into `mainOptions.entryList`. Our readiness test was "`_options` is non-empty", true on pass 1. The fallback pushed its card into `entryList` (drawn first) AND `_options` (drawn again after Random by setItems). `validateConditions` sets `enabled = true` on every loaded entry; ours had none, and `MainListEntry` draws such an entry at 25% alpha and the list fires clickDisabled.
**Fix.** 2.0.0 waits for `mainOptions.entryList` to be non-empty, searches it, adds the fallback card to entryList only, once, with `enabled = true`.
**Root cause:** the readiness signal was assumed from "files load asynchronously" without reading the SWF's constructor, and the build shipped untested. Hjerim Start 1.0.3/1.0.4 and Routa Start carry the same ApMenu.cpp (1.0.2's AddTask timing hid it).
**Rule.** Before injecting into another mod's Scaleform menu, decompile it (ffdec-cli -export script) and key readiness on the menu's own "done" step, and copy every member its loader sets on an entry.
Topics: alternate-perspective, starts, menu, ui, scaleform, testing.

## Finishing a stale combined run restores the profile from the batch-start backup and wipes every change made since (combined-run, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** `combined-run finish` on batch B-20261109-175707-718c, open 11.7 h, reported "5 of 603 file(s) written back": modlist.txt, plugins.txt, loadorder.txt, archives.txt and plugingroups.txt went back to the evening of 2026-11-09. That undid a whole night of deliberate owner-approved changes made outside the batch: the list sweep (47 category moves, mods turned off, a new patch), the pruned test builds, the newer builds switched on, and the new sword test mod.
**Cause.** finish treats every difference from its start-of-batch backup as a "test change" to undo. A batch left open while ordinary list work goes on cannot tell test edits from permanent ones. It looked safe because finish is the documented way to close a batch, and the restore report is only read afterwards.
**Fix.** Copied the batch's own "-final" snapshot (the files as they were just before the restore, in batches\<batch>-final\) back over the profile, then checked the night's changes line by line. The wrong restore is kept as *.bak-wrongrestore-20261110.
**Root cause:** finish has no notion of how old its backup is, or of changes made outside the batch, so a stale batch becomes a time machine for the profile. Nothing warns before writing back.
**Rule.** Before finishing a batch that has been open more than a few hours, or one during which the profile was edited for non-test reasons, diff the profile against the batch backup first and mark the permanent changes kept (`combined-run keep`). Better: finish should refuse to write back when its backup is older than the latest non-batch profile edit, and should list what it would undo. Never leave a batch open across a session's ordinary list work.
Topics: combined-run, mo2, njordlinger, testing, profile.

## Copying PGPatcher's metal TruePBR block onto a new mesh without a fuzz map gives a wrong material (nif, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** Found before it shipped: the A4 Nordic sword's metal shapes, which came from PGPatcher's output for Faultier's PBR sword, carry a shader block of type 11 with a fuzz layer (slot 6 = Faultier's _f map). Version A5c of the same sword, with its own texture set, has no fuzz map.
**Cause.** PGPatcher writes different TruePBR blocks per texture set: the metal block with fuzz (type 11) where the source set ships an _f map, and a plain TruePBR block (type 0, SLSF2 bit 23) otherwise. Copying "the sword's shader" from the previous version looked like the safe choice, because it was the block that had worked in game.
**Fix.** The A5c steel and wrap take PGPatcher's PLAIN TruePBR block (type 0, flags 82400301 / [id removed], slots 0 albedo, 1 normal, 5 RMAOS), read from a PGPatcher output NIF for a set without fuzz. verify_nif.py reads back every shape's shader and texture set.
**Root cause:** a shader block was treated as belonging to the mesh rather than to the texture set it was generated for, and nothing compares a NIF's shader slots with the files its texture set really has.
**Rule.** When a new or re-textured mesh borrows a TruePBR shader block, take it from a NIF whose texture set has the same maps (fuzz or not, coat or not), and check every referenced slot resolves to a shipped file. A slot pointing at a map the set does not have is a defect. A gate row could check this on our packages.
Topics: nif, pbr, textures, meshes, packaging, visual-design.

## "Followed the owner's drawn outline" while the result did not match it (weapon modelling, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** The owner drew a new axe-head outline in red over a render (64.png). The rebuilt head (battleaxe v5) was reported as "rebuilt to his red line", but next to the drawing it was boxy with a faceted edge, where his line was one smooth rounded arc. The owner: "you didn't listen at all ... I literally drew the lines on top of it."
**Cause.** The red line was read by eye into a few control points and mixed with the old shape. The helper reported the result as matching, and Main Agent passed the sheet on without laying the drawing over the result. A second miss came from the same step: Main Agent first read the outline as "keep this part", and the scribbled-out haft top as the back piece.
**Fix.** Battleaxe v6: extract the red pixels, fit one smooth spline, map it through the render camera, and build from it. Then draw his line over a same-camera render and put the measured deviation on the sheet before it is sent.
**Root cause:** no step compared the owner's drawing with the result. "Matches the drawing" was a claim, not a measurement, and the reading of his marks was never confirmed back to him in his own terms.
**Rule.** When the owner draws on an image, trace the marks from the pixels, never by eye. Check the result with an overlay at the same camera, with a measured deviation, before showing it. When marks are ambiguous (an outline could mean "keep" or "change to this"), say the reading in one line before building.
Topics: blender, meshes, testing, visual-design.

## A plate built in rows silently loses material where its outline rises again (Blender weapon builds, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** Battleaxe v6's first pass dropped a sliver of the owner's traced outline: the top bar sags and then rises into the neck. The renders looked fine, and only the overlay check caught it, at 4.2% off. Earlier builds showed sheared carving where the bars met the neck, and shading steps across the head.
**Cause.** The head was built as horizontal rows, one span per row along y. A boundary that turns back on itself needs two spans in some rows, so the second span vanished without an error. UVs measured from each row's inner edge sheared wherever that edge jumped between rows, and a thickness set per row gave each row its own slope.
**Fix.** The bar became its own part, built in columns along x on the same wedge plane. The head took planar UVs and one wedge plane for its thickness.
**Root cause:** the row builder assumed every outline is single-valued in y, and nothing checked the built silhouette against the intended one.
**Rule.** For any plate built from an outline, check the rendered silhouette against the source outline (overlay, measured deviation). Split parts wherever the outline is not single-valued along the build axis. Use planar UVs and one thickness function for a continuous plate.
Topics: blender, meshes, textures, visual-design.

## A vague visual complaint was answered with a rule instead of a question - "wider on one side" became a symmetry fix that reshaped the wrong part (weapon modelling, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** The owner said the warhammer's head "is wider on one side than the other ... my line was followed too literally, ignoring the rules of symmetry". Main Agent read that as "both sides must meet the haft at equal heights", and the build moved the PICK's root up by 2.1 units. The owner then said: "do this shape not the current spike shape, i didnt say to change that at all, i said that the hammer head was disproportionate" - he meant the HAMMER side's height profile, which should widen gradually toward the striking face, as v1 did.
**Cause.** The complaint named a symptom (one side looked wider) and a principle (symmetry). Main Agent picked the most literal geometric reading of the principle, did not say back which part would change, and wrote it straight into the skill as a general rule.
**Fix.** v2c puts the pick back exactly as v2 had it and gives the hammer side v1's height profile. The skill now says to state in one line which parts will be made to match and which will be left alone before applying any symmetry, and notes that a hammer and a pick are different parts.
**Root cause:** feedback on a shape was turned into an action without confirming WHICH part the owner meant, and a one-off reading was promoted to a standing rule in the same breath.
**Rule.** When visual feedback could apply to more than one part, or more than one property (height, width, proportion, symmetry), say back the reading in one line ("I'll change X's Y to match Z; A stays as is") before building. Promote a reading to a skill rule only after the owner confirms it.
Topics: blender, meshes, visual-design.

## A flat steel end face mirrored the render's warm backdrop and read as a brown wooden block in the side view (weapon renders, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** On the warhammer v2b sheet the orthographic SIDE view (from the hammer end) showed a tall brown block on a thin haft. The owner: "the top view you sent looks right but the side view looks disproportionate".
**Cause.** Not the camera (all three standard views are orthographic at the same scale), and not the proportions (the striking face is 6.0 x 5.4, as in v1 and vanilla, and the top view's thickness agrees). The end face is flat, dark, metallic steel, and seen head-on it reflects the scene's warm courtyard HDRI straight back into the camera. That reads as brown wood or leather and makes the block look large and separate.
**Fix.** The standard views use a neutral grey backdrop and environment, the wall and end faces carry the brushed steel texture, and every standard view carries a dimension note (height, thickness, length in units) so front, side and top can be checked against each other.
**Root cause:** the renders were judged on silhouette and engraving only. Nobody checked that a flat metal face shows the material and not the environment it reflects, and the views had no numbers to cross-check proportions.
**Rule.** For orthographic review views of metal parts, use a neutral grey environment. Look at each flat face head-on for a colour that is not the material. Put dimensions on every standard view.
Topics: blender, textures, visual-design.

## Fixing one part by "taking the old version's lines" also brought back a line the owner had already redrawn (warhammer v2c, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** To give the warhammer's hammer side v1's proportions, Main Agent's order said "use v1's hammer top and underside lines". v2c then lost the owner's one continuous top arc from the pick tip to the hammer. He noticed two versions later: "they reverted the consistent curve along the top of the head".
**Cause.** His complaint was about the hammer side's HEIGHT PROFILE (how tall it is along its length). The order swapped in whole outline lines from v1, including the top line, which he had replaced with his own traced arc at 18:49. Nothing listed which of his earlier marks the change had to keep.
**Fix.** v2e restores his traced top arc as one smooth curve from the pick tip to the striking face and keeps v1's bottom line for the proportion.
**Root cause:** each correction was written against the latest complaint only. The owner's earlier, still-standing marks were not carried into the order as constraints.
**Rule.** Every design order lists the owner's still-standing marks (traced lines, approved parts) as MUST-KEEP constraints, and the sheet's overlay re-checks ALL of them, not only the line being changed. When borrowing from an older version, borrow the one property asked for (a height profile), never its whole outline.
Topics: blender, meshes, visual-design.

## One px-per-unit value for a mixed-density atlas halved the normal strength on the parts painted denser (Truly Nordic weapons, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** Found while building dagger v2: the guards and small parts on several earlier weapon sheets had shallower-looking carving than the blades, although they were painted at the same depth.
**Cause.** The map painter (tn_knot.maps_v3) turns the height field into a normal map using ONE pixels-per-unit value for the gradient. Earlier sheets passed 31 px/unit, the blade's density, for atlases whose guards were laid out at 60 px/unit. That halved the guards' normal strength. It looked like an artistic difference, not a bug.
**Fix.** Dagger v2 computes normals per part at that part's own texel density.
**Root cause:** the painter's interface assumed one density per atlas while the layouts had grown mixed densities, and nothing compared the rendered groove depth across parts.
**Rule.** When an atlas mixes texel densities, compute normals per region at its own density, and re-check every sheet painted under the single-value assumption before it is made game-ready. That covers the sword, battleaxe, greatsword, war axe and warhammer guards and caps.
Topics: textures, blender, visual-design.

## The shared tube builder sizes a part's texture slot from the round shaft, so a wider square core overlaps its neighbours' UVs (Truly Nordic weapons, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** Found while painting mace v2: the mace's square core shares texture space with the knob and the shaft. It is harmless while those parts are plain steel, but carving on the core would bleed onto them.
**Cause.** The set's tube builder (tn_lib) gives every turned section a UV slot sized from the ROUND shaft cross-section. A square core is wider than the round section, so its strip runs past its slot into the next part's. Every weapon built with the same builder carries the same latent overlap wherever a section is wider than the haft.
**Fix.** None yet. Mace v2 keeps the core, knob and shaft plain, and the fault is recorded. Fix it in tn_lib before any core or socket is engraved on any weapon: size each slot from that section's own perimeter.
**Root cause:** the builder assumed every turned section matches the haft's perimeter, and no check looks for overlapping UV islands.
**Rule.** Before engraving a part, check its UV island does not overlap another part's. A gate on the atlas can find the overlaps: rasterise every island and fail where two land on the same pixel.
Topics: blender, textures, visual-design.

## A flanged mace head drawn with a smooth superellipse profile read as an egg or a cage, not a mace (weapon modelling, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** The first pass at mace v3 gave each flange a smooth superellipse outline. The head read as an egg or a birdcage, not a weapon.
**Cause.** A real flanged mace's flange has a characteristic Gothic profile: a straight lower shoulder rising from the socket, the striking corner high up, and a rounded top sloping back into the socket. A smooth closed curve loses the striking corner that makes it read as a crushing weapon.
**Fix.** v3 uses that profile (a Catmull-Rom spline through control points: shoulder, high striking corner, rounded top), and the head reads as a flanged mace at once. The flange count is six, the historical shestopyor: eight would crowd the faces at that core radius.
**Root cause:** the outline was chosen for smoothness, not taken from how the real object is built.
**Rule.** For a functional weapon form, take the profile's defining features (where it strikes, how it meets the socket) from real examples before drawing, and check the silhouette alone, as a flat black shape, reads as the weapon.
Topics: blender, meshes, visual-design.

## The owner's "fill to here" outline was built as a "trim to here" limit, and his position-marker triangles were built as real triangles (Nordic shield v2, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** On the shield he drew a green circle and four green triangles. Main Agent read the circle as a limit to TRIM the crest to, and the triangles as the points' new shapes. The helper built that, with a concentric gap measured to zero variation. The owner: "I literally drew the lines for what you should fill in with metal ... I just drew triangles. I didn't want them to be actual triangles. I just meant that as a positional reference."
**Cause.** The helper had flagged the ambiguity in its report: arcs drawn only over the board, never over the crest, could mean fill or trim. Main Agent had already told the owner one reading and acted on it. It then took his next message ("parts of the metal that do reach the outer rim should follow that curve") as confirming the trim. Rough shapes drawn as markers were also taken as exact geometry, because the previous lesson said "follow his lines exactly".
**Fix.** Shield v3 starts from v1: the crest grows OUTWARD to his circle, and v1's own convex points are placed at the triangles' positions, same size and mirrored.
**Root cause:** "follow his lines exactly" was applied to every mark, when some marks are areas to fill and some are position markers. The reading said back to him was a description of the build, not a question, so it read as already decided.
**Rule.** Classify each mark before building: an OUTLINE to follow, an AREA to fill (a closed shape over empty space usually means fill), or a MARKER for position only (a simple symbol such as a triangle, X or arrow over an existing feature). When the classification is not obvious, ask it as a question with the options ("fill to the circle, or trim to it?"), and wait for the answer. A reading told to the owner is not his confirmation.
Topics: blender, meshes, visual-design.

## Packaging the Truly Nordic set: five quiet traps between Blender and the game (nif/packaging, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** Building game NIFs for eight re-modelled items turned up five behaviours that fail silently. Each was caught by a read-back or a measurement, not by an error.
**Cause.**
1. `install-test-build.py` copies the whole package root when there is no `Common\` folder, and ignores a FOMOD's required files, so a "00 Core" layout installs as subfolders.
2. A plain bhkRigidBody's translation and rotation fields are not what the game applies: vanilla's greatsword holds 120 units of x the game ignores. The real frame is the node the collision hangs on; the bow's hangs on Bow_MidBone, turned 90 degrees. In the collision object block the node is at offset 0 and the rigid body at offset 6.
3. Blender's collapse decimation stretches faces across UV seams. One warhammer wrap face spanned the whole texture width.
4. PGPatcher.esp redirects the Nordic bow's first-person record to its own `_pgpatcher_dups` copy, so a loose file at the vanilla path loses in a list that runs PGPatcher.
5. SkyPatcher has no operation that sets an armour addon's model, so a shield can only be replaced by a loose file.
**Fix.** Name the core folder `Common`; zero the rigid body's translation and rotation and build the hull in the parent node's frame; lock seam vertices during decimation (an inverted vertex group, factor 1000); ship a local copy at PGPatcher's dup path (outside the package, removed if PGPatcher re-runs); ship the shield loose.
**Root cause:** each tool's behaviour was assumed from its name or a vanilla example, not read from what it does to the actual file.
**Rule.** For every game asset, read back what the tool produced: the installed folder layout, the collision frame against the mesh in game coordinates, the UV spans after decimation, and which file wins each path in the real load order (houseCARL). Check this before calling an asset built.
Topics: nif, packaging, mo2, visual-design.

## Chaining after another mod's 6-byte call hook used the trampoline's pointer-slot address as the function (UVC 1.6.0, 2026-11-10)

**Symptom.** UVC 1.6.0 (d9afd58) crashed Skyrim SE 1.5.97 at the first loading screen when Auto Input Switch was installed: EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION at [value removed]. RAX held the same address, which sits [value removed] below SkyrimSE.exe's base, where SKSE trampolines are allocated. The stack returned into the using-controller check at [offset removed].
**Cause.** Auto Input Switch writes `write_call<6>` at [offset removed]: an FF 15 indirect call reading its target from an 8-byte pointer slot. UVC chained with `g_inner = trampoline.write_call<6>(site, &Answer)`. In CommonLibSSE-NG, `write_call<6>` / `write_branch<6>` return `nextOp + disp`, the ADDRESS of the pointer slot, not the function stored in it. UVC then tail-called the slot as if it were code. The returned value looks like "the original" to anyone used to the 5-byte form, where it really is the target.
**Fix.** The hook was removed entirely (4786fd1). The owner pointed out the switching comes from Auto Input Switch, not the game. UVC now detaches Auto Input Switch's input sink while its Controls page is open and re-attaches it on close, with no engine patch. Had the hook stayed, the fix was `*reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t*>(ret)`.
**Root cause:** the 6-byte trampoline API's return value was assumed to mean the same as the 5-byte one's. And the design hooked the engine for behaviour that came from another mod, without asking which component actually caused it.
**Rule.** A `write_call<6>` / `write_branch<6>` result used as a function pointer must be dereferenced; flag any that is not (gate-rule candidate). Before hooking the engine to stop a behaviour, find which component produces it (vanilla, or a mod), and act on that component.
Topics: cpp, hooks, crash.

## A shield looked solid in every review render but was see-through from behind in game - design renders draw both sides of every face (Truly Nordic shield, 2026-11-11)

**Symptom.** In game the shield was see-through from one side. Every Blender sheet had shown it solid.
**Cause.** The build recalculated face directions BEFORE the separate surfaces were welded. On an open surface Blender's recalculation guesses, so the plank back of the board and the back of the steel crest were wound facing the front. The 1.0.0 steel had 1,480 edges wound against their neighbours. The game draws one side only. The review renders draw both sides, so the fault could never show in them.
**Fix.** A step in the game build (`orient_outward`): weld, give each surface one consistent winding, then cast rays to decide which side is outside. Proof renders of the game NIFs are made with backface culling ON. Also: the shield's PLACEMENT was compared against vanilla's back envelope in both directions. Vanilla's back is a shallow dish that curls back more at the left and right than at the top and bottom, and a profile fitted to the front face alone had hidden a 3-unit rim error on the arm side, which was the clipping.
**Root cause:** the review renders could not show a single-sided fault, and placement was judged on one surface rather than on the surface the arm actually touches.
**Rule.** Render game-NIF proofs with backface culling on. Fail any NIF whose shapes have edges wound against their neighbours (a gate-rule candidate). Compare a worn item's placement against vanilla's surfaces on the side that touches the body, in both directions. When an approved map needs one area changed, swap in only that area; a full repaint drifted the war axe's seam by about 10 px.
Topics: nif, blender, visual-design.

## A skinned mesh given a rigid weapon's shader block draws nothing (Truly Nordic bow, visual-design, nif, 2026-11-11)

**Symptom.** The re-modelled Nordic bow was invisible in first and third person, and equipping it started the motion and stalled halfway.
**Cause.** Every Truly Nordic shape got one plain TruePBR shader block copied from a rigid (unskinned) weapon. The bow is the one skinned item - its three shapes bend on Bow_* bones - and the copied SLSF1 lacked Skinned ([value removed]), which vanilla's bow carries. The bone tree, partitions and bones all matched vanilla, so the inspection by structure looked clean; the fault was one flag bit in the shader.
**Fix.** assemble.py ORs SLSF1 [value removed] into every skinned shape's shader (and sets vanilla's NiAVObject flags [value removed]); verify.py fails any shape whose skin reference and Skinned flag disagree.
**Root cause:** the shader template was chosen once for the whole set, and the assembly never asked whether each shape was skinned - a property the template could not know.
**Rule.** When a shader block is reused across shapes, check per shape that SLSF1 Skinned matches whether the shape has a skin instance; compare a new skinned mesh's shader flags with vanilla's, not just its bones.

## A hook on the object's own Activate misses presses a perk takes first (Dynamic Simple Knock vs ESO Lockpick Menu, cpp, skyrim, 2026-11-11)

**Symptom.** With ESO Lockpick Menu installed, the Knock prompt showed on a lived-in locked door, but pressing Activate went straight into lockpicking; our log had no Activate line at all for the press.
**Cause.** ESO's plugin gives the player a perk (SKYBUILockpickPerk) with an Activate entry point set to Run Immediately + Replace Default on any locked, pickable target. The engine runs perk activate entry points inside TESObjectREFR::ActivateRef, BEFORE the base object's vtable Activate, and Replace Default returns early, so TESObjectDOOR::Activate (slot [value removed]) - where Knock lived - is never called. It looked like a DLL conflict because ESO ships a DLL, but the DLL only drives its menu cursor; the vtable slot still held the game's own address.
**Fix.** Knock 1.3.1 takes the press one step earlier, in ActivateHandler::ProcessButton (slot 4 on SE/AE, 6 on the 1.7 line), when the crosshair door shows Knock; Pick the lock hands the door back to ActivateRef so the perks still run.
**Root cause:** the hook point was chosen as "where the door activates", without asking what runs between the button and that point (perk entry points, activate-choice boxes); the earlier Ordinator report fixed only the non-immediate choice box.
**Rule.** When a feature must own the player's activation of a reference, hook the input (ActivateHandler) or ActivateRef, not the base object's Activate - and check the load order for PERK records with an Activate entry point flagged Run Immediately / Replace Default before calling a hook point safe.

## Nexus v3 refuses a single-part upload over 100 MiB; the multipart endpoint is /uploads/multipart (Truly Nordic first file, nexus, upload, 2026-11-11)

**Symptom.** The first file of a new page (121 MB) failed at POST /v3/uploads: "File size exceeds maximum of 100 MiB for single-part uploads. Use multipart upload instead."
**Cause.** Our upload scripts only knew the single-part flow; no published v3 doc names the multipart route.
**Fix.** Probed it: POST /v3/uploads/multipart {size_bytes, filename} returns {id, part_size_bytes (50 MiB), part_presigned_urls[], complete_presigned_url}. PUT each part to its URL and keep the ETag header; POST `<CompleteMultipartUpload><Part><PartNumber>n</PartNumber><ETag>..</ETag></Part>...` to complete_presigned_url; then POST /uploads/{id}/finalise and poll until state=available, as with single-part. Implemented in .MD\scripts\nexus-description\tncw-1.0.0\post_first_file.py (upload_multipart).
**Root cause:** the upload role was written for small updates and never told what to do past Nexus's single-part limit.
**Rule.** Any Nexus upload path checks the archive size and goes multipart over 100 MiB; fold upload_multipart into nexus-upload.py with the first-file mode. Also: Sketchfab's page blocks fetches from localhost, so a large model goes in as <10 MB pieces joined in the page into one File handed to its upload input.


## A repo with both dist\ and data\: the packager ignores data\ and ships the previous release's copies (TK Dodge AIO 1.1.0, release, packaging, 2026-11-11)

**Symptom.** TK Dodge AIO's package still carried the third-party step-dodge clips and fSprintingPressDuration = 0.50 after both were changed in the repo (our clips added, the INI default set to 0.30), and package-mod reported "Packaged" with no warning.
**Cause.** package-mod.ps1 refreshes a package from the repo's Data\ tree only when the repo has NO dist\ folder (the 2026-09-20 rule for Perfected Wheeler). TK Dodge AIO keeps its translations in dist\ and its INI in data\, so data\ was skipped and the seed package's old files went out again.
**Fix.** Moved data\ into dist\ (1e6ba31); the repackage refreshed all four clips and the INI, checked byte-for-byte against the repo.
**Root cause:** the packager treats "dist\ exists" as "nothing else ships", and nothing compares a repo's data\ files to the package when both folders exist.
**Rule.** A repo ships from ONE tree. When both dist\ and data\ exist, package-mod must refuse (or merge and say so); after any change to a shipped data file, compare that file in the package with the repo's copy before installing.

## A rename that only changed the code left the old name in the behaviour patch Pandora shows (Simple Dodge 1.1.0, release, packaging, 2026-11-11)

**Symptom.** After the settings page was renamed "Simple Dodge", Pandora's patch list still showed "TK Dodge AIO"; the owner caught it.
**Cause.** The display name of a Pandora/Nemesis patch is the name= line of its info.ini (Nemesis_Engine/mod/<code>/info.ini). That file was not in the repo at all - it rode along only in the seed package - so a search of the repo for the old name could never have found it.
**Fix.** Moved the patch into the repo's dist/ (a406e5f), set name=Simple Dodge (code tkds kept, behaviours are keyed to it), copied it into the package and the installed folder, reran Pandora with --auto_run --auto_close: the log reads "Pandora Mod 18 : Simple Dodge".
**Root cause:** a rename was treated as a code change, and nothing searches the PACKAGE (what actually ships) for the old name; files carried only in a seed package are invisible to repo checks.
**Rule.** A rename searches the built package's every text file (info.ini, ini, json, xml, txt) for the old name, not just the repo; any shipped file that exists only in the package is moved into the repo first.

## A roll's "head stays off the floor" check passed while the crown could still hit - the head bone sits at the base of the skull (Simple Dodge rolls, animation, 2026-11-11)

Topics: animation, blender, testing

**Symptom.** The owner saw the head hit the ground in the forward roll, though the build's floor check kept the head joint 9-16 units up.
**Cause.** A skeleton joint is where a bone starts: NPC Head [Head] is at the base of the skull and NPC Neck at the base of the neck (top of the back). Upside down with the chin tucked, the crown is ~14 units further along the head, so "head joint above the floor" says nothing about the top of the head. Tucking the neck and head harder also changed nothing, because the low point is set by the chest's curl, not by the head's rotation.
**Fix.** check_roll_contact.py measures crown, head joint, neck joint and spine per clip from the build's own solver; the floor check now holds the CROWN 7 units up and lets the neck joint (back of the neck) reach the floor, which the owner allows.
**Root cause:** clearances were set on bone joints as if each were the surface of that body part.
**Rule.** A contact or clearance check on a pose measures surface points (crown, heel, fingertip) carried by the bone's rotation, not the joint where the bone starts - and prints the numbers per clip before anyone looks at a render.

## Open hands built as a small finger curl stayed curled - the vanilla rest pose is already half-closed (Simple Dodge unarmed, animation, 2026-11-11)

Topics: animation, blender

**Symptom.** The unarmed guard's "open" hands rendered as loose fists.
**Cause.** Finger curls were applied as rotations ON TOP of the skeleton's rest pose, and the SE skeleton's rest fingers are already bent; a positive 8-12 degree "open" curl closed them further.
**Fix.** The open hand uses negative curls (-12/-22/-12, thumb 0/-5/-5) that extend past rest; checked on a cropped render.
**Root cause:** "open" was taken to mean "small curl" without looking at what the rest pose is.
**Rule.** Before keying a hand, foot or face pose as an offset, render the rest pose of that part and say what it is; an offset's meaning depends on it.

## A replacement that inserted text with CRLF into an LF file hid whole lines behind bare carriage returns (build_stepdodge.py, animation tooling, 2026-11-11)

Topics: animation, powershell

**Symptom.** Blender failed with "name 'Rhip' is not defined" and the roll's head tuck and hand keys vanished, though each PowerShell replace reported no MISSING.
**Cause.** Edit-tool writes had left part of the file LF; a PowerShell replace inserted `r`n text, and lines after a lone CR were swallowed into the line before when the file was later normalised. Grep showed only the comment lines, so the loss looked like nothing.
**Fix.** Normalised the file to LF, re-added the lost lines, and ran ast.parse on the script after every scripted edit.
**Root cause:** scripted text edits did not match the file's own line endings and nothing re-read the result.
**Rule.** A scripted edit reads the file's line ending first and inserts with it; after it, parse (or compile) the file and re-grep for each inserted key before building.

## A package silently dropped files that share a NAME with another file in it - the packager's FOMOD by-name skip ran on a plain package (Simple Dodge 1.1.0, packaging, animation, 2026-11-11)

Topics: packaging, animation, powershell

**Symptom.** install-test-build moved eight "stale" OAR unarmed clips out of the test folder: the package had no [asset path removed] or [asset path removed], though dist\ held them and git tracked them. The same rule had also dropped the magic graph's new behaviour nodes (#tkds$92.txt exists in both 1hm_behavior and magicbehavior), so the first 8-way install had no diagonal states in magicbehavior.
**Cause.** package-mod.ps1 copies dist\ but skips any file whose file NAME is already anywhere in the package - a rule written for FOMOD packages, which move files about. A plain package of an animation mod is full of same-named files in different folders (armed vs OAR variants, one node number per graph), so they were skipped with no message.
**Fix.** The by-name skip now applies only when the package is a FOMOD (fomod\ModuleConfig.xml and Common\). Repackaged: all 12 unarmed clips and every magicbehavior node shipped; the install was then compared file-by-file with dist\ (371 files, only README.txt differs, as written by the packager).
**Root cause:** a deduplication rule keyed on file name where file identity is the relative path.
**Rule.** After packaging, compare dist\ with the package by relative path (not count, not name) before installing; any dist file absent from the package is a packaging defect, not "stale".

## Pandora's run-and-close mode built none of a new patch - --auto_run reuses the saved selection, where a new or once-unticked code stays OFF (Simple Dodge, BFCO, MCO, launch, 2026-11-11)

Topics: animation, gates, launch, combined-run

**Symptom.** After a Pandora run that reported success, BFCO's moveset did nothing, Simple Dodge's 8-way states (new code `sdge`) were missing, and MCO had run all afternoon with no behaviour. ActiveMods.json was edited by hand three times to fix it.
**Cause.** `Pandora --auto_run --auto_close` builds from `Pandora Output\Pandora_Engine\ActiveMods.json`, the selection the last GUI run saved. A patch Pandora has not seen before, or one unticked in an earlier GUI session (amco), is inactive there, and the run skips it without a word. The success line ("Pandora Mod 18 : Simple Dodge") lists what WAS built, so it read as proof.
**Fix.** New launch gate `pandora-active-patches-gate.py` (role `pandora-active-patches-gate`, called by game-relaunch.ps1): fails while any ENABLED mod's `Nemesis_Engine\mod\<code>` or `Pandora_Engine\mod\<code>` is missing or inactive in the selection; `--fix` marks them active (backup `.bak-gate`) so the next Pandora run builds them. Test: tests\test_pandora_active_patches_gate.py.
**Root cause:** the unattended Pandora run depends on GUI state nobody checks, and the launch trusted "Pandora ran" instead of "Pandora built every enabled patch".
**Rule.** A generator run unattended from saved settings is checked against what is enabled NOW, by a gate before launch, not by reading its success line.

## The installer put its backup INSIDE the mod folder - a full-path mod argument made os.path.join drop the backup root (install-test-build, Simple Dodge 1.1.0, 2026-11-11)

Topics: install-test-build, python, mo2

**Symptom.** install-test-build moved two stale files "to _install-backups" but the message named `mods\test Simple Dodge 1.1.0\20261111-180003\`; the read-back then failed on its own backup, and MO2 would have loaded it. Recycled by hand three times.
**Cause.** The mod was passed as a full path. `os.path.join(<instance>\_install-backups, <absolute path>, stamp)` discards every part before an absolute one, so the backup root vanished and the stamp folder landed in the mod. Each time it looked like a one-off stray folder, so it was recycled instead of traced.
**Fix.** A full-path mod argument is split into its mods folder and name; the installer refuses if the backup folder would sit inside the mod folder. Test: tests\test_install_full_path_mod.py.
**Root cause:** a path join with a user-supplied segment that could be absolute, and no check that the result stayed under its intended root.
**Rule.** Any path built from an argument is checked to lie under the root it is meant to (normpath + startswith) - and a stray folder that appears twice is traced, not cleaned up again.

## A build script wrote its package outside the pipeline - its OutRoot default pointed at an old folder (Ysgramor's Armor addon 1.1.0, build, 2026-11-11)

Topics: packaging, build, ysgramor

**Symptom.** The 1.1.0 package was not in `7. current test builds`, so the install and the pipeline tools could not find it; it was moved there by hand.
**Cause.** The addon's own build.ps1 (an asset mod, not built through package-mod.ps1) had a hard-coded OutRoot from before the pipeline folders were renamed.
**Fix.** build.ps1's OutRoot default is `7. current test builds\Skyrim - Ysgramor's Armor addon` (commit cb39a7d).
**Root cause:** a mod-local build script kept its own copy of a pipeline path instead of asking the resolver (rule 70).
**Rule.** A mod's own build script takes its output folder from the resolver (`Resolve-PackageRoot` / `resolve.py place`), never a typed path; when one is found typed, replace it rather than moving the output.

## A Blender top-down render came out as flat background - the ortho camera's default clip_end (100 units) cut the whole scene (Simple Dodge showcase GIFs, blender, 2026-11-11)

Topics: blender, render, animation

**Symptom.** Every frame of the first top-down showcase was a plain grey square; the run finished without error.
**Cause.** The camera was placed 1200 units above the floor; Blender's default camera clip_end is 100, so everything lay beyond the far clip plane. Nothing in the render reports that.
**Fix.** clip_start 1, clip_end 5000 for the top view, and `blank_check()` in showcase_render.py stops the run when frame 1 holds one flat colour (probed on a real frame and a flat one).
**Root cause:** the renderer had no check that its output contains the subject, so a framing error cost a full clip before anyone looked.
**Rule.** Any render loop checks its first frame for content (more than one colour, or the subject's pixels) before rendering the rest; a camera moved far from the scene sets its clip range explicitly.

## A PowerShell script used $p and $P (and $b and $B) as two variables - PowerShell names are case-insensitive, so one overwrote the other (combined-run launch scripting, 2026-11-11)

Topics: powershell, combined-run

**Symptom.** A combined-run call failed with a batch id that was a file path, and a later step read a profile path that had become a batch id.
**Cause.** `$P` (profile) and `$p` (path), `$B` (batch) and `$b` (build) are the SAME variable in PowerShell; the later assignment silently replaced the earlier one. Written by a mind used to case-sensitive Python, the script looked correct.
**Fix.** Distinct names ($profileName, $batchId, $pkgPath).
**Root cause:** variable naming carried over from a case-sensitive language into one that is not.
**Rule.** In PowerShell never use two names that differ only in case; use full words for anything that holds a path, a batch id or a profile.

## A reshaped weapon face broke the old build and engraving - a double crescent needs a slanted seam, a new split, and a weave field (Truly Nordic battle axe v10, visual design, 2026-11-11)

Topics: visual-design, blender, meshes, textures

**Symptom.** Reshaping the battle axe head to the owner's double-crescent outline (a second point and a notch along the bottom) would have lost the second bottom point with v9's vertical row/column seam; v9's rings of knot bands broke into fragments inside the new face; keeping v9's crescent/knot-panel split squeezed the roundel; and the first render had no wrap textures.
**Cause.** Each v9 choice was tuned to v9's outline: the vertical seam assumed the outline never turns back at both ends, the band rings assumed a convex face, the split was placed for the wider blade, and the wrap textures had been copied into work_v9\tex by hand (the paint script does not make them).
**Fix.** v10 (helper session): the seam slants from the notch's apex to the horn's inner corner so both halves stay single-valued; the crescent field uses the warhammer's over-under weave inside the braid border; the split was MEASURED (roundel radius vs panel width, x = -6.6) instead of kept; wrap textures copied into work_v10\tex. Fit to his outline: mean 1.2 px, worst 4.2 px.
**Root cause:** a version's design constants were reused as if they were properties of the weapon rather than of one outline.
**Rule.** When an outline changes, re-derive every outline-dependent choice (mesh seam, field pattern, panel split) and measure it; and a new version folder gets every input the render needs (wrap textures) before rendering.

## A point the owner drew beside an existing point meant MOVE it there, not ADD a second one (Truly Nordic battle axe v10 -> v11, visual design, 2026-11-11)

Topics: visual-design

**Symptom.** v10 was built with two bottom points and a notch; the owner: "There's not supposed to be a second point on the bottom. It was meant to move the point back to that point that I drew."
**Cause.** His green outline still touched the old beard tip (where his line started from the existing shape) and added a new point further back; the written reading turned both into features, and the helper built exactly what was written.
**Fix.** v11: one sharp beard point at his drawn point, no notch (fit mean 1.07 px).
**Root cause:** a drawn mark next to an existing feature was read as an addition; the same misread happened with the shield's position triangles.
**Rule.** When a mark on his drawing sits beside an existing feature, read it as MOVING that feature unless he says "add"; when it could be either, ask in one line before building.

## A sheath offset from the blade's outline can't be drawn - it must hold the blade's whole draw path (Truly Nordic sheaths v1, visual design, 2026-11-11)

Topics: visual-design, blender, meshes

**Symptom.** A sheath built by offsetting the sword's outline would trap the blade: the A5d sword widens at its edge shoulder and its point turns up, and the kukri's belly is wider than its throat. The first guard reading also put the sword's throat at y 11-15 instead of 4-7, and an arc search scored blade motions going the wrong way (up, out of the sheath) as the slimmest.
**Cause.** A blade at rest is not what a sheath must contain; tn_lib blades are several loose grids (flats, edge strips, caps), so "the loose part reaching highest" is not the whole blade; and a rotation's sign about a centre was not checked against the direction of the draw.
**Fix.** The helper swept each blade along 100 candidate draw paths (straight and arcs either side), kept the slimmest that holds the blade at every point (sword arc r150, dagger arc r51, greatsword straight), classified blade parts by reach (anything reaching the blade's upper half is blade), and checked each motion moves the blade down before scoring.
**Root cause:** the container was derived from the object's resting shape, not from how it moves in and out of it.
**Rule.** Any part that something slides into (sheath, holster, quiver) is built from the swept volume of the draw path; verify the motion's direction before scoring candidates; classify a multi-part mesh by geometry reach, not by "the biggest loose part".

## Two rebuilds came from tracing the owner's drawing by eye off a chat image - get it on disk and trace its pixels (Truly Nordic battle axe v10/v11 -> v12, visual design, 2026-11-11)

Topics: visual-design

**Symptom.** v10 and v11 were built from a point list I read off his chat image; he said v11 "doesn't look right at all". v12, traced from the same kind of drawing saved as a file, matched his green to 0.62 px mean on the first try.
**Cause.** Coordinates estimated by eye from a displayed image, then smoothed through a handful of points, lost the shape (horn width, where the tips sit, the line through both tips). The first drawing never reached the disk: an image pasted in chat is only on disk when the harness gives it a source path.
**Fix.** His resent drawing came with a file path; it was copied into set2\, his green/yellow pixels traced directly (stroke centre lines, each line carried to its tip, the shape closed against the socket before filling), and his yellow parallel marks applied as a constraint.
**Root cause:** the design input was a paraphrase of the drawing instead of the drawing itself.
**Rule.** Before building from an owner's drawing, put the drawing itself on disk (copy it from the image's source path, or ask him to save it) and trace its pixels; never build from coordinates read by eye. Show the drawing and the build side by side at the same camera before asking him to judge.

## A narrow face dropped the owner's symbol because it inherited a wider face's layout; and open tubes came out wound inside-out (Truly Nordic sheaths v2 / straight sword, visual design, 2026-11-11)

Topics: visual-design, blender, meshes, textures

**Symptom.** The dagger sheath's locket (v1) and the straight sword's locket had no room for the triquetra because the wider lockets' layout (border all round, ring inside) was scaled down onto them; the owner then asked for the symbol "even if you have to lower its size a bit". Separately, the approved greatsword's ricasso wrap was found wound inward on ~2,250 of ~2,570 faces - invisible in the review renders.
**Cause.** A layout tuned to one face proportion was reused on a narrower face; and tn_lib guesses face direction on open tubes, and the renders draw back faces, so a wrong-way surface never showed.
**Fix.** Each narrow face got its own measured layout built around the symbol (dagger: margin 0.32 -> 0.25, braid runs round the ring's sides, triquetra r 1.45; straight sword: border, weave, then the triquetra r 1.1 on a lengthened locket). The winding defect is on the to-do list with a gate to add.
**Root cause:** layout and orientation were assumed carried over from a working case instead of checked on the new one.
**Rule.** When the owner asks for a symbol, change the layout around the symbol before shrinking it below readability; after every mesh build, check orientation (open surfaces vs the centre line, closed solids by ray-cast, no edge wound against its neighbour) and fail the build on a hit - review renders with back faces drawn cannot show it.

## The sheath tips got a braid border with nothing inside it to go around - against the owner's braid rule (Truly Nordic sheaths v1-v4, visual design, 2026-11-11)

Topics: visual-design, textures

**Symptom.** Every sheath chape (the end tip) was carved as a border braid round a weave field. The owner (22:06): "mark it as a mistake on the tools end that the braid was used to go around the end tips as there's no center symbol to go around which is against the rule".
**Cause.** The sheath paint tool applied the skill's broad-face recipe (braid perimeter -> weave -> symbol) to every face and simply left the symbol out where it did not fit, keeping the braid. The rule (2026-11-10 20:07) says the braid goes AROUND something - a perimeter round a centerpiece or a straight run along a long field; with no centerpiece the braid frames nothing.
