**Fix.** Chapes become one framed panel of weave (flush rim + groove), mirrored, point plain steel - in the sheaths v2 round; the lockets lost the braid and ring round the triquetra the same day (dagger v4, approved). The weapon-engraving skill now states the small-fitting layout and that a braid perimeter is used only where it frames something.
**Root cause:** the tool encoded a recipe (always start with a braid border) instead of the rule's reason (the braid's job is to go around something).
**Rule.** Before laying out any face, name what each element is FOR: no centerpiece and no long run -> no braid; the face is a framed weave panel. A tool that drops the symbol must also drop the braid that only existed to frame it.

## A model mod's installer named its alternate models in words only - the player could not see what he was choosing (Truly Nordic 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0, packaging, 2026-11-11)

Topics: packaging, visual-design, release

**Symptom.** Truly Nordic 1.0.0's FOMOD mace step offered "Six-flanged" or "Classic" with no picture of either. The owner (23:23): pictures from the renders in the FOMOD "should be standard practice from now on, so they know what they're installing at the point of installation" - narrowed (23:25) to mods "that are for models like these".
**Cause.** The installer was written as text options, and nothing required an option that installs a model to show it.
**Fix.** 1.1.0's four installers show a picture on every model option (sword, mace, shield; 1000x600 renders). Gate row `fomod-model-options-have-a-picture` (.MD\scripts\gates\fomod-option-image-gate.py, with a self-test): an option that installs any .nif must carry an image whose file ships; options installing no .nif are never checked.
**Root cause:** the choice was described, not shown, and the release checks had no notion of what a choice installs.
**Rule.** A model choice is shown, not named: any FOMOD option that installs meshes carries a picture of exactly that model; decide which options need one from what they install, not from a list of mods.

## A reshaped part clipped through its neighbour - and the original had clipped too, hidden inside the ferrule (Truly Nordic saber A5g -> A5h, visual design, 2026-11-11)

Topics: visual-design, meshes, blender

**Symptom.** The owner saw the flat-sided pommel (A5g) "clipping with the base of the handle". A mesh intersection check found 174 intersecting triangle pairs with the ferrule and 42 with the grip wrap; the original rounded pommel (A5/A5f) had 124 and 44 - hidden inside the ferrule, so no render showed it.
**Cause.** The reshape was checked by silhouette and by the sheath clearance, never by intersection with the parts it meets; the original's overlap had never been measured either.
**Fix.** A5h: the pommel's first 1.9 units are a level round mouth inside the ferrule's ring, easing into the flat section below it; 0 intersecting triangles, smallest gap 0.108 to the ferrule and 0.238 to the wrap.
**Root cause:** part-to-part contact was judged by eye from renders instead of measured.
**Rule.** After reshaping any part where it meets another, run a triangle intersection check against every neighbouring shape (and run it on the original, which may already clip); report 0 intersections and the minimum gap before showing the owner.

## Two approved weapons broke the owner's braid rule and nothing caught it - the engraving checks measured margins, not layout (Truly Nordic battleaxe v12 and war axe v3, visual design, 2026-11-11)

Topics: visual-design, gates, textures

**Symptom.** The owner (23:39): "i noticed the battleaxe broke a rule so do a check and see if the gate catches it in the design" - "it does the same issue in 2 areas". Battleaxe v12 filled its crescent with knot bands round the triquetra, and its socket bar and back spike with braid that framed nothing; war axe v3 (shipped in 1.0.0) had knot bands filling its blade face. No check failed.
**Cause.** Every engraving_check.json recorded coverage, margins and crossings - geometry - but not what each face IS (braid perimeter / weave field / centerpiece / run), so the rule (weapon-engraving skill: braid only frames a centerpiece or runs straight; weave fills; no centerpiece -> no braid) could only be checked by eye, and v12 was approved on its shape.
**Fix.** engraving-layout-gate.py (gate row engraving-layout-follows-the-rule; design-time set2\design_gate.py called by the render scripts): each face carries a layout record; braid/knot/bands as a field FAILS, a braid perimeter framing nothing FAILS, a face with no record FAILS. Battleaxe v13 and war axe v4 are being repainted to the rule.
**Root cause:** a design rule given in words was never turned into recorded data a check could read.
**Rule.** When the owner sets a design rule, make the paint step record the property the rule is about and add a gate that reads it, at design time and at packaging - a review by eye is not the check.

## A swept part folded through itself where it bent tighter than it was wide - the owner saw it as a crack (Truly Nordic saber pommel A5h -> A5i, visual design, 2026-11-12)

Topics: visual-design, meshes, blender

**Symptom.** The owner: "theres a crack" - a thin bright slit down the inside of the pommel hook's U. The helper had noted "a small crease ... A5 already had" on A5g and moved on.
**Cause.** At the bottom of the U the sweep's bend radius was smaller than the pommel's half width, so 10 section rows ran backwards and the inner wall cut through the flat face (89 self-intersecting triangle pairs, plus 30 open edges at the tip); the rim light showed through the fold. A mirrored weave also creased along a mirror line that ran down that same spot.
**Fix.** A5i: the rows round the U re-aimed so no two sections cross, the inner corner rounded, both ends closed, the weave continuous instead of mirrored - 0 self-intersections, 0 open edges.
**Root cause:** a defect inherited from an older version was labelled "existing" and not measured; sweeps were never checked for backward rows or self-intersection.
**Rule.** Check every swept shape for rows that run backwards and for self-intersecting triangles before rendering; a flaw "inherited from the original" is still a flaw - measure it, don't wave it through.

## Finishing a stale combined-run batch rolled the test profile back nine hours, undoing the owner's decisions (Main session, combined-run, 2026-11-12)

Topics: combined-run, profiles, mo2

**Symptom.** To launch for the Simple Dodge re-check, the launcher refused batch B-20261111-151325-af22 as stale (9.7 h, limit 8 h). Running `combined-run finish --allow-not-run` then restored modlist.txt and plugins.txt to the batch's 15:13 snapshot: Simple Dodge.esp, the Ysgramor No Companions plugin, the TK Dodge AIO -> Simple Dodge swap and the Paragon "TKDodgeAddon plugin only" folder were all undone.
**Cause.** finish treats every profile change since the batch started as a temporary test change and puts the start snapshot back unless the change was marked with `combined-run keep`. Over a long session most changes were the owner's permanent decisions, and none had been marked.
**Fix.** finish had saved the pre-restore files in `<batch>-final\`; they were copied back with MO2 closed (CRLF intact), the rolled-back copies kept as `*.bak-wrongrestore-20261112`.
**Root cause:** a batch was left open across many owner decisions, and finish restores by default with no review of what it is about to undo.
**Rule.** Before `combined-run finish`, read the diff it will undo and `keep` every change the owner decided; never finish a long or stale batch blind. The tool should refuse to finish a batch older than its own stale limit until each changed line is marked keep or restore (to-do).

## A release with several main files had no pipeline path - every release tool assumed one archive (Truly Nordic 1.1.0, release, 2026-11-12)

Topics: packaging, nexus, release, testing

**Symptom.** Truly Nordic 1.1.0 became four main files (Replacer No ESP / ESP, Standalone Nordic / Ebony); the one-zip distro rule, finalize-mod and nexus-upload.py each assumed a single archive, so the release could only have been posted by hand. While committing the fix, two unrelated tests failed: a golden package-gate copy missing two "skip" lines from gate rows added on 11-07/11-08, and a repack-fomod test that hard-coded a borrowed DLL's version (1.2.0, now 1.6.0).
**Cause.** The release tools were written for the common single-package mod; nothing described a release's files. The golden copy was never re-recorded when those rows were added, and the test pinned a value it borrows from a live build.
**Fix.** A per-mod `nexus-files.json` manifest (role `nexus-files`, scripts\release\nexus_files.py) read by finalize, the distro sweep, the archive gate row and nexus-upload's multi-file mode (multipart over 100 MiB; the version recorded posted once, after every file verifies); tests in test_nexus_files.py. The golden copy got the two missing lines; the repack test now reads the DLL's real version. .MD db7fac0.
**Root cause:** a shape the release could take (several downloads) had no data describing it, and tests compared against copies and constants that drift.
**Rule.** When a release takes a new shape, describe it in data the tools read rather than handling it by hand; re-record a golden file in the same commit that adds a gate row; a test that borrows a real build reads its values, never hard-codes them.

## A Nexus image posted with an empty description, after a title the form refused (nexus-media, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** The first Truly Nordic composite would not publish: "Publish my image" did nothing visible. Once it did publish, the image page's "About this image" was empty, though the description with the mod link had been set by script. Editing it afterwards failed with "You have to agree to our Terms of Service". The eleventh image was then refused: "You can only upload 10 images every 24 hours".
**Cause.** Four rules of Nexus's image form, each silent until hit: (1) titles allow only letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, underscores and apostrophes, so "(Saber)" raised a modal error behind the page; (2) the Description field is a WysiBB editor, so setting `#image-description`'s value is overwritten from the editor body on submit; (3) the edit form needs the terms box ticked again; (4) an account may post 10 images per 24 hours. The script reported success because it checked only the fields it had set.
**Fix.** Titles rewritten with " - " instead of brackets; the description written through the editor (`$('#image-description').data('wbb')`: modeSwitch to BBCode, `$txtArea.val(T)`, modeSwitch back, then `$('#image-description').val(w.getBBCode())`); the saber image (319972) fixed on the edit page with the terms box ticked. Ten images posted (319972-319981); the clean shield waits for the 24-hour window.
**Root cause:** the posting script verified the values it wrote rather than reading the published page back, and a form's limits (title characters, rate) were not known before a batch was started.
**Rule.** After any scripted form post, read the published page back for each field that matters (here: "Get it here" and the mod link present); check a site's title characters and rate limits before a batch, and split a batch larger than the limit across days up front.

## Building from the owner's markup without recovering the camera it was drawn on (weapon-engraving, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Bow v4 missed three of the owner's outline marks ("not all my outlines were followed").
**Cause.** v4 was built from a written reading of his marks on a picture assumed to be the v3 close-up; the markup was in fact drawn on a v2 render of the riser's far side, so the reading placed the lines wrongly.
**Fix.** v5 fitted his picture's camera from the steel in it (yaw 180, orthographic, ~24 units), mapped his pixels onto the bow's coordinates, built from them, and laid his lines over the new render to check.
**Root cause:** a drawn instruction was translated into words before being turned into geometry, and the picture it sat on was never identified.
**Rule.** When the owner marks up a render, first identify which render it is and recover its camera; build from his marks in model coordinates and prove the result by overlaying his lines on a render from that camera. His marks are a rough guide, not a blueprint (2026-11-12 02:35: v5 reshaped the narrow end of the teardrop panel, which he never asked to change): change only what a mark clearly asks for, and where a rough line disagrees with a shape he did not ask to change, keep the existing shape.

## A "scratch" copy of Pandora rebuilt the live modlist's behaviour output (pandora, behaviour, sandbox, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** A helper ran a scratch copy of Pandora Behaviour Engine+ with `--tesv:<scratch game> -o <scratch out> --auto_run --auto_close` to test Simple Dodge offline. The LIVE `<MO2>\<test instance>\mods\Pandora Output` was rebuilt from the bare Stock Game with only "Pandora Base", and its `Pandora_Engine\ActiveMods.json` became `[]` - every behaviour patch (MCO, BFCO, Simple Dodge, Precision...) gone. Closing a GUI-only peek of the copy wrote `[]` again.
**Cause.** Pandora takes its game and output paths from the `Settings.json` next to its exe (and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Pandora Behaviour Engine\Settings.json`), not from the command line, and saves the patch selection to that output on exit. The copy carried the live instance's Settings.json, so "scratch" was only the exe's location.
**Fix.** `pandora-active-patches-gate --profile "Njordlinger Test" --fix` restored the selection (31 patches); Pandora was re-run through MO2 for the profile with `--auto_run --auto_close` set temporarily on its MO2 executable entry (reverted after): Engine.log lists 32 Pandora mods including Simple Dodge.
**Root cause:** a tool's sandbox was assumed from its command-line flags without checking where the tool actually reads its paths and writes its state.
**Rule.** Before running a copy of a tool "outside" a live setup, read every config file it loads (beside the exe and in %LOCALAPPDATA%/%APPDATA%) and point them at the sandbox, or run it as a different user profile; check after the first run that nothing under the live instance changed (mtimes). Behaviour engines (Pandora, Nemesis) run against the live instance only through MO2, by Main Agent.

## "Tested with Pandora" said nothing about Nemesis: an empty info.ini field crashed Nemesis at start (nemesis, pandora, behaviour, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Simple Dodge 1.0.0 (Nexus bug 1171565): "Starting Nemesis with this mod active crashes it, gives a critical error and instantly crashes." Pandora built the same patch without a word.
**Cause.** `Nemesis_Engine\mod\sdge\info.ini` had `site=` empty. Nemesis reads every patch's info.ini at start, ticked or not, and refuses one with an empty name, author or site ("Missing info in info.ini", TBT 1014). Pandora accepts it. The mod was only ever run through Pandora, so the Nemesis half of the package was untested while the page claimed both.
**Fix.** `site=` filled with the mod page URL; reproduced and proven with Nemesis 0.84 in a scratch Data folder (generation complete, all dodge events in the output). New gate `nemesis-patch-info-gate.py` (row `nemesis-patch-info-ini-complete`).
**Root cause:** a package supporting two engines was tested on one, and nothing checked the other engine's input rules.
**Rule.** Each engine a package claims (Pandora, Nemesis, FNIS) is proven by running that engine on it; until then the claim is "built, untested". Gate the engine's known hard requirements mechanically.

## A tap detector built from "down" events fired on a held key (input, skse, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Simple Dodge, double-tap mode with the dodge on the sprint key: holding sprint also dodged (Arvaetar, 12 Nov).
**Cause.** 1.0.0 counted a double tap as two down events within 0.3 s. The sprint hook rewrites a held press's `heldDownSecs` to 0 so the game starts the delayed sprint, and the dodge sink, which runs after the player controls on the same event, read every such frame as a new press.
**Fix.** `TapDetector.h`: a press counts once from its first down to its release on our own clock; a tap is a press released within the tap window; a double tap is two taps; a hold cancels a pending tap; 15 offline cases.
**Root cause:** the detector trusted event fields another handler had already rewritten.
**Rule.** Detect taps and holds from your own press state (first down to release, own clock), never from a down event's held-time field; an input sink that runs after the player controls sees events they changed.

## Packaging keyed files by NAME in an animation patch, dropping a node file (packaging, behaviour, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Simple Dodge 1.1.0's package lacked `magicbehavior\#sdge$97.txt`; the dist check passed.
**Cause.** package-mod.ps1's FOMOD skip-by-file-name saw `1hm_behavior\#sdge$97.txt` and skipped the second file of the same name; the dist gate also matched by name.
**Fix.** The skip counts only files outside Common\; `package-ships-repo-dist` matches by relative path.
**Root cause:** file identity was the name, in a layout (behaviour patches) where node file names repeat in every graph folder.
**Rule.** Identify package files by relative path, never by name alone.

## A translation check that compares languages to English misses a key missing from English too (translations, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** 42 existing Simple Dodge settings showed English labels in every language.
**Cause.** The check compared the other ten files with English; the keys were missing from all eleven, English included, so nothing differed.
**Fix.** `tr-keys-translated-gate.py` (row `settings-keys-in-every-translation-file`): every key the source uses must be in every language file.
**Root cause:** the reference for "complete" was one of the files being checked, not the source.
**Rule.** Check translation files against the keys the source code uses, not against one language file.


## A sticky was edited on the wrong mod page because the script ran before the navigation finished (nexus-media, browser, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Saving Sprint or Sneak for Controller's 1.1.0 sticky overwrote Simple Dodge's sticky with Sprint or Sneak's text; the script reported success ("done 179662917" - Simple Dodge's comment id).
**Cause.** A browser_batch ran navigate (to page 198488) then a script that waited a fixed 4 s and took the first comment containing "Recent changes". The tab was still showing the previous page (198824), so the script found and edited that page's sticky.
**Fix.** The Simple Dodge sticky was re-edited with its own text (checked on a fresh load), then Sprint or Sneak's was edited with a guard on the page address; both read back STICKY + LOCKED with the right text.
**Root cause:** the page-editing script trusted that the tab was on the page it had just asked for, and picked its target by content that exists on every mod page.
**Rule.** Every script that edits a page's content first asserts location.pathname holds the intended mod id (throw if not) and targets the post by its known comment id; read the edited post back on a fresh load of THAT page before moving on.

## The same full-package install reverted the hand-smoothed world maps a second time, a day after it was caught and logged (World Map Render, 2026-11-10, found 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** The owner, 2026-11-12: Dayspring Canyon had its rectangular block at the left edge back, and the dark straight trenches were back in the seas. Every picture in `test World Map Render 1.0.0` equalled the package in `7. current test builds` (11-05 02:3x-02:48), none the hand-smoothed `C:\Builds\worldmap-render\stage\data` set installed 11-05 19:31; `WorldMapRenderTiles.txt` had been moved out to `_install-backups\test World Map Render 1.0.0\20261110-054506`.
**Cause.** On 2026-11-10 05:45 the no-weather DLL (418d4f0) was installed with a plain `install-test-build.py "<package>" "test World Map Render 1.0.0"` - the same full install that had reverted the maps on 11-09 07:50 (entry above, restored by hand that time). The package is still built from the repo `dist`, which never received the stage pictures, and the 11-09 entry's rule (back up or refuse a newer installed file; a machine-read DLL-only flag) was written but never built.
**Fix.** `install-test-build.py` now REFUSES when a package file would replace a mod-folder copy that is newer than the package's and has other bytes (DLL/PDB and settings INIs exempt; `--replace-newer` backs them up first); test `scripts\tests\test_install_newer_files.py`. The good set is committed and tagged `good-2026-11-05` in the local repo `6. current wip mods\WorldMapRender-Textures`, and build_maps.py / retouch.py now commit every finished build there (`tools\snapshot_textures.py`).
**Root cause:** a lesson recorded as a rule in prose, with no gate built, does not stop the next run - the same session repeated it the next morning.
**Rule.** When a past-mistakes entry ends in a "the tool should refuse..." rule, build the refusal the same day (rule: close loops with gate rules); and a build's newer data goes into the source the package is made from (the repo dist), never only into an install.
Topics: worldmaprender, map, install, packaging, mo2, testing.


## A "first look" built from a re-texture and from block-outs was rejected as low effort (visual design, engraving, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** The owner rejected both first-look sheets (06:12): the arrow and quiver directions "look like you just copied the arrows and quiver from the game and recolored it with a bit of flair for the weave. It looks really bad, and you should do better"; the Ysgramor armour block-outs "look like trash. It looks nothing like the in-game mesh. It's supposed to roughly look like the statue."
**Cause.** Both helpers were briefed for a cheap "look" and took the cheapest route: the quiver directions re-painted the vanilla meshes with the set's painter; the armour was primitive block-out shapes on a body form with carving painted on, never compared with the statue the armour is meant to follow.
**Fix.** Redone: the arrow, quiver and spear as original designs modelled from scratch in the set's language, distinctly different from vanilla; the armour started from an exact copy of the in-game Ysgramor statue mesh loaded in the same Blender scene as the reference, and worked from there.
**Root cause:** "look only, no build" was read as "low effort"; and a design meant to match an existing object was started without that object in the scene.
**Rule.** A design look for the owner is real modelling at the quality of the approved set, never a re-texture of vanilla or a primitive block-out. New items are designed from scratch and must read as distinctly ours. A design that must resemble an existing object (a statue, a vanilla piece) starts from an exact copy of that object's mesh loaded as the reference in the same scene (Bethesda permits modding its content), and every view is compared against it before the owner sees it.

## A Sketchfab reupload reported as "uploaded and processing" was never live - it waited for an approval click (Truly Nordic 1.1.0, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** After the rev2 reupload, the public API kept showing the first version (updatedAt unchanged, monitor `geometry.tangent_fallback_generated`), and the owner still saw the old smeared model about an hour later.
**Cause.** Sketchfab processes a reupload as a candidate version. The model page then shows "Reupload is almost finished - please review the new version", and nothing changes until "Choose reuploaded model" is clicked on `/3d-models/<uid>/compare`. Clicking REUPLOAD MODEL looked like the last step.
**Fix.** Opened Check model, waited for the candidate to load, checked it and approved it; the monitors then read `tangent.provided`.
**Root cause:** the upload note's steps ended at "wait for processing" and never named the approval, and completion was judged by the upload, not by reading the live model back.
**Rule.** A reupload is done only when the public API's monitors or file version show the NEW file (here `tangent.provided`). After processing, open the model page, and if it says "Reupload is almost finished", approve it on the compare page.

## A scripted text insert doubled the whole to-do list because str.find returned -1 (to-do list edit, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** An insert into an existing to-do entry left the 1.1 MB file at 2.2 MB: a second copy of the file, minus its first 29 characters, after the new text.
**Cause.** The script looked for the entry's closing text with the Python string-literal quote still attached (`...2026-11-12.")`), which is not in the file, so `find` returned -1. `s[:j] + new + s[j+n:]` with j = -1 keeps everything except the last character, then appends nearly all of the file again. The script didn't check j, so it reported "updated".
**Fix.** Rebuilt the original exactly from the doubled file, with two assertions that the layout matched, then applied the insert at the right place.
**Root cause:** text edits by index with no guard on the index, and no size check on the result.
**Rule.** Every scripted insert or replace by position checks that the index is >= 0 and refuses otherwise, and compares the new length with the old length plus the inserted text before writing. Prefer an exact-string replace that must match exactly once.

## A reply draft claimed eight first-person dodges because the eight event names were in the first-person graph (Simple Dodge reply, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** The draft told a player Simple Dodge gives eight-way step dodges in first person. The Fable review found that first person has four distinct dodges, one fixed clip each, and no step/roll choice.
**Cause.** I grepped the first-person behaviour patch for the event names, found all eight TKDodge* events, and read their presence as eight dodges. In the graph, the diagonal events transition into the Forward and Back states. FirstPerson~1 has only the four straight motions, there's no iStepSelector, and the 8-way report said so in plain words.
**Fix.** Rewrote the reply from the transitions, the clip list and the report. Added a to-do entry for true first-person diagonals.
**Root cause:** a capability claim was checked against the names a system accepts, not against where each name leads. The mod's own design report wasn't read before the claim.
**Rule.** Before telling anyone a behaviour graph supports something, follow each event to its state and clip (toStateId / toNestedStateId, the .hkx it plays, the selector variables), and read the mod's own patch report. An event that is accepted is not one that has its own animation.

## Copying the game's state writes is not enough - the game refreshes the HUD after its setter, not inside it (Sprint or Sneak for Controller 1.1.0, 2026-11-12)

**What happened.** A player reported the sneak eye staying on screen after standing up with our mod (Contextual Crosshair
hid it). The mod's SetSneaking made the same state writes as the game's own sneak setter, so the player really stood up -
but the eye (HUD StealthMeter) is shown and hidden only by the kCrosshairSneak HUD message, sent by the game's stealth
update, which the per-frame player update runs only WHILE the sneaking bit is set. The game's own sneak changes send the
"hide" refresh themselves, straight after the setter; the mod's stand-up skipped it, so nothing ever hid the eye.

**Root cause:** "Same writes as the game's setter" was taken as "same behaviour as the game", when the game's effect on the
HUD lives in the callers after the setter. A symptom only on screen while the game behaves correctly was a HUD-update gap.

**Do instead.** When a mod sets an actor state directly (sneaking, swimming, sitting), find every caller of the game's own
setter in the code dump and copy what they do after it - here, post the hide message (1.1.1, include\StealthMeter.h). A
HUD element refreshed from the frame loop only during a state never clears itself when the state ends. Topics: sneak,
hud, skse, controller.

## A "DevBench" folder name does not make code test-only, and a bound on a read value does not protect the pointer read (Perfected Wheeler 1.7.0, 2026-11-12)

**What happened.** A Dragonslayer AE (1.6.1170) player crashed in wheeler.dll [source reference removed], code under
src\bin\DevBench\. It looked test-only, but the gameplay D-pad hold-to-toggle tap replay (on by default) reused the
injector. It read ControlMap->contextPriorityStack directly at SE's [value removed]; from 1.6.1130 the field is at [value removed], so the
link count ([value removed]) was read as the pointer and the capacity (10) as the size - the guard "depth <= 64" passed. The gate row
that forbids such reads (runtime-data-members-through-the-accessor) had never matched a file: its marker looked only in
vcpkg.json and its path class [\/] missed Windows paths.

**Root cause:** The folder name was trusted over the callers; the layout of the compiling CommonLib checkout was baked in
and only ever tested on 1.5.97; and a gate row was trusted without a test proving it fails real offending source.

**Do instead.** Check every caller of "test" code before calling it inert. Read runtime-data members through the versioned
accessor, and check pointer, size against capacity, then depth (Wheeler 1.7.1 ContextStackRead.h). Every gate row needs a
test that it FAILS a real offender (gate-rules 1.0.38, test_runtime_data_accessor_row.py). Compare crash register values
with the running game's struct layout before suspecting threads or other mods. Also: MSVC 14.51 -> 14.52 breaks cached
build trees; reconfigure with cmake --fresh. Topics: wheeler, devbench, commonlib, gates, crash, build.

## A texture check that matched an old path prefix passed while checking nothing (Truly Nordic verify.py / build-packages.py, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** verify.py and build-packages.py reported PASS on Truly Nordic 1.1.0 and 1.1.1, but they had checked none of
our textures. Found during the 1.1.2 ring pass.
**Cause.** Both matched texture paths on the old `textures\pbr\apocryphatest` prefix. The 1.1.0 rename moved every texture
to the TrulyNordic prefix, so the filter selected zero files, and "0 problems in 0 files" printed as a pass.
**Fix.** Repo commit 99b4e53: the prefix now comes from the shipped paths, and the check fails when it selects zero files.
**Root cause:** a check that filters its input by a hard-coded path never states how many items it actually inspected, so an
empty selection looks the same as a clean one. A rename changed the input and no check noticed.
**Rule.** Every verifier prints how many items it checked and FAILS on zero. When a mod's paths are renamed, grep its tools
for the old prefix in the same pass.

## A measuring script given "--nif NAME" silently measured the first NIF in the folder (surface_profile_measure.py, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Surface-profile numbers for a named NIF were really the numbers for another NIF in the same folder.
**Cause.** The script reads `--nif=NAME` only. With a space, the value is not taken and it falls back to the first NIF.
**Fix.** Always pass `--nif=NAME`.
**Root cause:** a hand-rolled argument parser that ignores what it cannot read, instead of refusing it.
**Rule.** A script that falls back to a default when an argument was given but not understood must refuse instead. Read the
measured file's name back in the output before trusting the numbers.

## KID creates an unresolved keyword EditorID instead of skipping the line (Truly Nordic spear KID ini, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** The spear plan assumed a KID line naming a keyword from a mod that is not installed would simply be skipped.
**Cause.** Per the KID reference, an EditorID keyword that does not resolve is created as a new empty keyword. That is
harmless for our spear, but a plan relying on "skipped" has the mechanism wrong, and an animation pack checking by
FormID will not see the created keyword.
**Fix.** No change needed for the spear. At its first test, read po3_KeywordItemDistributor.log for each keyword line.
**Root cause:** the behaviour of a distributor on a missing form was assumed, not read from its reference.
**Rule.** Before relying on how SPID / KID / SkyPatcher treat a missing form, read the reference section for it, and check
the distributor's log at the first test.

## Re-running an old painter on today's libraries changed pixels outside the face being repainted (Truly Nordic ring pass, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Repainting only the sheath lockets also changed the chapes.
**Cause.** The shared paint libraries had moved on since the shipped maps were made, so a full re-run repainted everything
slightly differently. Separately, the `_sf` work folders hold a different dump.npz from the paint dump.
**Fix.** Copy the shipped maps back everywhere outside the repainted face plus 25 px, and prove 0 px differ there. Repaint
from the non-sf folder's dump.
**Root cause:** a repaint was treated as a local edit when the tool regenerates the whole map from current code.
**Rule.** A targeted repaint is proven by a pixel diff against the shipped map outside the target region (0 px), not by
eye.

## "Our code never calls it" came from a grep that skipped the headers (Simple Dodge, Perk Entry Point Extender report, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** I told the owner Simple Dodge never calls Perk Entry Point Extender, so a user's error could not be ours. The
user's own log then showed our DLL printing "[critical] PerkEntryPointExtender.dll not found" on every dodge.
**Cause.** I grepped the .cpp files for the API namespace. The call lives in an inline helper inside the vendored header
(HandleEntryPoint in API/PerkEntryPointExtenderAPI.h), and dodging.cpp calls it as RE::HandleEntryPoint, so the namespace
never appeared in the .cpp. I also answered before reading the user's log.
**Fix.** Read the report's log first: the exact message text, grepped across src including headers, found the source at once.
The dependency is optional; the fix is to look it up once and log one info line.
**Root cause:** a claim of absence was made from a search narrower than the code that runs (headers excluded), and the
primary evidence (the user's log) was not read before answering.
**Rule.** Before saying "not our issue", read the reporter's log and grep the exact error text across ALL source, headers
and vendored code included. A claim that something never happens needs a search as wide as the binary.

## Behaviour nodes copied to another graph carry that graph's hard-coded event and variable numbers (Simple Dodge 1.2.0 sheathed dodge, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Simple Dodge dodged only with a weapon drawn. With weapons sheathed, the DLL sent the dodge every frame for
the whole input-buffer window and nothing played.
**Cause.** The dodge patch existed only in 1hm_behavior and magicbehavior. While sheathed, 0_master runs MT_Behavior,
which had no dodge state, so the event went nowhere and nothing cleared the buffer. Copying the 1hm nodes into mt is not
enough: clip triggers, notify events and variable bindings hold vanilla numbers that differ per graph (FootLeft 21 in 1hm,
35 in mt), and one exit used iWantBlock, which mt does not have.
**Fix.** patch_sheathed.py generates the mt patch from the 1hm one, renumbering every event and variable by name and
failing on a name the target lacks. The vanilla node IDs came offline from Nemesis's cached_behaviors through hkxcmd,
checked against TUDM's mt patch. The build was verified by counting names in the 64-bit output, which hkxcmd cannot read.
A refusal the buffer can't change (weapon sheathed, setting off) now clears the buffer.
**Root cause:** the patch was written for the graphs the original mod covered, and nobody listed which graph runs in each
player state, so "dodge" was never tested sheathed.
**Rule.** For a behaviour feature, list the graph for every player state (sheathed, drawn, magic, first person, mounted,
swimming) and say which ones the patch covers. Nodes copied between graphs get every numeric event and variable
reference renumbered by name. An input buffer clears on a refusal waiting won't fix.

## The packager copied only fomod/info.xml, so a new installer choice never reached the package (Simple Dodge 1.2.0, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Simple Dodge 1.2.0 added an installer step ("Step distance") as fomod/ModuleConfig.xml plus a
fomod-options/Step-Shorter folder in the repo. The packaging script would have shipped neither.
**Cause.** package-mod.ps1 copies a repo's fomod/info.xml only. Until now the installer XML had always been written by
hand straight into the package, so nothing noticed the gap.
**Fix.** The packager now copies fomod/ModuleConfig.xml and fomod-options/**. A gate row fails packaging when the repo
has a ModuleConfig.xml that the package lacks.
**Root cause:** packaging copied a fixed list of files, and no check compared what the repo ships against what the
package holds.
**Rule.** A packager copies by the repo's declared layout, not a fixed list. A gate compares the repo's shipped
folders with the package.

## An IK knee aim set in the foot's frame follows a turned-out foot outward (Simple Dodge step rework, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** On landing, the step dodges' knees pointed outward or locked straight. One diagonal landed with 0.6 degrees
of knee flexion.
**Cause.** The knee pole was aimed from the foot's forward, so a turned-out rear foot swung the knee out with it. Laying
a side dodge onto a diagonal also added the stance's fore-aft offset, which stretched the lead leg to full length.
**Fix.** Aim the landing knee from the hips' forward, in toward the centre line. Carry the body lower and further at
landing, and check leg stretch on every frame.
**Root cause:** the knee aim was set in the wrong reference frame, and nothing measured knee flexion or leg stretch per
frame.
**Rule.** Aim knees from the pelvis frame. Measure knee flexion, knee direction and leg stretch on every frame of a
generated clip before calling it done.

## A low-priority OAR weapon set loses to any combat overhaul replacing the same clip names (Simple Dodge 1.2.0 bow, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** In the 1.2.0 test, every weapon type played its new grounded step except the bow. With a bow drawn, the back,
left and right dodges played airborne flips; forward was correct. The DLL log still said "Dodge: step (iStep 2)".
**Cause.** Bow Rapid Combo V3's OAR submod "Base 2" (priority 9901001, weapon drawn and bow equipped) replaces
[asset path removed] with flip clips. It ships no Forward or diagonal files. Our Bow set sits at priority
115 on purpose, so it lost.
**Fix.** Simple Dodge keeps its low priority. The README names the conflict, and an optional compat user.json raises our
Bow set above it for players who want ours. The owner decides whether to ship it high by default.
**Root cause:** the test ran before anyone listed which other mods in the profile replace the same clip names under the
same conditions, so a known-shape conflict was found in game rather than on disk.
**Rule.** Before testing an OAR or DAR set, sweep the profile for every file replacing its clip names
(housecarl_asset_status under= the OAR and DAR trees) and list the winners. A direction pattern (forward fine, three
others wrong) points at a pack that ships only some of the names.

## Shading patches on a large face came from base-colour grime sized to the atlas, not from normals (Truly Nordic shields, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** The owner saw dark and light patches across both shields' whole surface.
**Cause.** tn_knot.maps_v3 paints "patina" grime as a 7x7-cell noise across the whole 2048 atlas. On a 50-unit dome that
becomes blotches about 7 units wide, with the base colour swinging roughly 2x. The board's leather patches and plank tone
added to it. Normals and the normal map looked like the suspects, but they weren't.
**Fix.** A render matrix of the shipped NIFs with one map switched off at a time measured the patch strength. Mesh-only
rendering came out at 0.006, flat base colour at 0.012, and shipped at 0.14, so the cause was the base colour alone. The
shield painters now set GRIME 0 and soften the plank tone, which brings it to 0.058. The height maps, normal maps and
meshes are byte-identical, so the carving is untouched.
**Root cause:** a texture effect was sized in atlas pixels instead of model units, and no check looked at how base colour
varies over a large face.
**Rule.** For a "patchy shading" report, render with one map off at a time and measure before changing anything. Size
procedural texture noise in model units. Gate candidate: fail a large face whose low-passed base colour varies by more
than about 10% of its mean. Every other item still carries full-strength grime.

## A batch's profile restore put the old mod back but left Pandora's output built for the new one (combined runs, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** In batch B-20261112-191855-3b1e (Knock and Truly Nordic) the player could not sit, could not dismount, and
never showed a drawn bow, vanilla bows included, on two saves. The Truly Nordic steps were blocked and the fault looked
like a Truly Nordic or Simple Dodge bug.
**Cause.** Batch d389 installed Simple Dodge 1.2.0 and re-ran Pandora, so Pandora Output was built with 1.2.0's new
mt_behavior patch. Its `combined-run finish` restored modlist.txt, which ticks 1.1.0 again, but Pandora Output is a
generated folder outside the profile backup, so it still carried 1.2.0's graphs. The next batch ran 1.1.0's files under
1.2.0's behaviour graphs: states pointing at clips and OAR sets that were not installed.
**Fix.** Before testing again: either keep the build that Pandora was generated from ticked, or re-run Pandora after the
restore. Re-run the blocked steps after a control check (sit, dismount, draw a vanilla bow).
**Root cause:** the profile restore treats a generated output (Pandora / Nemesis) as if it were not part of the state it
restores, and no launch gate compares the output with the patches that are enabled now.
**Rule.** A launch gate must fail when Pandora Output was generated from a different set of patch files than the ones
enabled now (record the patch files' hashes at each Pandora run; compare at launch). `combined-run finish` re-runs
Pandora, or marks the output stale, whenever a batch changed a behaviour patch. Every run starts with a control: sit,
mount and dismount, draw a vanilla bow.
**Gate (built 2026-11-12, same day).** Role `pandora-run` is now the one way to run Pandora (active-patches fix, Pandora through mo2-launch with `--auto_run --auto_close`, Engine.log check, then role `pandora-stamp`, which writes `Pandora Output\_pandora-stamp.json`); `pandora-output-fresh-gate.py` (game-relaunch, after the active-patches gate) refuses while the enabled patch files differ from the stamp; `combined-run finish` marks the output stale (`_pandora-stale.json`) when its restore changes the patches and there is no stamp. gate-rules row `pandora-output-matches-enabled-patches`; test `scripts\tests\test_pandora_output_fresh_gate.py`. The live Njordlinger output (18:24, carries 1.2.0's SDGChainRoll, 1.1.0 ticked) was marked stale by hand the same evening.

## A two-handed grip solved at the hand bone left the palm 14 units off the shaft (Simple Dodge polearm sets, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** The owner saw the hands not lining up on the pike and quarterstaff dodges.
**Cause.** The arm IK aimed the hand bone at a point offset by the rest-pose palm vector, and the hand kept the forearm's
rotation. So the left palm missed the shaft by up to 14 units, and both grips were turned 46-88 degrees across it. The
earlier reach and clearance checks passed, because neither measured contact.
**Fix.** Turn each hand until its own grip node (the right Weapon node, the left Shield node) lines up with the weapon,
then put the wrist where that node lands. check_grip_contact.py fails a grip more than 1 unit or 15 degrees off, in any
frame, and checks sets copied from vanilla idles against that idle's own hand-to-weapon relation.
**Root cause:** the checks measured what was easy (reach, clearance), not the property the owner sees (hand on weapon),
and they measured at the hand bone rather than the attachment node.
**Rule.** Grip contact is measured at the node the game attaches the weapon to in that hand, every frame. A finger-centroid
measure reads 2 units and 15 degrees off even on correct vanilla grips.

## Pandora dropped a patch's new nodes over one invalid enum value, still listed the mod as built, and the save crashed (Simple Dodge 1.2.0 chain patch, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Round 2 of the Simple Dodge 1.2.0 test crashed loading a save, in MT_RootBehavior's transitions. Pandora's
Engine.log still listed "Simple Dodge" as built.
**Cause.** The step-to-roll chain patch set selfTransitionMode = SELF_TRANSITION_MODE_BLEND on 6 hkbStateMachine objects.
BLEND is a transition-effect value, not a state-machine one. Pandora logged 6 enum errors and dropped every NEW node the
patch adds (SimpleDodgeState and the clips), along with other mods' new states in the same graphs, then wrote the output
anyway. The offline proof had used Nemesis and counted event names, which survive when every new node is dropped.
**Fix.** The 6 objects go back to NO_TRANSITION, and the chain re-entry uses a valid mechanism. Three checks were added: a
patch check on enum values (behavior-patch-enum-gate), pandora-run failing on any dropped-node or enum-error line in
Engine.log, and an output check for a new node name.
**Root cause:** an offline build with the other engine was taken as proof, the success line was taken at its word, and the
output check counted names that survive even when the patch's new nodes are dropped.
**Rule.** Validate a behaviour patch with the engine the player list uses. Treat any error line in its log as a failure,
whatever the summary says. Prove the output by a NEW node's name, not an event's. Also: Git Bash `sed -i` strips CRLF from
MO2's modlist.txt; edit MO2 files with Python byte replaces. And in a shared repo, commit with a pathspec
(`git commit -- <file>`) so one session's commit never sweeps up another's staged work.

## Amendment: a fresh Pandora output did not bring back the player's sitting, so stale output was not the whole cause (combined runs, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** In batch B-20261112-204654-4a40 the player still could not sit (GetSitState 0, while NPCs in the same cell
sat). This was with a freshly stamped Pandora output that matched every enabled patch, on a save from before any 1.2.0
batch. Mount, dismount and drawing a bow worked.
**Cause.** Not yet known. The earlier entry's stale output explains that batch's dismount and bow failures, but not the
no-sit. A falsification run (current 1.1.0 profile, then 1.2.0 with its DLL hidden, then 1.2.0 whole) is under way.
Saves made during batch 3b1e carry stuck state (Papyrus Dismount fails), so they are not to be used for controls.
**Fix.** Pending the falsification run.
**Root cause:** one plausible cause was found and assumed to cover every symptom, without re-running the symptom on a
build that had that cause removed.
**Rule.** After a fix, re-run the original symptom before saying it is explained. Never call a symptom covered because
another symptom from the same run was. Two pipeline gaps from the same run, both to fix: pandora-run, run outside a
batch, leaves its instance lock held after MO2 closes; and the test profile's own load order had two plugins after
DynDOLOD.esp, which every launch audit refused until it was corrected.

## "The player never sits" was a sit that started and ended inside the poll interval (combined runs, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** Batches 3b1e and 4a40 reported the player could not sit: GetSitState read 0 after 8 s and 14 s. In batch
9256 (every activation-path suspect disabled, new game) the same chair, polled every 0.25 s, read furniture set, sit
state 2 for about 2 s, then 4 (wants to stand), then 0 - the clip shows the player sitting down and standing straight
back up. Grindstone, anvil and alchemy lab opened their Crafting Menu and closed it again within 2 s; the workbench stayed
open. Papyrus Activate failed the same way, so "script Activate works" was not true either.
**Cause.** Not yet known (something ends the furniture state right after entry; the E-key path and the suspects are
cleared). The wrong framing came from sampling the end state only: a read 8 s after the press cannot tell "never
entered" from "entered and was thrown out".
**Root cause:** a transient was judged from a late single sample, and a control ("Papyrus Activate works") was carried
forward without being re-measured the same way.
**Rule.** For any furniture, menu or animation-state test, poll the state at 4 Hz or faster from the press for at least
10 s, and record a clip; report the full state sequence (0 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 0), not one value. Re-run a control with the
same measurement before quoting it as a contrast.

## The player's furniture exit came from code, not from an animation replacer - the graph-event log settled it in one run (combined runs, 2026-11-12)

**Symptom.** The player sits (sit state 2) and is stood up again; crafting menus open and close themselves; the armor
workbench is the one station that keeps him. The offline sweep found a neat player-only suspect: Crafting Camera Fix, an
OAR set conditioned on IsActorBase 7 and on exactly the failing stations' keywords, excluding the workbench.
**Cause.** Not yet found, but not an animation. Furniture Activation Guard's graph-notify log (batch
B-20261112-230355-9651) showed the exit event SENT TO the player's graph by the engine's stand path (sit state 4, then
idleChairRightExit or IdleChairExitStart) 20-150 ms after the graph reported the seated idle, with no clip emitting an
end event first. Disabling Crafting Camera Fix, No Furniture Camera, Camera Persistence Fixes, and then the two RowRim
boat DLLs changed nothing; disabling the player's movement controls changed nothing. Separately, the first activation of
a chair after every coc never reached TESFurniture::Activate (outermost hook: SureOfStealing.dll).
**Root cause:** a keyword match between a replacer's conditions and the failing set looked like an explanation; it said
nothing about who sends the exit.
**Rule.** For an "animation ends early" fault, log the events going into AND out of the actor's graph before naming a
replacer: an exit emitted by a clip points at a replacer or behaviour patch, an exit sent into the graph points at code
(the engine's stand path called by a plugin or script). Next step for this fault: bisect the SKSE layer with the guard's
attempt outcome as the observer.

## A trace's "culprit" was the outermost hook on the player's update, not the code that stood the player up (combined runs, 2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** TestBench's new trace named [offset removed] as the culprit for the player's sit state going 3 -> 4
one frame after sitting. Earlier the same night ValhallaCombat.dll was the suspect, because it owned the player's
Update, NotifyAnimationGraph and animation event sink.
**Cause.** Not found yet, but not a plugin calling the stand. In batch B-20261112-233955-7132, hiding ValhallaCombat.dll,
SureOfStealing.dll, Onward.dll or DynamicWind.dll left the chair failing the same way each time. The trace stack shows
DoSetSitSleepState(4) called by engine code only (SkyrimSE ids [id chain removed] <-
39375, PlayerCharacter::Update). Every frame above 39375 is the chain of plugins hooking that update, and the "culprit"
field is just the outermost of them. The engine decides to stand from state that something wrote earlier. moveStart is
sent with every exit, which points at a movement request or AI state on the player.
Separately, with Sure of Stealing hidden, the first activation after a coc reached the furniture. In the four launches
with it on, it never did.
**Fix.** Still open. The next trace has to watch what 38606 reads before it calls 38835: the player's movement input,
the AI-driven flag, the movement controller. Then hide whatever writes it.
**Root cause:** a heuristic culprit (the first non-engine frame) was read as an attribution. A hook chain on a per-frame
function puts every hooking plugin on every stack under it.
**Rule.** Read a trace stack from the write upward. A plugin is the caller only if its frame sits BETWEEN the write and
the nearest engine per-frame function. Frames above that function are the hook chain and say nothing. Also:
`combined-run with` strips the launch ticket, so a bisect has to run under `combined-run launch`. bisect-profile.ps1
discards the launcher's output, so give it a logging -Launcher wrapper. A bisect observer must not expect RaceMenu after
StartNewGame, because half the DLLs off can take ShowRaceMenu with them.

## The player's furniture stand-up was our own test tool: TestBench.esp gives the player an AI package from game start (combined runs, 2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** In every Njordlinger Test run the player sat (sit state 3) and was stood up one frame later (3 -> 4,
idleChairRightExit, moveStart); crafting stations closed themselves. NPCs were fine. Hiding Valhalla, Sure of Stealing,
Onward, DynamicWind, camera and activation mods changed nothing, and the trace put the decision inside the engine's
PlayerCharacter::Update.
**Cause.** TestBench.esp's AutoCombatRunQuest ([id removed]) is Start Game Enabled and forces the player into an alias that
carries AutoCombatRunPackage ([id removed], a Travel package with no conditions). When the walk-to-furniture package ends at
sit 3, the engine evaluates the player's package, finds that Travel package, and pushes its GetUpFromChairBed package.
The AI package dispatcher (SE [id removed]) maps procedure GetUpFromChairBed, step 0, to action [value removed], which calls the stand-up
routine 38835. Proof (batch B-20261113-004011-a582): with the quest stopped the player stayed seated; with it started
again the stand came back. Movement input read exactly zero throughout (episode 134 killed, 135 survived).
**Fix.** Done 2026-11-13. TestBench.esp: Start Game Enabled cleared on AutoCombatRunQuest (DNAM flags [value removed] -> [value removed],
one byte; nothing else changed). TestBench.dll: playerbot starts the quest for travel / engage / flee and stops it when
the order ends, on `stop`, and after a load if an old save still has it running. Gate row
`harness-plugin-puts-no-package-on-the-player` (test-bench-gate.py check 2) refuses a launch if the flag comes back.
Proved in batch B-20261113-010622-0e47: on a fresh new game the quest stays stopped with nobody stopping it, the chair
holds sit 3 for 14.5 s, and the grindstone and anvil menus stay open; a travel order runs the quest only for its 4 s.
Gotcha found on the way: CommonLib's `TESQuest::IsRunning()` is "not stopping and no start pending", so it is TRUE for a
quest that was never started (Papyrus `Quest.IsRunning` said false at the same moment). The first build used it and
logged a stop that never happened, and it would never have started the quest for a travel order. Decide "running" with
`IsEnabled()` (the kEnabled flag), which is what Papyrus reads.
**Root cause:** the test tool was never treated as a suspect. Every bisect and hide kept TestBench, because it is the
observer, and nobody asked what state its plugin puts on the player.
**Rule.** When a player-only fault survives hiding every suspect, read the player's live AI state (current and runOnce
package, alias packages) before bisecting further. Treat the test harness's own plugin as a suspect like any other:
a Start Game Enabled quest with an alias on the player changes the player's behaviour in every test. Reading the engine
from the outside works: the on-disk SkyrimSE.exe is SteamStub-encrypted, so dump .text from the running process and
read it with the Address Library ids.

## A Sketchfab reupload kept the 1.0.0 materials by name - ten pieces showed old textures on new UVs, "defaced" and blurry (Truly Nordic 1.2.0, sketchfab, nexus-media, 2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** After the 1.2.0 reupload processed and was approved (face count matched the GLB, monitors read
`tangent.provided`), the owner opened the live model on his phone: every piece except the clean shield, the straight
sword and the spear had no engraving and looked blurry. The nif-vs-glb proof of the uploaded GLB showed the carving on
every piece, and the first thumbnail was the old 16-piece row.
**Cause.** Sketchfab keeps material settings saved in its 3D editor and re-applies them BY MATERIAL NAME on every
reupload. The 1.0.0 upload had its materials saved in the editor (when the environment brightness was set), so the ten
materials that existed in 1.0.0 (curved sword, war axe, both maces, dagger, battleaxe, greatsword, warhammer, bow, carved
shield) kept pointing at 1.0.0's textures: their normals were `.png` (1.2.0 ships only JPEG), their texture indices
matched the 1.0.0 file's image order, and not one of 1.2.0's textures for those materials existed in the model's
texture library. 1.0.0 textures on the reshaped 1.2.0 UVs read as smears. Materials new since 1.0.0 (straight sword,
clean shield, sheaths, spear, quiver, arrow) were built from the file and were right - exactly the owner's list. The
1.1.0 smears were very likely the same fault.
**Fix.** build_glb.py names every material `v<version> <piece> - <part>`, so no reupload can match a saved material;
re-uploaded (rev2) and checked the live materials with sketchfab_live_check.js (every channel's texture comes from this
upload's images, none from an older file).
**Root cause:** "done" was judged from the file (proof renders, face count, monitors) and Sketchfab's preview, not from
what the live model's materials point at. A reupload is a merge with saved editor state, not a file swap.
**Rule.** A Sketchfab upload is done only when the LIVE model has been checked per material after processing: run
assets\sketchfab\sketchfab_live_check.js in a signed-in sketchfab.com tab (it reads /i/models/<uid>/options and
/textures and fails when any material's albedo, normal or ORM channel points at a texture whose name is not one of the
uploaded GLB's images, or a channel is off), then look at carving on every piece in the live viewer at HD. Never save
materials in Sketchfab's 3D editor; set only scene settings (environment, camera) there.

## A proof that applied the same rotation as the export could not catch the export's wrong rotation (Truly Nordic Sketchfab GLB, quiver, 2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** On the live Sketchfab model the quiver showed a plain brushed-steel box: no carved collar plate, braided spine
or foot plate. The owner said it did not look right. The game NIF was correct.
**Cause.** build_glb.py stood the quiver up with a -90 degree turn about X (its mouth is at -Y). That also swings the
NIF's +Z face, the design's front carrying the plate, to the back. proof_closeups.py applied the same turn to the NIF
before comparing, so it proved only "the GLB equals the turned NIF".
**Fix.** Pieces flipped end to end also spin 180 degrees about the vertical. The build stops if any non-shield piece's
NIF +Z does not face the front. The proof is checked against the design rig's own front (the plate close-up) from the
viewer's default camera.
**Root cause:** the check shared the transform it was meant to check, so it could never disagree with it.
**Rule.** Verify an export against an independent reference (the design rig, or a known front feature), never against
the input put through the same transform. When a live-viewer shot shows a part as missing, first say which side of the
piece the shot shows.

## TestBench advanceTime ran the game clock backwards, so time-based checks after a jump were invalid (Knock 1.3.2 test, 2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** In batch c03f, after TestBench `game advanceTime` the game time went 0.677 to 1.963 to 0.549, running
backwards. Knock's night refusal still looked under an hour old the next day, so the day let-in step failed for a reason
that had nothing to do with Knock.
**Cause.** TestBench's advanceTime corrupts GameDaysPassed. Our test briefs had told testers to prefer it over
`set gamehour`, because that one could also move the clock back.
**Fix.** The run reset Knock's refusal through its own control op. TestBench's advanceTime needs fixing before it is
trusted. Other test-harness traps from the same run: opening InventoryMenu through TestBench's menu tool crashes in
Scaleform (use real Tab, then Items); TestBench `wait` with its autosave crashed in usvfs; `setav speech` does nothing in
this profile (use speechcraft); Game.GetCurrentCrosshairRef always returns None here.
**Root cause:** a harness tool that changes game time was never checked for the property tests depend on (monotonic
GameDaysPassed) before being written into briefs as the safe way.
**Rule.** Before a time-dependent step, read GameDaysPassed before and after the jump and refuse the step if it didn't
increase by the expected amount. A harness tool goes into a brief as "the way" only after its effect has been measured.

## A packaging gate started Pandora's window over the owner's game (pandora-patch-builds gate, 2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** While the owner was playing, "Something keeps on pulling up Pandora."
**Cause.** The gate row pandora-patch-builds-with-its-new-nodes builds each patch with a private Pandora copy, and it runs
inside package-mod. A helper packaging Simple Dodge triggered it twice. Pandora is a single-file Avalonia app with no
headless option, and it shows its window even when started minimised with no focus.
**Fix.** No Pandora runs while a game process is running. Proposed: run it on a private Win32 desktop (CreateDesktop
plus STARTUPINFO.lpDesktop), so its window can never reach the owner's screen. That still needs one trial run.
**Root cause:** a gate was built around a GUI tool without asking whose screen it would appear on, and packaging was
treated as screen-free work.
**Rule.** Any pipeline step that starts a GUI program must either run on a private desktop or refuse while the owner's
game or screen is in use. Check that before wiring it into packaging. Related: with AMR, a clip's own animmotion
annotations decide distance and animationdatasinglefile is ignored, so a distance check must read the clips.

## A sheath designed and approved off the body was buried in the owner's armour at the hip - nothing measured it on a body (Truly Nordic saber C2 / straight sheath v3, 2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** The owner, playing in Nordic carved armour: "The saber clips into the armor, hiding it a little". Every
design and review render of the saber and its sheath showed the weapon alone, never on a body in armour.
**Cause.** The weapon NIF hangs from XPMSSE's WeaponSword node. Its local -z points away from the thigh and +y runs down
the blade. Our grip and throat sat at z +0.67 like vanilla's bare Nordic blade, but our sheath and guard are bulkier at the
throat, so 9 two-unit slices (18 units of the weapon) were completely behind the Nordic carved cuirass from the side, against
6 for vanilla's steel sheath. The buried depth sum was 21.5 against 6.8. The lower sheath was clear; the clip was all at the
throat. A tilt about the grip barely moves the throat; only a shift outward does.
**Fix.** items.py 'hip' on the saber and the straight sword: the third-person NIF's shapes and collision hull are turned -4
degrees about x through the grip centre and moved 1.25 along -z (assemble.py hip_xf). The grip stays in the fist; its centre
goes from z +0.67 to -0.58. Nordic carved is now 6 slices with a depth sum of 6.0, Nord plate 1 slice with 0.8 (vanilla 1 and
1.5), and steel 0. The first-person NIF is unchanged. The measurement scripts and renders are in
set2\saber-hip-clearance-20261113.
**Root cause:** the sheath was judged as an object, not where it is worn. The armour it sits against was never in the check.
**Rule.** Any part worn on the body (sheath, quiver, shield on the back) is measured in its worn node on the XPMSSE skeleton
against a body and two or three bulky armours, compared slice by slice with a vanilla item in the same node, before approval.
Fix clearance with the shape transforms of the third-person NIF about the grip, never by moving the first-person NIF.
Topics: visual-design, nif, meshes, testing.


## A mod DLL flagged as malware right after a compiler update, with no code change behind it (Simple Dodge 1.2.0 / Knock 1.3.2 quarantined on Nexus, 2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** Nexus quarantined Simple Dodge 1.2.0 and Dynamic Simple Knock System SKSE 1.3.2 by its automated checks; a player reported the files flagged as malicious. On VirusTotal both DLLs (and their zips) showed 7-8 of ~71 detections, all one label, Gen:Variant.Ulise.617802, from the Bitdefender engine family (BitDefender, ALYac, Emsisoft, eScan, GData, VIPRE, Arcabit, CTX). nexus-upload.py reported the uploads "OK" because it checks the md5 and the primary version, never the quarantine state. A plain re-upload of the same zip was quarantined again.
**Cause.** Visual Studio 18 updated itself on 2026-11-12 06:41 (MSVC 14.51 -> 14.52.37025, the old toolset removed). Every DLL built after that with CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION ON (/GL + /LTCG) carries byte features the Bitdefender heuristic matches. Proven by a 2x2 on Knock 1.3.1's own (clean) source with 14.52: IPO on -> flagged at /O2 and /O1; IPO off -> 0/71 at both. Knock 1.3.1's shipped DLL, built with 14.51, stays clean on a fresh rescan. It looked like "something in our new code" because the first flagged builds were also new versions; the shared factor was the build date, not the source.
**Fix.** set(CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION OFF) in both repos (SimpleDodge 55dd264, DynamicSimpleKnock 7137085), rebuilt as Simple Dodge 1.3.0 / Knock 1.3.3, each DLL scanned on VirusTotal before posting. The GitHub release stays the download until Nexus releases the files.
**Root cause:** the pipeline treated the compiler as fixed: an automatic toolchain update changes every binary we ship, and nothing compared a new build's toolchain with the last released one or scanned a DLL before upload, and the upload tool did not read the quarantine state.
**Rule.** Gate row dll-built-without-ltcg refuses IPO/LTCG ON in a CommonLibSSE CMake repo. A DLL is scanned (VirusTotal hash lookup or upload) before it is posted, and nexus-upload must read the file's quarantine state after upload (to-do). When a whole batch of builds goes bad at once, compare the toolchain (PE Rich header / linker version) of the last good and first bad binary before reading code. 56 other CMake mods still set IPO ON - each gets it turned off at its next build (the gate forces it).


## A sed replacement holding a Windows path split the line and also hit an older line (Truly Nordic notes.txt, 2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** Marking notes.txt "saved live" with sed turned "assets\nexus-description-..." into a line break before "exus-..." and changed the 1.2 line as well as the 1.3 line, both of which ended "NOT yet saved live.".
**Cause.** In a sed replacement, `\n` (even written `\\n` inside a bash string) becomes a newline, so a Windows path starting with n is cut; and the match text was not unique in the file.
**Fix.** Restored by a Python script that asserted the bad text appeared exactly twice, put the 1.2 line back and joined the 1.3 line; a diff against the backup showed only the intended change.
**Root cause:** a text edit was made with a tool whose escape rules were not checked, on a match that was not checked for uniqueness.
**Rule.** Edit distro text files with a Python script that asserts [code removed] and writes with the file's own line endings; never put a Windows path in a sed replacement.

## Nexus media editor: the gallery order is not set through media/save, and the Sketchfab properties page locks on a set file input (2026-11-13)

**Symptom.** (1) Posting `imageIds` / `order` / `images` to `/api/flamework/mods/media/save` returned success but the gallery order did not change. (2) On Sketchfab's model properties page, setting the joined GLB zip on `#upfile` (and even a page-local file input that bubbled a change event) made the page say "You have unsaved changes, please save them before reuploading a model", and the tab then refused to close behind a "Leave site?" prompt.
**Cause.** (1) Nexus keeps the order in the editor's client store; it is written by the sortable list's `onDragEnd({active:{id}, over:{id}})` (ids are the tiles' backendId strings, React fiber about 12 levels above a tile `li`) and the page's own Save button. (2) `#upfile` belongs to the properties form; the reupload goes through the popup opened by `button[data-selenium="open-reupload-popup"]`, whose own input is `#input`.
**Fix.** (1) Call that `onDragEnd`, then click Save; verified after a reload (Truly Nordic: the two 1.2.0 banners first, new dagger and mace tiles in the old ones' places). (2) Load the parts in a page that is not the properties form (or keep the joined File in IndexedDB), open the reupload popup, set the File on `#input`, check the hash, click REUPLOAD MODEL.
**Root cause:** an API call that answered `{"success":true}` was taken as proof the change was made; the only proof is a reload showing it.
**Rule.** After any media-editor or Sketchfab change, reload and read the result back; reorder through the sortable's onDragEnd + Save; reupload through the popup's `#input`, never the form's `#upfile`.


## A test install that "read back equal to the package" laid the files out in the package's option folders (Nordic Ebony Armor and Weapons Replacer 1.1.0, 2026-11-14)

**Symptom.** install-test-build reported "installed 156 files ... read back: the mod folder equals the package", yet the mod folder held `00 Core\meshes\...`, `30 HIMBO meshes\...` and `fomod\` instead of `meshes\...`. PGPatcher, run next, found only the vanilla ebony bow and made a duplicate of it; an in-game test would have shown vanilla items.
**Cause.** The tool's FOMOD reader installs `Common\` (or the package root when there is no Common) plus the chosen options; this package's ModuleConfig names its required files `<requiredInstallFiles><folder source="00 Core"/>`, which the tool does not read, so it fell back to copying the package root verbatim - and its read-back compares the folder to that same root, so it passed.
**Fix.** Copied `00 Core\*` to the mod root by hand (the mis-laid copy kept in `_removed-20261114`), re-ran PGPatcher.
**Root cause:** the installer's read-back checks the copy against what it chose to copy, not against what a mod manager would install from the ModuleConfig; a package without a Common folder silently gets the wrong layout.
**Rule.** install-test-build must install `requiredInstallFiles` folders and refuse to fall back to the raw package root when a ModuleConfig exists; after any install, check that a known game path (meshes\, textures\, the plugin) sits at the mod root before PGPatcher or a launch.


## A part that rendered fine in Blender came out flat black in game (Ebony Wolf warhammer face, 2026-11-14)

**Symptom.** In game the warhammer's added extension, gold lip and tooth face were completely black and flat; the rest of the hammer and every design render looked right.
**Cause.** The added piece was built with a UV layer named "UV"; the pieces PyNifly imports carry "UVMap". Blender's Join matches UV layers by NAME, so after the join the exported first layer held (0,1) for every vertex of the new piece: 16.7% of the surface had no UV area and no valid tangent frame, so the game sampled one corner texel and had no frame for the normal map. The design sheets were rendered before the join, so they could not show it.
**Fix.** build_stage.py join(): every piece keeps only its active UV layer, renamed UVMap, before joining; asserts one layer after. verify.py surface_frame() fails a shape with >1% zero-UV-area surface or any non-unit tangent/bitangent. proof.py renders with the game's _n.dds so Blender computes tangents from the exported UVs (reproduced the bug, then the fix).
**Root cause:** proof renders were made from the pre-export scene and with materials that ignore tangents, so nothing checked the exported shape's UVs and tangent frames - the data the game actually draws from.
**Rule.** Read back UVs and tangent frames of every exported shape after any mesh join, and render proofs from the exported NIF with its normal map; the mod's verify.py surface_frame gate is the mechanical check.

## Light came through a bow every render drew solid - pieces that did not meet and open shells, invisible to a two-sided render and to a winding vote (Ebony Wolf bow and arrow, nif, blender, 2026-11-14)

**Symptom.** In game (first person) the owner saw window light through the bow's handle and through the nocked arrow; the bow's upper guard stood where the arrow rests; the string met the bare metal at the limb tips.
**Cause.** Not the shader: flags, alpha and shadow bits matched vanilla's bow exactly (checked first - the killing condition for the shader hypothesis). The bow is assembled from pieces cut out of the Wolf sword and war axe. The scaled grip ended short of its guard bands and the limbs started above them - a gap round each end of the grip - and the war axe's fang (the spurs), the limbs' bases and the arrowhead's foot were open shells whose openings had been hidden inside the next piece on the source weapon. The game culls back faces, so through an opening the far wall vanishes and the light behind shows. The design renders drew both sides, and verify.py's winding check votes each surface's outside - neither asks whether a ray can pass through.
**Fix.** build_stage.py: the rim-sharing pieces (each spur's five, each limb's six, the arrowhead's four, each vane's five) are welded into one piece, the real holes capped (cap_holes) and the caps made two-sided after orientation (double_caps); the grip is stretched and the limb bases pulled down to meet 0.25 inside each arched guard band; the upper guard, the upper limb's base and the grip's flared top are drawn in to vanilla's riser width (1.95) as an arrow shelf; each limb tip gets a notch both sides 2.6 below its point with a loop of the wrapped cord through it, and the string ends there on the belly, on vanilla's string-bone pivot. verify.py: see_through (rays at our shapes that meet a back face first and no front face after - vanilla and Legacy of Ysgramor all 0.000; gated <= 0.004 on the bow and arrow files) and bow_checks (riser gaps by rays from the riser's centre line, the arrow rest against vanilla's riser at Bow_MidBone's height, the nocks). Gate row built-weapon-nifs-checked-for-light-through.
**Root cause:** pieces re-used out of their context carry openings their old neighbours hid, and both checks in place looked at surfaces (drawn two-sided, or voted one at a time) rather than at what a ray sees from outside with back faces culled.
**Rule.** For any mesh built from cut pieces, prove it closed the way the game draws it: cast rays from outside with back faces culled (a back face first and nothing in front after = light through), and render proofs with backface culling against a bright backdrop. Capping per piece is not enough where pieces share rims - weld them first, or the caps meet back to back and the surface cannot be told inside from outside. Still open: the mace (0.0047) and warhammer (0.006) measure above zero on the same check and are reported, not gated.

## A UV and tangent gate that passed the bow because it never read it - a skinned shape keeps its vertices in the skin partition (Ebony Wolf bow r02, nif, 2026-11-14)

**Symptom.** verify.py's surface_frame gate (no-UV-area faces, broken tangent frames, smoothed-over hard edges) reported the bow as clean in r01, and Main Agent's brief listed "UV/tangent read-back" among the bow's passing gates. Reading the bow's real vertex data showed 6.4% of the riser's surface with no UV area, 1508 vertices with no tangent frame (the collars' gold lips and end discs) and 198 smoothed-over faces on the nock loops.
**Cause.** surface_frame read the BSTriShape's own vertex block and returned None when it was empty - which it always is for a skinned SSE shape, whose vertices live in its NiSkinPartition. None was treated as "nothing to report", so the only skinned item in the build was never checked. The collars' gold rows all sat on one texture row (and later on rows thinner than a half float can hold), the cord source's end caps had their UVs on one row, and the loops' tight turns averaged their normals over a fold.
**Fix.** verify.py reads a skinned shape's vertex buffer from its partition (layout [value removed], 40 bytes) with the partition's triangles; collar.py maps the collar's gold onto the atlas's broadest plain gold (rows by profile, angle a half turn at a time) and welds the rings the arrow groove presses together; build_stage.py remaps per-triangle flat UVs on the string and loops (measured in half floats) and splits the loops' sharp folds. The bow now reads 0 bad tangent frames, 0 smoothed faces, 0.06% and 0.1% no-UV area.
**Root cause:** a check that returns "nothing" for a case it cannot read is indistinguishable from a pass.
**Rule.** A gate must say UNREAD (and fail) for a shape it cannot read, never None/skip; and UV area must be measured as the file stores it (half floats) and per triangle, as the game draws it.
Topics: nif, textures, testing, python.


## A "is the player moving" check read the rider, not the horse, so a mounted feature broke (Walk or Run for Controller 1.2.1, 2026-11-14)

**Symptom.** A player (Nexus, lesbianfiction) reported that "run after sprint" never worked on horseback: the horse dropped from gallop straight to walk on letting go of Sprint, unless Default Motion was Run.
**Cause.** The 1.2.1 fix for a never-ending run on 1.7.104 made CarryRun() require PlayerMoving(), which reads the player's own ActorState movement bits. On horseback the horse is the actor that moves, so the rider's bits stay clear and the run ended at once. The 1.2.1 test steps were all on foot.
**Fix.** 1.2.2 (commit 1878c4f): on Sprint release while mounted, hold the horse (IsOnMount/GetMount) and keep the run while the horse's movement bits are set; on foot unchanged. Queued for a riding test (20261114-222523-...-9e2b), falsification episode 136 open until it passes.
**Root cause:** a movement check assumed the player is always the actor that moves, and the regression test of a fix that touched that check never rode a horse.
**Rule.** Any check of "moving / sprinting / running" asks which actor moves (the mount when riding). A mod whose motion setting also drives the horse gets a riding step in every test request.

## Copying another framework's pause copied what it looked like, not how it was done (AMF 2.4.0, found 2026-11-14)

**Symptom.** A Nexus user (HorstiIator, 13 Nov 2026) could not close NPC Preset Applier 3.0.1's window after making a preset under AMF; the game was stuck.
**Cause.** AMF 2.4.0 (06ab84c) made other mods' windows "pause the game the way SKSE Menu Framework does" by raising UI numPausesGame, a full pause that also stops game work. SMF only sets Main freezeTime: time stops, the game keeps running. NPA's save-look closes its window only after game work (removing a stand-in NPC) finishes, which the full pause never let happen.
