**Fix.** AMF 2.4.2 (7aae265): mods' pausing windows set freezeTime (cleared only if AMF set it); AMF's own menu keeps numPausesGame. Test request 20261114-232904-...-6cd8, falsification episode 138 open until it passes.
**Root cause:** matching another framework's visible result ("the game looks paused") without checking which engine mechanism it used.
**Rule.** When copying a framework's behaviour, name the exact engine field or call it uses and use the same one. numPausesGame and freezeTime are different pauses; code, logs and help text say which one is meant. Also: the same engine field can be a plain member on the SE/AE line and behind GetRuntimeData() on the 1.7 line.

## Blind scripted mesh edits pick the wrong vertices and tear the model; a hole needs new faces, not dragged ones (Ysgramor cuirass, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** Filling the gap left by a removed fur collar by moving a plate's "top-edge" vertices up to the collar tore the plate open and dragged half the shell; a "raise this region" pass made a black hood. Several attempts in a row, each judged only from the final render.
**Cause.** The selection was a numeric filter (open edges, z above X, radius below Y) that also caught other boundaries (a medallion hole rim, wing borders); and the gap was a real hole in the mesh, so moving existing vertices could only stretch faces across it.
**Fix.** Stopped under rule 49; plan written: highlight-render every selection before applying it, bridge the correct boundary loop to the target rim with new faces of the same piece, raise a layer as its own solidified region with a side wall.
**Root cause:** the pipeline had no step that shows a selection before a scripted edit applies it, so wrong picks were only discovered after the damage, in a render of the whole model.
**Rule.** Before any scripted mesh edit, render the exact selection highlighted and check it; fill holes by bridging loops, never by dragging boundary vertices.

## A crash with no Crash Logger log was blamed on the mod under test; the Windows dump named another mod (Deep Snow 1.3.0, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** Two crashes (ucrtbase.dll [value removed]) about 1 s after an in-session load during Deep Snow 1.3.0 tests; Crash Logger wrote nothing, and the run notes suspected Deep Snow's after-load clean-up because its log stopped there.
**Cause.** [value removed] is a fail-fast (here abort from VCRUNTIME140!_purecall), which Crash Logger does not catch. Windows still wrote full dumps to %LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps; cdb on them showed the same stack both times in Directional Movement Keys ([offset removed], an SKSE task calling a destroyed reference's GetAnimationGraphManager). DeepSnow.dll was not on the crashing thread. One of the two crashes had also happened after Deep Snow's clean-up had finished, which the "clean-up timing" reading did not fit.
**Fix.** No Deep Snow change; falsification episode 139 and a control repro (e99b: DMK off / Deep Snow off runs).
**Root cause:** the last line of the mod under test's log was read as the place it died, without a stack.
**Rule.** When the game dies with no Crash Logger log, read Windows event 1000 (module + code) and the dump in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps with cdb before naming a cause. A log that just stops says when, not who.

## An INI re-read at load changed the setting but not the value in force (Walk or Run for Controller 1.2.2, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** Test a669 step 5: the INI's run speed was edited 150 -> 120 while the game ran, then a save loaded. The log said "movement speed 120%" and the mod's state read runPercent 120, but appliedPercent and the player's SpeedMult stayed 150.
**Cause.** The kPostLoadGame handler re-read the INI (settings::ReloadIfChanged) and then only nudged the game to recompute (speed::Refresh). The cached scale the hook multiplies by is set only by speed::ApplyCurrent, which the menu path calls and the reload path did not.
**Fix.** 1.2.2 rebuild (c9f7ed4): the load handler calls speed::ApplyCurrent after the reload, refreshing once. Re-test requests 3da0 (SE) and 9fcb (1.7).
**Root cause:** a second way of changing a setting (reading the file again) skipped the apply function the first way (the menu) used, so the log and the mod's own report looked right while the game's value stayed stale.
**Rule.** Every path that changes a setting goes through the same apply function as the menu. A test of an INI-edit path checks the value in force in the game (getav, the hook's applied value), not just the setting and the log line.

## A Nexus description save does not move "Last updated" or the recently-updated list - only a file change does (Auto Draw pilot, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** The owner wanted every Skyrim page to show as recently updated by saving a minor description change.
**Cause.** Nexus's public "Last updated" date (and the v1 API / GraphQL updatedAt, and the updated sort) moves on file uploads only. A pilot save on Auto Draw (189995) - saved, re-read in the editor and on the public page - left the date at 2026-10-01 03:04 UTC; three earlier live description saves (10-12, 10-22, 10-25) had not moved it either.
**Fix.** Pilot stopped at one page; no other page edited. No Nexus rule forbids bumping (ToS, File Submission Guidelines, Moderation Policy, Best Practices read), but it would not work.
**Root cause:** the assumption that any page save counts as an update was never checked against the date Nexus shows; the earlier description saves would have shown it.
**Rule.** To make a page appear as updated, post a real file update; check the public "Last updated" date after any page save before assuming it counted. Also: typing /mods/<id>/edit/general now redirects to the public page - the editor is /games/<domain>/mods/<id>/edit/general. Topics: nexus.

## A Controls-page binding row that nothing read (AMF on-screen keyboard, found 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** Asked to move the on-screen keyboard's Shift off X, the build found the "On-screen keyboard: shift / backspace / done" rows on AMF's Controls page had never changed anything: Keyboard.cpp HandleOpenPad had X = shift, Y = backspace and RT = space fixed in code, so a player who rebound those rows saw no effect.
**Fix.** AMF 2.4.2 (b4ce495): the keyboard reads Shift, Space (new rebindable action, default X) and Backspace from the bindings; Shift's default moved to RT; a saved player binding wins over a new default. The Done row is still not read (left as found).
**Root cause:** a bindable row was added to the Controls page without wiring the code that handles the control to read it.
**Rule.** Before treating a Controls-page row as where a control's button comes from, find the code that handles that control and check it reads the binding. A new bindable action gets a test step that rebinds it and checks the new button works.

## The FOMOD package shipped an old INI because the repo kept its INI at dist's root (UVC 1.6.0, found 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** Gate row shipped-ini-is-the-repos failed on the UVC 1.6.0 package: the INI under SKSE\Plugins was 1.5.0's (6 Nov), not the repo's.
**Cause.** package-mod's general dist copy put dist\UnbindControls.ini at the installer's Common root; the INI step then refreshed that first-found copy of the same name, so the one under SKSE\Plugins was never replaced. Earlier 1.6.0 packages probably shipped the old INI too.
**Fix.** Repo side (UVC d4c454c): the INI moved to dist\SKSE\Plugins. The packager is unchanged, so any FOMOD repo with its INI at dist's root is still exposed.
**Root cause:** the packager's copy loop and its INI step pick files by name, first found, so two copies of one INI in a package decide silently which one wins.
**Rule.** A repo's shipped INI lives at its install path under dist (SKSE\Plugins), never at dist's root. A package with two files of the same name is a defect; the gate row shipped-ini-is-the-repos is the check.

## A mod's own INI in its MO2 folder can hold saved settings that User.ini does not show (AMF 2.4.2 test 9ce3, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** The AMF on-screen-keyboard test assumed no saved bindings (User.ini had none), so the new defaults (X =
space, RT = shift) should have shown - but the profile would still have shown the old ones.
**Cause.** The mod folder's own ApocryphaMenuFramework.ini (lines 152-154) carried sOskShift / sOskBackspace / sOskDone,
written there by an earlier install or session; checking only User.ini looked like "nothing saved".
**Fix.** Read every INI the plugin loads (the mod folder's, User.ini, overwrite) before asserting defaults apply; the
executor flagged it instead of passing the step.
**Root cause:** the test request's "no saved bindings" premise was checked against one of the plugin's INI sources, not
all of them - the request template has no "where this plugin reads settings from" field.
**Rule.** A test that depends on DEFAULTS lists every settings file the plugin reads and confirms each is free of the
keys under test (or names the line to remove), before the run.

## A gate piped through `| tail -1` reported OK while it FAILED (katana scabbard runner, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** The katana scabbard's runner printed "engraving-layout-gate: OK" and the scabbard was shown and approved; the
dai-katana build later found the same koiguchi FAILs the gate (weave motif too large for its panel; 4 fragments).
**Cause.** `run_sheath_katana.sh` (and the rapier's, copied from it) ran the gate as `gate.py ... | tail -1 || true`:
the gate prints one line per finding, FAIL lines first, and its last line can be an OK summary for another face - the
FAILs scrolled away, and `|| true` threw the exit code away too.
**Fix.** Both runners print the gate's output in full; the katana scabbard's koiguchi is to be fixed before its game build.
**Root cause:** runner scripts were written to keep logs short, and nothing checks that a gate's FAIL reaches the report
- the pipe and the `|| true` together removed both the text and the exit status.
**Rule.** Never pipe a gate through `tail`/`head` or swallow its exit code; print it whole or grep it for FAIL and stop.

## A quiver "kept all six arrows at 3 and 1" because the same ammo was re-equipped - the quiver only rebuilds on an ammo change (Nordic Skyforged 1.1.0 test c381, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** The driven quiver check set the Skyforge Steel Arrow count to 6, 3 and 1 with removeitem, re-equipped the arrows each time, and every frame showed six arrows in the quiver - read at first as a defect in the quiver NIF.
**Cause.** The NIF was fine (same shape names as the Ebony quiver that worked: Arrow1..Arrow6, Arrow:0, ArrowQuiver:0/1). EquipItem on ammo that is already equipped changes nothing, so the 3D quiver was never rebuilt after the count dropped. Controls in the same game - vanilla Steel Arrows and Ebony Arrows at 1, freshly equipped - showed the right count; the relaunch that switched to another ammo and back before each frame showed 6, 3 and 1.
**Root cause:** the test changed the count by a path a player never uses (removeitem) and assumed re-equip refreshes the model; no control with a known-good quiver was taken in the same way before suspecting the mesh.
**Rule.** To test a quiver's arrow count, switch to another ammo and back (or shoot) before each frame, and take the same measurement on a known-good quiver first. Same session: Skyforge Immersion Addon (its ability closes the Crafting Menu near the Skyforge until C03/C06/MS09) is why the Skyforge "would not open" in 5b7a, and Archery Rebalance rescales every arrow at load (13 -> 11), so compare a mod's arrow with a vanilla arrow's in-game damage before calling a number wrong.
Topics: testing, devbench, skyrim.

## The package render died on a BodySlide NIF at a 263-character path - PyNifly cannot open past MAX_PATH (Nordic Skyforged 1.1.0 finalize, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** finalize-mod finished the copy, zip and distro sync, then exited 4 (finalized, not postable): package-render's Blender run stopped at once with "Could not open '...\31 BodySlide - HIMBO\CalienteTools\BodySlide\ShapeData\Nordic Skyforged - HIMBO - [asset path removed]' as nif".
**Cause.** The file is a valid SE NIF (its header reads fine); its full path in 10. finalized mods is 263 characters. PyNifly's native reader opens by plain path and fails past MAX_PATH (260); one unreadable item aborted the whole render, so no NIF was rendered.
**Fix.** package-render.py: an item whose path is 240 characters or longer is copied (through the long-path prefix) to a short path in the render's work folder and rendered from there; the hash and shipped paths are unchanged, textures still come from the package.
**Root cause:** the finalized folder nests the mod's display name twice plus the BodySlide ShapeData tree, which repeats the mod name again - long display names push installer-option files past MAX_PATH, and the renderer handed raw paths to a native library.
**Rule.** Any tool that hands a package path to a native or third-party reader (PyNifly, texconv, 7-Zip) must handle paths of 260+ characters - copy to a short staging path or use the long-path prefix - and one unreadable item must be reported per item, not end the run.
Topics: packaging, python, nif.

## Two asset mods reached "post it" with a NOTICE that checked only the main source's permissions - Xtudo's textures and the HIMBO files need their authors' permission (Nordic Ebony / Nordic Skyforged 1.1.0, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** At posting time, the Nexus permissions boxes of every credited source were read: Legacy of Ysgramor (NordwarUA) allows modification and asset use with credit, but Legacy of Ysgramor - My patches and fixes (Xtudo, 111121) says "You must get permission from me" for both modification and asset use (and no donation points), and the HIMBO Conversion (Trexasle, 110002) says the same for asset use. Both mods ship Xtudo's diffuse textures (the whole black colourway) and the HIMBO files as an option. The posting was stopped.
**Cause.** The repos' NOTICE.md recorded NordwarUA's box in full and then said "the other sources ... are checked against their own pages" - a promise nobody kept. The owner's 2026-11-12 permission note covered "the mod its from" (Legacy of Ysgramor) and was read as covering every source.
**Root cause:** permission was checked per MOD (the one it is built from) instead of per SHIPPED FILE SOURCE; a credit line was treated as if it were a permission. The same class removed Nordic Dragonbone Armor Replacer from Nexus (2026-09-30).
**Rule.** Before any first post of a mod that ships another author's files, list every source the build script opens (download archive names), read each source's live Nexus permissions box, and record per source: asset use, modification, donation points, upload elsewhere. A "You must get permission" box is a hard stop until a written permission is saved in the repo (NOTICE.md, with the message link) or the files are dropped. Gate idea for gate-rules.json: refuse finalize/upload of a skyrim-asset mod whose NOTICE.md has no per-source "Permissions read <date>" line for every Nexus id the build script names.
Topics: licensing, nexus, packaging, release.


## A FOMOD package whose core folder is not "Common" was installed raw - "00 Core" sat inside the MO2 mod folder, and in game the armour was invisible (Nordic Ebony / Nordic Skyforged 1.1.0 TruePBR test, 2026-11-15)

**Symptom.** After the TruePBR rebuild, `install-test-build.py "<package>" "<mod folder>"` reported "read back: the mod folder equals the package" - and in game the Ebony cuirass, boots and gauntlets (body included) were invisible; the helmet, shield and weapons floated. The first suspect was the new TruePBR shader blocks (skinned shapes that draw nothing).
**Cause.** The install copied the package root as it is: `00 Core\`, `10 Cuirass - No fur collar\`, `30 BodySlide - CBBE 3BA\` and `fomod\` landed INSIDE the mod folder, and the stale files of the earlier install (flat `meshes\`, `textures\`) were moved out. MO2 does not look inside `00 Core\`, so the game read the root `.esp` (moved there earlier) whose armour addons point at meshes that no longer existed at the root. The script resolves a FOMOD's options and conditional installs and copies `Common\` (or the root when there is no `Common\`) - it does not honour `<requiredInstallFiles>` from a folder with another name.
**Root cause:** "read back equals the package" was taken as "installed as a player's mod manager would" - the read-back compares against the RAW package, so a package installed unresolved passes it.
**Fix.** Installed the FOMOD-resolved core (the contents of `00 Core\` plus the docs) through `install-test-build.py` from a staging folder, inside the combined run (`combined-run with`). The armour then drew (see the run's result).
**Rule.** Before an in-game test of a FOMOD package, check that the MO2 mod folder holds `meshes\` / `textures\` / the plugin at its ROOT, not a numbered option folder. Gate idea for install-test-build: resolve `<requiredInstallFiles>` folders whatever their name, and refuse a read-back where an installer-step folder (`NN Name\`) is present at the mod root.

## A FOMOD option that "replaces the cuirass" shipped its meshes on the vanilla path while the plugin pointed the worn armour at our own folder - the option changed only the ground model (Nordic Ebony 1.1.0, before posting, 2026-11-15)
**Symptom.** A close-up helper noticed that "10 Cuirass - No fur collar" installed `meshes\armor\ebony\m|f\cuirass_*.nif`, but the light plugin's ebony cuirass ARMA reads `[asset path removed]` / `[asset path removed]`. Choosing the option would have left the worn cuirass fur-collared; only the ground model changed.
**Cause.** build-fomod.py placed the option's meshes with the same vanilla-path map as the core, then mirrored ONLY the core's worn meshes into `meshes\NordicEbony\` (where 1.1.0's plugin points the four armour addons). The option was never mirrored. The in-game test ran with the default (fur) option, so nothing looked wrong.
**Root cause:** the move of the worn armour to our own folder was applied to the core and not to every option that replaces a worn mesh; no check compared an option's mesh paths with the model paths the plugin actually names.
**Fix.** The build mirrors the option's worn cuirass under `meshes\NordicEbony\` too (FOMOD priority 2 over the core's 0) and fails if those files are missing; the resolved install (core then option) now gives the collarless cuirass at the plugin's paths. Commit 5e1dcd2, tag v1.1.0 moved to it with the owner's standing approval for this release.
**Rule.** When a plugin redirects a record's model path, every installer option that replaces that model must ship at the redirected path. Before posting a FOMOD, resolve each option over the core and check that every mesh the plugin's ARMA/ARMO/WEAP records name is present in the result, and that each option actually changes at least one of those named files. Topics: packaging, fomod, nif.

## A recolour gain chosen from "the black look keeps ~0.5x" turned an already dark fur into a flat black silhouette - and the proof renderer drew every alpha-tested shape black anyway (Nordic Ebony / Skyforged 1.1.0 fur collar, 2026-11-15)
**Symptom.** The owner saw the TruePBR fur collar as a flat black shape with no strands. The shipped furcollar.dds measured visible-fur median 10/255, max 33 (the planned colourway's was median 59).
**Cause.** recolour_black.py multiplied the fur's luminance by 0.5 - a factor measured from Xtudo's black versions of OTHER textures - but NordwarUA's fur is already dark (visible median 20.6). Separately, the close-up renderer's alpha-clip branch never linked its BSDF and transparent shaders into the mix node, so every alpha-tested shape rendered pure black whatever its texture; the comparison sheets could not show the problem or the fix.
**Root cause:** a gain was carried over from one texture class to another without measuring the target texture, and the proof render's black fur was read as the texture's look instead of checking the renderer against a known-bright input.
**Fix.** The fur now maps by luminance ** 0.6 (median ~53, strands kept, alpha untouched); the renderer's clip branch now links both shaders (scratchpad copy rgp_fix.py). Sheets: 4. plans\nordic-carved-missing-weapons-20261115\closeups\fur-fix-<set>.jpg.
**Rule.** A recolour states its target numbers per texture (median/percentiles of the visible texels) and the build prints them; and any proof render of an alpha-tested material is checked against a control whose colour is known (a texel range that must come out light) before its darkness is trusted. Topics: textures, pbr, packaging.

## Armour equipped while TestBench's free camera is on does not redraw - it looks invisible (Ebony chainmail test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** During an in-game look, a newly equipped cuirass (Skyforge, a re-equipped Ebony one, and a vanilla Iron Armor control) showed as invisible / a bare body.
**Cause.** The pieces were equipped while TestBench's free camera was ON; the game did not rebuild the actor's worn geometry until the camera mode changed. With free camera OFF the same equip drew at once - no mod defect.
**Fix.** Equip with free camera off, then switch it on for the framing.
**Root cause:** the test procedure framed armour with the free camera without knowing that an equip under it skips the redraw, and a vanilla control was needed to tell it from a mesh fault.
**Rule.** Before calling armour "invisible", re-equip with free camera off and check a vanilla control; equip first, frame second.

## nexus-upload's single-file path still did a single-part upload - a 119 MB first file was refused although multipart was already written (Nordic Ebony 1.1.0, nexus, upload, 2026-11-16)
**Symptom.** `nexus-upload.py "Skyrim - Nordic Ebony Armor and Weapons Replacer"` stopped with Nexus's 400 "File size exceeds maximum of 100 MiB for single-part uploads".
**Cause.** The 2026-11-11 multipart support (`upload_archive`) was wired into the nexus-files.json manifest path only; `main()`'s single-archive path kept its own inline single-part upload.
**Root cause:** the fix for a limit went into the new code path that hit it, not into the shared one; two copies of "upload an archive" existed.
**Fix.** `main()` now calls `upload_archive()` (single-part up to 100 MiB, multipart above); the Ebony zip went up in 3 parts. tests\test_nexus_upload_verify.py still passes.
**Rule.** One function per external operation; when a limit is fixed, grep for every other caller of the same endpoint. Topics: nexus, upload, python.

## Disabling and re-enabling a test NPC strips the armour equipped on it (in-game FPS test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** After `disable` / `enable` on spawned NPCs between measurement runs, they wore their own outfit again, not the set under test.
**Cause.** Re-enabling a reference re-applies its default outfit; equipment added by console is not kept. It looked like the set was still on because nothing reported the swap.
**Fix.** Re-equip the set after every enable, before measuring.
**Root cause:** the test steps assumed equipment state survives a disable/enable cycle, and no step read the equipped items back before a measurement.
**Rule.** Before any measurement on spawned actors, read back what they are wearing (inspect or a frame); never assume console-equipped items survive disable, enable, cell reload or resurrect.

## Weather set with fw drifts back to the region default in Njordlinger (in-game FPS test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** Measurements meant for clear weather were partly taken in light snow (DefaultWeather) in a later launch.
**Cause.** `fw` forces a weather only until the region weather system replaces it; the run checked the weather once at setup.
**Fix.** Check the scene (`inspect scene`) right before each measurement and re-apply the weather when it has changed.
**Root cause:** weather was treated as a setup step rather than a condition to verify at each measurement.
**Rule.** Any condition a comparison depends on (weather, time, NPC count, equipment) is re-checked immediately before each measured run, not only at setup.

## A long unattended in-game run started while the permission classifier is failing can be stranded half-way (combined-run executor, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** The executor for a two-set 3D test got "classifier gave no verdict (error)" on 13 of 16 shell calls before opening the batch.
**Cause.** Auto mode stops the turn after 10 calls in a row without a verdict. A run of 100+ shell calls started in that state could be cut off with the game open, the profile edited, frame caps lifted and the batch lock held, and nobody left to close or restore anything. The executor correctly declined to start.
**Fix.** Recorded the run as not started; re-dispatch once a few cheap calls in a row succeed.
**Root cause:** the run procedure assumed every tool call would get a verdict; nothing checked the permission layer's health before taking on state that only a later call can undo.
**Rule.** Before opening a batch or any multi-step change that needs a later step to clean up, make three cheap shell calls; start only if all three succeed, and stop before the first state change (install, profile edit, launch) if misses begin.

## With AI off (tai), SetPosition moves an actor's data but not its drawn model (in-game FPS test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** NPCs placed on a grid with SetPosition while AI was frozen still drew at their old spots.
**Cause.** With AI processing off the actor's 3D is not updated from its new position, so the reference reports the new coordinates while the model stays put.
**Fix.** Toggle AI on for about a second after positioning so the models snap into place, then freeze again.
**Root cause:** the setup step trusted the position the reference reported instead of a frame of what was drawn.
**Rule.** After moving actors for a staged scene, confirm the placement from a frame, not from GetPos; with tai on, briefly run AI to apply moves.

## FPS compared across launches is skewed by scene differences such as snow cover (in-game FPS test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** One launch's empty scene ran about 1 ms slower than the others; a later launch had grass where an earlier one had snow.
**Cause.** Weather and seasonal ground cover differ between launches at the same spot, which changes the empty-scene cost, so raw cross-launch FPS overstates or hides an item's cost.
**Fix.** Bracket every measured run with empty-scene runs in the same launch, report costs relative to that launch's own empty runs, and compare GPU busy as well as frame time when the scene is CPU-bound.
**Root cause:** the comparison treated the scene as identical between launches without measuring it.
**Rule.** A cost is the difference against a baseline measured in the same launch; in a CPU-bound scene, report GPU busy too, because frame time hides GPU cost.

## Close-ups of leveled NPCs do not repeat between launches; use frozen ground models (in-game test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** Before/after close-ups across launches showed different faces, heights and poses, so they could not be compared.
**Cause.** Leveled NPC bases roll a new face and height each spawn.
**Fix.** For a before/after pair, place the item's ground model at fixed coordinates, freeze its physics (SetMotionType keyframed), and use the same camera.
**Root cause:** the subject of the comparison was not fixed.
**Rule.** A visual A/B pair needs a subject that cannot change between the two captures.

## Right after an Alternate Perspective new game, start-up scripts re-dress the player (in-game test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** About 20 s after equipping the test set on a fresh AP character, an iron kit replaced it.
**Cause.** Start-up scripts for the chosen start run after the player gains control and hand out their own gear.
**Fix.** Wait for the start scripts to settle, then equip and read back what is worn before checking anything.
**Root cause:** the test assumed control of the player meant the start sequence was finished.
**Rule.** After a new game, read back equipped items immediately before every check that depends on them.

## A parallax claim went onto banners before the effect was seen in game (3D armour banners, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** "Parallax" chips and lines were put on the -with-3d banners and page drafts; the in-game on/off pair later showed the carving looks the same with parallax on and off.
**Cause.** The claim was built from file evidence (slot-3 _p maps and a displacement scale in the NIFs), and the open to-do item "displacement-scale field confirmed in game" was treated as a formality.
**Fix.** Remove the parallax claim until an in-game on/off pair shows a difference.
**Root cause:** marketing text was allowed to depend on a feature still marked unconfirmed in the to-do list.
**Rule.** A feature goes on a banner or page only after it has been seen working in game; file presence is not evidence that an effect renders.

## A record copied from another mod's template carries that template's defects (Skyforged shield not shown on the back by IED, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** A favourited, unequipped Skyforge Steel Shield did not appear on the player's back with Immersive Equipment Displays, while the vanilla-record Ebony Shield did; both meshes were structurally identical.
**Cause.** build-esp.py copies Legacy of Ysgramor's NW_Wolf_Shield_Steel record as the template, and that record's object bounds are all zero, so our shield shipped with zero bounds. The record checks only validated FormID references, so the zero went through. (Hypothesis under test in game at the time of writing.)
**Fix.** build-esp.py computes bounds from the ground model as it ships (repeating the packaging resize) whenever a template's bounds are all zero, and refuses a zero result; gate row item-object-bounds-not-all-zero (esp-obnd-gate.py).
**Root cause:** the build trusted a third-party template record's data fields as correct and checked only its links.
**Rule.** When a record is copied from another mod's template, validate its data fields (bounds, models for both sexes, sounds) as well as its references; derive anything geometric from the model as shipped, after every packaging step that changes it. Zero bounds are a defect only on records a plugin defines itself and that are not templated - Skyrim.esm has zero bounds on enchanted variants and some plain items.

## A record generator that copies subrecords but writes its own header drops the template's record flags (Skyforged shield not on the back with Simple Dual Sheath, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** With Simple Dual Sheath's ShieldOnBack, our equipped Skyforge Steel Shield stayed on the left arm while sheathed and only flashed onto the back during the draw; the vanilla Ebony Shield worked. Records looked identical in field views (slot 39, ArmorShield, equip type, bounds after their own fix).
**Cause.** build-esp.py copied the template's subrecords but packed every record header with flags 0, so the ARMO lost the [value removed] "Shield" record flag that its template (and every playable vanilla shield) carries; shield-on-back code reads that flag (CommonLib TESObjectARMO::IsShield).
**Fix.** Carry each template's header flags through (minus the compressed bit); refuse a slot-39 ARMO without [value removed]; gate row shield-armour-carries-shield-flag (esp-shield-flag-gate.py), non-playable armour exempt.
**Root cause:** the generator treated the record header as boilerplate; field-list views do not show header flags beside fields, so a comparison of fields could not catch it.
**Rule.** When copying a record, copy its whole header (flags included), not only its subrecords; when comparing a working record with a broken one, compare the header flags too.

## A PreToolUse guard that matches tool names anywhere in a command blocks notes that only mention them (windowed-tool-while-game-guard, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** The first version of the guard refused a heredoc that appended a past-mistakes entry, because the text mentioned xEdit.
**Cause.** It searched the whole command string, so prose inside heredocs and quoted commit messages counted as a launch.
**Fix.** Strip heredoc bodies and quoted strings before matching, except a quoted path ending in .exe/.py/.ps1/.bat/.cmd (which is how a launch quotes a program); tests cover both sides.
**Root cause:** the guard matched words, not the command's executable positions.
**Rule.** A command guard removes text payloads (heredocs, quoted prose) before matching, and its tests include a command that merely mentions the guarded name.

## A FormID typed from memory equipped the wrong item (in-game test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** [id removed] was typed for the Ebony Shield; it is Dragonplate Gauntlets, which went onto the owner's character.
**Cause.** The executor recalled a FormID instead of looking it up; vanilla armour IDs are close together.
**Fix.** Reverted the gauntlets; the right ID ([id removed]) came from a lookup.
**Root cause:** no lookup step stood between recalling an ID and sending it to the game.
**Rule.** Look up every FormID by EditorID (housecarl_records or esm_lookup) and print the record name before sending it; never type one from memory.

## Papyrus DrawWeapon/SheatheWeapon on the player desyncs the weapon state (in-game test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** SheatheWeapon did nothing on the player; mixing it with R presses gave a draw/sheathe race and contradictory frames.
**Cause.** The Papyrus calls do not drive the player's own weapon state reliably; the R key does.
**Fix.** Toggle only with the real R key and read the state from a frame after the animation finishes.
**Root cause:** the test treated a script call as equivalent to the player's input.
**Rule.** For the player's draw/sheathe state use the real Ready Weapon key, then confirm with a frame.

## At the main menu, Down then Enter picks Continue, not New Game, when a save exists (in-game test, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** Two launches meant to start a new game loaded the owner's own Save2 instead.
**Cause.** The menu's first item is Continue when saves exist, so the key sequence lands on a different button; the saves listing had been read wrongly as empty.
**Fix.** Nothing was saved; the owner's character was restored.
**Root cause:** the key sequence assumed a fixed menu layout without reading which button was highlighted.
**Rule.** Read the highlighted main-menu button before pressing Enter; when saves exist, a new game needs one more Down.

## A request queued after combined-run start is not in the batch and cannot be recorded (batch B-20261116-050228-04d1)

**Symptom.** 549d (Simple Dodge) was run in both phases but its result could not be written.
**Cause.** combined-run start snapshots the queue; there is no add route for a request that arrives later.
**Fix.** Notes kept for recording it in the next batch.
**Root cause:** the batch has no way to take late requests, so a run done in good faith leaves no record.
**Rule.** Check test-request status before running a request; a late one goes into the next batch, or combined-run gains an add route.


## A two-download package failed repo-fomod-installer-ships - the gate looked for fomod\ at the version folder only, and the packager rewrote one installer's title (Truly Nordic Ebony / Skyforged 1.0.0, packaging, 2026-11-16)

Topics: packaging, fomod, release

**Symptom.** The first 1.0.0 package of Truly Nordic Ebony Armor and Weapons (a 3D\ main and a Flat\ optional package under one version folder, each its own FOMOD) failed the gate row repo-fomod-installer-ships: "package has no fomod\ModuleConfig.xml (the repo has one)", and every folder the installer names was "missing".
**Cause.** fomod-repo-installer-shipped-gate.py checked <version folder>\fomod\ only. Truly Nordic Carved's multi-download packages never hit this because that repo keeps no fomod\ModuleConfig.xml at its root. The packager also rewrote the Flat package's moduleName ("... - Flat textures"), so even a per-subfolder check would have found the installer not byte-equal to the repo's.
**Fix.** The gate judges each subfolder that holds fomod\ModuleConfig.xml when the version folder has none of its own (self-test case 5). The packagers no longer touch the installer: both packages carry the repo's file byte for byte.
**Root cause:** the gate was written for one package per version, and the packager treated a shipped installer as something it could adjust after copying.
**Rule.** A gate that reads "the package" must know about multi-download version folders (nexus-files.json); a packager never edits a file the gates compare with the repo - change the repo file instead.

## After a mod rename, finalize leaves the old-named zip in the distro folder and the audit reads the old version (Truly Nordic 1.0.0, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** nexus-version-audit read 'distro 1.1.0' for both renamed mods after a clean finalize.
**Cause.** finalize and the distro sweep prune zips by the mod's current name; the old 'Nordic ... 1.1.0.zip' did not match and stayed.
**Fix.** Moved the old zips to assets\superseded-1.1.0-zip-20261116.
**Root cause:** the prune step keys on the display name, which a rename changes.
**Rule.** After renaming a mod, sweep its distro folder for zips under the old name before the audit; prune by registry key, not display name.

## A Nexus page that is not yet published fails nexus-upload's verify, so the number is not recorded posted (Truly Nordic 1.0.0, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** The uploads to the two new draft pages succeeded, but the tool's v1 verify could not see them and did not record 1.0.0 as posted.
**Cause.** The v1 API does not serve a mod that is not published.
**Fix.** Publish the page, then record with version-gate -Action posted using the file ids from md5_search.
**Root cause:** the upload tool assumes a published page.
**Rule.** For a first upload to a new page: upload, publish, then verify and record posted.

## A comment's sticky/lock calls on Nexus raise confirm() dialogs that block the browser (Truly Nordic 1.0.0, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** Setting a sticky comment STICKY and LOCKED opens a confirm() dialog, which stops the browser extension.
**Cause.** Nexus asks for confirmation in a JavaScript dialog.
**Fix.** Override window.confirm for the call, then read the Posts tab back on a fresh load with a new query string (a sticky shows only then).
**Root cause:** the posting steps did not account for modal dialogs.
**Rule.** Before clicking a Nexus control that confirms, neutralise confirm() for that call; verify stickies on a cache-busted reload.

## Importing a page script for its data re-ran every page build (nlysg-1.1.0 gen_pages.py, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** Importing gen_pages.py to reuse its data re-rendered the old cards and tried to write to the old distro paths.
**Cause.** The script does its work at import time, with no __main__ guard.
**Fix.** It failed harmlessly because the old folders no longer existed.
**Root cause:** page scripts are written as run-once files without an entry guard.
**Rule.** Page and build scripts keep their work under if __name__ == '__main__'; import data from a module that does nothing on import.

## Package renders started at posting time held a release for hours (Truly Nordic 1.0.0, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** Both new pages waited about 2.5 hours on package-render (135 and 145 NIFs of full-3D meshes, two Blender runs in parallel) while the owner asked for the post; he waived the gate at 09:46.
**Cause.** nexus-upload refuses a model mod without a current render, and the render only starts at finalize.
**Fix.** Owner waiver (NEXUS_RENDER_WAIVED, logged in .MD\logs\package-render-waivers.log); to-do entry to start renders when a package is built and cache them by NIF hash.
**Root cause:** a slow gate ran at the last step instead of in the background as soon as its input existed.
**Rule.** A slow verification starts the moment its input is final and runs one at a time; the posting step only reads its result.

## A full build on a WIP branch replaced the release's test package in place (Truly Nordic Carved 1.4.0, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** The paused blade-families branch was built with build_all.sh; its last step, build-packages.py, wrote straight into "7. current test builds" and replaced the 1.4.0 test package that was waiting for its in-game run.
**Cause.** build_all.sh always ends by packaging into the release location; nothing about the branch being unreleased changes where it writes. The helper put the old package back (pkg_hash diff against before_pkg.json: 0 changes) and set the branch build aside.
**Fix.** Restored from the saved copy; the branch package moved to 7. current test builds\_work\superseded-packages\2026-11-16\.
**Root cause:** the build script has one output root, and the pipeline assumes a build is always for the open release; a WIP build has no separate place to land.
**Rule.** A build on any branch other than main writes its packages under an out-root of its own (or refuses); only main's build may replace the test package. Snapshot the test package's hashes before any full build.

## Matching _0/_1 armour meshes came out with different vertex orders and triangles (own-armour exercise 1 bracers, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** The bracers' _0 and _1 NIFs failed the same-topology check: different vertex counts at UV seams and different triangles.
**Cause.** PyNifly splits seam vertices per shape key in its own order, and Blender's shortest-diagonal triangulation picks different diagonals on the thinner _0 body. Each build looked fine alone.
**Fix.** Split vertices by UV and triangulate in our own code, taking every quad's diagonal from the _1 build; the two exports now share byte-identical index arrays.
**Root cause:** the pipeline left topology decisions to tools that make them per mesh, while the engine needs the pair to agree exactly.
**Rule.** For any _0/_1 pair, own the triangulation and seam split, and check that the index arrays are byte-identical before export. Fit plates against the hands mesh's wrist cuff too: it reaches into the forearm, and leaving it out gave 4 vertices through the plate at rest.

## Equip changes didn't show while TestBench's free camera was on, and sleeves hid forearm armour (combined run B-20261116-163944-953a, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** A frame still showed the prisoner shirt after it was unequipped. The new bracers were invisible on a clothed character.
**Cause.** With the free camera on, the player's 3D isn't refreshed after an equip change. Separately, arm-covering clothes draw over anything worn on the forearm, so a clothed test can't show forearm armour at all. The launch also reached the main menu while the owner was typing in Chrome; the game freezes without focus.
**Fix.** Free camera off, change the equipment, free camera back on, then judge. Forearm armour is tested both under a shirt and on a bare arm. The game is brought forward only after the owner has been idle for 60 s.
**Root cause:** the test steps assumed every equip change shows at once, and that a clothed character shows forearm pieces.
**Rule.** Toggle the free camera around every equip change before judging a frame. Test arm and leg armour with and without covering clothes. Wait for the owner to be idle before focusing a launched game. Crafting keys in this list: forge Enter = create, E = close; grindstone Enter = select, R = improve; a "(+1)" preview isn't proof, so check that the ingot count dropped.

## A new page's first update would have posted its files as new files, not new versions (Truly Nordic Skyforged 1.0.1, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** The 1.0.1 dry run listed both downloads as "NEW FILE" and said the old main file "is replaced by no entry".
**Cause.** nexus-files.json's "replaces" fields were left null after the first upload to the new page, so the tool had no file to supersede.
**Fix.** "replaces" set to Nexus's own file ids for the two files (8400447 3D, 8400453 Flat); the uploads went up as new versions, and 1.0.0 moved to Old versions.
**Root cause:** the first upload doesn't write the ids it created back into the manifest, and no gate checks that an update replaces an existing page file of the same name.
**Rule.** After a first upload, write the new file ids into nexus-files.json "replaces". Refuse an update post whose entry has a live page file of the same name and no "replaces". A release whose meshes are byte-identical to the last one may reuse its render result, or be waived with the hash proof, until package-render caches by NIF hash.

## A dark notch on the greatsword's bevel was another part painted onto the blade's texels (Truly Nordic Carved, shipped since 2026-11-12, found 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** A small dark bar across the greatsword's left bevel, mid-blade, in both qualities, shipped in 1.3.0 and 1.4.0.
**Cause.** greatsword_v4_build.py put the lower-guard boss's thin wall strip at a fixed texture spot, WALL_UV = (8, 900), and checked it only against the parts the packer laid out. The blade is laid out separately down the left side, so 720 wall triangles shared the bevel's texels. The painter lets the last triangle win, so the wall's dark plain metal went across the bevel in every map. The mesh, normals and the bevel's own UVs were clean, which is why a geometry check found nothing.
**Fix.** greatsword_v6_wallfix.py moves the wall's UVs to a free patch and restores the blade texels from v3. Only 724 UV pairs change in the NIF.
**Root cause:** a hand-placed UV island was checked against one part list, not against every island in the atlas, and no gate looked for two parts sharing texels.
**Rule.** Every atlas is checked for UV overlap between distinct parts before painting. The gate draft nif-uv-overlap-gate.py (not yet registered) also flags the war axe, warhammer and battleaxe, which still need judging. A fixed UV spot is checked against ALL islands, including ones laid out outside the packer.

## A test combination was refused because a generated patch masters our Standalone plugin; KID's log can't count one ini's items (combined run B-20261116-185706-77ad, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** The first launch was refused by nj-order-audit when "Standalone Ebony" was unticked. The KID log said 56/8712 for WeapTypeKatana, not the 2 items our ini adds.
**Cause.** PG_1.esp (PGPatcher output) lists TrulyNordicCarvedWeapons - Standalone.esp as a master, so that folder can't be unticked without failing the order audit. KID prints one total per keyword across every ini that adds it.
**Fix.** Standalone Ebony stayed ticked in both runs; it overrides none of the tested records. The per-item keyword was checked live with Form.HasKeyword: true only on TNCW_Saber and TNCW_SaberGreatsword.
**Root cause:** the test steps assumed our plugins can be ticked freely, and that a log line counts per source.
**Rule.** Before writing "enable only X" in test steps, check which generated patches (PG_1, DynDOLOD, Synthesis) master our plugins. Prove a KID/SPID line's targets with HasKeyword or HasPerk on the named items, never from the log total. Character creation through Mirrorwright ends with vanilla boxes: finish-and-name, the name box, Done Writing, Done. Screenshots only through steam-capture, never TestBench capture kind=native.

## The blade's hard seams came from the 1.1.0 shading-fix pass, not from unwelded vertices (mirror-finish study, Truly Nordic Carved, 2026-11-16)

**Symptom.** The straight sword's blade faces showed about 175 hard shading seams per face. The study blamed unwelded vertices.
**Cause.** The faces were already welded. set2\shading_fix_split.py, run on the blade in 1.1.0, matches triangles by centroid, marks some blade triangles as carved, and splits their normals. The NIF from before that pass has 12 seams. The study counted seams and inferred a cause without opening the pre-pass file.
**Fix (demo).** Keep the blade out of that pass and weld the blade before marking sharp edges: 12 seams on the current layout, 0 on the rebuilt blade.
**Root cause:** a measured count was explained by the likeliest-sounding cause, and the step-by-step history of the mesh was never compared.
**Rule.** To explain a mesh defect, diff the NIF before and after each build pass. Check the greatsword (244 seams) for the same pass. A polished, low-roughness finish shows every normal-map dent, so flat normals on plain steel must ship with any roughness drop.

## UE4SS probes crashed Norse twice: hundreds of hooks at once, and ForEach over an array with null slots (Norse Phase 0, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** Run 1 crashed with an access violation at [value removed] seconds after hooks went in. Run 2 crashed with an access violation at [value removed] one second into combat.
**Cause.** Run 1 registered about 330 UFunction hooks at once (whole classes: Combat_GM, Initiative, AIC, UnitComponent, IntegerLibrary). Run 2 iterated InitiativeSubsystem.CurrentTurnOrder with UE4SS TArray:ForEach, and that array holds null "open slot" entries.
**Fix.** Hook only named functions (23 in run 3, stable). Read arrays by index with an IsValid check on every element (objs() helper).
**Root cause:** probes were written as if every function were safe to hook and every array element valid. In a native UE game neither holds.
**Rule.** In UE4SS: hook named functions in small batches, never whole classes; IsValid-check every UObject read from an array or property; native-to-native calls (Combat_GM:StartUnitTurn, GetSuccessChance) never reach a Lua hook, so test that a hook fires before building on it. Norse specifics: every level load waits on a hidden "Press any key" screen that blocks the game thread; TriggerCombatManually draws no deployment area, but SetUnitPlacementsToCurrentPosition + StartCombatOverridden does; computer use can't be approved while the owner is away, so drive with sendkey.py (Norse is in game_foreground GAME_EXES).

## RE-UE4SS C++ mods need a private submodule; build against the installed UE4SS.dll instead (NorseRealtimeNative 0.1.0, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** Cloning RE-UE4SS at v4.0.0 to build a C++ mod failed: the UEPseudo submodule returns 404 to the ApocryphaRealm GitHub account.
**Cause.** UEPseudo (Unreal type definitions) is private and needs an Epic-linked GitHub account.
**Fix.** include\ue4ss_abi.hpp declares only the UE4SS functions the mod uses (copied from the v4.0.0 mod base-class header, matching the DLL's export names). The mod links against an import library generated from the installed UE4SS.dll (tools\make-importlib.ps1). A wrong declaration then fails at link time instead of at runtime.
**Root cause:** the official build path assumes an account linkage we don't have.
**Rule.** For UE4SS C++ mods, generate an import library from the exact UE4SS.dll that ships, and declare a minimal API slice. If the game crashes at mod load, suspect the hand-copied header first. NorseMovementComponent overrides nothing on the input path (vtable diff, tools\vtable_diff.py), so a discard of movement input there lies elsewhere (unit or controller tick); settle it with nrn.diag before patching.

## A UObject pointer kept across frames crashed the game once the game rebuilt the object (NorseRealtimeNative 0.2.1, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** The first 0.2.1 build crashed on release (EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION in UE4SS.dll, called from our main.dll, reading [value removed]). A Lua loop over FindAllOf("NorseCharacter_Unit") teleported about ten units instead of one.
**Cause.** The mod saved the combat-portrait widgets at possess time and restored them at release; between the two, the HUD rebuilt its portraits, so the saved pointers named destroyed objects. FindAllOf also returns objects from earlier loads of the same map that garbage collection has not removed yet. Both looked safe because the pointer was valid when it was taken.
**Fix.** Never keep a widget or actor pointer past a frame without proving it alive: re-find the set with a fresh FindAllOf and act only on entries still in it (ScanPortraits / LivePortraits); filter FindAllOf results by the current world.
**Root cause:** the code treated "found once" as "alive later"; nothing in the mod checked object lifetime, and the UE4SS ABI slice has no weak pointer.
**Rule.** In UE4SS mods, any UObject pointer held across frames is re-validated against a fresh lookup (or a weak pointer) before use; FindAllOf results are filtered to the current world before anything is changed.

## The log said the projectile flew, the screen said it never moved: K2_TeleportTo refused every move (NorseRealtimeNative 0.5.x arrows, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** The owner: arrows stuck in mid-air where they were fired unless he stood close to an enemy. The mod's log showed every arrow "away" and its hits landing, so two wrong explanations were offered first (too fast to see; removal leaving hit arrows behind).
**Cause.** The mod simulated each arrow's position itself and moved the spawned BP_Arrow every frame with AActor::K2_TeleportTo. The arrow spawned inside the hero's capsule, and K2_TeleportTo refuses to move an actor that would overlap something - so the visible arrow never left its spawn point while the simulated one flew on and hit. Close to an enemy the hit landed in a frame or two, which looked right.
**Fix.** Switch the arrow's collision off at spawn (SetActorEnableCollision false; the mod does its own hit tests) and log when a move is refused.
**Root cause:** the code ignored the return value of the call that moves the visible object, and the log described the simulation, not the object on screen.
**Rule.** When a mod moves an actor it simulates, check and log the move call's return value; a log line about the simulated state is not evidence that the visible actor moved. Ask what the player sees before explaining a visual report from the log.

## A reused game animation clip ran the game's own gameplay through its notifies (NorseRealtimeNative 0.5.x bow, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** After the mod's arrow left, the hero drew the bow a second time, the drawn arrow dropped to the ground, and the hand twitched; game arrows lay on the ground after every volley. Four builds tried stopping, pausing and blending the montage, removing stray arrows and hiding the nocked arrow - each fixed one visible symptom and left the cause.
**Cause.** The mod played the game's turn-based shot clip (A_Body_Attack_Bow) as a montage. The clip carries named animation notifies - "Shoot" and "WeaponHit" among 9 - that the game's anim blueprint answers by firing its own arrow and running its own shot sequence. Playing the clip played the game's shot.
**Fix.** Read the clip's Notifies (a probe listed them in one call), then mute the gameplay ones in memory on every clip the mod plays: FAnimNotifyEvent.TriggerWeightThreshold ([value removed]) = 1.5, matched by NotifyName ([value removed]); sound notifies stay. Nothing on disk changes.
**Root cause:** the clip was treated as a pose, not as an asset that also drives gameplay; nobody looked inside it before using it.
**Rule.** Before reusing a game's animation clip or montage in a mod, list its notifies and notify states. Any named gameplay notify (Shoot, Hit, Spawn, Damage...) runs the game's own logic - mute or replace it before blaming the playback.

## A movement test passed because the owner's stick was moving the hero, not because the feature worked (NORSE dodge root motion, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** The new dodges were recorded as travelling 120-215 units "with root motion"; the owner then reported the character does not move at all.
**Cause.** The test ran while the owner was holding the left stick (the mod's SAMPLE lines showed src=pad at the same seconds). His input moved the actor; the clips' root motion was never applied (NorseMovementComponent discards it). The measured travel looked plausible because it was in the dodge's direction.
**Fix.** Re-measured with no input (actor fixed at one point while IsPlayingRootMotion was true), then replaced engine root motion with the mod's own root path per clip.
**Root cause:** the test had no control for the one other thing that moves the actor - live player input - and its result was not checked against the input log of the same seconds.
**Rule.** A movement measurement counts only with input ruled out: check the input source log (SAMPLE src=none / no pad) for the measured window, or run the action with input injection off and the owner told; travel that happens during live input is not evidence for the feature.

## A reflected UFunction call with a hand-sized parameter block fails silently (NORSE aim hold, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** The bow's aim hold stayed on frame 0 (-60 deg) whatever the camera did; no error.
**Cause.** Montage_SetPosition / SetPosition were called with guessed parameter sizes ([value removed], 5). The mod's Reflect::Call checks the size and returns false, and the return value was ignored. A probe calling the same engine function from Lua on the live hold gave the right pose at once, which isolated the fault to our call.
**Fix.** Pass Reflect::Get().ParmsSizeOf(obj, fn) and log a warning when the call returns false.
**Root cause:** parameter-block sizes were typed from memory of the UFunction signature instead of read from the reflected function, and the call's result was not checked.
**Rule.** Every reflected call takes its size from ParmsSizeOf (or a constant checked against it once), and a false return is logged; when a native call "does nothing", first call the same UFunction from a Lua probe on the live object to split engine behaviour from our call.

## A runtime post-process anim blueprint "does nothing" because the game disables the post-process stage (NORSE upper layer, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** SetOverridePostProcessAnimBP installed our layer (GetPostProcessInstance reported our class, our montage was active on it) but the body never showed it; even an override that outputs idle left the walk untouched.
**Cause.** The game sets bDisablePostProcessBlueprint=true on the MetaHuman body, so the post-process instance exists but is never evaluated. Re-enabling it rebuilds the instance from the mesh's own post-process class, so the order matters: enable first, then set the override.
**Fix.** LayerOn reads GetDisablePostProcessBlueprint, enables the stage, then sets the override; LayerOff restores both.
**Root cause:** the probe checked that the object was installed (class name) instead of that its output reached the bones; the cheapest discriminator - an override whose output is unmistakable (idle while walking) - came late.
**Rule.** When a runtime anim override "does nothing", first prove its output reaches the bones with a graph whose effect is unmistakable, and read the component's enable flags (bDisablePostProcessBlueprint, bEnableAnimation, update-rate options) before debugging the graph.

## A test hero that keeps walking one way ends up off the walkable area, and the safety guard's stop looks like a feature bug (NORSE walk tests, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** "The feet stop striding as soon as the bow is drawn" - the hero's speed was 0 from just before the draw.
**Cause.** Repeated forward test walks had carried the hero to the navmesh edge; the mod's nav guard stopped the drive and put him back each time. Nothing to do with the animation layer under test.
**Fix.** Recentre the hero before each movement test; read the SAFETY lines for the test window.
**Root cause:** movement tests reused the hero's position from the previous test instead of starting from a known spot.
**Rule.** A movement test starts by placing the hero at a known open spot, and its verdict checks the guard/safety log lines for the measured window.

## A UE4SS C++ mod's callbacks registered in its constructor are dropped without any error (NorsePatcher 0.1.0, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** NorsePatcher loaded, logged "callbacks registered", and then never ran its InitGameState callback - no dumps, no patches - while the other mods saw the same map load.
**Cause.** The registration ran in the mod's constructor. UE4SS constructs C++ mods before Unreal is initialized and its hook lists exist; a callback registered then is accepted and silently lost. The success log line was mine, written after a call that returns nothing, so it proved nothing.
**Fix.** Register in the `on_unreal_init()` override (NorseRealtimeNative already did; the new mod was written from memory of its constructor instead of its code).
**Root cause:** a new mod was assembled from a remembered pattern rather than copied from the working mod's actual lifecycle code, and the "registered" log line reported the call, not an effect.
**Rule.** In a UE4SS C++ mod, register engine/console/game-state callbacks in `on_unreal_init`, never the constructor; and a "registered" log line is not evidence - the first test must look for the callback's own output.

## A deleted test file kept changing the game: Root Builder's clean-up was cut short by killing MO2 (NORSE, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** A test patch removed from its MO2 mod two runs earlier was still read by NorsePatcher as a "loose file" and changed enemy health, confusing the next framework's test.
**Cause.** Root Builder copies a mod's Root files into the real game folder at launch and removes them when the launched game exits. The earlier runs closed the game and then immediately ran Stop-Process on MO2, so the clean-up was interrupted and the copy stayed in the game folder - outside every mod, invisible in MO2, and no longer tracked for removal.
**Fix.** Deleted the stray copy from the game folder; this run waited after the game quit (the deployed ue4ss\Mods folder was gone before MO2 was closed).
**Root cause:** the test close-down treated MO2 as a plain process to kill, not as the tool that undoes its own deployment on game exit; nothing checked the game folder for leftovers afterwards.
**Rule.** After a Root Builder game exits, wait until the deployed files are gone from the game folder before killing MO2; and before judging a config-driven framework's test, list the game folder's copy of its config folder - a file there that no enabled mod provides is a leftover.

## A setting edited in a Root Builder mod while the game ran was silently reverted at game exit (NorseHUD, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** Two relaunches in a row drew the HUD bars at exactly the same pixels although the bar-height setting had been changed (and the projection code too), which looked like a projection bug.
**Cause.** Root Builder copies a mod's Root files into the game folder at launch and, when the game exits, copies them back into the mod. The INI was edited in the MO2 mod folder while the game was running; the deployed copy still held the old value, and at exit that old copy was written back over the edit. Every "changed" test ran with the old value.
**Fix.** Edited the INI with the game closed and read the value back from the mod folder just before launching; a log line now prints the value the mod actually uses.
**Root cause:** the change was checked where it was written (the mod folder) but not where it is read (the deployed copy at launch), and Root Builder's write-back on exit was not part of the mental model.
**Rule.** Never edit a Root Builder mod's files while the game it deployed is running (or edit the deployed copy for a live test and expect it to come back at exit); before a test that depends on a changed setting, read the value back from the mod folder after the previous game has fully exited, and have the mod log the value it uses.

## An address library that verifies bytes rejects a function another mod has already hooked (Norse Address Library, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** NorseCrashLog could not name any game function: every ID that another Norse mod hooks came back "NOT resolved - signature found 0 time(s)", although the same IDs resolved fine in the mods that hook them.
**Cause.** The library checks the table address by comparing its bytes with the stored signature, and falls back to scanning for the signature. A MinHook hook replaces the function's first bytes with a jump, so both fail for every mod that resolves the ID after the hook is in. Each hooking mod had resolved its IDs before hooking, which hid the problem until a mod resolved them later.
**Fix.** For this build's own table: a jump at the start (E9 rel32 or FF 25) whose following bytes still match the signature is a hooked function - the address is used and logged as such.
**Root cause:** the library was designed and tested with one consumer per function; "hook once and share" (NorseEvents) means many consumers, and nothing tested a second consumer resolving after the first had hooked.
**Rule.** Anything that verifies or scans code bytes must expect another mod's hook at the function start; test every shared-address feature with a consumer that resolves after the hook is installed.

## A UObject pointer cached across frames crashes once its actor is destroyed (Norse UE4SS frameworks, 2026-11-17)

**Symptom.** NORSE crashed about 3 s after a map reload: ACCESS_VIOLATION in UE4SS `GetValuePtrByPropertyNameInChain`, called from NorseHUD. NorseHUD had passed every earlier test, including fights where units died.
**Cause.** NorseHUD refreshes its unit list once a second and reads each unit's health every frame through the stored pointers. A unit that is destroyed (NorseEncounters emptying a spawn point, or the old map's units after a map change) stays in memory until the garbage collector frees it. Inside that one-second window the stored pointer then points at freed memory. Dead units never showed it, because they stay as actors and are never destroyed.
**Fix.** The shared `Ue.hpp` now has `IndexOf(obj)` (UObjectBase [value removed]) and `Alive(obj, index)`: the object array slot still holds the same object, and it is neither pending kill nor unreachable. NorseHUD stores the index beside each pointer and checks `Alive` before every read.
**Root cause:** the frameworks treated a UObject* like a stable handle. Nothing in the shared headers offered a weak-pointer check, so every module that caches actors (HUD units, lock target, impact targets) inherited the same gap, and no test destroyed an actor mid-scene.
**Rule.** Any UObject* kept past the call that found it is stored with its InternalIndex and checked with `Alive()` before use. A test plan for a module that caches actors includes a map reload and a destroyed actor while it is running.

## An object written into a start-up asset is garbage-collected at the next map change (Norse UE4SS frameworks, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** NorseSound swapped the Hit audio event's sound at the title screen and the dump showed the new sound. After the next map change the same field read `<unreadable>` (the export faulted on freed memory).
**Cause.** The swapped-in sound was loaded only by our code, and its one reference sat in an asset loaded at start-up. Assets like that can be kept outside garbage-collection tracking, so the reference was never traced and the sound was freed at the next collection. A swap made after the map had loaded looked fine because no collection had run yet.
**First fix, which turned out wrong.** `LoadKept()` in NorseReflect loads the asset and puts it in the root set (`UObject::SetRootSet`). The NorseSound rerun passed (Hit still read the new sound after two map changes), and the pin was taken as the reason.
**Correction (NorseModelSwap, the same night).** Swapped-in meshes and materials loaded through `LoadKept` were freed at the next map change anyway. `IsRootSet()` read "yes", yet each one came back under a new object index, and the stale pointers crashed the game in SetSkeletalMeshAsset/GetFullName. So the root set does not keep an asset alive across a map change here. The NorseSound rerun most likely passed only because something else (a NorseImpact rule) also uses the punch sound. NorseModelSwap now stores each target's object index, checks it with `Alive()` before every use, and loads a freed target again.
**Second correction (refinement test, the next night, falsification episode 143 - KILLED).** With the same setup, the freeing did not repeat. A sound nothing else uses (Ms_Boar_Jumpscare_001) was swapped into Hit at the title screen and survived two map changes. NorseModelSwap's targets, loaded at the title, kept their object indexes through two map changes. So "the root set does not hold across a map change" is NOT established: freeing happened once and is not reproducible on demand, and its cause is open. The safety net stays because it costs nothing. NorseModelSwap/ObjectSwap/AnimSwap check targets with Alive() and reload them; NorseSound/ModelSwap/ObjectSwap/Loot record their writes (RecordWrite) and re-import any whose assets are no longer loaded at each map load (RecheckWrites, NorseReflect.hpp). Each logs when it acts, so a repeat will show.
**Root cause:** the frameworks assumed that a reference, or the root-set flag, keeps a loaded asset alive across a map change. Neither held, and the passing test had a second explanation that went unchecked: another user of the same asset.
**Rule.** A framework that keeps an asset pointer, or writes one into game data, checks it with `Alive()` (stored index) before each use and reloads it if it was freed. Data written into assets is re-checked at each map load. The test edits at the title screen, changes map twice, and reads back with an asset nothing else uses. A pass that something else could explain is not proof of the fix.

## A frame-count delay runs many times slower when the game window is not in front (Norse UE4SS frameworks, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** NorseSound's MapLoaded moment (set to 120 engine frames after map load) never seemed to fire. A tick counter showed the callback ran, but 120 frames took 28 seconds.
**Cause.** The game runs at about 4 frames a second while its window is in the background, which is where it is during automated tests. A frame count is not a time.
**Fix.** A real-time deadline (`GetTickCount64() + 3000`), checked in the engine tick.
**Root cause:** the delay was written as frames to be "a few frames after load", with no stated time it should take. Frame rate depends on focus, load and hardware.
**Rule.** Any delay that means a time is written as a time (a millisecond deadline), never as a frame count.

## A condition engine that needs a unit for every term makes world conditions false with no unit (NorseConditions, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** `When = Map(CombatTestMap)` read false on CombatTestMap for NorseSound's MapLoaded rule, while `nc.eval Map(CombatTestMap)` said true for all 34 units.
**Cause.** `Value()` returned "cannot read" for every condition when the context had no unit, including conditions about the world (Map, InFight, Chance) that never use one. Every earlier caller evaluated with a unit, so this was never visible.
**Fix.** `Registry::AddWorld` marks a condition as not needing a unit; Map, InFight and Chance use it. 3 offline tests were added (30 of 30 pass).
**Root cause:** the engine was built for unit moments only, and its tests never evaluated without a unit. The null check belonged on each condition, not on the engine.
**Rule.** A shared evaluator's tests include the empty context (no unit, no target), and each condition states whether it needs a subject.

## A game widget set up before it is constructed ignores the setup, and its setter's name can mislead (NMMF, Norse UMG, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** NMMF's switches in the Options screen showed the opposite of the stored value, and labels showed literal quote marks. After the first fix, the switches were still inverted.
**Cause.** Three separate facts. (1) The on/off row fills its two options when it is constructed, so SetIsChecked called just after creating the widget had nothing to select. (2) Even after construction, SetIsChecked(true) put the row on option 1, which displays "Off", because the options are [Toggle_On, Toggle_Off]. The function's name did not match what it showed. (3) An FText imported from a plain quoted string keeps the quotes; the literal-text form INVTEXT("...") does not.
**Fix.** Set a switch on the first poll where the row has its options. Find the On option by its string-table key (Toggle_On, the same in every language) and set the index directly. Labels go in as INVTEXT(...).
**Root cause:** the code trusted a reflected function's name and a widget's lifecycle without reading the result back on screen. The first test only checked the log, which agreed with the code's own model, not the displayed text.
**Rule.** For a game UI row: set values only after it is constructed, verify by reading the displayed state (a frame, or the row's option keys), and never infer semantics from a setter's name. FText values go in as INVTEXT(...).

## A good result credited to a fix whose own call never ran (NMMF decimal display, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** After the float-rounding fix, NMMF's decimal slider showed "0.8" when the Options screen opened, and that was reported as the fix half-working. After a click the number still showed rounded. Three more attempts at the click case changed nothing.
**Cause.** Logging added after four attempts showed NMMF's text write had never once succeeded ("wrote 1 ok 0" every poll). The "0.8" on opening was the game's own formatting: the row formats with one decimal when it is built, and with a whole number when the mouse lets go. Every fix had been aimed at a call that never reached the screen, and a pass that the game produced on its own had been read as evidence the fix worked.
**Fix.** After five attempts, fixes were stopped (rule 49) and the planned analysis logged every guard. It showed "SetText parms 16": an FText is 16 bytes in this engine build, and the helper's guard required 24, so it refused every call. With the sizes taken from the engine, and the text made by KismetTextLibrary.Conv_StringToText, the slider showed 1.5 and 0.7 after clicks (request 6fad).
**Root cause:** the helper's success flag was never logged. Each test judged the outcome by what was on screen, and something other than the fix could put the right thing there.
**Rule.** A fix that works through a call logs that call's success on the first test. A pass is credited to a fix only when the fix's own call is seen succeeding. The analysis logging comes before the second attempt, not after the fourth.

## A check that returns quietly on missing input looks exactly like "nothing happened" (NorseRealtimeNative fight end, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** Real-time fights never ended: after every enemy died, FightTick never logged "every enemy ... is down", and FightEnded was never published. A log added every 5 s inside the check printed nothing at all.
**Cause.** The check ran every half second, but returned before its count whenever the combat area's UnitsInArea list was empty. That list is filled by the turn-based start, which real-time mode skips, so it was always empty. The first fix attempt swapped the area-validity test (a FindAllOf search, which also fails silently) for Alive(); that changed nothing, because the return was one line later.
**Fix.** When UnitsInArea is empty, count the hostiles from every unit in the area's level. The fight then ended and FightEnded was published (request 20a8).
**Root cause:** early returns on "can't read the input" had no log line, so "the input is missing" and "the condition is false" looked the same from outside. The diagnostic log was placed after those returns, not before them.
**Rule.** Every early return in a per-frame check logs its reason once. A diagnostic line goes at the top of the function, not after its guards. A list the game fills in one mode is checked for emptiness in the other mode before it is relied on.

## A "remove" that only switches a flag off does nothing where the flag was already off (NorseEncounters on a real mission, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** On SideMission_SeasideSkirmish the log said "SpawnPoint_6: removed / emptied", yet when the point was told to spawn (as the mission does when the fight starts) the poacher appeared. An Extra unit stood at its point from map load, before its encounter.
**Cause.** Remove was built and tested on the combat test map, whose points spawn at load (AutoSpawn on). Its whole mechanism was "write AutoSpawn False and destroy what spawned". Every enemy point of a real mission already has AutoSpawn False and spawns later, so the write changed nothing and there was nothing to destroy yet. The log line described the action taken, not the outcome. Second trap while fixing it: the first fix waited for UE4SS's BeginPlay callback, which never fired for a unit spawned later by the point - the check simply never ran.
**Fix.** A removed or extra point that has not spawned is watched (0.1 s real-time poll while any is watched): emptied each time it spawns, extras spawned with its own unit. Proven by calling the point's SpawnActor twice.
**Root cause:** the framework was proven only on a test map whose objects were in a different starting state (AutoSpawn on) from every real use, and the success log reported the write rather than its effect on the thing the rule is about.
**Rule.** Test a rule on the state the real content is in (here: a real mission's deferred points), and log the effect ("point spawned nothing") not the action ("AutoSpawn=False written"). A flag write that leaves the value unchanged is a no-op - check the old value. And when a hook-driven check "does nothing", first prove the hook fires (one log line inside it).

## A test kit built during a session lived only in its scratchpad - a whole night's helpers would vanish when the session was archived (Norse frameworks retrospective, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** Two nights of Norse framework testing ran on helpers written as they were needed: the Lua bus sender, the key/click sender, the screenshot script and 33 Lua probes. At the retrospective, every one of them was in the session's temporary scratchpad; no role named them, no skill pointed at them, and the next session would have rewritten them.
**Cause.** Each helper was made as a one-off for the step in front of it, and the scratchpad is the default home for temporary files. Nothing asks, at the third reuse, "this is a tool now". The summary that carried the session across a context reset listed them by name, which made them feel recorded.
**Fix.** Moved to `.MD\scripts\norse\` (role `norse-test-kit`), named in the new `norse-ue4ss` skill.
**Root cause:** the pipeline has a step for promoting a lesson (library entry, gate) but none for promoting a helper - a script reused across batches has no point at which it must leave the scratchpad.
**Rule.** A helper used in a second test batch is moved out of the scratchpad into `.MD\scripts\<area>\` and given a role that day. At a retrospective or session wrap-up, list the scratchpad's scripts used more than once and move them.

## The library held the same lesson three times and it was repeated a fourth - "read the area's entries first" did not fire because a copy did not feel like an area (Norse frameworks retrospective, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** A rebuilt DLL was copied into a Root Builder mod while the game ran and the old code was tested twice. The library already held this exact lesson three times (2026-09-29, and twice on 2026-11-17, the night before).
**Cause.** Rule 52 says to grep the library by area before acting. "Copy a DLL into the mod" felt like a mechanical sub-step of a test, not an area, so no lookup happened; and three entries for one lesson read as three separate stories, so the count itself never signalled "this keeps happening".
