**Fix.** Gates: the PreToolUse hook `root-builder-live-write-guard` and the Norse launch check `norse-deployed-build-check`; plus `repeated-lesson-scan`, which lists subject terms the library holds in three or more headings with no gate naming them (its first run also surfaced the stale-UObject class, four entries, now `ue-cached-pointer-gate`, which then found two real cases in NorseImpact).
**Root cause:** a lookup that depends on recognising "I am in an area" fails on the steps that feel too small to be one, and nothing counted repeats - the library's growth was never read as a signal.
**Rule.** The third entry for the same lesson is the trigger for a gate, not a fourth entry. Run `repeated-lesson-scan` at each retrospective / optimizer pass and decide every NO GATE cluster: gate it, or record in `repeated-lesson-scan-ignore.txt` why it is a topic and not one lesson.

## A test that passed by itself failed inside the pre-commit hook - the hook's GIT_DIR aimed the test's git calls at the repo being committed (kit-daily-push, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** tests/test_kit_daily_push.py passed run by hand (5/5) and failed under the pre-commit hook that runs the tests of a changed tool ("2 failed", commit refused).
**Cause.** Git runs hooks with GIT_DIR (and GIT_INDEX_FILE and others) set to the repository being committed. Every child `git -C <other repo>` inherits them, and GIT_DIR wins over -C - so the test's clone, remote and commit calls were aimed at the .MD repo instead of the temporary clone. Checked afterwards: the .MD remote and config were unchanged (the calls failed rather than wrote), but a git call aimed at the wrong repo can write.
**Fix.** The job and its test pass an environment with every GIT_* variable removed to each git call; the test now also passes with GIT_DIR set by hand.
**Root cause:** a tool that drives git in another repo assumed a clean environment, and it is run from inside git hooks (the test runner, and the global pre-push hook can call tools too).
**Rule.** Any script that runs git against a repo other than the one it lives in strips GIT_* from the child environment. Test such a script once with GIT_DIR set to a different repo.

## Blender resolved a relative texture path against the .blend file, not the working folder - renders came out untextured (Pipeline Kit 1.1.0 render_lib, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** The generalised render_lib.py, run from the kit, produced renders with missing (pink or flat) textures while the same NIFs rendered correctly from the Ebony repo's own render scripts.
**Cause.** Blender resolves a relative image path against the folder of the current .blend file (or its temp location when none is saved), not the process's working folder. The Ebony scripts only worked because they were always started from the folder that happened to match.
**Fix.** render_lib makes every texture root absolute before it loads an image. The Ebony repo's original copy keeps the same latent fault (not changed; it works where it is run).
**Root cause:** a path that worked from one start folder was taken as a correct path; Blender's own rule for relative paths was never read.
**Rule.** Every path handed to Blender (images, NIFs, outputs) is absolute. A render tool is tested once from a different working folder before it is shared.

## The self-test hid Blender's add-ons by moving USERPROFILE - PyNifly read as "not installed" when it was (Pipeline Kit 1.1.0 self-test, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** The kit self-test's Blender probe reported PyNifly missing on a machine where it is installed and renders work.
**Cause.** kit-selftest.ps1 points USERPROFILE at a temporary folder so the install steps cannot touch the real profile. Blender finds user add-ons under %APPDATA%, which follows the profile, so the probe ran a Blender with no user add-ons.
**Fix.** The Blender probe runs under the real profile; the rest of the self-test keeps the temporary one.
**Root cause:** an isolation step meant for one kind of check (install writes) was applied to a check that reads the real environment.
**Rule.** When a test sandboxes the profile, any check that probes an installed third-party tool runs outside the sandbox, and a "not installed" result is confirmed against the real environment once before it is believed.

## The kit copied the skills folder whole, so a skill another session was still writing would have shipped (Pipeline Kit 1.1.0 build, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** The 1.1.0 build picked up norse-ue4ss, a skill another session was writing that night for another game, untracked and unfinished.
**Cause.** build_kit.py copies every text file under .MD\skills\ (minus a cut list), so anything placed there ships on the next build, finished or not and relevant or not.
**Fix.** A SKILLS_LEFT_OUT list in build_kit.py holds norse-ue4ss out. An allowlist of shipped skills was proposed instead, so a new skill ships only when someone decides it should.
**Root cause:** a build that includes by folder treats "present on disk" as "meant to ship", and several sessions write into that folder at once.
**Rule.** A public build includes by list, not by folder, wherever other sessions write. Until the skills step is an allowlist, check `git status` of .MD\skills for untracked skills before every kit build.

## A skill line said the Pipeline Kit is never mentioned on Nexus, and a memory a month newer said it is free - the skill was believed (Nexus reply to nexusguy, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** Told the owner the reply could not point at the Members Pipeline Kit post because Nexus bars paid or members-only content. He corrected it: "its not paid or members only, its free to download".
**Cause.** The nexus-page skill still said "The Pipeline Kit is never mentioned on Nexus", written when the kit was a paid product. The memory pipeline-kit-is-free-and-open (2026-10-24) had replaced that, but the skill was not updated and the memory was not looked up.
**Fix.** The skill line now says the kit is free and may be linked, and names the memory; the memory gained a line on linking it from Nexus.
**Root cause:** a standing instruction was taken from the first document that mentioned it, without checking the newer memory for the same subject; and a memory that reversed a rule did not carry its change into the skill that repeated the old rule.
**Rule.** Before stating a policy about a product or channel to the owner, grep the memory index for that product's name. A memory that reverses a rule also edits every skill or rules line that repeats the old one, the same day.

## A read-only Lua probe crashed the game - pcall does not catch a UFunction called on a null object (Norse, UE4SS Lua, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** A probe that only read unit state (position, controller, its BrainComponent and move status), every read wrapped in pcall, closed the game. NorseCrashLog: ACCESS_VIOLATION in UE4SS.dll inside LuaMadeSimple::process_lua_function, reading address [value removed].
**Cause.** UE4SS hands Lua a wrapper even for a null object property; calling a UFunction through it runs native code on a null `this`. That is a hardware fault, not a Lua error, so pcall never sees it. Wrapping everything in pcall looked like safety and was none.
**Fix.** Check `IsValid()` on every object before any call on it ([code removed]), and use only calls other probes have already run safely; a new call is tried once on its own.
**Root cause:** pcall was trusted as a crash guard in a runtime where the dangerous failures are native.
**Rule.** In UE4SS Lua, `IsValid()` before every call on an object you did not just create; never rely on pcall to contain an engine call.

## Four PreToolUse guards let every call through when stdin began with a UTF-8 BOM - they exit 0 on unparseable input (Pipeline Kit 1.1.0 self-test, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** The kit self-test passed 65/65 from Git Bash and failed 2/65 from the PowerShell tool: the bash-backslash-guard and mo2-elevated-launch-guard "REFUSES" checks let the call through.
**Cause.** Windows PowerShell 5.1 under code page 65001 puts a BOM in front of text it pipes to a native program. The guards read stdin with json.load, which throws on the BOM, and every guard treats a parse error as "nothing to check" and exits 0 - so the guard failed open. Real Claude Code hook calls send no BOM, which is why it never showed in use.
**Fix.** All four guards read the bytes and decode them as utf-8-sig; bash-backslash-guard and mo2-elevated-launch-guard gained tests (they had none; the mo2 test fails on the old guard), and the other two tests gained a BOM case (.MD commit b59969b).
**Root cause:** "fail open on unparseable input" was chosen so a guard never blocks work by mistake, without asking what else makes input unparseable besides a missing payload.
**Rule.** A guard that exits 0 on unparseable input decodes its input as utf-8-sig and has a test that feeds it a BOM-prefixed refusal case. Run a hook's self-test from both consoles (Git Bash and PowerShell) before shipping it.

## Every bow draw stalled 125-224 ms - each clip lookup searched the whole object list, and our clips were collected between uses (NorseRealtimeNative, UE4SS, 2026-11-18)

**Symptom.** The owner felt the game "stutters quite a bit". A per-frame timer added to the mod (QPC around each of its systems, a HITCH line for any frame over 50 ms naming the system) showed frames of 125-224 ms inside this mod's own code at every bow draw and release, and ~200 ms at hit reactions - with no enemies on the map.
**Cause.** Two costs that looked free in the code: `StaticFindObject_InternalSlow` (every LoadByPath / FindObj began with it) walks the engine's whole object list on each call, and each clip's first use loaded it from disk mid-play. Caching the lookups and preloading at map load was not enough: the preloaded clips were garbage-collected before the fight (nothing of the game referred to them), so possession reloaded all 40 (1.9 s). Without the timer, "stutter" read as an animation fault, and both causes were invisible.
**Fix.** A path -> (object, object-array slot) cache in front of every lookup, Alive-checked; every clip and class the mod plays preloaded at map load and kept in the root set; FindAllOf routed through one timed wrapper and a 0.25 s unit cache. After: second draw 0 slow frames, possession preload 0 ms, object searches 7 ms per 5 s.
**Root cause:** a mod's per-frame cost was never measured, so expensive engine calls (`*_InternalSlow`, FindAllOf, synchronous loads) sat on hot paths, and assets only the mod referenced were assumed to stay loaded.
**Rule.** Ship a frame-time log in any mod that acts per frame (PERF summary + HITCH naming the part) and read it before judging a stutter. Never call StaticFindObject_InternalSlow / FindAllOf / a blocking load on a per-frame or per-event path without a cache; load at map load and pin (root set) anything only the mod references.
